However, the design and implementation of computerized tests in an online environment come with various challenges. This article probes the issues, needs and challenges for the development of online assessment of reading and maths, and related cognitive abilities. The paper aims to inform researchers about logistical and technical considerations of developing a customized platform for online child data collection, including (a) technical considerations, (b) interface design, (c) data management, and (d) planning for validation against paper-and-pencil measures. These issues are illustrated with experiences gleaned from the development of an online assessment platform (ACE Kids platform), designed to deliver over 40 tests and questionnaires related to Chinese and English literacy as well as mathematics abilities in K3 - P6 children. The paper also highlights the unique challenges surrounding building online, self-directed biliteracy assessment involving a large assessment battery. Furthermore, we discuss features that improve the ease of use, instructional clarity, and retention of attention. We discussed the use of questionnaires to sample child usage experience during early stages of assessment development to optimize design. Finally, we give consolidated advice for the planning, development and data collection stages for such a customized assessment platform.

Virome dynamics of Aedes albopictus during the 2025 chikungunya outbreak in Foshan.
Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has re-emerged globally, yet little is known about how natural CHIKV transmission influences the resident virome of mosquito vectors under field conditions. Here, we combined continuous entomological surveillance, viral genomics and metagenomic sequencing to characterize CHIKV transmission and virome dynamics in Aedes albopictus during the 2025 chikungunya outbreak in Foshan, China. Mosquitoes were continuously collected throughout the outbreak using pooled and individual sampling strategies, and viral metagenomic sequencing was performed to compare virome composition between CHIKV-positive and CHIKV-negative mosquitoes. CHIKV-positive mosquitoes first appeared shortly after the onset of local human transmission and expanded geographically in parallel with the epidemic. Mosquito- and human-derived CHIKV genomes were nearly identical and belonged to a genetically homogeneous East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineage, supporting sustained local mosquito-human transmission. Despite widespread CHIKV circulation, the resident mosquito virome remained broadly stable, with sampling time contributing more to virome variation than CHIKV infection status. Only two resident viruses, Orthophasmavirus barstukorius and Guato virus, were significantly associated with CHIKV infection. Integration of pooled and individual sequencing further showed that pooled samples reliably represented the population-level core virome, whereas individual mosquitoes revealed substantial inter-individual heterogeneity. Five previously undescribed RNA viruses were also identified, expanding the known virosphere of Ae. albopictus. Together, our findings show that natural CHIKV emergence is accompanied by limited species-specific shifts rather than wholesale restructuring of the resident mosquito virome, and highlight the value of integrating genomic and metagenomic surveillance into vector-borne disease monitoring.

Population-level measles RT-PCR cycle threshold values and their relationships with disease severity, transmission, and incidence metrics: a time series analysis of the 2025-2026 outbreak in Mexico.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether the weekly median real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) quantification cycle (Cq) value of notified measles cases precedes the incidence, transmission, and severity metrics of an outbreak. We focused particularly on the effective reproduction number (R t ). We also assessed whether any association persisted after adjustment for a linear time trend, specimen composition, and the outcome's own past. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis of 10,910 Cq determinations and 11,735 confirmed cases recorded in a single Mexican national case-level surveillance extract for Chihuahua and Jalisco. Twelve reported weekly metrics of incidence, transmission, and severity were examined by cross-correlation, four nested lagged regression models (M1-M4), formal Toda-Yamamoto Granger tests, and a secondary calibrated-lag autoregressive model. Moving-block bootstrap intervals were the primary method for regression inference. Autocorrelation-robust and classical methods were used in sensitivity analyses. Individual Cq determinations were analyzed separately against collection timing, severity, and vaccination history. RESULTS: Selected-lag associations were negative across all reported metric families, at leads of 1-9 weeks. The strongest negative correlation between Cq and DGE-derived R t occurred at +8 weeks in the second Chihuahua wave (r = -0.745). In Jalisco, it occurred at +7 weeks (r = -0.464). Only Jalisco supported the fully adjusted model 4 (M4). There, bootstrap intervals excluded zero for both the laboratory-positive-case and final surveillance-confirmed-case R t estimates but not for the two severity proportions. Excluding up to four endpoint weeks preserved the direction of both R t estimates. At the individual level, Cq increased with zero, one, and two documented vaccine doses (0.761 cycles per dose, 95% CI 0.589 to 0.932) and was 1.02 cycles lower in hospitalized cases. CONCLUSIONS: Aggregate Cq showed the most consistent retrospective leading association with R t . The retrospective associations occurred at data-calibrated lags of 7-8 weeks during the second Chihuahua wave and in Jalisco. Conversely, leak-free forecasting supported incremental gain in one analytic unit at a median 2-week horizon. The operational predictive horizon of aggregate Cq therefore remains unvalidated. If prospectively validated, weekly aggregate Cq could complement conventional measles surveillance using laboratory information that is already routinely collected.

Case Report: Henoch-Schönlein-like purpura as an unusual presentation of acute hepatitis E virus infection.
INTRODUCTION: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection is increasingly recognized as a cause of extrahepatic manifestations; however, cutaneous purpuric manifestations are exceptionally rare, with only one previous case of Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP) reported in association with acute HEV infection. METHODS: This study describes the case of a 91-year-old man admitted with palpable purpura of the lower limbs, associated with jaundice, hypertransaminasemia, and cholestatic abnormalities. Molecular and serological assays were performed. RESULTS: Serological testing showed anti-HEV IgM and IgG positivity, and HEV RNA was detected in plasma at a viral load of 15,002 IU/mL. The patient reported consumption of wild-boar meat in the month preceding symptom onset. The purpura resolved spontaneously approximately 10 days after onset, and liver parameters progressively improved, with HEV RNA becoming undetectable at follow-up. Phylogenetic analysis of the patient-derived sequence identified the strain as HEV genotype 3f, belonging to the 3f2 subcluster. The patient-derived sequence showed similarity with European HEV-3f/3f2 human strains and with swine and wild boar strains, supporting a likely zoonotic food-borne origin. Plasma interleukin-6 (IL-6) was elevated at admission during the purpuric manifestation. DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first Italian report of an HSP-like purpura temporally associated with acute HEV genotype 3f infection. This case highlights that acute HEV infection may be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with palpable purpura, while emphasizing the exceptional rarity of this manifestation.

Pathogen spectrum and triple-criteria interpretation algorithm of BALF-targeted NGS in children with refractory severe community-acquired pneumonia in mountainous Northeastern Sichuan: a single-center retrospective study.
BACKGROUND: Severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) causes substantial pediatric hospitalization and respiratory failure in mountainous western China. Conventional microbial assays show limited sensitivity for fastidious pathogens and mixed infections. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) using bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) enables broad-spectrum pathogen detection at lower cost than whole-metagenomic sequencing. However, many previous tNGS studies directly equate multiple microbial nucleic-acid signals with true coinfection, which may lead to unnecessary combined anti-infective therapy. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 86 children aged 1.0 × 106 copies/mL), inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, PCT), and chest imaging to discriminate genuine active coinfection from airway colonization. This load threshold was empirical and not internally validated by ROC analysis in our dataset. Patients were stratified into four age subgroups; diagnostic concordance was assessed among 34 patients with parallel routine microbial tests. RESULTS: In total, 229 pathogen isolates were identified. Viruses predominated (58.9%, 135/229), followed by bacteria (32.8%, 75/229). The three most frequent pathogens were Haemophilus influenzae (32.56%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (30.23%), and respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV-A, 18.60%). While 82.6% (71/86) of patients harbored ≥2 pathogen nucleic-acid signals, only 17.4% (15/86) fulfilled criteria for clinical coinfection, dominated by virus-bacterial dual infection. Viral detection rates tended to decline with increasing age, whereas bacterial positivity was higher among preschool- and school-age children. A prominent spring epidemic peak was observed during May-June 2023. Only 22.86% of paired routine microbial tests showed full concordance with tNGS. These single-center data cannot be generalized to all pediatric severe-pneumonia populations. Most abundant multi-pathogen tNGS signals represented colonization or residual dead-microbe nucleic acid instead of true active infection. CONCLUSION: Our triple-criteria interpretive framework offers standardized rules for grassroots mountain hospitals to reduce over-prescription of combined antibiotics and antivirals when interpreting BALF-tNGS results for children with refractory SCAP.

Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Severity and Population-Specific Outcomes of Human Metapneumovirus Infection.
BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a prevalent respiratory pathogen, but comprehensive estimates of severe clinical outcomes across populations are lacking. We synthesized the proportion of severe outcomes among people with laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection. METHOD: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, medRxiv, bioRxiv, and Google Scholar from inception to 20 January 2026, without language restrictions. Observational studies reporting severe outcomes (hospitalization, intensive care unit [ICU] admission, respiratory support, mechanical ventilation, mortality) in laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection were eligible; studies enrolling only people who are immunocompromised without comparators were excluded. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed quality using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects generalized linear mixed models with logit transformation. Subgroup analyses examined healthcare setting and age. RESULTS: Ninety-four studies (∼26 000 people who are HMPV positive) were included. Pooled proportions were 48% (95% CI, 20%-78%; 8 studies, n = 1445) for hospitalization; 12% (95% CI, 8%-16%; 26 studies, n = 14 522; Egger P = .03) for ICU admission; 40% (95% CI, 26%-56%; 18 studies, n = 4328) for respiratory support; 8% (95% CI, 5%-13%; 16 studies, n = 5543) for mechanical ventilation; and 3% (95% CI, 2%-5%; 29 studies, n = 13 657; I2 = 78.5%) for in-hospital mortality. Mortality was highest among adults (6%). CONCLUSIONS: Human metapneumovirus causes substantial hospitalization, ICU admission, and mortality, supporting strengthened surveillance, integration into respiratory virus prevention strategies, and accelerated vaccine development.

Oleanolic Acid-Loaded Organosilica Nanoparticles for Synergistic Anti-Inflammatory and Antibacterial Therapy via Inducing Macrophage Polarization.
Chronic inflammatory diseases caused by bacterial infections are notoriously difficult to treat due to the formation of a vicious cycle in which bacterial infection and immune dysregulation mutually reinforce each other at the lesion site. Current antibiotic therapies face the dual challenges of escalating drug resistance and insufficient immunomodulatory capacity. Inspired by stimuli-responsive nanodrug delivery systems, we herein constructed a glutathione-responsive dendritic mesoporous organosilica nanoparticles (DMOS NPs) loaded with oleanolic acid (OA), namely DMOS@OA NPs, aiming to achieve synergistic antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy. The DMOS@OA NPs exhibited a uniform hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 232.1 ± 9.49 nm with typical dendritic spherical morphology, a drug loading capacity of 30.01%, and an encapsulation efficiency of 85.74%. In vitro release experiments demonstrated that DMOS@OA NPs displayed significant pH-responsive release behavior, achieving a cumulative OA release of 58.98% under acidic conditions (pH 5.5). Furthermore, the DMOS@OA NPs could respond to high concentrations of glutathione by cleaving tetrasulfide bonds to release therapeutic hydrogen sulfide (H2S). Antibacterial assays revealed that DMOS@OA NPs exhibited remarkable bactericidal activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), with superior efficacy compared to DMOS NPs and OA, and effectively inhibited bacterial biofilm formation with an inhibition rate of 85.78%. Scanning electron microscopy observations further confirmed that the DMOS@OA NPs could disrupt bacterial membrane integrity, leading to bacterial lysis and death. In vitro anti-inflammatory experiments demonstrated that DMOS@OA NPs possessed good biocompatibility and could significantly downregulate the expression of the M1 macrophage marker CD86 while upregulating the M2 marker CD206, and reduced the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and TNF-α, effectively inducing macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory phenotype to the anti-inflammatory phenotype. In conclusion, we successfully constructed a GSH-responsive DMOS@OA nanosystem with dual antibacterial and anti-inflammatory functions. Through the synergistic action of H2S and OA, this nanosystem achieves integrated efficient bactericidal activity and immunomicroenvironment regulation, providing a highly promising novel nanotherapeutic strategy for the treatment of chronic infectious inflammatory diseases.

Clinical characteristics, molecular features and in vitro susceptibility to sulbactam-durlobactam, cefiderocol, and eravacycline in NDM-1-producing versus OXA-23-producing carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from children in Guangxi, China.
BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB) has been recognized as a critical priority pathogen responsible for a wide range of hospital-acquired infections. METHODS: We included pediatric CRAB infection cases at a Maternal and Child Health Hospital in Guangxi, China, from January 2019 to December 2024. The bacterial isolates had previously undergone whole-genome sequencing (WGS). An NDM-1-producing CRAB strain isolated from a bloodstream infection was subjected to Nanopore sequencing to characterize the NDM-1-encoding plasmid. We then retrospectively analyzed the risk factors for NDM-1-producing CRAB infection in children. In addition, the NDM-1-producing and OXA-23-producing CRAB strains were subjected to antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) against sulbactam-durlobactam, cefiderocol, and eravacycline using the micro-broth dilution method, and their susceptibility profiles were compared. Associated resistance genes were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 131 pediatric patients with CRAB infections were included in this study. Based on the WGS data, 33 CRAB strains harboring bla NDM-1 were classified into the NDM-1-producing group, while 98 CRAB strains harboring bla OXA-23 were classified into the OXA-23-producing group. On multivariable analysis, indwelling urethral catheters (OR = 0.293; P = 0.009) and white blood cell (WBC) count (OR = 0.896; P = 0.039) were negatively associated with NDM-1-producing CRAB infection, yet positively associated with OXA-23-producing infections (P < 0.05). WGS analysis revealed that 32 of the 33 (97.0%) NDM-1-producing CRAB isolates co-carried bla PER-1, which has been reported to be associated with cefiderocol resistance in A. baumannii. Plasmid mapping showed that the same plasmid co-harbored bla NDM-1 and bla PER-1, together with a type IV secretion system (T4SS). The resistance rate of NDM-1-producing CRAB isolates to sulbactam-durlobactam was 100%, and to cefiderocol was 66.7%-both rates being significantly higher than those observed in the OXA-23-producing group (1.0% and 0.0%, respectively; P < 0.001). However, all 131 isolates demonstrated susceptibility to eravacycline in vitro. CONCLUSION: Clinical characteristics and antibiotic susceptibility differed significantly between NDM-1-producing and OXA-23-producing CRAB infections. Carbapenemase surveillance is critical for the management of CRAB infections among pediatric patients in Guangxi, China, and AST is essential to guide treatment.

Case Report: Liangxue Jiedu Huayu Formula as adjunctive therapy for leptospirosis with Weil's syndrome.
BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis is a global zoonotic disease with over one million cases annually worldwide. Approximately 5%-10% of patients progress to Weil's syndrome, characterized by multi-organ failure and high mortality, but treatment options remain limited. This report describes a patient with severe leptospirosis who showed marked improvement following treatment with Liangxue Jiedu Huayu Formula (LXJDHYF), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, and explores potential mechanisms. CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old male farmer developed high fever, jaundice, acute kidney injury, and early disseminated intravascular coagulation after working in a lotus pond. Leptospirosis was confirmed by a four-fold rise in MAT titer from 1:50 to 1:200. Despite initial treatment with conventional therapies including antibiotics, continuous renal replacement therapy, and plasma infusion, the patient remained febrile with persistently elevated white blood cell and bilirubin levels. From day 5 of hospitalization, LXJDHYF was added. Fever gradually subsided, total bilirubin progressively decreased, serum creatinine eventually normalized, and coagulation function returned to normal. At 6-month follow-up, the patient had fully recovered. MECHANISTIC EXPLORATION: Network pharmacology identified 14 common targets, including ICAM1, SELE, TLR4, and SERPINE1. KEGG enrichment revealed pathways related to TLR4/NF-κB signaling, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, and complement/coagulation cascades. Molecular docking showed strong binding affinities (≤ -7.0 kcal/mol) between core components (cryptotanshinone, nortanshinone, rhein, naringenin) and core targets (TLR4, ICAM1, ALB). These computational findings are hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation. CONCLUSION: This case suggests that adjuvant treatment with LXJDHYF may be beneficial for leptospirosis complicated by Weil's syndrome, based on conventional therapy. Network pharmacology has generated testable hypotheses regarding multi-target modulation of inflammatory, adhesion, and coagulation pathways. These computational findings require experimental validation.

Clinical factors associated with carbapenem resistance and in-hospital mortality in Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection: a 7-year retrospective cohort study.
BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection (CRKP BSI) is associated with substantial mortality and limited therapeutic options, yet institutional epidemiology and risk profiles vary. We evaluated antimicrobial susceptibility, non-blood-site detection, factors associated with carbapenem resistance, and in-hospital all-cause mortality among patients with K. pneumoniae BSI at a secondary-care hospital over seven years. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 141 adults with K. pneumoniae BSI hospitalized at Shidong Hospital, Shanghai, China, from January 2019 through December 2025, including 49 patients with CRKP BSI and 92 with carbapenem-susceptible K. pneumoniae BSI (CSKP BSI). Clinical and microbiological data were analyzed using univariable comparisons and multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Crude in-hospital mortality was higher among patients with CRKP BSI than among those with CSKP BSI (40.8% vs. 16.3%; p = 0.002). Among the tested CRKP isolates, high in vitro susceptibility to ceftazidime/avibactam and tigecycline was observed. In multivariable analysis, pulmonary disease (aOR, 9.441; 95% CI, 2.958-30.136; p < 0.001), urinary catheterization before BSI onset (aOR, 13.821; 95% CI, 3.987-47.904; p < 0.001), prior carbapenem exposure (aOR, 3.982; 95% CI, 1.274-12.448; p = 0.018), and prior cephalosporin exposure (aOR, 11.341; 95% CI, 3.411-37.713; p < 0.001) were associated with carbapenem resistance. Non-blood-site detection of K. pneumoniae was more frequent in CRKP BSI than in CSKP BSI (73.5% vs. 35.9%; p < 0.001). In the overall mortality model, sepsis or septic shock assessed at BSI onset or within 48 h thereafter was associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR, 4.738; 95% CI, 1.916-11.720; p < 0.001), whereas the adjusted association of CRKP BSI status with mortality did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSION: In multivariable analysis, pulmonary disease, urinary catheterization before BSI onset, prior carbapenem exposure, and prior cephalosporin exposure were associated with carbapenem resistance. Although crude mortality was higher among patients with CRKP BSI, sepsis or septic shock was associated with higher odds of mortality after adjustment for age and CRKP BSI status, whereas the adjusted association of CRKP BSI status with mortality did not reach statistical significance. These findings support targeted infection prevention, antimicrobial stewardship, appropriate urinary catheter use, and early recognition and management of sepsis.

Diethyl fumarate exhibits potent activity against differentially culturable Mycobacterium tuberculosis persisters.
Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. During infection, Mtb forms drug-tolerant persisters, including differentially culturable (DC) cells that fail to grow on solid media and contribute to prolonged TB treatment and disease relapse. DC Mtb formation is driven by host inflammatory responses, particularly nitric oxide (NO), suggesting that anti-inflammatory agents may limit persister generation. Here, we developed a workflow to evaluate the activity of drug candidates against DC Mtb persisters. This approach was validated using dimethyl fumarate (DMF) derivatives, as DMF has previously been shown to eradicate DC Mtb but is limited by instability and poor solubility. We assessed DMF and nine DMF derivatives for antimycobacterial activity. The workflow included antimicrobial susceptibility testing against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) and Mycobacterium abscessus (Mabs), followed by cytotoxicity evaluation and measurement of NO release in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated macrophages. Selected DMF derivatives were further tested against DC Mtb persisters generated in vitro using a NO donor as well as persisters recovered from interferon γ-stimulated macrophages. DMF and diethyl fumarate (DEF) inhibited Mtb growth, while ethyl-3-benzoylacrylate (EBL) and methyl-trans-4-oxo-2-pentenoate (MTOP) exhibited bactericidal activity against both Mtb and Mabs. DEF effectively eliminated DC Mtb in infected macrophages, with activity comparable to DMF. This anti-DC Mtb persister effect was associated with reduced NO production, highlighting the importance of anti-inflammatory activity in targeting DC Mtb persisters. DMF and its more soluble and stable derivative DEF represent promising candidates for the development of therapies targeting DC Mtb persisters. Their dual anti-inflammatory and anti-mycobacterial properties support their potential as a novel therapeutic strategy against persistent tuberculosis infections.

Leishmaniasis and vaccine development: current progress, challenges, and future perspectives.
Leishmaniasis remains one of the most important neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), affecting millions of individuals across tropical and subtropical regions. Caused by protozoan parasites of the genus Leishmania and transmitted by infected female phlebotomine sandflies, the disease manifests in a spectrum of clinical forms ranging from localized cutaneous lesions to fatal visceral infections. Despite substantial progress in disease control programmes, leishmaniasis continues to pose significant public health, socioeconomic, and healthcare challenges in endemic countries. Current chemotherapeutic options, including pentavalent antimonials, amphotericin B formulations, miltefosine, paromomycin, and pentamidine, are constrained by toxicity, prolonged treatment regimens, high costs, and the emergence of drug-resistant parasite strains. Moreover, the absence of a licensed human vaccine remains a major obstacle to sustainable disease control. Consequently, the development of effective vaccines has emerged as a major research priority. Advances in molecular parasitology, immunology, and vaccine technology have led to the development of first-generation killed and live-attenuated vaccines, second-generation recombinant protein and subunit vaccines, and third-generation nucleic acid-based vaccine platforms. Recent innovations involving mRNA vaccines, viral vectors, genetically attenuated parasites, and controlled human infection models have further accelerated translational research. In parallel, advances in genomics, immunoinformatics, artificial intelligence, and nanotechnology are facilitating the identification of novel therapeutic targets, vaccine antigens, and precision intervention strategies. Nevertheless, the complex biology of Leishmania, antigenic diversity, and sophisticated immune-evasion mechanisms continue to impede vaccine licensure. This review discusses the global burden of leishmaniasis, host-parasite interactions, current therapeutic approaches, mechanisms of drug resistance, vaccine development strategies, and emerging technologies that are shaping the future of leishmaniasis prevention and treatment.

In sickness and in health: profiling the bovine fecal eukaryome using optimized 18S metabarcoding with a mammal-blocking primer.
INTRODUCTION: Calf diarrhea, caused by the apicomplexan pathogen Cryptosporidium parvum (C. parvum), poses significant economic and production challenges to the livestock industry. While 16S rRNA sequencing has advanced understanding of the bovine bacterial gut microbiota, the eukaryotic community remains underexplored due to methodological constraints, notably host DNA contamination. This study aimed to optimize an 18S rRNA metabarcoding workflow using mammal-blocking primers for bovine fecal eukaryome profiling and to characterize eukaryotic community differences between healthy and naturally C. parvum-infected diarrheic calves. METHODS: We compared four 18S rRNA primer sets (V8f/1510R, TAReuk454FWD1/TAReukREV3, 528F/706R, and 616F/1132R) with two mammal-blocking primers using fecal samples from healthy (n = 28) and C. parvum-positive diarrheic calves (n = 24) across Japan. The optimal primer-blocker combination was selected based on host-read depletion and taxonomic recovery. Using this optimized workflow, we characterized and compared the fecal eukaryotic microbiota between healthy and C. parvum-infected calves via 18S rRNA amplicon sequencing. RESULTS: The V8 primer-blocker demonstrated the most consistent host suppression (30-50% reduction), unmasking diverse eukaryotic taxa while improving evenness and preserving community richness. Cryptosporidium dominated the diarrheic group and was confirmed as C. parvum via nested GP60 PCR. Infected calves were associated with lower eukaryotic richness, with reduced Chao1 richness (p < 0.00001) and Shannon diversity (p < 0.041), and distinct community composition (Bray-Curtis: R 2 = 0.145, p = 0.001; Jaccard: R 2 = 0.060, p = 0.001). After accounting for geographic variation, clinical status remained significantly associated with community composition (PERMANOVA, R 2 = 0.129, p = 0.0001), whereas geography was not significant (p = 0.180). LEfSe identified Cryptosporidium (LDA score = 5.6) as the strongest discriminator in the Crypto group, while Kazachstania (4.35), Giardia (4.0), and Aspergillus (0.8) were enriched in healthy calves, reflecting complex interkingdom interactions. CONCLUSION: The optimized V8-mammal-blocking strategy provides an effective framework for bovine fecal eukaryome profiling by reducing host interference and improving recovery of clinically relevant microeukaryotes. C. parvum infection is associated with significant restructuring of the fecal eukaryotic community. This workflow strengthens livestock disease surveillance, facilitates future epidemiological studies, and advances our understanding of complex host-parasite and microeukaryome interactions.

Toxoplasma gondii Outbreak Associated With Catered Venison Dinners, Westchester County, New York-January-February 2024.
On January 19 and 20, 2024, a caterer in Westchester County, New York, served a seven-course game dinner to approximately 250 guests each evening (500 total). Six courses contained venison from 10 deer harvested in early January through a donation program in another county. All venison courses were reheated on site except the backstrap steaks, which were never frozen and were grilled rare to medium-rare. On February 1, an infectious diseases physician notified the health department of attendees with fever, headache, and myalgia without gastrointestinal symptoms. The caterer and food preparation site were investigated on February 5, and the first positive Toxoplasma gondii serology on February 7 prompted a press release and provider alert. Sixty-three attendees contacted the health department, of whom 30 (48%) sought medical care and 26 (41%) were tested. Specimens from 16 of the 26 (62%) could be forwarded to the Remington Laboratory for confirmatory testing; the remaining 10 (38%) were tested at non-reference laboratories only. Symptom onset ranged from 23 January to 8 February 2024. Among attendees with onset within a biologically plausible interval after the dinners, 15 (24%) were confirmed, 10 (16%) probable, and 16 (25%) suspect; one (2%) had evidence of past infection only. Two raw venison samples were PCR positive for T. gondii, tissue cysts were observed on histopathology, and genotyping identified haplogroup 12, associated with wildlife and more severe human disease. Wild game from donation programs should not enter commercial food service, and at-risk guests should be informed when it is served.Keywords.

Structure-Activity Relationship Profiling of Substituted N-Phthalimidopiperidine Analogs as Broad-Spectrum Antifungal Agents.
Invasive fungal infections are a major and escalating global health concern, frequently resulting in life-threatening systemic infection. The combination of limited therapeutic options, increasing mortality, and the rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens highlights the critical need for novel antifungal agents. With this goal in mind, a high-throughput screening assay identified SLB1122168, and a subsequent structure-activity relationship study led to more potent analogs, including SSD2032594, which demonstrated fungicidal activity with a minimum inhibitory concentration of 1-4 μg/mL against Candida auris, Cryptococcus neoformans, Aspergillus fumigatus, and Mucormycosis-causing species. Additionally, SSD2032594 showed potent activity against mature biofilms of C. auris and exhibited a negligible resistance tendency in vitro. Furthermore, SSD2032594 showed a survival benefit in the Caenorhabditis elegans nematode model of C. auris infection, resulting in a ∼30% higher survival rate. Taken together, these results highlight SSD2032594 as a candidate for antifungal drug development, targeting infections caused by different fungal pathogens.

Development of a centrifugation-based method for the qualitative molecular detection of Cryptosporidium spp., Giardia duodenalis and Enterocytozoon bieneusi in surface water samples.
Workflow for waterborne parasites DNA detection in surface water. Screening for environmental surveillance in monitoring and resource-limited settings. Zoonotic protozoa and microsporidia are waterborne pathogens with implications for animal and human health. Their resistant stages can persist in freshwater. Standard reference methods for water analysis are often limited to specific parasites, require large water volumes, and depends on expensive equipment. Practical alternatives are needed to facilitate parasite detection in water. This study aimed to develop a pellet-based workflow to allow the DNA detection of Cryptosporidium spp., Giardia duodenalis and Enterocytozoon bieneusi from the same surface water sample. Three organism-specific spiked controls and eight environmental samples from four freshwater sites, collected over two months, were processed by centrifugation to concentrate the pellet fraction, while the supernatant recovered post-centrifugation was filtered through membranes. The samples were collected as part of a broader ongoing year-long monitoring project. DNA was extracted from both fractions and analysed by qualitative PCR assays. Pellets yielded positive results whereas no positivity was detected in filter membranes, suggesting pellet fractions as the most suitable for downstream molecular analysis. This qualitative pellet-based processing approach was designed to provide an assessment and a practical screening strategy for environmental surveillance.

African swine fever virus protein R298L opposes the NF-κB signaling pathway and interferon-mediated pathway.
African swine fever virus (ASFV) is a large DNA virus that is highly pathogenic to domestic pigs and severely threatens the global pig industry. ASFV has evolved a range of strategies to evade or suppress the innate antiviral immunity of the host in order to promote its own infection and proliferation. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the inhibition of innate antiviral immunity by ASFV-encoded proteins remain unclear. Here, we report the ASFV-encoded protein R298L (p298L) inhibits inflammation and interferon (IFN)-mediated signaling pathways. To verify the function of pR298L in vivo, a recombinant ASFV with deletion of the R298L gene (ASFVΔR298L) was constructed and assessed. The results showed that ASFVΔR298L infection induced higher levels of inflammatory cytokines and IFN-stimulated gene factors compared with its parental ASFV CN/GS/2018 strain. Mechanistically, as a bridge protein, pR298L prevented p65 from phosphorylation and activation by blocking the interaction between IKKβ and p65 in the NF-κB pathway. The expression of pR298L prevents the important kinases, JAK1 and JAK2, in the interferon pathway from interacting with their substrates, which blocks the activation of the IFN-triggered signaling pathway. These findings offer new insights into the functions of the ASFV-encoded R298L gene and its role in the viral infection-induced immune response, which may aid in the development of antiviral agents and live attenuated vaccines to treat African swine fever. IMPORTANCE: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes a highly fatal swine disease that is prevalent in numerous countries and has a significant impact on the pig industry. The lack of clarity regarding the mechanisms of ASFV infection and immune escape is a major impediment to vaccine development. The ASFV genome is large and encodes more than 200 proteins whose functions are unknown. To gain a more in depth understanding of how ASFV regulates the host immune response, we conducted a comprehensive screening and functional validation of viral proteins that regulate the interferon pathway and inflammatory response. This study focused on investigating the production and regulation of antiviral and inflammatory factors in the natural antiviral immune response of the host. This study reveals the significant contribution of ASFV-encoded protein R298L (p298L) in both the NF-κB signaling pathway and IFN-mediated pathway. This study offers novel perspectives on the immune evasion mechanisms of ASFV, thereby contributing to the development of effective vaccines and therapeutics.

Multiple introductions and spread of novel reassortant highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses via wild birds, South Korea, 2024-2025.
Between 14 October 2024 and 24 March 2025, 43 cases of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) type A (H5N1) infections in wild birds and 1 case in a leopard cat were detected through the national HPAI surveillance program. We performed whole-genome sequencing of 51 isolates and investigated their phylogenetic relationships. Phylogenetic analyses identified nine distinct genotypes, designated Kor24-25A to Kor24-25I. The most commonly detected genotype, Kor24-25A (n = 24), was frequently detected in Pelecaniformes and was most prevalent between December 2024 and January 2025. Bayesian continuous and discrete trait phylodynamic analyses using HA gene sequences identified the three most probable routes of viral introduction via Gyeonggi, Jeju, and the southern coastal areas of the Korean Peninsula and suggested that wild ducks served as the primary reservoirs facilitating viral transmission in the wild bird population. During the 2024-2025 season, great egrets (Ardea alba) appeared to be more frequently affected than other wild bird species, suggesting possible seasonal differences in species-specific disease outcomes among wild birds. This study provides valuable insights into the phylodynamics, host associations, and transmission patterns of HPAI H5N1 viruses. It emphasizes the importance of enhanced surveillance programs targeting key avian hosts and high-risk geographic areas.

Emerging respiratory infectious diseases: Clinical aspects for rapid identification and management.
Emerging respiratory infectious diseases increasingly arise at the human-animal-environment interface and challenge clinicians with rapidly evolving diagnostic, therapeutic, and infection-control decisions. This narrative review summarizes clinically relevant viral and bacterial pathogens that may present as severe respiratory disease, but are easily mistaken for common community-acquired infections during early illness. We focus on zoonotic influenza A viruses, including contemporary H5N1, Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV), hantaviruses, Nipah virus, and inhalational bacterial threats such as anthrax, pneumonic plague, tularemia, and melioidosis. These infections may progress from non-specific symptoms to severe pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome, shock, neurological complications, disseminated infection, or death. Timely recognition depends on careful assessment of travel, occupational and recreational exposures, animal contact, outbreak signals, and pathogen-specific syndromic clues. Multiplex molecular diagnostics can support early triage and exclusion of common pathogens, but targeted PCR, culture, serology, sequencing, and reference laboratory confirmation remain essential. Management requires prompt supportive care, appropriate isolation, public health notification, and pathogen-directed antimicrobial, antiviral, antitoxin, or prophylactic strategies where available. By integrating clinical presentation, diagnostics, treatment, vaccines, and One Health considerations, this review aims to translate knowledge on emerging infections into practical bedside preparedness.

Pre-existing cross-subtype serological responses against H5Nx in health care workers.
UNLABELLED: A rise in cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b in humans has been reported since 2023. Although influenza seasonal vaccination (H1N1/H3N2) was shown to be effective against cases of reinfection with endemic influenza A viruses (IAVs), its capacity to elicit cross-reactive antibodies against (H5N1) remains unclear. Here, we measured vaccine-elicited antibody responses against seasonal (H1N1/H3N2) and various avian subtypes A (H5Nx) using plasma samples from the CRCHUM Health Care Workers cohort in Montreal, Canada, during the 2024 influenza seasonal vaccination. The capacity of their plasma to recognize hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) antigens from ten influenza strains was measured. Their neutralizing activity, as well as their capacity to mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) against cells stably expressing HA and NA, was measured. Overall, seasonal vaccination against H1N1/H3N2 elicited antibodies able to recognize several HA and NA, and in some individuals, this translated to increased neutralization and ADCC activity, including against H5Nx. This study provides insightful information on how vaccination shapes cross-reactive antibody responses against avian H5Nx. IMPORTANCE: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are endemic in the human population and responsible for hundreds of thousands of deaths every year, occasionally leading to influenza pandemics. Since 2023, there has been a rise in avian IAV infections in humans, with some deaths reported, mostly related to the H5N1 subtype clade 2.3.4.4b. Seasonal vaccines against IAVs are effective, but their efficacy against avian IAVs is not well known. Here, following influenza seasonal vaccination in a cohort of adults, we report highly heterogeneous serological responses, possibly due to pre-existing immunity and HA sequence similarity. These findings provide insight into the breadth of pre-existing and vaccine-induced immunity against H5 influenza viruses and may inform the development of vaccination strategies aimed at providing broader protection against emerging influenza viruses.

Association between Ebola prevention training and prevention-related cognitive and behavioral factors among Chinese expatriates in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a cross-sectional study informed by the RANAS framework.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the associations between Ebola prevention training experience and multiple prevention-related outcomes (infectious disease knowledge, risk perception, protective attitudes, and psychological self-regulation) among Chinese expatriate workers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), and to further assess potential ceiling effects and whether educational attainment modified these associations. METHODS: Based on the Risk-Attitude-Norms-Ability-Self-regulation (RANAS) framework, a cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 951 Chinese expatriates in the DRC. Mann-Whitney U test and χ2 test were applied for univariate comparisons. General linear models (GLMs) adjusted for age, educational attainment, and residence duration in the DRC were constructed to evaluate independent associations between training experience and each outcome. Ceiling effects were quantitatively described, and sensitivity analyses excluding maximum-score participants were performed to assess potential analytical bias. Two-way interaction terms were further incorporated to test the effect modification of educational attainment. RESULTS: Adjusted GLM results showed that participants with training experience exhibited significantly higher adjusted marginal means in basic knowledge, prevention-and-response knowledge, and psychological self-regulation (p < 0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed in risk perception and protective attitudes. Obvious ceiling effects existed in perceptual and attitudinal indicators, with 66.67% of participants achieving full scores in risk perception and 62.99% in protective attitudes. Sensitivity analyses indicated that ceiling effects might mask potential associations for psychological and behavioral outcomes and cause instability in the association of prevention-and-response knowledge. Significant educational modification effects were detected for the associations of training with basic knowledge and psychological self-regulation (p < 0.05). Stratified analyses further showed that positive associations were observed among participants with high-school education or below and those with junior-college/bachelor-level education, but not among those with postgraduate education or above. CONCLUSION: Ebola prevention training experience was independently associated with higher epidemic-prevention knowledge scores and better psychological self-regulation, while associations with risk perception and protective attitudes were substantially constrained by ceiling effects. The associations between training and health outcomes are heterogeneous across educational strata. Targeted and stratified health education strategies, rather than uniform training schemes, should be adopted for overseas populations to better tailor infectious-disease prevention training programs to heterogeneous overseas populations.

Dengue infection in kidney transplant recipients during a major epidemic and the implementation of systematic donor screening: a cohort study.
BACKGROUND: During Brazil's unprecedented dengue epidemic in 2023-2025, we develop a rationale for organ donor screening to mitigate the risk of donor derived transmission using rapid, widely available, and low-cost tests. Here we aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical presentation, and outcomes among kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) who developed different routes of dengue infection and establish a policy for mitigating the risk of donor transmission. METHODS: This study conducted at a large kidney transplant center in Brazil-Hospital do Rim (HRIM) examined dengue in KTRs through three components: initial cases of donor-derived infection that led to systematic donor screening; donor screening and adjudication for potential transmission from August 2023 to April 2025; and outcomes of vector-borne dengue among recipients followed at HRIM from December 2023 to July 2024. Donors were screened using immunochromatographic NS1 antigen and IgM rapid tests, with RT-PCR for those NS1-negative and IgM-positive. FINDINGS: Before August 2023, we recorded four donor-derived transmissions from two deceased donors, resulting in three deaths. After that, among 1252 deceased donors screened, eight were NS1-positive and four had clinical evidence of dengue; these 12 donors were excluded from donation. Among 58 NS1-negative/IgM-positive donors, 38 were considered for donation. From these, 52 recipients were transplanted, with no confirmed donor-derived transmission. Among 1542 recipients of kidneys from NS1- and IgM-negative donors, 17 developed dengue within 30 days after transplantation: one had fatal transfusion-transmitted dengue, two had confirmed donor-derived transmission, ten had potential donor-derived transmission, and four were considered to have vector-borne infection acquired before transplantation. Every recipient with confirmed or potential donor-derived transmission identified during the screened period recovered from the infection. Lastly, among 12,402 KTRs on follow-up, we recorded 373 confirmed vector-borne cases. They were 50·0 years old, 203 were male (54·4%), 170 were female (45·6%), and 232 were White (62·2%). The case-fatality rate was 1·88%, compared with 0·10% in the general population during the same period. INTERPRETATION: KTRs with vector-borne dengue experienced a high observed case-fatality rate. Organ or blood transmission led to life-threatening outcomes. The rapid test screening was associated with low transmission, and when it occurred, the risk of severe cases was mitigated. These findings support the incorporation of dengue screening strategies in endemic regions. FUNDING: Fundação Oswaldo Ramos.

Potent Antivirals for Respiratory Syncytial Virus Detected via Peptide-Based Fusion Inhibitor Screening.
The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes fatal pneumonia in neonates, infants, and older adults. However, no approved antiviral drugs exist for RSV; furthermore, the currently available antibody-based therapies are expensive and do not provide complete protection against RSV infections. Thus, developing anti-RSV agents for treating RSV infections is crucial. We previously established a rational strategy for designing peptide-based fusion inhibitors targeting class I fusion proteins, which are essential for the membrane fusion of viruses and host cells. Here, we used this strategy to identify peptide-based fusion inhibitors that block the interaction between the heptad repeat 1 and 2 (HR1 and -2) regions of the RSV F protein and identified four key amino acid regions involved in the HR1-HR2 interaction. Peptides, including the key amino acid regions VirRS2 and VirRS8, inhibited the replication of the RSV-A2 strain. We confirmed the structure-activity relationships using crystal structure coordinates and AlphaFold2-based structural predictions. These results may advance novel RSV fusion inhibitor development.

A novel double-mAb sandwich ELISA utilizing broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies as an in vitro alternative to the rabies vaccine NIH potency assay.
BACKGROUND: Rabies remains a devastating zoonotic disease, with prevention measures relying heavily on post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Evaluating rabies vaccine potency traditionally relies on the in vivo National Institutes of Health (NIH) mouse challenge assay, which is limited by long testing cycles, low reproducibility, and high animal consumption. Developing broad-spectrum monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and alternative in vitro assays is essential to advance rabies prevention and improve vaccine quality control. METHODS: In this study, we characterized three human-mouse chimeric mAbs (05-2F10, 06-2A12, and 07-4D8-1C1) with broad-spectrum neutralizing activity. Leveraging in vitro pseudovirus neutralization assays, we evaluated candidate mAbs for high neutralizing capacity and low sensitivity to variation to select optimal pairs for assay development. Using these selected mAbs, a double-antibody sandwich ELISA was established to quantify glycoprotein (G) antigen content in human rabies vaccines. RESULTS: The three chimeric mAbs exhibited exceptional in vitro neutralization potency and breadth. The established double-antibody sandwich ELISA successfully quantified G antigen content in human rabies vaccines. Importantly, a high correlation was demonstrated between the antigen content quantified by this ELISA and the potency data generated via the traditional in vivo NIH mouse challenge test. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings provide a robust technical framework for replacing the traditional NIH potency assay with a reliable in vitro method, fully aligning with the 3Rs principles of animal welfare.

[Nightmare or wonder : a bat on the ceiling].
Rabies is an invariably fatal zoonosis in humans caused by a neurotropic virus of Lyssavirus genus. Three genotypes are endemic in Europe. Genotype 1 or RABV (Rabies lyssavirus) is the agent of classical rabies, for which dogs and certain wild carnivores serve as reservoirs; genotypes 5 and 6, respectively EBLV-1 and EBLV-2 (European bat lyssavirus type 1 and 2), have bats as reservoirs. In Switzerland, classical rabies (RABV) has been eradicated since 1999, a status shared by the majority of European Union countries. Cases of human rabies encephalitis transmitted by bats in Europe are associated with EBLV-1 and EBLV-2 but are exceptional. This article aims to present the epidemiology, pathogenesis and prevention of rabies in Switzerland.

Pediatric RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection burden in G20 countries in 2023.
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood lower respiratory infections, but updated G20 burden estimates are lacking. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database, we analyzed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0-14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country. In 2023, an estimated 5,373 deaths and 483,162 DALYs occurred, with mortality and DALY rates having declined by ∼5.5% annually since 1990. The COVID-19 pandemic drove burden to a historic low in 2021, but a marked rebound followed in 2022-2023, though rates remained below pre-pandemic levels. Infants aged <1 year bore the heaviest burden (mortality 8.688 per 100,000), and India ranked highest, whereas Australia ranked lowest. Burden strongly correlated inversely with Sociodemographic Index. These findings highlight the need for precision prevention, targeting the youngest children and lower-resource G20 members.

"Make sure you involve us" - Youth experiences, care needs, and areas for intervention across the TB care journey in East Africa: a qualitative study.
Background Tuberculosis (TB) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality for youth (ages 15-24) globally. We comprehensively investigated youth experiences, care needs, and areas for intervention across the TB diagnosis, treatment, and post-TB care cascade. Methods Youth with pulmonary TB and healthcare workers providing TB care in Eldoret, Kenya, and Mbarara, Uganda, were purposively sampled. In-depth semi-structured interviews examined factors influencing youth TB care engagement, care needs, and areas for intervention before, during, and after TB treatment. Reflexive thematic analysis was conducted. A youth advisory board supported study implementation. Results We conducted 39 interviews, including 25 healthcare workers and 14 youth with TB. Youth median age was 22, 8 (57%) were male, and one was living with HIV. Youth experiences were driven by poor access to care, including for TB testing, treatment support, and post-TB sequelae. School-related factors included risks for TB acquisition, delayed diagnosis, and barriers to adherence, but also opportunities for treatment support. Stigma and limited TB awareness resulted in delayed diagnosis, inadequate treatment adherence, social isolation, and mental health burdens. Experiences of severe illness, post-treatment morbidity, and TB recurrence impacted physical and mental wellbeing. Treatment support and social support were essential, yet were critically undermined by stigma, economic insecurity, and family circumstances. Areas for intervention centered on accessible, person-centered, youth-friendly care, including after TB treatment. Conclusions Youth and healthcare workers detailed the landscape of gaps in care, opportunities, and solutions for youth with TB. Dedicated youth-led interventions may improve TB care access, outcomes, and quality of life.

Fulminant serogroup B meningococcemia in an adolescent vaccinated against serogroups A and C: highlighting the serogroup B vaccination gap in China-a case report and literature review.
BACKGROUND: Invasive meningococcal disease (IMD) remains an acute clinical challenge associated with high mortality and permanent disability. Although routine immunization has successfully suppressed historical lineages, an expanding epidemiological shift toward serogroup B in specific regions has exposed a population vulnerability, given that protein-based serogroup B vaccines are excluded from China's National Immunization Program (NIP, historically referred to as EPI). We present a case that characterizes the clinical trajectory of this vaccination mismatch. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 12-year-old boy from Guangdong Province, China, who had previously received vaccination against Neisseria meningitidis serogroups A and C. He presented with fever and a rapidly progressive purpuric rash. Within hours, his condition deteriorated to septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), consistent with purpura fulminans. Blood cultures confirmed N. meningitidis serogroup B. Following aggressive intensive care support-including antibiotics, vasopressors, mechanical ventilation, plasma exchange, and continuous renal replacement therapy-the patient survived, exhibiting complex ischemic sequelae that secondary cutaneous necrosis necessitated multi-stage surgical autologous grafting, which subsequently resulted in long-term functional extremity deficits. CONCLUSION: This case underscores the hyperacute progression of serogroup B meningococcemia in an adolescent previously immunized against serogroups A and C. The clinical course illustrates an individual vulnerability under the current polysaccharide-based framework and highlights the public health relevance of reassessing regional vaccine strategies and enhancing surveillance for emerging serogroups.

Isoalantolactone exhibits activity against Echinococcus multilocularis associated with mitochondrial perturbation and changes in the lesion microenvironment.
BACKGROUND: Alveolar echinococcosis (AE) is a severe parasitic disease caused by Echinococcus multilocularis. Current therapy relies mainly on benzimidazole drugs and is largely parasitostatic, highlighting the urgent need for new candidate compounds with improved efficacy. We hypothesized that isoalantolactone (ISO) exerts direct anti-Echinococcus multilocularis activity and evaluated whether ISO treatment was associated with changes in the lesion microenvironment and host immune responses during AE progression in vivo. METHODS: In vitro experiments were conducted using isolated Echinococcus multilocularis protoscoleces, metacestode vesicles, and germinal layer cells, with assessments of protoscolex survival, phosphoglucose isomerase release, and germinal cell viability. Scanning and transmission electron microscopy, mitochondrial membrane potential detection, molecular docking, and protein expression analysis were also performed. In vivo efficacy was verified using a murine intraperitoneal infection model treated with ISO or albendazole, combined with evaluations of lesion burden, histopathology, safety indicators, immune cell subsets, and cytokine levels. RESULTS: ISO promoted phosphoglucose isomerase release, with a half-maximal effective concentration of 16.36 ± 3.24 μM, and reduced germinal cell viability, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 17.46 ± 2.25 μM. It exerted dose- and time-dependent parasiticidal effects, achieving complete protoscolex death within 1-5 days at concentrations of 40 μM and 10 μM, respectively. In infected mice, ISO reduced lesion burden and spleen index and was associated with parasite structural damage, mitochondrial abnormalities, and changes in fibrosis-, inflammation-, and immune-related readouts under the present experimental conditions, with no marked abnormalities in most of the evaluated short-term safety parameters. CONCLUSION: ISO shows anti-Echinococcus multilocularis activity in vitro and suppresses AE progression in vivo. Its activity was associated with parasite structural injury, mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization, and changes in the lesion microenvironment and host immune responses. Further preclinical evaluation of ISO as a candidate compound against AE is warranted.

High prevalence of intestinal protozoan infections among asymptomatic individuals in rural and urban communities in conflict-affected Northwest Cameroon.
BACKGROUND: Intestinal protozoan infections remain an important public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa. In Cameroon, there is limited evidence comparing the epidemiology of intestinal protozoan infections in rural and urban settings. This study determined the prevalence of intestinal protozoan infections, identified associated factors, and compared selected diagnostic techniques among asymptomatic individuals in rural and urban communities of Northwest Cameroon. METHODS: A school and community-based cross-sectional study was conducted between May and August 2025 in rural Bafut and urban Bamenda, Northwest Cameroon. A structured questionnaire was used to collect sociodemographic and hygiene-related data. Stool samples were analyzed using direct wet mount, formol-ether concentration, and modified Ziehl-Neelsen staining techniques. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 28. The Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate, and odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used to assess associations. Statistical significance was set at p 0.05). The formol-ether concentration technique yielded the highest number of positive parasite detections and identified all eight parasite species detected in the study, whereas direct wet mount and modified Ziehl-Neelsen techniques identified five and two species, respectively. CONCLUSION: Intestinal protozoan infections remain highly prevalent among asymptomatic individuals in conflict-affected communities of Northwest Cameroon. Improved water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions, along with the use of sensitive diagnostic techniques, may enhance control and surveillance of these infections.

Economic burden of Peste des Petits Ruminants in India: A meta-analysis with probabilistic uncertainty assessment.
Peste des petits ruminants (PPR) is an enzootic disease of small ruminants and imposes substantial economic losses. This study estimated the national-level economic burden attributable to PPR in India through meta-analysis based on mortality loss, body-weight loss, treatment cost, opportunity cost of labour, distress sale loss and milk loss (for goats) by systematically synthesizing available evidence. Since several studies reporting per-animal economic losses did not provide measures of dispersion, a reference variability of 15% of the reported loss estimates was assumed for the primary meta-analysis, while alternative assumptions of 5%, 10%, 20% and 30% were evaluated through sensitivity analysis. Incidence and mortality rates were separately pooled through meta-analysis. Goat and sheep populations for 2024 were forecasted using log-trend growth models. The pooled epidemiological parameters, per-animal loss estimates and forecast populations were integrated to estimate the national economic burden. Under the 15% reference variability assumption, the estimated economic loss due to PPR in 2024 was USD 331.32 million (INR 27,830.59 million), comprising USD 219.91 million in goats and USD 111.41 million in sheep. Ten thousand bootstrap samples were generated with replacement for different loss components to characterize uncertainty associated with the limited evidence base and meta-analysis was performed for distribution parameterization. Monte Carlo simulation was subsequently employed to characterize uncertainty in the epidemiological and economic parameters. The findings demonstrate that PPR continues to impose a substantial economic burden on India's small-ruminant sector and provide an updated evidence base for strengthening disease-control and eradication efforts.

Within- and between-host dynamics of highly pathogenic avian influenza in domestic birds from Pennsylvania farms and live bird markets.
Since late 2021, highly pathogenic H5 avian influenza viruses have spread across the Americas, resulting in hundreds of outbreaks in agriculture and 71 human spillovers. In the United States, human infections overwhelmingly derive from exposure to infected agricultural animals. However, little is known about how these viruses evolve during outbreaks in agriculture, or how they spread locally, key information for understanding human infection risk. We produced high-quality deep sequence data from commercial and live bird market (LBM) outbreaks in Pennsylvania from 2023-2025. We uncover repeated spillovers from wild to domestic birds, and evidence of high circulating diversity in LBMs that likely moved across state lines. Samples collected from the same outbreak shared a significant fraction of viral variation, suggesting high circulating diversity and a strong signal of transmission linkage. Samples from poultry collectively harbored 9 known adaptive variants, including PB2 D701N, suggesting that rare, adaptive variants may circulate in settings where human exposure risk is high. Our data suggest that outbreaks in poultry pose opportunities for subsequent viral evolution, supporting continued efforts to stamp out transmission. We also find that LBMs experience outbreak risk from domestic and wild sources and promote viral mixing between species, suggesting that enhanced tracking and biosecurity may be useful in these settings. Finally, our data suggest the potential to use within-sample variation for enhanced outbreak linkage within these outbreak settings.

Synthetic Flavonoid Analogues as CatB/CatL Inhibitors with Potential Anti-SARS-CoV‑2 Activity.
The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly affected global public health. Intensive efforts have led to the development of vaccines and antiviral drugs. However, the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants has raised concerns about resistance to therapies, making the exploration of alternative molecular pathways a promising strategy. Cathepsins stand out in this context due to their crucial role in mediating SARS-CoV-2 entry via endosomes. Structurally, these enzymes share high similarity with proteases from other organisms such as Leishmania CPB. Previously, we reported the synthesis and activity of 17 flavonoid derivatives as CPB inhibitors with robust antimicrobial activity. Motivated by the high resemblance between the active sites of CPB and CatB, we evaluated the anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity of these compounds and validated cathepsins as their main molecular target. Among them, nine flavonoid derivatives exhibited potent simple-linear noncompetitive dual CatB/CatL inhibition, with K i values ranging from 3.20 to 29.05 μM for CatB and from 2.41 to 12.44 μM for CatL. Chalcones 1c, 2a, and 2b translated this enzymatic activity into significant reductions in SARS-CoV-2 titers (IC50 = 12.06, 1.05, and 2.12 μM, respectively), while demonstrating low toxicity in both Vero-CCL81 and L929 cells. Their potential direct effects on viral replication were also evaluated using SARS-CoV-2 main protease assays and virucidal tests. No compound showed activity on viral targets, suggesting that cathepsin inhibition is their potential antiviral mechanism. Although additional mechanistic assays are still required, these data provide initial support for the involvement of dual CatB/CatL as antiviral targets and offer insights for the development of chalcone-based leads against COVID-19.

Arbovirus diagnostics: from conventional methods to emerging technologies-a chikungunya virus-centric review.
Arboviruses remain an important global health concern because of their expanding distribution, diverse transmission patterns, and the challenges associated with accurate and timely diagnosis. This review is centered on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) as a representative model, focusing on diagnostic strategies across different stages of infection and the key diagnostic pitfalls that affect CHIKV detection in co-circulation settings. In this review, we summarize current laboratory-based approaches for CHIKV detection and differential diagnosis, including virus isolation, antigen detection, nucleic acid amplification and serological assays, with discussion of their applications, strengths and limitations. We further review recent developments in emerging diagnostic technologies, including next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based detection methods, aptamer-based recognition systems, biosensors, and point-of-care testing platforms, highlighting their potential advantages and current limitations. Comparative examples involving dengue virus (DENV) and Zika virus (ZIKV) are discussed specifically to illustrate cross-reactivity and misclassification risks relevant to CHIKV diagnosis. Particular attention is given to persistent issues affecting diagnostic accuracy and practical implementation, including serological cross-reactivity among co-circulating arboviruses and the challenges of translating advanced technologies into accessible tools for field and resource-limited settings. Overall, this review summarizes progress in CHIKV-relevant diagnostics and outlines future opportunities for developing more reliable, rapid, and widely applicable detection strategies.

Fine-scale spatio-temporal dynamics of kdr mutation V1016G in Aedes albopictus along a transect encompassing the Rome metropolitan area.
Pyrethroid insecticides are largely exploited in Italy to reduce Aedes albopictus nuisance and to discontinue autochthonous transmission of exotic arboviruses. V1016G mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene is strongly associated with resistance to pyrethroids in this species. Here, we provide an unprecedented high-resolution spatiotemporal analysis of the distribution/frequency of the V1016G mutation over an 11-year period in Ae. albopictus populations sampled across a transect encompassing the eco-geographical variability of Mediterranean Europe, including Rome, the only European metropolitan area that has experienced both dengue and chikungunya outbreaks. The results reveal marked spatial heterogeneities in 1016G frequencies, with the highest values in a coastal tourist town (47.7%) and in a few sites within Rome (up to 38.5%), as well as an 8.7% mean increase in allele frequency from 2012 to 2023. Frequency increases in samples collected in the early vs late 2023 season were also observed, particularly in some of the sampling sites. Overall, the results highlight a complex spatio-temporal pattern which is likely due to the trade-off between heterogeneous selective pressure, the effect of gene flow between populations exposed to different levels of pyrethroid spraying and a possible fitness cost of the 1016G allele. Frequencies up to 20% of GG homozygotes detected in some sites underline a possible risk of a reduction in the full effectiveness of pyrethroid treatments implemented in case of autochthonous arbovirus transmission, which - if confirmed phenotypically - should prompt the development of pyrethroid resistance management plans.

Cluster investigation report: a probable urine-associated transmission event of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome-a case report.
INTRODUCTION: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne viral disease with a high case fatality rate. Human-to-human transmission has been increasingly documented, primarily through direct contact with blood or bloody secretions. On June 21, 2025, a case of SFTS was reported in Zhumadian City, Henan Province. On July 3, a second case-epidemiologically linked to the first-was reported to the local Centers for Disease Control (CDC) through the notifiable disease reporting system, following laboratory confirmation on July 1. CASE PRESENTATION: A 77-year-old female farmer with underlying comorbidities was hospitalized with fever, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia, and subsequently died of SFTS. Her 31-year-old granddaughter, who had an open wound on her hand, cared for the patient and cleaned her urine. Eleven days later, she developed fever, nausea, vomiting, headache, fatigue, and myalgia. Laboratory tests confirmed SFTS virus infection by RT-PCR, with an initial cycle threshold (Ct) value of 38.85, which subsequently decreased to 31.48 over the following 2 days, indicating active viral replication. She recovered after antiviral therapy and was discharged on July 7. Comprehensive epidemiological investigation ruled out other potential transmission routes, including blood contact, tick bites, and environmental exposure. However, direct virological evidence from the index patient's urine and genomic sequencing to confirm viral homology between the two cases were not available. CONCLUSION: This report describes a probable human-to-human SFTS transmission event associated with urine exposure through an open wound. While the absence of direct virological and genomic evidence precludes definitive confirmation, the convergence of epidemiological, clinical, and temporal evidence strongly supports this transmission route. This case highlights the need for enhanced protective measures-particularly the use of gloves when handling any body fluids, including urine-during care of SFTS patients.

The geography of waiting: surveillance latency as the hidden driver of Ebola risk in East Africa.
Ebola virus disease remains a persistent public health threat in East Africa, yet preparedness strategies continue to emphasise response after outbreaks are recognised rather than the period preceding detection. This Perspective argues that surveillance latency the cumulative delay between the earliest clinically meaningful signal and organised public health action is a critical but insufficiently measured determinant of Ebola risk. Although diagnostic and reporting delays have been widely documented, they are often treated as isolated operational challenges. We introduce the concept of the geography of waiting, an integrative framework that links biological, clinical, diagnostic, administrative and community delays to spatial inequalities in physical, technical and relational infrastructure. Unequal access to diagnostics, transportation, laboratory networks, trusted communication channels and community reporting systems creates substantial variation in detection timelines across settings. Where surveillance latency is prolonged, transmission may continue undetected, increasing the likelihood of larger and more complex outbreaks. Drawing on evidence from outbreaks in Uganda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Guinea and Rwanda, we examine the mechanisms underlying delayed detection and consider them alongside performance frameworks such as Uganda's 7-1-7 strategy. We propose a practical approach that integrates syndromic and event-based surveillance, decentralised molecular testing, community early-warning systems and regional data sharing. Because shorter detection intervals are associated with smaller eventual outbreaks in the cases reviewed here, reducing surveillance latency is a plausible high-value investment for Ebola preparedness, although this remains a hypothesis pending formal economic evaluation rather than an established finding.

A subunit vaccine protects A129 mice from death and joint swelling against lethal Chikungunya virus challenge.
INTRODUCTION: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is primarily transmitted to humans through bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes, causing febrile illness as well as acute or chronic arthritis. With increasing reports in previously non-endemic regions, it poses an emerging threat to public health and a growing risk to travelers. Despite the recent approval of live-attenuated and virus-like particle-based vaccines, a safe, efficacious, and cost-effective vaccine remains urgently needed. The envelope glycoproteins E1 and E2, which play crucial roles in viral attachment and entry, are the major immunodominant structural proteins and can effectively elicit protective antibodies. METHODS: We engineered mammalian cells to produce the ectodomains of the E1 and E2 glycoproteins and evaluated the protective efficacy of the resulting vaccine formulations in vivo. RESULTS: A two-dose vaccination regimen elicited high levels of antibodies and provided full protection against lethal challenge in A129 mice, preventing both death and joint swelling. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate the potential of this vaccine candidate against CHIKV and warrant its further development.

Ambient air pollution and meteorological factors associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease risk in Shenzhen, China: a time-series study.
BACKGROUND: In China, hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) persists as a prevalent infectious disease with high transmissibility. Nevertheless, the link between environmental determinants and HFMD incidence has not been fully elucidated. The study assessed associations between air pollution, meteorological conditions, and HFMD incidence in Shenzhen, China, while also evaluating shifts in these associations before and after the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and during the COVID-19 epidemic. METHODS: Daily data on HFMD cases, air pollutants (such as PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, and O3), and meteorological variables (including mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed) were collected for the period from 2013 to 2022. Associations were assessed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), accounting for immediate and delayed effects. RESULTS: Spearman correlation analysis showed that HFMD was positively correlated with SO₂, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, and negatively with PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO₂ and CO both elevated cumulative risk at extremely high concentrations, with SO₂ showing delayed effects. However, SO₂ unexpectedly displayed protective effects in single-lag analysis. NO₂ exhibited a U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations despite an overall decreasing trend. O₃ showed dual peaks, with protective effects at extremely high concentrations after lag 1. PM2.5 and PM10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations. Temperature exhibited a dual-peak risk pattern at extremely low and extremely high temperatures, with extreme heat producing sustained effects and extreme cold shorter-lived risk. HFMD risk increased under conditions of extremely high humidity. In general, the risk associated with atmospheric pressure rose as pressure levels increased, and asymmetric lagged effects were observed at both low- and high-concentration extremes. Extremely high wind speed causing short-term harm and extremely low wind speed leading to delayed cumulative risk. CONCLUSION: Meteorological factors exhibit more consistent associations than air pollutants. Mean temperature showed a dual-peak distribution with persistent effects from high temperatures, while atmospheric pressure presented long-lasting impacts of low pressure. There is a positive correlation between relative humidity and the incidence of HFMD. Air pollutants showed inconsistent associations with HFMD. These findings support targeted public health interventions for meteorological factors.

[Research progress and vaccination strategies of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines for pregnant women].
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a predominant global pathogen responsible for severe lower respiratory tract infections and hospitalizations in infants, especially those aged under six months. To date, no vaccines have been approved for active immunization against RSV in infant populations, leaving monoclonal antibodies as the primary modality for immediate, direct RSV protection.
