Maternal vaccination during pregnancy has evolved as a critical passive immunization approach, wherein vaccine-elicited maternal antibodies cross the placenta to confer early-life protection on neonates and young infants. This review elaborates on the pathogenesis of RSV infection and the features of host immune responses to RSV, summarizes key advances and remaining bottlenecks in RSV vaccine development, and focuses on evaluating the efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of the prefusion F protein-based RSV vaccine (RSVpreF) based on latest clinical trial findings and post-marketing surveillance data. Additionally, it compares RSV vaccination guidelines and strategic recommendations issued by major global health authorities, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA). This article further discusses persistent challenges and prospective research priorities in this field, covering public awareness of RSV vaccination, global vaccine accessibility, long-term safety profile monitoring, and vaccine applicability in special populations. Collectively, this review aims to provide evidence-based references to guide clinical practice and optimize public health decision-making regarding RSV prevention.

[Advances and challenges in the prevention and control of respiratory syncytial virus infection].
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a predominant pathogen responsible for acute respiratory tract infections globally. It poses substantial health threats to infants, young children, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals, constituting a critical public health concern. This article systematically reviews the epidemiological features of RSV, encompassing global epidemic trends, seasonal distribution patterns, genetic diversity of viral subtypes, as well as high-risk populations and associated risk factors, and elaborates on its disease burden across diverse regions and populations. Additionally, it summarizes the current progress and core strategies for RSV prevention and control from three perspectives: vaccine development, the clinical application of antiviral agents and monoclonal antibodies, and non-pharmaceutical interventions. Furthermore, this review analyzes the key challenges constraining effective RSV management, including viral variation and immune escape, the complexity of host immune responses, and the inequitable distribution of global public health resources. On this basis, we propose that a precise, multi-level, and integrated prevention and control system should be established in the future by enhancing epidemiological surveillance systems, optimizing vaccine and drug research and development technologies, strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration, and advancing the equitable allocation of global health resources. The findings of this review provide a reliable reference for fundamental research and public health practice targeting RSV prevention and control.

[Establishment and application of an indirect ELISA method for detecting respiratory syncytial virus pre-fusion F protein-specific IgG antibodies].
Objective: To establish an indirect ELISA method for detecting IgG antibodies specific to the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) pre-fusion F protein (pre-F), and to conduct systematic validation and application analysis. Methods: The gene sequence of the current circulating RSV strain was obtained through the Beijing respiratory multi-pathogen surveillance system, and the pre-F protein was synthesized as the coating antigen. Key reaction conditions were optimized using a checkerboard titration assay to establish the RSV pre-F ELISA method. Serum samples were randomly selected from healthy community populations and RSV infection convalescent cases. Using plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) results as the reference standard, the established method was evaluated for application performance, including sensitivity, specificity, and repeatability, followed by practical application assessment. The assay was also compared in parallel with two commercial ELISA kits, designated kits A and B. Results: The optimal reaction conditions were determined as follows: antigen coating concentration of 5 ng/well, and secondary antibody dilution of 1∶20 000. The cut-off value for positivity was defined as 0.315. The method demonstrated a sensitivity of 98.02%, specificity of 100%, overall agreement of 98.25%, and a Kappa value of 0.92 (P<0.001). Both intra-and inter-assay coefficients of variation were below 5.0%, indicating good repeatability. No significant cross-reactivity was observed with serum samples positive for other common respiratory viruses. Conclusion: This study established an indirect ELISA method for detecting RSV pre-F specific IgG antibodies. The method provides a reliable tool for RSV sero-epidemiological studies and vaccine immunization efficacy evaluation.

[Temporal characteristics of respiratory syncytial virus in Jiangsu Province from 2024 to 2025: a study using the annual cumulative proportion method].
Objective: To define the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) epidemic period using the annual cumulative proportion (ACP) method, and to analyze the temporal characteristics of RSV in Jiangsu Province from 2024 to 2025. Methods: RSV nucleic acid testing data from 17 sentinel hospitals between week 23 of 2024 and week 22 of 2025 were included. Epidemic onset and offset were defined using 10% and 90% ACP thresholds, respectively, with stratification by region, age, clinical presentation, and subtype. Positivity rates were compared using χ² tests, and between-group differences in epidemic timing were assessed using bootstrap analysis. Sensitivity analyses were also performed. Results: A total of 19 830 respiratory specimens were included, of which 360 were RSV-positive, yielding an overall positivity rate of 1.82%. RSV positivity rates differed significantly by region, age group, and clinical surveillance category (P<0.05). The positivity rate was higher among severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases than among influenza-like illness (ILI) cases (2.52% vs. 1.42%; χ²=30.52, P<0.001). The ACP-defined epidemic period extended from week 50 of 2024 to week 18 of 2025. Compared with northern Jiangsu, epidemic onset in southern Jiangsu occurred 8 weeks earlier (95%CI:-18 to -3), and the epidemic duration was 7 weeks longer (95%CI: 1 to 16). Epidemic onset among SARI cases occurred 4 weeks earlier than among ILI cases (95%CI:-10 to -1). Conclusion: RSV is prevalent during winter and spring in Jiangsu Province from 2024 to 2025. Differences in epidemic timing are observed across geographic regions and clinical surveillance categories.

Repurposing the Insecticide Flufenerim, the Only Anti-Cryptococcus Compound Identified in the MMV Global Health Priority Box, as a Candidate for the Environmental Control of the Cryptococcosis Agents.
Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are environmental fungi that cause cryptococcosis, a severe, life-threatening infection, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Current treatments are limited by toxicity, restricted availability, and the emergence of resistance, highlighting the need for novel antifungal agents. Here, 240 compounds from the Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) Global Health Priority Box were screened for activity against these two species. Flufenerim, originally developed as an insecticide, was the only compound that exhibited inhibitory activity at 1 μM (0.364 μg/mL). Minimum inhibitory concentrations ranged from 0.03 μg/mL to >8 μg/mL across 15 isolates, and the compound exhibited a predominantly fungistatic profile, except for one C. gattii strain. At subinhibitory concentrations, flufenerim significantly reduced capsule thickness in both species, melanization in C. neoformans, and urease production in C. gattii, without affecting phospholipase activity. In silico ADMET predictions indicated predicted toxicological risks requiring further evaluation. Cytotoxicity assays further demonstrated that the compound did not exhibit significant toxicity in murine and human macrophages, nor in human brain endothelial cells (HBECs). Exposure of Galleria mellonella larvae to flufenerim produced sublethal physiological effects without mortality. Due to the unfavorable ADMET profile, we evaluated whether this compound could be used for environmental control of fungal reservoirs. Tree-hollow samples spiked with C. neoformans and treated with flufenerim yielded fewer yeast colonies than untreated controls when plated on Staib's agar. These findings identify flufenerim as a new anti-Cryptococcus compound and provide preliminary evidence supporting its potential for reducing C. neoformans recovery from environmental substrates. However, the ecological complexity of Cryptococcus reservoirs and the potential effects on nontarget microorganisms require extensive investigation before any environmental application can be considered.

Imported mixed malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium ovalecurtisi: An Italian case report.
Malaria remains a major global health threat, particularly in endemic regions of sub-Saharan Africa. In 2024 alone, an estimated 282 million cases were reported worldwide, with approximately 610,000 associated deaths. Beyond the high disease burden, mixed-species Plasmodium infections represent an additional clinical challenge, as they are frequently underdiagnosed and may significantly complicate both diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic management even in non-endemic countries. We report the case of a 67-year-old man from Guinea who presented to the Emergency Department with high-grade fever and asthenia shortly after returning to Italy; initial microbiological investigations were negative, despite markedly elevated inflammatory markers were diagnosed. The patient reported a previous untreated malaria episode approximately six months earlier, raising suspicion of a novel Plasmodium infection. A comprehensive malaria diagnostic workflow was promptly initiated, integrating rapid immunoenzymatic testing (IE), microscopy, and molecular assays. The IE test suggested Plasmodium falciparum or a mixed infection as result, while loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP-PCR) confirmed the presence of Plasmodium spp DNA. Microscopic examination of stained blood smears revealed typical P. falciparum ring forms and suspected P. ovale trophozoites; so, species-specific real-time PCR confirmed a mixed infection with P. falciparum and P. ovale, supporting prompt antimalarial treatment. Final molecular confirmation was achieved by Sanger sequencing, which identified the Plasmodium ovalecurtisi as co-aetiological agent of disease. The rapid and integrated diagnostic approach enabled timely initiation of appropriate antimalarial therapy with artemether-lumefantrine and primaquine, leading to complete clinical recovery and gene sequencing allowed a correct species confirmation and epidemiological characterization. This case highlights the importance of combining microscopic analysis with advanced molecular diagnosis for an accurate identification of mixed Plasmodium infections even in country and contributes novel epidemiological data through molecular characterization of P. ovalecurtisi in an imported case.

Case Report: mNGS-negative Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome with small bowel obstruction as the initial manifestation in a glucocorticoid-exposed COPD patient: a fatal case.
BACKGROUND: Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome (SHS) is a life-threatening condition in immunocompromised hosts with an extremely high mortality rate. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) demonstrates limited sensitivity for parasitic detection, and its clinical value remains to be fully elucidated. The conventional microscopy remains an indispensable tool for the diagnosis of parasitic infections. CASE DESCRIPTION: A 73-year-old male patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and cerebral infarction presented with abdominal pain and distension for 7 days and no bowel movement for 3 days. He was diagnosed with incomplete small bowel obstruction at an outside hospital and treated with fasting, enemas, meropenem, and methylprednisolone. He was subsequently transferred to our hospital due to acute lower respiratory tract infection. Chest radiography revealed bilateral diffuse infiltrates, and his condition rapidly deteriorated, requiring admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Stool smear and retrospective sputum examination both identified larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis. However, mNGS of sputum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) obtained upon admission failed to detect any parasitic sequences. The patient was treated sequentially with albendazole and ivermectin, in combination with broad-spectrum antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral therapy. He ultimately died on February 11, 2025, due to severe pneumonia, sepsis, and bone marrow suppression. CONCLUSION: For immunocompromised hosts with multiple risk factors, particularly those exposed to glucocorticoids, active parasitic microscopic examination of stool and respiratory secretions should be pursued when unexplained pulmonary infiltrates coexist with gastrointestinal symptoms, even in the setting of negative mNGS results, to avoid missed diagnosis.

Reconsidering vaccinate-to-live strategies in EU foot-and-mouth disease control.
In January 2025, FMD was detected in water buffalos near Berlin. A few weeks later, a different FMDV-strain was confirmed on dairy farms in Slovakia and Hungary. Since February 2026, Cyprus and Lesvos are confronted with FMD-outbreaks. While Europe is rethinking its FMD-strategies, the two affected member states, Cyprus and Greece, take opposite approaches to control the disease. FMD-vaccination was pivotal for its eradication in many parts of the world. Such regions fought new outbreaks by traditional animal-disease-control. In 2001, a devastating FMD-epizootic swept across the UK and continental Europe. Several million sheep, cattle, and pigs were culled. In the aftermath, OIE (now: WOAH) and EU revised their FMD-strategies. Now, WOAH's Terrestrial Animal Health Code puts strong emphasis on reactive vaccination. An FMD-free status can be regained without slaughtering all vaccinated animals. By contrast, the European FMD Directive of 2003, which contained similar provisions, was repealed. Under the new Delegated Regulation, all restrictions on a vaccination zone are upheld until the last vaccinated animal is removed. Cyprus implemented country-wide FMD-vaccination despite these restrictions. Fearing trade barriers, Greece decided not to vaccinate. Were the consequences not so dramatic, a better head-to-head comparison would hardly be conceivable. Modern FMD-vaccines induce robust immunity after just seven days, minimize virus transmission and allow for DIVA strategies. In addition to the risks posed by global trade and travel, Europe faces major social, economic, and geopolitical challenges. The risk of FMDV incursions is imminent. Cyprus can afford to live with trade restrictions, because export of live animals, raw dairy products and fresh meat only play a minor role in its economy. This would be entirely different if livestock-dense regions in the heart of the continent were affected. The EU must not forgo highly effective and ethically superior control measures that could mitigate socio-economic consequences of future FMD-outbreaks.

How information source and scale shape pandemic behavior change.
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of incorporating human behavior into infectious disease models. Doing so requires predicting how individuals will respond to outbreaks and policies. Key questions that limit the integration of dynamic behavior into disease models are: Is behavior change driven by policy, objective disease information, or subjective risk perception? Can disease data approximate risk perception? Is mitigation behavior influenced by information at broad or fine spatial scales? METHODS: In this ecological study, we leverage US survey data (4.3 million responses from September 2020 through January 2021) on social distancing and concern about infection, alongside data on COVID-19 cases and mitigation policies. Using a county-level spatiotemporal regression model, we evaluate whether social distancing is associated with policy, social information, or epidemiological information at broad or fine spatial scales. We use transmission models to demonstrate the epidemic consequences of different behavioral drivers. RESULTS: We find that epidemiological and social information are predictive of mitigation behavior: a one standard deviation increase in epidemiological or social information led to a decrease in non-household contacts of 0.10 or 0.47 people per day, respectively. State-level variables are more predictive of social distancing than county-level variables, especially for policies. However, conditions in socially adjacent counties are better predictors of behavior than those in spatially adjacent counties. In our transmission model, epidemiologically and socially-informed contact patterns yield similar epidemic dynamics, though broader spatial scales of information explain more behavioral variation. CONCLUSIONS: The US population modified their behavior during the COVID-19 pandemic in response to case incidence and policy at broader spatial scales, potentially reflecting the lack of localized surveillance or mandates. Modeling assumptions of behavioral responses to disease incidence at larger spatial scales are reasonable.

Chikungunya case cluster with nonspecific symptoms: implications for primary care in Switzerland.
BACKGROUND: Early clinical presentation of chikungunya fever and other arbovirus infections is often nonspecific, potentially delaying diagnosis, particularly in settings where these diseases are less frequently considered. Competent vectors are expanding in Switzerland, increasing the risk of autochthonous arbovirus transmission. CASE SERIES: We report seven cases in a group of travellers returning from Kenya in summer 2025. All patients presented with fever, arthralgia affecting the small joints of the hands and feet, nausea, diarrhoea, and rash. Additional symptoms included generalised lymphadenopathy and peripheral oedema. Initial diagnostic tests were inconclusive, with negative results on rapid diagnostic tests for chikungunya antibodies, dengue antibodies, and malaria antigen. The definitive diagnosis was established after 35 days following the emergence of chikungunya IgG and IgM antibodies. DISCUSSION: The presentation resembled a nonspecific febrile illness. Repeated, appropriately timed laboratory testing was necessary to establish the diagnosis. Early diagnostic results may be misleading, particularly when testing methods are not selected appropriately for the stage of the disease. With competent mosquito vectors established in Switzerland, imported cases present a risk of local transmission. Severe infections and persistent joint pain may lead to long-term disability. CONCLUSION: Primary care doctors should consider chikungunya fever in returning travellers and, during the mosquito-active season, in non-travellers in areas with established competent vectors. Patients may present with symptoms ranging from nonspecific febrile illness to more typical manifestations of chikungunya, including fever, arthralgia of the small joints, and rash. Appropriate test selection, timing, and repeated testing when indicated are essential for accurate diagnosis, management, and documentation of the disease.

Global resurgence of norovirus GII.17[P17] accompanies shifting phylogeographic connectivity patterns: surveillance in Jiangsu, 2023-2025.
BACKGROUND: Norovirus GII.17[P17] has re-emerged and has been circulating globally since 2023. In Jiangsu, China, we found that its proportion increased from 2024 onward. Using local surveillance data combined with global sequences, we reconstructed the global spatiotemporal dynamics of GII.17[P17] and explored its evolution and molecular mechanisms. METHODS: Samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing using next-generation sequencing. We used bioinformatics tools to analyze the full viral protein 1 sequences for molecular evolution, spatiotemporal phylogeographic associations, and amino acid changes. RESULTS: From October 2024 to May 2025, 209 GII.17[P17] outbreaks were reported (approximately 26 per month), while only 23 outbreaks occurred in the full year of 2023 (fewer than 2 per month). In sporadic case surveillance, the proportion of GII.17[P17] increased from 9.6% in 2023 to 62.4% in January-May 2025. The maximum clade credibility tree showed that GII.17[P17] clustered into two large clusters. Most samples from 2024 to 2025 belonged to Lineage 3 of Cluster II. In the phylogenetic network and minimum spanning tree, we identified three core hub strains. Inferred phylogeographic connectivity patterns suggest a shift in the primary centers of viral lineage dispersal from East Asia (Cluster I, 2014-2016) to Northwest Europe (Cluster II, 2021-2025). Molecular evolutionary analysis revealed that the current dominant lineage (Lineage 3, Cluster II) exhibited an evolutionary rate of 4.126 × 10-3 substitutions/site/year (95% HPD: 3.27-4.98 × 10-3), substantially higher than the earlier Cluster I lineages (1.798 × 10-3; 95% HPD: 1.41-2.19 × 10-3; posterior probability >0.99; 95% HPD intervals non-overlapping). CONCLUSION: Inferred phylogeographic connectivity patterns indicate that the primary centers of GII.17[P17] lineage dispersal have shifted from East Asia (2014-2016) to Northwest Europe (2021-2025). The current dominant lineage (Lineage 3, Cluster II) exhibits an accelerated evolutionary rate, approximately 2.3-fold faster than Cluster I lineages, and carries lineage-specific amino acid substitutions in antigenic epitopes temporally associated with its global expansion. These findings highlight the value of sustained genomic surveillance in regions with high inferred phylogeographic connectivity for monitoring norovirus evolution.

Vedolizumab treatment in adults with immunodeficiency-associated enteropathy: a case series.
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory gastrointestinal disease is a common manifestation of inborn errors of immunity (IEI) and may affect any segment of the gastrointestinal tract. Vedolizumab, a gut-selective anti-integrin approved for inflammatory bowel disease, has been scarcely studied in IEI. We describe our experience with vedolizumab in adults with immunodeficiency-associated enteropathy. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series of adults with humoral or combined immunodeficiency and inflammatory gastrointestinal disease treated with vedolizumab at a single tertiary referral center. Clinical, endoscopic, laboratory and histopathological responses were assessed. RESULTS: Four adult patients with immunodeficiency-associated enteropathy received vedolizumab. Two patients achieved sustained clinical and endoscopic/histological remission, both of whom had predominant villous atrophy (one with TRAF3 haploinsufficiency, and the other had multiple autoimmune manifestations, refractory immune thrombocytopenia and agammaglobulinemia following rituximab). Another patient with combined immunodeficiency and protein-losing enteropathy had marked clinical improvement with mild histologic response, but relapsed at two years in the setting of norovirus and Clostridium difficile infection. In contrast, a woman with common variable immunodeficiency, autoimmune hepatitis, and severe refractory pancolitis failed to respond to vedolizumab and subsequently developed CMV superinfection, requiring treatment escalation. CONCLUSIONS: In this case series, vedolizumab was associated with clinical improvement predominantly in patients with villous atrophy rather than refractory colitis. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support further evaluation of vedolizumab as a therapeutic option for selected patients with immunodeficiency-associated enteropathy.

Metabolic Signatures of Resistance to Mycobacterium Tuberculosis Infection: Insights from a Multi-Country Plasma Metabolomics Study.
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading infectious disease cause of mortality worldwide. A subset of individuals exposed to Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) remain TST/IGRA-negative despite sustained exposure, termed "TB resisters". The biological mechanisms underlying this resistance remain poorly understood. We applied untargeted high-resolution metabolomics to determine whether systemic metabolic profiles differ between TB resisters and matched Mtb -infected close contacts. METHODS: We compared untargeted high-resolution plasma metabolomics using liquid chromatography mass spectrometry between 269 TB resisters and 269 matched Mtb -infected close contacts, enrolled across Brazil, India, and South Africa. TB resisters were defined as highly exposed close contacts who slept in the same room or spent at least 5 hours indoors per day with an infectious pulmonary TB index patient, but remained TST/IGRA-negative. Mtb -infected close contacts were those who were TST/IGRA positive. Metabolome-wide association studies (MWAS) were conducted using paired t-tests. RESULTS: There were 1,787 features with nominal differences between TB resisters and matched Mtb -infected contacts (p < 0.05). Pathway enrichment identified fructose and mannose metabolism and bile acid biosynthesis in the overall cohort, while lipid-related pathways were enriched in Brazil. Among metabolites with confirmed chemical identities, glyceric acid concentrations were higher in TB resisters by 0.53 µM, whereas hydroxyproline was lower by 0.90 µM, butyrobetaine was lower by 0.06 µM, and homogentisate was lower by 0.0036 µM at false discovery rate of 0.2. CONCLUSIONS: Plasma metabolomic profiles differed between TB resisters and matched Mtb -infected close contacts. These findings indicate that systemic metabolic differences are associated with resistance to Mtb infection.

An Unusual Mechanism of Stroke in Neurobrucellosis: Middle Cerebral Artery Infarction Secondary to Direct Abscess Compression - A Case Report and Literature Review.
INTRODUCTION: Brucellosis is a zoonotic infection that remains endemic across the Middle East, Central Asia, the Mediterranean basin, and parts of Africa and Latin America. Neurobrucellosis (NB) develops in fewer than 5% of cases and constitutes the most severe systemic complication. Cerebrovascular involvement is uncommon and most often attributed to small-vessel vasculitis, immune-mediated endarteritis, or septic embolization. Ischemic stroke caused by direct mechanical compression of an intracranial artery by a Brucella abscess has not been previously reported. CASE PRESENTATION: A 47-year-old previously healthy male with occupational livestock exposure presented with sudden onset of left-sided weakness, facial droop, and global aphasia. Initial imaging demonstrated an acute right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory infarct, and standard ischemic stroke management was initiated. Over the next 24 h, intermittent low-grade fever, persistent confusion, and focal motor seizures emerged despite levetiracetam. Subsequent magnetic resonance imaging showed a 2.5 cm rim-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with central diffusion restriction, consistent with a pyogenic abscess. Magnetic resonance angiography demonstrated focal occlusion of the anterior segment of the right MCA, immediately adjacent to the abscess. Cerebrospinal fluid showed lymphocytic pleocytosis (36 cells/mm3, 85% lymphocytes) and elevated protein (112 mg/dL). Serum Brucella IgG returned positive on day 20, confirming neurobrucellosis. Triple antimicrobial therapy with intravenous ceftriaxone, oral doxycycline, and oral rifampicin produced gradual neurological improvement, and the patient was discharged on long-term oral therapy. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates a novel cerebrovascular mechanism in NB, in which mass effect from a peri-vascular abscess produced ischemic stroke. Coexisting perilesional inflammation likely contributed through a vasculitic component, and the two mechanisms are not mutually exclusive. The absence of systemic brucellosis features delayed recognition and underscores the protean clinical presentation of NB. Brucellosis warrants consideration in the differential diagnosis of acute ischemic stroke when imaging reveals concurrent intracranial infectious lesions, particularly in endemic regions. Early antimicrobial therapy is critical to limit progression and improve neurological outcomes.

Empyema Due to Listeria monocytogenes in a Patient With Rheumatoid Arthritis.
Listeria monocytogenes is an uncommon cause of pleural empyema, particularly in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Disease and treatment-related immunosuppression increases susceptibility to invasive listeriosis, which carries significant mortality. A 78-year-old man with seropositive RA treated with methotrexate and low-dose corticosteroids presented with fever, hypotension, pleuritic chest pain, and weakness. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and elevated C-reactive protein. Imaging revealed a left pleural effusion with lower-lobe collapse. Thoracentesis drained 800 mL of exudative fluid, and cultures of pleural fluid and blood isolated L. monocytogenes. Cranial CT and lumbar puncture performed due to neurological symptoms were normal. High-dose ampicillin plus cotrimoxazole was administered for 7 days, followed by ampicillin monotherapy to complete a total of 14 days of antibiotic treatment, achieving progressive clinical and radiological improvement. Empyema caused by L. monocytogenes is rare and occurs mainly in immunocompromised hosts, with only isolated cases described in RA. This case underscores the need to consider Listeria infection in immunosuppressed RA patients presenting with pleural empyema.

Agri-food connectivity drives the resurgence and geographic expansion of human brucellosis in China.
Agri-food systems are increasingly recognised as drivers of zoonotic disease emergence, yet the mechanisms by which modern food production, trade, and distribution reshape pathogen transmission remain poorly quantified. Here we integrate two decades of nationwide surveillance, epidemiological modelling, and phylogenomic analyses of 4215 Brucella genomes from 79 countries and regions to elucidate the drivers of brucellosis re-emergence in China. Nationwide, human cases increased by 282.6% between 2005 and 2023, far exceeding the 8.1% increase in sheep inventory. This decoupling indicates a fundamental shift in transmission pathways. In northern China, livestock reservoir and production indicators accounted for 88.9% of the relative model contribution, consistent with direct occupational exposure; whereas in southern China, the agri-food logistics and market connectivity domain showed the largest contribution (64.1%), providing quantitative evidence that modern food-distribution infrastructure now drives brucellosis risk in those regions. Demographic shifts reaffirm this transition, with marked incidence increases among children and the elderly, indicating expanded foodborne and household exposures. Phylogenomics reveals that China's epidemic reflects long-term endemic amplification of a dominant Brucella melitensis clade (Lineage 2.4), with a hierarchical hub-and-spoke transmission network linking northern pastoral source regions to historically non-endemic southern provinces through national livestock and logistics networks. Comparative genomics further identifies lineage-specific gene acquisitions, adaptive variation in the outer membrane protein Omp2b, and recurrent convergent disruption of puuD enriched among winter isolates. Together, these findings reframe brucellosis resurgence as an emergent property of agri-food connectivity and highlight domestic supply chains, transport hubs, and cold-chain infrastructure as priority targets for surveillance and intervent ion.

Candidozyma auris (formerly Candida auris): A P6 medicine framework integrating genomics, surveillance and the prevention of multidrug-resistant fungal threats.
Healthcare-associated infections are major drivers of global morbidity; yet, fungal threats remain under-characterized. Candidozyma auris (C. auris; formerly known as Candida auris) has emerged as a critical public health challenge due to its extensive multidrug-resistant profile, environmental resilience and high transmissibility. Its resistance to major antifungal classes, including azoles, polyenes and echinocandins, severely limits therapeutic options and exposes the limitations of fragmented, discipline-specific healthcare responses. The present conceptual commentary proposes that the persistence of C. auris highlights limitations in fragmented, discipline-specific healthcare responses. Herein, the predictive, preventive, personalized, participatory, psycho-cognitive and public (P6) model of medicine is proposed as a comprehensive framework to move beyond reactive containment. By repositioning clinical microbiology as the entry point for surveillance through early, accurate diagnosis, the P6 model integrates genomic epidemiology, antifungal stewardship and behavioral science to support earlier detection of emerging threats and inform timely clinical, infection prevention and control, and public health responses. The emergence of C. auris provides a practical test of the ability of healthcare systems to integrate microbiological intelligence, prevention strategies and public-health governance by replacing delayed laboratory identification, fragmented surveillance, or poor data sharing. Addressing its high resistance and rapid spread requires an integrative approach that leverages advanced analytics and public health governance. The P6 framework provides a scalable strategy to strengthen health systems against both current and future multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens.

A chicken microRNA expressing LaSota targets Newcastle disease virus phosphoprotein and impacts interferon expression.
Newcastle disease (ND), a major cause of economic loss in the poultry industry worldwide, is caused by outbreaks of virulent avian paramyxovirus type 1(APMV-1) virus. We previously demonstrated that chicken miRNA-27b-5p (gga-miR-27b-5p) can regulate the APMV-1 phosphoprotein (P) and alter viral replication. In this study, the LaSota vaccine strain of APMV-1 was used as a backbone to express the chicken pre-miRNA-27b and expected to increase intra-cellular levels of both gga-miR-27b-5p and gga-miR-27b-3p. This novel recombinant virus, rLS-miR-27b, was rescued, propagated in embryonating chicken eggs (ECEs) and did not exhibit toxicity in ECEs. Expression of both gga-miR-27b-5p and gga-miR-27b-3p was increased significantly relative to controls. An inverse correlation was observed between increased expression of gga-miR-27b-5p and reduced APMV-1 P transcripts. Additionally, increased expression of interferons (alpha, beta and lambda) and interferon stimulated gene MX1 was observed. Suppression of P did not alter the P:V ratio in rLS-27b virus infected cells. These data support the observation that miR-27b-5p expression alters viral transcriptional kinetics in cell culture without affecting overall progeny virus yield in ECEs and could be utilized to improve current APMV-1 vaccines.

Development of an scFv-based electrochemical biosensor for robust detection of Tilapia Lake Virus.
Tilapia Lake Virus (TiLV) poses a severe threat to global tilapia aquaculture, causing high mortality rates and significant economic devastation. Conventional diagnostic methods are limited by their operational complexity and requirement for centralized laboratory infrastructure. To address these challenges, this study reports the development of a label-free electrochemical biosensor utilizing a newly engineered recombinant single-chain variable fragment (scFv) antibody targeted against TiLV (scFv-TiLV). The scFv-TiLV construct was expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) using a low-temperature induction strategy assisted by chemical chaperones, yielding a highly purified (>95%) and soluble bioreceptor. The purified scFv-TiLV was immobilized onto gold nanoparticle-modified electrodes via EDC/NHS coupling chemistry. The immunoelectrode monitored concentration-dependent suppression in square-wave voltammetry (SWV) peak currents resulting from surface alterations upon viral capture. The biosensor demonstrated a broad dynamic linear range from 102 to 106 copies/mL in both standard PBS buffer (R2 = 0.9918) and a fish serum matrix (R2 = 0.9914), achieving high sensitivity and matrix tolerance. The platform achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 42.85 copies/mL in the complex serum matrix. Furthermore, preliminary cross-reactivity trials against off-target viral pathogens confirmed excellent selectivity and negligible false-positive responses. This scFv-based electrochemical platform offers a robust, simplified, and accessible alternative for decentralized viral diagnostics.

Virological and epidemiological investigations of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak, Vietnam, 2023.
We report on the virological and epidemiological features of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak in Vietnam in 2023. Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) subgenogroup B5, first emerging around November 2022, and imported into Vietnam through a single introduction, was the primary cause. Convalescent plasma collected from patients infected with subgenogroups B5 in 2014 and 2023 could neutralize both contemporary viruses with comparable titers, suggesting no evidence of immune evasion. However, at one and six months before the start of the outbreak, only 6.7% of 0- < 3 year-old children in Ho Chi Minh City, an epicenter of the outbreak, had neutralizing antibodies against EV-A71. Seroprevalence increased as the outbreak progressed, coinciding with a drop in EV-A71 infected patients residing in Ho Chi Minh City, suggesting that serosurveillance could be a useful tool to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. Our collective findings have provided novel insights into the epidemiological factors driving EV-A71 emergence, and therefore would inform outbreak preparedness and response, and in particular the development of serosurveillance-based approach to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. EV-A71 infection represents an ongoing public health threat, currently affecting countries in the Asia-Pacific region, but with a high potential to become a global problem, and therefore should be closely monitored.

All-in-One Photocatalytic-Photothermal-SERS Nanoknives Platform for Solar-Driven Inactivation of Antibiotic-Resistant Superbugs and Selective Azoaromatic Synthesis.
Harnessing sunlight-driven renewable energy provides a sustainable strategy for the rapid eradication of antibiotic-resistant superbugs and selective organic synthesis. However, the development of highly efficient solar photocatalytic materials remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report the rational design of a plasmonic MXene-Ag@Au-nanostar based all-in-one photocatalytic-photothermal-SERS nanoknives platform that harnesses solar energy to simultaneously achieve highly efficient inactivation of antibiotic-resistant superbugs and selective azoaromatic synthesis. By synergistically integrating broad-spectrum solar harvesting (350-950 nm), high photothermal conversion efficiency (∼70%), intense SERS enhancement, and efficient hot-electron and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, the heterostructure delivers exceptional photocatalytic activity toward selective azoaromatic synthesis. Under solar irradiation, the multifunctional nanoplatform promotes the selective oxidation of 4-aminothiophenol (4-ATP) to 4,4'-dimercaptoazobenzene (4,4'-DMAB) with conversion yields exceeding 69%, while enabling the selective reduction of 4-nitrothiophenol (4-NTP) to 4,4'-DMAB with conversion efficiencies greater than 72%. Mechanistic investigations further demonstrated that ROS, photothermal heating, and hot-carrier transfer collectively contribute to the remarkably enhanced photocatalytic performance. Furthermore, the heterostructure achieved rapid solar-driven inactivation of carbapenem-resistant E. coli, multidrug-resistant Salmonella DT104, and MRSA superbugs, within 15-25 min of irradiation. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the outstanding superbug inactivation activity originated from the synergistic interplay of MXene nanoknives that physically disrupted bacterial membranes, which facilitates the penetration of ROS into bacterial cells, resulting in severe oxidative stress and rapid cell death. Collectively, this work establishes a strategy for designing active-site-engineered "All-in-One" platforms for sustainable solar-driven chemical synthesis and rapid superbug inactivation.

Antibodies targeting a conserved cryptic epitope at the influenza hemagglutinin head-stem interface via distinct binding modes.
Influenza A virus continues to pose pandemic threats, as demonstrated by the recent global spread of highly pathogenic H5N1 strains. Consequently, the development and characterization of vaccines targeting zoonotic influenza subtypes have become a major focus of the field. In this study, we characterize two broadly reactive antibodies previously isolated from H5N1 vaccinees. Although they have distinct immunoglobulin germline gene usage and binding modes, cryo-EM analysis shows that both antibodies share a highly conserved cryptic epitope at the interface of the hemagglutinin (HA) head and stem domains. The antigenicity of this epitope is influenced by natural amino acid variation at residue 293 of HA subunit 1, and its access is facilitated by acid-induced conformational change of HA. Nevertheless, both antibodies are non-neutralizing and possess only marginal protective efficacy against seasonal and H5N1 viruses in vivo , thus representing suboptimal vaccine responses. Overall, our findings expand the interactions of cross-reactive antibodies with an under-characterized HA epitope and provide insights for next-generation influenza vaccine design.

How can veterinary personnel recognize and protect themselves from domestic cats infected with highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses?
Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses circulate globally in wild birds, causing poultry outbreaks and spillover infections in mammals and sporadic human infections. Recent detections in domestic cats highlight occupational risks for veterinarians handling cats in areas where A(H5N1) virus is circulating. Although the potential risk for cat-to-human A(H5N1) virus-transmission is currently low, vigilance is warranted. Veterinarians can use published recommendations to evaluate exposure risks, implement infection control practices, use recommended personal protective equipment, train staff, and coordinate with health officials. The One Health approach can help reduce risks of A(H5N1) virus infection to veterinary staff, cat owners, and other animals.

Cross-clade protection against human H5N1 isolates by a clade 2.3.4.4b HA mRNA vaccine in mice.
The recent spread of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) viruses into mammals, despite limited human infections to date, has raised serious public health concerns and highlights the need for rapidly deployable vaccines, such as mRNA-based platforms, to strengthen pandemic preparedness. Here, we evaluated the effectiveness of an mRNA vaccine encoding the HA of NIID-002, a WHO-recommended H5 candidate vaccine virus (CVV) derived from A/Ezo red fox/Hokkaido/1/2022 (clade 2.3.4.4b) against A/Texas/37/2024 (TX37; clade 2.3.4.4b) and A/Cambodia/2311257/2023 (Cam23; clade 2.3.2.1e). The mRNA was formulated with ssPalmO, a low-inflammatory self-degradable ionizable lipid nanoparticle (LNP). BALB/c mice were immunized intramuscularly twice with the mRNA-LNP vaccine containing either 1 μg or 10 μg of H5 HA mRNA. After boosting, strong, dose-dependent serum IgG responses against NIID-002 HA were detected by ELISA. The mice were then challenged with a lethal dose of homologous TX37 or heterologous Cam23. All mice in the 10-μg group survived both challenges, demonstrating robust cross-clade protection. In the 1-μg group, complete protection without significant body weight loss was observed against TX37, whereas partial protection was observed following Cam23 challenge. Viral titers were significantly reduced in multiple tissues of the vaccinated mice compared to the unvaccinated controls. Our findings demonstrate that the NIID-002-HA mRNA vaccine confers protection against homologous and heterologous zoonotic H5N1 strains in a mouse model. This low-inflammatory ssPalmO-LNP platform thus supports safe, rapid vaccine development against emerging H5N1 viruses with pandemic potential.

Protective efficacy of bacterial sialidase-based intranasal inactivated avian influenza vaccine against H5N1 infection in poultry.
The avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a serious threat to the poultry industry, leading to substantial economic losses and having the potential to cause severe zoonotic diseases worldwide. The development of mucosal vaccines has prompted greater attention due to their ability to mimic the natural infection process and streamline the delivery method. In this study, we evaluated the efficacy and immunomodulatory responses of an intranasal vaccine containing inactive H5N1 virus and bacterial sialidase with mucoadhesive chitosan adjuvant. The results demonstrated that the challenged intranasally vaccinated group exhibited a significantly suppressed mortality rate and viral shedding compared to the group infected with H5N1 AIV. Additionally, elevated mucosal IgA at several days post intranasal vaccination indicated activation of the nasal-associated lymphoid tissue (NALT) and improvement of cell-mediated immune responses. Gene expression analysis of the innate immune system revealed significant downregulation of TLR7 and diminished interferon responses in brain and lung tissues, suggesting restricted viral recognition and replication. In the trachea, challenged birds exhibited selective upregulation of IFN-γ, while the vaccinated group had no substantial activation, indicating that intranasal vaccination modulated local immune responses at the viral entry site. In conclusion, intranasal vaccination reduced tissue damage, suppressed viral shedding, and improved mucosal protection, demonstrating its potential as a candidate strategy to manage H5N1 AIV outbreaks.

Early Detection and Response to the First Imported Case of Zika Virus Disease - Hainan Province, China, 2025.
WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ABOUT THIS TOPIC?: Zika virus (ZIKV) is primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The Zika epidemics in China were primarily imported cases. WHAT IS ADDED BY THIS REPORT?: This study documents the first laboratory-confirmed imported ZIKV case in Hainan Province, China. Phylogenetic analysis identified the Asian lineage, sharing 98.79% homology with a Thai strain. WHAT ARE THE IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH PRACTICE?: This investigation highlighted the need to strengthen the patriotic health campaign, reducing local mosquito-borne transmission risk at the source. Multi-pathogen (dengue/chikungunya/Zika) testing of a single sample by Haikou Customs enabled Zika detection, while timely cross-department notification and coordinated response effectively enhanced outbreak containment.

The vaccination paradox: how East Africa's success in Ebola vaccine preparedness may be creating new public expectations for future outbreaks.
This perspective synthesizes published evidence on Ebola vaccination and outbreak preparedness in Africa. Successful vaccination against Zaire ebolavirus has strengthened vaccine-based outbreak control but may also create a preparedness risk when public expectations exceed species-specific vaccine availability. We propose the Vaccine Expectation Gap, Vaccine Anticipation and Species-Specific Vaccine Literacy as linked, hypothesis-generating constructs, supported by a Preparedness Trust Contract for practical implementation. The framework draws on expectation-disconfirmation and crisis and emergency risk communication theories and distinguishes established evidence from interpretation and testable hypotheses. Recent Sudan virus and Bundibugyo virus outbreaks illustrate the relevance of this gap because licensed vaccines remain species-specific. Evidence is concentrated in Uganda, making broader East African application a hypothesis requiring empirical testing. If validated, the framework could strengthen risk communication, community trust and regional health-security planning.

Integrated Proteomics and Metabolomics Can Shed Light on Potential Biomarkers of Inflammation and Infection in Chicken Embryos as an Experimental Model.
Salmonella Pullorum (SP) infection has been proposed as an experimental model of inflammation in late-stage chicken embryos (CEs). We refined this model by inoculating 9.5 day embryos via allantois with a low SP dose and evaluating outcomes at 24 and 48 h postinfection. This approach aims to provide a framework for systematically exploring early molecular events triggered by infection and inflammation while using the CE as an ethically acceptable and biologically relevant model of systemic inflammation. Clinical parameters (mortality and weight), serum proteomics, and untargeted metabolomics were assessed. Proteomics was performed by LC-MS/MS, followed by PANTHER and KEGG functional enrichment; metabolomics was performed to assess serum alterations. Mortality increased at 48 h postinfection (30%), and surviving embryos showed a trend toward reduced weight. Proteomic profiling revealed an increase in overall protein concentrations in the infected group compared to the control, despite high zero inflation, with α-2-macroglobulin significantly upregulated at 48 h, indicating an endogenous immune response. For pathway-level enrichment, Bayesian analysis suggested subtle effects on proteome dynamics. Metabolomics identified time-dependent changes, including increased levels of α-tocopherol-related and phenylalanine-derived metabolites and decreased levels of oxidized fatty acid derivatives at 48 h. These findings support the CE model before 12 days as an ethically refined and sensitive system for studying acute inflammatory responses.

Aircraft wastewater virome surveillance from domestic and international flights reveals viral diversity among travellers: A proof-of-concept study from Gujarat, India.
BACKGROUND: Aircraft wastewater surveillance (AWS) at airports is an emerging method for detecting pathogens shed by international and domestic travellers. Global spread of infectious diseases occurs rapidly through air travel, and implementing surveillance systems at airports can help identify emerging viruses and track pathogens at scale. We aimed to characterize the viral diversity shed by travellers, which may represent routine viral circulation or active infection, at Ahmedabad airport in Gujarat. METHODS: We collected wastewater samples from domestic and international terminals where domestic flights connect to 18 states and 3 Union Territories, while international flights operate across 16 destinations in 11 countries. Samples were collected from June 2024 to November 2025. We used a capture probe-based enrichment approach for virome surveillance and detected multiple viruses of public health importance. RESULTS: We identified a total of 40 viral families and 315 viral species, with a median of 71 genomes/segments detected per sample in domestic wastewater and 48.5 genomes/segments per sample in international wastewater. We detected several respiratory and enteric viruses, including Influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2, Human mastadenovirus A, Human mastadenovirus B, Noroviruses, Rotavirus A, Hepatitis A virus, Astrovirus MLB1, Human mastadenovirus F. Among these, certain viruses showed relatively higher mean RPKMF abundance in either domestic or international wastewater samples such as Bovine rotavirus A, Human rotavirus ID45/2, and BK polyomavirus observed in international wastewater samples, whereas Aichivirus A1, Norovirus GII.2, and Human immunodeficiency virus 1 showed higher abundance in domestic wastewater samples. We also detected multiple Influenza virus subtypes, including Influenza A subtypes H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, H7N1, and H9N2, along with Influenza B and Influenza C viruses. CONCLUSIONS: Continuous surveillance can provide early warning signals to public health authorities, timely decision-making and coordinated responses can reduce the spread of disease which also requires collaboration with national and international health authorities.

Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Virus Subtype 5 in Cetaceans, Brazil.
We identified highly pathogenic avian influenza virus subtype H5 in stranded dolphins along the coastline of Brazil during 2023-2025. Infected animals included species classified as vulnerable or endangered. Our results highlight the need for ongoing surveillance of cetaceans susceptible to viral infections, which pose an additional threat to threatened species.

Baloxavir-Based Combination Therapy for Protection against Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus Infection in Mice.
Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b virus continues to cause animal outbreaks and sporadic zoonotic infections. In a mouse model of lethal influenza disease, we compared oseltamivir, baloxavir, and molnupiravir monotherapies with 2-drug combinations. Baloxavir-based combinations improved survival, reduced lung viral loads, and prevented extrapulmonary dissemination, supporting H5N1 preparedness strategies.

Detection of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus in Cat and Rats during Outbreak in Backyard Poultry, United States, 2025.
In 2025, highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus was detected in a poultry flock in Illinois, USA. Quantitative reverse transcription PCR, sequencing, and histopathology on cat and rat samples from the farm showed multiple positive tissues and high sequence identity to an avian isolate. Small mammals might contribute to H5N1 transmission.

Detection of Divergent Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus, São Paulo, Brazil, 2025.
In 2025, we detected highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus in dead waterfowl at Ibirapuera Park, São Paulo, Brazil. Genomic characterization indicated a reassortant virus that emerged from locally circulating low pathogenicity avian influenza viruses and highly pathogenic North American lineages. Our results highlight cross-species transmission risk and underscore the need for enhanced surveillance.

Distribution of Donor Types and Time to Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation for Acute Myeloid Leukemia Across Ethnic Groups: A Retrospective Study.
INTRODUCTION: Identifying suitable donors and optimizing transplant timing are critical in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for acute myeloid leukemia. This retrospective study evaluated 124 Israeli adult AML patients (99 Jews, 25 Arabs) who underwent their first allo-HSCT between 2012 and 2022. We assessed donor types, key transplantation time intervals, overall survival, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. METHOD: Overall, 80.7% of patients received fully matched grafts. Donor type distribution differed significantly between ethnic groups (p = 0.007): Israeli Arabs predominantly received matched related donors (64%) with few matched unrelated donors (8%), whereas Israeli Jews showed a balanced distribution (41.4% each). Despite these differences, there were no significant disparities in time from diagnosis to transplantation (119 vs. 122 days, p = 0.871) or in overall survival. The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with prolonged time from coordinator referral to transplantation (p < 0.001) but did not significantly affect overall survival (p = 0.059). CONCLUSION: In conclusion, differences in donor type by ethnicity did not translate into disparities in transplantation timing or overall survival. These findings highlight the resilience of the transplantation process and the importance of evaluating ethnicity within the context of a specific healthcare system.

Trends and Disparities in Mortality From Pneumonia and Cerebrovascular Disease in the United States (1999-2020).
BACKGROUND: Pneumonia is a frequent and often fatal complication of cerebrovascular disease (CVD). Stroke care has improved considerably since the late 1990s, but national trends in deaths involving both conditions and their distribution across demographic and geographic groups have not been described. METHODS: We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER) Multiple Cause of Death files to identify United States decedents aged 55 years and older who died between 1999 and 2020 with pneumonia (ICD-10 codes J18.0, J18.1, J18.2, J18.8, and J18.9) and CVD (I60-I69), both recorded among the causes of death. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 populations were standardized to the 2000 United States population. Joinpoint regression estimated the annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC) overall and by sex, age group, race and ethnicity, urbanization, and census region. A sensitivity analysis of the overall series used a broader pneumonia definition (J12-J18). RESULTS: We identified 316,760 deaths involving both conditions. The overall AAMR fell from 45.4 per 100,000 in 1999 to 9.1 in 2019 (80.0% decrease) and rose to 15.8 in 2020 (73.6% above the 2019 rate); the AAPC for 1999 to 2020 was -5.09% (95% confidence interval [CI] -5.92 to -4.26). Every stratum showed a net decline over the full period and an increase in 2020. Rates were higher throughout in men, in adults aged 75 years, and older and in nonmetropolitan counties and were highest in non-Hispanic Black adults in every year except 2017. Absolute differences between groups narrowed as overall rates fell. The relative increase in 2020 was largest in non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native (160%), Hispanic (144%), and non-Hispanic Black (115%) adults and in adults aged 55-74 years (97%). The broader pneumonia definition added 15,521 deaths (4.9%) and produced the same joinpoints and a similar AAPC (-4.89%). CONCLUSION: Deaths involving pneumonia and CVD fell by about 80% between 1999 and 2019 and rose sharply in 2020, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic. Disparities by sex, age, race and ethnicity and urbanization persisted, and the 2020 increase was proportionally larger in several minority groups. These aggregate certificate data describe patterns but cannot identify their causes. Studies with individual-level clinical data are needed to test whether dysphagia screening, vaccination, and infection prevention explain the long-term decline and the disparities.

Gentamicin and antibiotic use in Norwegian hospitals: a study from 35 point-prevalence surveys, 2015 to 2023.
BACKGROUNDInappropriate and excessive use of broad-spectrum antibiotics drives antimicrobial resistance. Gentamicin, an Access antibiotic in the WHO AWaRe framework with low resistance potential, has long been recommended in Norway for empirical treatment of serious infections. However, real-world data on aminoglycoside use remain limited.AIMWe aimed to describe gentamicin and overall antibiotic use in Norway, including COVID-19 pandemic-related changes, and report the extent of gentamicin use across selected indications.METHODSData were obtained from patients ≥ 20 years from 35 national point-prevalence surveys (2015-2023) across 68 Norwegian hospitals.RESULTSAmong 241,546 hospitalised patients, 66,586 received antibiotics (yearly prevalence 26.9-28.1%), with the highest proportions in the 70-79 (26.4%) and ≥ 80 (23.4%) years age groups. Aminoglycosides, mainly gentamicin, ranked ninth among all antibiotic prescriptions. From 2021, third-generation cephalosporins (13-14%) surpassed β-lactamase-sensitive penicillins (12-13%). Gentamicin use increased from 4.1% in 2015 to 5.8% in 2023, mainly in combination with ampicillin, benzylpenicillin, or ampicillin plus metronidazole. Main indications were urinary tract, lower respiratory tract and intraabdominal infections, and sepsis. An increasing pre-COVID-19 pandemic trend in gentamicin use (β1: 0.105; p < 0.001) was no longer observed after the COVID-19 outbreak was declared a global pandemic on the 11 March 2020 (β3: - 0.112; p = 0.013).CONCLUSIONGentamicin use among hospitalised patients in Norway remains low but appears higher than in other European countries. Increases in gentamicin use pre-COVID-19 pandemic were no longer observed after COVID-19, supporting the need for surveillance and antibiotic stewardship to minimise unnecessary use of broad-spectrum antibiotics.

Minimised SARS-CoV-2 transmission during Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games: insights from enhanced integrated surveillance, Japan, July to September 2021.
BACKGROUNDAmid the COVID-19 pandemic, stringent public health measures were taken during the Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games (Tokyo 2020).AIMWe describe SARS-CoV-2 transmission among Games participants and in-person contributors (GPIPC)s.METHODSTokyo 2020-related SARS-CoV-2 infection cases were individuals linked to the event, testing positive for the virus between 1 July-19 September 2021, reported to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. Attack rates among athletes and team officials were determined. Enhanced case-based surveillance integrating genomic sequencing data supported viral spread investigations among various GPIPC groups.RESULTSA total 804 cases (median age: 35 years, interquartile range (IQR): 27-45; 194 female/610 male) were reported. Among athletes and team officials, attack rates were 0.6% (65/11,400) in Olympic Games and 0.6% (30/4,800) in Paralympic Games. These 95 infections concerned mainly overseas travellers (n = 92), 85 of whom were diagnosed within 14 days of arrival in Japan. Among the 804 cases, whole-genome sequencing data were obtained for 304 (median age: 38 years, IQR: 29-47; 67 female/237 male) with sufficient viral load (as indicated by RT-PCR Cq ≤ 32), including 79% (75/95) of athletes and team officials cases, 74% (131/176) of Games' organisers and media cases, and ˂ 20% (98/533) of remaining cases. Delta variants dominated (94%; 285/304), with domestic (AY.29 lineage) Delta strains prominent among Delta-variant-affected resident cases (96%; 104/108) and Games' organisers and media cases diagnosed ≥ 15 days after entering Japan (97%; 63/65). Overseas Delta strains mostly affected travellers within 14 days of entry, particularly athletes and team officials (97%; 66/68) and Games' organisers and media (29/34).CONCLUSIONMultilayered-risk-reduction measures likely minimised SARS-CoV-2 transmission to athletes.

Andes virus reaches Europe: a narrative review on clinical challenges, diagnostic gaps and public health preparedness, 2026.
BACKGROUNDUp to 2 July 2026, a total of 13 cases of Andes virus (ANDV) including three deaths were reported in connection to an outbreak on the cruise ship m/v Hondius, which departed from Argentina in April and subsequently travelled to Europe to evacuate the passengers. This event prompted all European health authorities to take action to limit the spread of the virus.AIMTo synthesise current knowledge on ANDV, with particular attention on laboratory diagnosis and capability gaps.METHODSA literature search on ANDV was conducted, with a focus on human infection, transmission, outbreak investigations, countermeasures and diagnostics. To provide context for the ship-linked outbreak, updates from official public health sources, including the World Health Organization and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control were used. Moreover, activities by European Union Public Health Reference Laboratories for Emerging, Rodent-borne and Zoonotic Viral Pathogens (EURL-PH-ERZV) were briefly presented.RESULTSAndes virus is unique among hantaviruses because of sustained person-to-person transmission. Diagnosis relies on integration of clinical and epidemiological information with molecular detection of viral RNA or serological evidence. At the time of the outbreak, European diagnostic preparedness was generally well established, but important gaps remained prompting rapid support from the EURL-PH-ERZV.CONCLUSIONSThe recent event demonstrated how a geographically restricted zoonotic infection can pose public health challenges beyond endemic areas. This highlights the need for strong collaboration between clinical services, public health authorities and reference laboratories to strengthen surveillance, early detection, risk assessment and diagnostic preparedness for emerging pathogens.

Repeated detection of West Nile virus in Aedes caspius during an unusually early transmission season in humans in northern Italy, 2026.
In Lombardy, northern Italy, 2026, the first neuroinvasive West Nile virus (WNV) human case was reported on 7 July. Concurrently, high abundances of Aedes caspius and low numbers of Culex pipiens occurred at several surveillance sites. Testing seven archived Ae. caspius pools collected in July revealed WNV lineage 2 in six pools from three independent sites. A virus sequence from Ae. caspius shared > 99.94% nt identity with contemporaneous human-derived sequences. Further investigating possible Ae. caspius vector competence, particularly for WNV lineage 2, is warranted.

Quantitative Flow Ratio- vs Angiography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Secondary Analysis of the FAVOR III China Trial.
IMPORTANCE: Whether the association of quantitative flow ratio (QFR)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with long-term outcomes differs according to multivessel disease (MVD) status is uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To assess the association of QFR-guided vs angiography-guided PCI with 3-year outcomes according to MVD status. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this prespecified secondary analysis of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial, patients were screened across 26 centers in China from December 25, 2018, to January 19, 2020. Eligible participants were adults undergoing PCI for stable or unstable angina or for myocardial infarction (MI) occurring at least 72 hours before screening who had at least 1 lesion with 50% to 90% diameter stenosis in a vessel of 2.5 mm or larger. The analysis compared QFR-guided with angiography-guided PCI according to MVD status. MVD was defined by involvement of at least 2 epicardial vessels or the left main coronary artery. The primary analyses of the current prespecified secondary analysis were completed in October 2024. INTERVENTIONS: Randomization 1:1 to QFR-guided PCI or angiography-guided PCI. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, MI, and ischemia-driven revascularization. The current analysis evaluated 3-year MACE. RESULTS: Among 3825 patients in the intention-to-treat population (mean [SD] age, 62.7 [10.0] years; 2699 [70.6%] male), 2066 (54.0%) had MVD. Zoonotic diseases affecting non-human primates, such as yellow fever (YF), may trigger negative human behaviors toward these species. The consequence of simultaneous and sequential coinfections of Aedes aegypti with DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV on vector competence.
Vector-borne diseases (VBD) caused by arboviruses represent a major public health threat in tropical regions. According to WHO's Global Vector Control Response, more than 80% of the global population live in areas at risk for VBD. For instance, Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and its widespread distribution, particularly in Brazil, contributes to the occurrence of outbreaks. During these outbreaks, mosquitoes may acquire either monoinfections or coinfections, which can occur either simultaneously or sequentially, potentially influencing transmission dynamics. At 7 days post-infection (dpi), DENV-1 infection rates and viral loads were significantly reduced compared with monoinfections, whereas DENV-2 showed increased viral loads in saliva. At 14 dpi, CHIKV infection rates were significantly reduced in both the CHIKV+DENV-1 (CD1) and CHIKV+DENV-2 (CD2) groups, whereas CHIKV viral loads were reduced only in the CD2 group. These results highlight the complexity of arboviral coinfections within this shared vector and emphasize the importance of considering different coinfection scenarios when evaluating vector competence and transmission risk in endemic settings.

High-Flow Nasal Cannula and Virological Surveillance in Severe Bronchiolitis: A Retrospective PICU Study in Southern Brazil.

Despite its clinical relevance, data describing the epidemiological profile of AVB cases in Pediatric Intensive Care Units (PICUs) remain limited, particularly regarding advanced statistical modeling adjusting for modern respiratory support and testing biases. The mean Modified Tal Score at admission was 7.4. RSV was the most frequently identified virus (72.4%). The apparent increase in viral diversity in later years, specifically Rhinovirus A/B/C (23.4%) and Enterovirus (7.7%), reflects a profound detection bias introduced by the adoption of an expanded 24-pathogen multiplex panel rather than a true epidemiological shift. A QS21+ CpG-Adjuvanted Inactivated Vaccine Elicits Superior Humoral and Moderate Cellular Immunity.
Rabies remains a fatal zoonotic disease caused by rabies virus (RABV), posing substantial global health challenges. Current vaccine production faces challenges in manufacturing efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Comparing the Post-Omicron Impact of COVID-19 and Non-COVID-19 Respiratory Viral Infections in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
INTRODUCTION: Effective treatment and prevention for respiratory viral infections (RVI) in solid organ transplant recipients (SOTR) are lacking; clinical differences in COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 (ncRVI) post-omicron are unknown. RESULTS: Overall, 520 RVI episodes in 504 patients were included: 488 had 1 episode and 16 had 2 episodes. Lung, kidney, and heart transplant recipients comprised of 40.9%, 34.3%, and 20.8% of the cohort. There were 352 episodes of COVID-19 RVI and 148 ncRVI. All-cause and RVI-related hospitalization were comparable between COVID-19 and ncRVI (47.7% vs. 43.9%, p = 0.50; 32.1% vs. 31.1%, p = 0.91 respectively). Oxygen supplementation occurred in 11.9% of COVID-19 RVI and 11.5% of ncRVI with a maximum requirement (median, IQR) of 4.0 (2.0-18.8) and 2.0 (2.0-3.0) liters respectively (p = 0.005). Intensive care unit (ICU) admission occurred in 7.1% and 6.1%; non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in 2.3% and 4.1%; mechanical ventilation (I&V) in 4.0% and 2.0%; and inotropic/vasopressor support in 1.7% and 1.4%, for COVID-19 versus nCRVI, respectively. Patients with COVID-19 had ongoing symptoms in 16.8%, 10.2%, and 2.6% at 30 days, 3 month, and 12 month follow up respectively, compared with 16.9%, 4.7%, and 2.0% in ncRVI. Twelve-month mortality, rejection and graft dysfunction were similar between groups. CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 and ncRVI pose significant and comparable risk to SOTR in this post-omicron era, in hospitalization, oxygen requirement, and persistent symptoms. Treatment and prevention should be prioritized in this population.

Use of Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing to Investigate Respiratory Pathogens in Influenza-Negative Nasopharyngeal Swabs From Cameroon's National Influenza Surveillance.
BACKGROUND: In Cameroon, national influenza surveillance identifies influenza-positive cases, but the causes of non-influenza ARIs remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We analyzed 199 influenza-negative nasopharyngeal swabs collected between September and December 2023 from patients with influenza-like illness or severe acute respiratory infection. Mixed DNA/RNA libraries were prepared and sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq platform. Taxonomic classification was performed using METAMIC (v2.0) and SPAdes (V3.15.5) bioinformatic pipelines. RESULTS: Viral sequences were detected in 120/199 samples (60.3%, 95% CI: 53.5%, 67.1%), representing 15 viral species. The most frequent viruses were rhinovirus (43/131), respiratory syncytial virus (33/131), influenza virus, parainfluenza virus and enterovirus. Two non-respiratory viruses (Rotavirus and Papillomavirus) were also detected. Sequencing generated an average of 26.1 million reads per sample, with a mean depth of 870.3 per sample and an average genomic coverage of 82%. Eleven viral co-infections were identified. Several bacterial and fungal genera were also detected. CONCLUSION: Our study shows that mNGS provides a powerful, unbiased approach for characterizing respiratory pathogens in Cameroon, revealing substantial viral diversity among influenza-negative ARI cases. However, cost and bioinformatics capacity remain major barriers to routine implementation. Longitudinal studies and clinical correlation are needed to strengthen interpretation and guide integration of mNGS into national surveillance.

RSV Molecular Epidemiology Pre- and Post-COVID-19 Pandemic Periods in Seattle, Washington, USA.
BACKGROUND: Globally, RSV declined to historically low levels following stay-at-home orders in 2020 and re-emerged as restrictions lifted, with large inter-seasonal outbreaks and other shifts in epidemiology. The effect of the pandemic restrictions on genomic diversity has not been well studied. METHODS: Individuals with respiratory symptoms were enrolled into community-based surveillance studies and provided nasal swabs over three respiratory virus seasons from 2019 to 2022 in the Seattle metropolitan area in Washington State, USA. Samples were tested for RSV by RT-qPCR, with whole genome sequencing performed for a subset. RESULTS: Among children and adults, respectively, 1.8% (232/13,014) and 0.2% (86/46,042) of samples tested positive for RSV-A and 1.1% (139/13016) and 0.3% (119/46043) for RSV-B. Median age for all participants was 33 years (IQR: 23, 48) and 3 years (IQR: 3, 33) for those who tested positive. Cough (≥ 85%) and rhinorrhea (≥ 85%) were the most common symptoms for RSV cases. During 2019-2020, six RSV-A and three RSV-B lineages circulated (majority lineages A.D.1 and B.D.4.1.1). Almost no RSV was detected during 2020-2021.
