Assessing post-challenge mortality, we observed that Wolbachia infection reduced cumulative mortality and delayed the onset of senescence amongst mosquitoes challenged with each bacterium. However, this protective effect was stronger against gram positive bacteria. Bacteria-primed Ae. albopictus were then orally challenged with DENV. We observed that mosquitoes that experienced a pre-challenge with gram negative bacteria were associated with reduced DENV prevalence and viral load, whereas Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes exhibited further reductions in viral load. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: We highlight novel characteristics of native Wolbachia infection in Ae. albopictus mosquitoes, with protection against bacterial-induced mortality, and interactions between pathogen blocking and bacterial priming that may depend on bacterial gram status. These findings provide insight into the immune interactions associated with native Wolbachia and build on our understanding of adaptive immunity in mosquitoes.

Correction: Standardized LDH-to-lymphocyte ratio improves early mortality prediction in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome: A 15-day competing-risk bedside model.
[This corrects the article DOI: 10.1371/journal.pntd.0014289.].

Rift Valley Fever at the Crossroads of Ecology Mobility and Fragmented Health Governance.
Rift Valley fever (RVF) remains one of the most recognisable yet persistently elusive zoonotic diseases in Africa, despite decades of scientific advances in virology, epidemiology, and early warning. While RVF dynamics are well characterised in eco-epidemiological terms, its continued emergence, amplification, and persistence suggest that biological complexity alone does not fully explain ongoing transmission patterns. This review adopts a socio-ecological One Health systems perspective to examine how interactions between eco-epidemiological processes, livestock mobility, and health governance structures shape RVF risk. Drawing on an integrative synthesis of interdisciplinary literature, it conceptualises RVF dynamics as arising from three interconnected domains: biological risk generation, spatial redistribution through mobility and trade systems, and institutional response through governance architectures. The analysis highlights a fundamental misalignment across these domains. Ecological signals and animal health indicators often precede outbreaks but are not translated into timely action; livestock mobility redistributes risk across regions beyond the reach of nationally bounded response systems; and governance arrangements remain fragmented, with no single institution holding end-to-end responsibility. As a result, RVF response remains largely reactive and case-triggered despite the availability of predictive tools and preventive interventions. Addressing this persistent gap requires a shift from reactive, case-chasing response toward anticipatory, integrated governance that aligns ecological intelligence, mobility-informed risk management, and coordinated cross-sectoral action. Viewing RVF through this systems lens underscores that its persistence reflects less a failure of knowledge than a failure of alignment between the systems through which risk is generated, redistributed, and governed.

Serological and molecular detection of pathogenic Leptospira in shelter dogs in Okayama and Yamaguchi Prefectures, Japan.
Leptospirosis is a zoonotic disease that poses public health risks associated with stray and shelter dogs. We examined Leptospira infection in shelter dogs from Okayama and Yamaguchi Prefectures, Japan, using serological and molecular approaches. Anti-Leptospira antibodies were detected by microscopic agglutination test in 48% (10/21) of dogs from Okayama and 49% (24/49) of dogs from Yamaguchi, with serogroup Hebdomadis predominating. Pathogenic Leptospira DNA was detected in urine samples from two of 12 dogs; both were asymptomatic and infected with Leptospira interrogans ST36 belonging to serogroup Hebdomadis. Given that stray dogs are commonly sterilized and rehomed in Japan, these findings highlight potential transmission risks to veterinarians and adoptive households and underscore the need for management strategies to reduce zoonotic transmission.

Purulent MRSA Pericarditis Secondary to Chronic Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis: A Case Report.
Purulent pericardial effusion is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of bacterial infection, most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia. We report the case of an 86-year-old female with chronic diabetic foot osteomyelitis complicated by persistent methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia. The patient subsequently developed purulent pericarditis, bilateral exudative pleural effusions, septic shock, and acute renal failure requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) after intolerance to intermittent hemodialysis due to refractory hypotension. Despite broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy and drainage of infected compartments, the patient developed refractory multiorgan failure and expired on hospital Day 26. This case highlights the high mortality associated with purulent pericarditis in the setting of persistent bacteremia and delayed source control.

Salmonellosis outbreaks associated with pork, United States, 2012-2021.
Nontyphoidal Salmonella causes an estimated 1.3 million domestically-acquired foodborne infections in humans annually in the United States (Scallan Walter et al., 2025). From 1998 to 2023, pork was the fourth most common food category attributed to foodborne Salmonella illnesses (Interagency Food Safety Analytics Collaboration, 2024). We analyzed salmonellosis outbreaks associated with pork products between 2012-2021, using data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Foodborne Diseases Outbreak Surveillance System, System for Enteric Disease Response, Investigation, and Coordination, PulseNet, and the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System. There were 50 Salmonella outbreaks linked to pork from 2012-2021. Twenty-one different Salmonella serotypes were identified; serotype I 4,[5],12:i:- was the most common, causing 19/50 outbreaks, followed by Typhimurium (7/50). Raw ground pork was associated with three outbreaks (6%) and 444 illnesses (23%). Pork roast or shoulder was associated with 13 outbreaks (26%) and 408 illnesses (21%). Whole pigs were associated with 11 outbreaks (22%) and 368 illnesses (19%). Among Salmonella isolates with available antimicrobial resistance information, 226/389 (58%) showed multidrug resistance and 230/389 (59%) showed clinically significant resistance; 216/222 (97%) and 22/34 (65%) of I 4,[5],12:i:- and Typhimurium isolates, respectively, exhibited any resistance. Antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella isolates from outbreaks linked to pork was more frequent than for nontyphoidal Salmonella infections in the United States overall. Preharvest disease prevention efforts that target serotypes I 4,[5],12:i:- and Typhimurium may be valuable in reducing Salmonella outbreaks and illnesses. Downstream exploration of individual- and community-level factors related to handling, preparation, and consumption of specific pork types may help reduce salmonellosis rates through targeted education.

Global phylogenomic structure and accessory resistance dynamics of Acinetobacter baumannii ST2.
Acinetobacter baumannii sequence type 2 (Pasteur ST2), associated with international clone 2, is a major antimicrobial-resistant lineage, but its within-lineage population structure and accessory resistance variation remain incompletely resolved. We analyzed 5612 quality-filtered public genomes from an existing global dataset using PopPUNK, core-genome SNP analysis, AMRFinderPlus, MobileElementFinder and MOB-suite. A dominant PopPUNK cluster contained 5604 genomes (99.86%). Its SNP phylogeny showed dense short-distance relationships within a connected lineage; pairwise distances had a median of 314 SNPs. Four antibiotic classes-beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, phenicols and fosfomycin-were detected in at least 95% of dominant-cluster genomes. The median antibiotic-class annotation hit count was 14 per genome (IQR, 13-15), including intrinsic and lineage-associated determinants. Predicted conjugative and mobilizable plasmid signatures occurred in 52.6% and 42.7% of dominant-cluster genomes, respectively. Across the full cohort, mobile-element and antibiotic-class hit counts were weakly positively correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.191). This unadjusted association was absent among 700 representatives selected one per ≤10-SNP component (ρ = -0.0721; p = 0.0567), and a component-bootstrap interval included zero. Assembly-adjusted associations differed between the full cohort and representatives. The small positive unadjusted collection-year association was not robust to location adjustment and was unsupported in dated representatives. Complete-genome annotations documented both chromosomal and plasmid blaOXA-23 copies and upstream ISAba1 proximity, without establishing promoter activity or resistance phenotype. These findings describe a cohesive ST2 lineage with heterogeneous accessory resistance and plasmid-mobility signatures, while emphasizing the sensitivity of genome-wide associations to assembly characteristics and clonal and geographic sampling.

Water-Soluble Chlorophyll Proteins as Biocompatible Photosensitizers for Photodynamic Therapy to Combat Antibiotic Resistance and Biofilm Through Disrupting Bacterial Membranes.
The escalating crisis of antibiotic resistance and biofilm-associated infections urgently demands therapeutic strategies with distinct mechanisms of action. Antibacterial photodynamic therapy (abPDT) offers a promising alternative, yet its clinical translation is often limited by the poor solubility, low biocompatibility, or complex delivery requirements of conventional photosensitizers (PSs). Here, we report the application of recombinant water-soluble chlorophyll proteins (WSCPs) from the Brassicaceae family as fully natural, self-contained PSs for abPDT. WSCP forms exceptionally stable tetrameric complexes with chlorophylls, providing outstanding water solubility, high photostability, negligible dark toxicity, and food-grade biocompatibility. Upon 660 nm light irradiation, WSCP-mediated abPDT achieves broad-spectrum killing of clinically relevant Gram-positive (including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, MRSA) and Gram-negative bacteria and effectively disrupts mature biofilms. Mechanistically, WSCP adheres to bacterial surfaces and generates singlet oxygen in situ, causing rapid membrane permeabilization, leakage of intracellular contents, and cell death, through a resistance-evading, physical mode of action. In a murine MRSA-infected wound model, a single topical application of WSCP followed by light exposure significantly reduces bacterial burden, suppresses inflammation, accelerates tissue regeneration, and promotes wound closure without observable toxicity. This work establishes WSCP-based abPDT as a safe, simple, and highly effective platform to combat antibiotic-resistant and biofilm-associated infections.

Combined effects of heat and rhamnolipids against Listeria monocytogenes: Influence of water activity and pH.
Foodborne diseases remain a major public health concern, with Listeria monocytogenes being one of the most significant foodborne pathogens due to its high mortality rate and persistence in food-processing environments. This study evaluated the combined effects of heat, pH, and water activity on the antimicrobial activity of rhamnolipids (RL) against L. monocytogenes within the framework of hurdle technology. Treatments were performed at 62 °C for 10 min under different pH and water activity (aw) conditions adjusted with NaCl or sucrose. Increasing NaCl concentrations reduced the efficacy of heat treatment alone; however, its combination with RL produced a synergistic effect, achieving reductions exceeding 5 log CFU/mL in low-aw media containing NaCl. In sucrose-containing media, the combined treatment reduced viable populations by 4-5 log CFU/mL across all pH and aw conditions evaluated. The hurdles also showed potential as a sanitizer formulation against L. monocytogenes attached to stainless steel surfaces, while scanning electron microscopy revealed extensive structural damage to treated cells. The combination of moderate heat and rhamnolipids exhibited synergistic antimicrobial activity under a range of pH and water activity conditions, representing a prospective strategy for controlling L. monocytogenes, particularly in low-water-activity foods with high salt or sugar contents.

Exploring the pharmacological basis of adverse effects in oxazolidinone and antidepressant cotherapy: an in silico study.
Linezolid and related oxazolidinones are frontline antibiotics against multidrug-resistant Gram-positive pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), yet their co-administration with antidepressants has been clinically associated with serotonin syndrome (SS) or hypertensive crisis (HC). While traditionally attributed to monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibition, clinical observations remain variable and the underlying mechanism is not completely understood. In this exploratory study, we applied an integrated in silico framework combining target prediction, network similarity, and structural modeling to generate testable hypotheses regarding potential alternative targets. Consensus profiling using SwissTargetPrediction and an integrative structural- and physicochemical-based target prediction methodology predicted possible interactions of linezolid and tedizolid with MAO isoforms, alongside exploratory aminergic targets including the 5-HT1A (HTR1A) receptor and adrenergic clusters. Comparing predicted targets with clinical datasets revealed an overlap with genes associated with SS and HC. Pathway enrichment and Jaccard similarity showed notable functional convergence with sertraline (OC > 0.90). Structural comparisons and physicochemical clustering grouped oxazolidinones near neurotransmitter intermediates, such as N-acetylserotonin. Furthermore, molecular docking across multiple crystallographic structures and ligand efficiency (LE) estimations suggested theoretically favorable interactions within MAO and HTR1A binding pockets, supported by shared pharmacophoric features. These computational findings provide a preliminary, hypothesis-generating basis suggesting that oxazolidinone-induced toxicity may involve targets beyond MAO, highlighting HTR1A modulation as a candidate mechanism requiring dedicated in vitro and in vivo validation.

Outcomes of Clostridium difficile infection in liver transplant patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
BACKGROUND: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a significant healthcare-associated complication, especially for liver transplant (LT) recipients who are at increased risk due to their immuno-suppressed status and antibiotic use. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed at elucidating the outcomes of CDI in LT recipients. METHODS: We adhered to PRISMA guidelines and searched databases including CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase and Scopus until December 2024. Studies included LT recipients with and without CDI. Outcomes were pooled using meta-analytic techniques with risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous data and mean differences for continuous data. RESULTS: Among 10 included studies (1,216,500 LT recipients; 3.2% with CDI), the primary pooled analysis showed no significant difference in mortality (OR, 1.34; 95% CI, 0.38-4.72; I2 = 100%). Sensitivity analyses excluding influential studies showed higher mortality in LT recipients with CDI (OR, 1.87; 95% CI, 1.45-2.41; I2 = 43%). Length of stay was longer among LT recipients with CDI (mean difference, 6.00 days; 95% CI, 2.83-9.17; I2 = 100%), with sensitivity analysis showing a mean difference of seven days after exclusion of one study (I2 = 0%). Elevated model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) scores were significantly higher in CDI cases (mean difference, 2.77; 95% CI, 1.34-4.20), indicating higher disease severity at baseline. Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use was not significant in the primary pooled analysis (OR, 2.18; 95% CI, 0.29-16.27; I2 = 69%) but was significant after sensitivity analysis excluding one study (OR, 5.87; 95% CI, 2.65-13.03; I2 = 0%). CONCLUSION: In addition to a significant association between PPI use and increased risk of CDI, CDI significantly affects mortality, duration of hospital stays and pre-operative MELD scores in LT recipients, underscoring its impact on post-operative outcomes.

Diagnostic accuracy of TB-LAMP assay on tongue swabs for pulmonary tuberculosis.
UNLABELLED: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading cause of infectious disease mortality worldwide. However, underdiagnosis and delayed diagnosis continue to facilitate disease transmission. Tongue swab sampling has emerged as a promising non-invasive alternative for the diagnosis of pulmonary TB. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Eiken TB-LAMP assay when utilizing tongue swab specimens and refined the processing protocols following tongue swab collection. In this prospective study, consecutive outpatients with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis who were able to provide sputum specimens were enrolled. Tongue swab specimens were tested using the WHO-endorsed Eiken TB-LAMP platform (EIKEN CHEMICAL CO., LTD., Tokyo, Japan). Sputum samples were analyzed by Xpert MTB/RIF and culture tests. The microbiological reference standard (MRS) was defined as positivity by either sputum culture or Xpert MTB/RIF. Diagnostic performance was compared to both MRS and Xpert MTB/RIF assay. Among the 243 enrolled participants, 136 (56.0%) were MRS-positive, and 107 (44.0%) were MRS-negative. The tongue swab Eiken TB-LAMP assay achieved a sensitivity of 80.2% (95% CI: 72.5%-86.1%) and a specificity of 94.6% (95% CI: 88.8%-97.5%) compared to sputum Xpert MTB/RIF, and 80.1% sensitivity (95% CI: 72.7%-86.0%) and 98.1% specificity (95% CI: 93.4%-99.7%) compared to the MRS. Sensitivity varied by bacterial load, ranging from 100% (95% CI: 77.2%-100.0%) in high-load cases to 62.5% (95% CI: 45.3%-77.1%) in very-low-load cases. The Eiken TB-LAMP assay using tongue swabs offers a rapid, reliable, and non-invasive diagnostic alternative for TB diagnosis with high specificity and favorable sensitivity. It could significantly reduce the current diagnostic gap, facilitating earlier intervention and helping to curb the ongoing transmission of tuberculosis in high-burden regions. IMPORTANCE: Effective control of the disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis is often hindered by the challenges of collecting sputum samples and the high costs associated with specialized laboratory equipment. This study examines a new diagnostic approach using tongue swabs combined with loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP). Unlike traditional methods that can be difficult for patients to perform and risky for healthcare workers to manage, tongue swabs are non-invasive, safe, and easy to collect. Because LAMP amplifies DNA under isothermal conditions without requiring thermal cycling, it is more affordable and requires minimal infrastructure, making it particularly suitable for clinics in remote or resource-limited areas. By demonstrating that this approach is effective, the research provides a foundation for faster and more accessible diagnosis. This shift could significantly improve patient care and help bridge the global gap in detecting this infectious disease.

Ultrafast visual detection of Streptococcus suis via HtpsC-targeted LAMP-CRISPR-Cas12a coupled with lateral flow immunochromatography.
This study describes a rapid, visual detection platform for Streptococcus suis, a significant zoonotic pathogen, by integrating loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) with CRISPR-Cas12a and a lateral flow immunochromatographic strip (LFIA) readout. Targeting the conserved HtpsC gene, specific LAMP primers and a PAM-compliant CrRNA were designed. Following isothermal amplification, the Cas12a/CrRNA complex recognizes the HtpsC amplicon, initiating target-specific cleavage and subsequent trans-cleavage of a dual-labeled ssDNA reporter (FAM-BIO), enabling visual detection on a LFIA; a design which reduces false positives. The optimized assay detected HtpsC-positive S. suis strains within 45 min and achieved a visual detection limit of 1.1 × 102 CFU/mL under laboratory conditions, with no cross-reactivity observed against the tested nontarget bacteria. In addition to pure-culture dilutions, the assay was further evaluated using spiked porcine blood samples and achieved similar detection performance, supporting its preliminary applicability in a complex biological matrix. Overall, this study provides an HtpsC-targeted visual detection workflow for screening of S. suis and is expected to be further applied to on-site rapid detection of clinical samples.

Iturin A disrupts Cryptococcus neoformans membrane integrity, attenuates virulence, and synergizes with amphotericin B.
Cryptococcus neoformans is a major fungal pathogen with severely limited therapeutic options. We evaluated the antifungal activity of the lipopeptide iturin A against eight clinical isolates of C. neoformans. Iturin A exhibited robust anti-cryptococcal activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 12.5 to 25 μg/mL, and demonstrated minimal toxicity in A549 lung epithelial cells and HepG2/C3A liver cells. Combination treatment with amphotericin B was synergistic (fractional inhibitory concentration index, 0.37). Mechanistic analyses showed that iturin A disrupts cryptococcal membrane integrity and induces intracellular reactive oxygen species accumulation, leading to fungal cell death. Iturin A also reduced biofilm formation and impaired capsule production. In the Caenorhabditis elegans infection model, treatment with iturin A alone or in combination with amphotericin B prolonged host survival and reduced fungal burden. Although iturin A decreased cryptococcal phagocytosis by J774 macrophage- and NR-9460 microglia-like cells, it enhanced intracellular killing by these phagocytes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that iturin A exhibits multifaceted activity against C. neoformans through membrane disruption, oxidative stress induction, and interference with virulence determinants, supporting its potential as a novel anti-cryptococcal therapeutic agent.

The household burden of sleeping sickness: out-of-pocket costs for diagnosis and treatment.
PURPOSE: This study estimated out-of-pocket (OOP) expenses associated with Human African Trypanosomiasis (HAT) care in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and explored how they influenced care-seeking behaviour and participation in HAT control, aiming to inform effective and financially accessible elimination strategies. METHODS: A sequential mixed-methods study was conducted using 16 SSIs and six focus group discussions, followed by a structured survey of 444 recently tested participants across six health zones. Medical and non-medical expenditures were collected by health structure type and screening strategy (active vs passive). Catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) was defined as OOP costs, excluding food, exceeding 10% or 25% of annual household income. RESULTS: Payments at health facilities, transport costs and long distances delayed care-seeking, particularly in passive screening (PS). Active screening (AS) was associated with minimal OOP, 93% of visits were cost-free, with a median OOP of US$0.76 among those incurring costs. PS generated higher expenses, only 12% of PS visits were cost-free, with a median OOP of US$9.08 among those with expenditures. Among confirmed cases, median OOP was lower through active (US$9.84) than PS (US$24.23). Nearly 90% of confirmed cases sold assets or borrowed money to cover expenses. CHE was uncommon under average household income (<4%) however 36% of passively detected cases exceeded the 10% threshold under minimum-wage income assumptions. CONCLUSION: Despite free diagnosis and treatment, accessing HAT care in rural, low-resource foci in the DRC still imposes a substantial financial burden. Reaching elimination targets and ensuring equitable access will require minimising indirect costs and logistical barriers to screening and diagnosis. As AS declines and routine health systems assume greater surveillance responsibilities, reducing indirect costs and logistical barriers will be critical to sustain coverage and maintain an effective and equitable HAT elimination strategy.

Uncovering spatially heterogeneous predictors of reported malaria cases in the Ashanti Region of Ghana: a triangulated framework integrating correlation analysis, random forest, and multiscale geographically weighted regression.
INTRODUCTION: Malaria remains a major cause of illness and death in sub-Saharan Africa. In 2023, WHO reported 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths globally. Ghana records a substantial malaria burden, and the Ashanti Region is among the regions contributing a large share of reported cases. Despite successive interventions, reported malaria incidence remains high. METHOD: This study used a triangulated analytical framework to examine environmental and anthropogenic correlates of district-level reported malaria case counts in 2023 (n = 43 districts). Spearman's rank Correlation, Random Forest, and MGWR models were fitted to raw district-level laboratory-confirmed case counts, and a population-normalized incidence rate was used only for the descriptive spatial map. Spearman's rank correlation characterized global monotonic associations, Random Forest (RF) with partial dependence plots (PDPs) examined nonlinear marginal patterns, and Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR) examined spatially varying local associations, following a variance inflation factor (VIF) screen for multicollinearity. RESULTS: Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) was the most consistently ranked correlate across the three analytical methods and was the only RF importance estimate distinguishable from the permutation null at the unadjusted 0.05 level (permutation p = 0.017; not adjusted for 11 comparisons). RF validation showed substantial overfitting and limited out-of-sample generalization (in-sample R² = 0.629; LOOCV R² = 0.056; MAE = 6897 cases; RMSE = 8851 cases; MAPE = 55.8%). Eight predictors had a bandwidth of 3 k-NN, suggesting strong estimated spatial non-stationarity under the MGWR model. With only 43 districts, these narrow bandwidths may also reflect coefficient instability rather than a confirmed spatial scale. CONCLUSION: Environmental and anthropogenic correlates of district-level reported malaria case counts varied across the Ashanti Region. These ecological associations are exploratory and hypothesis-generating, not evidence of causal transmission mechanisms or intervention effectiveness. Future studies should use reliable population denominators, facility-level coordinates, multiyear surveillance, entomological information, and socioeconomic covariates.

Bioactive compounds and therapeutic potential of the Brazilian genus Kielmeyera (Calophyllaceae): a comprehensive review.
The genus Kielmeyera Mart. (Calophyllaceae) comprises dozens of species, most of which are endemic to South American biomes, particularly the Cerrado, coastal ecosystem, and rupestrian grasslands. Several species have long been used in Brazilian traditional medicine for the treatment of inflammation, wound healing, gastrointestinal disorders, ulcers, leishmaniasis, fevers, and diverse infectious diseases. Despite the ecological and medicinal relevance of the genus, phytochemical and pharmacological investigations remain relatively limited. Available studies indicate that Kielmeyera species possess a specialized secondary metabolism rich in phenolic polyketide-derived compounds, especially xanthones and benzophenones, together with flavonoids and triterpenes. Based on the taxonomic treatment adopted in this review, we identified 55 accepted species of Kielmeyera. Of these, 22 species have been investigated phytochemically, whereas biological or pharmacological activities have been reported for only 13 species. Thus, 33 species had no phytochemical or pharmacological studies identified in the literature surveyed. Experimental studies have reported antimicrobial, antiparasitic, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, cytotoxic, and other bioactivities that partially support their traditional medicinal uses. However, no published clinical evidence, including randomized controlled trials, observational studies, or well-documented case series-currently supports the therapeutic efficacy of Kielmeyera preparations in humans. This review provides the first comprehensive and critical synthesis of more than six decades of published research on the taxonomy, ethnobotany, phytochemistry, and pharmacological properties of Kielmeyera species, while highlighting current knowledge gaps and future research priorities.

Occurrence of Cryptosporidium sp. in fresh produce from the Metropolitan Area of Costa Rica: an update.
Foodborne diseases represent a major global public health problem, causing significant morbidity and mortality, and substantial economic losses. Fruits and vegetables are considered among the main vehicles for transmission of infectious agents like bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites, including Cryptosporidium sp. This protozoan parasite comprises many species that infect a wide range of hosts, is environmentally and geographically ubiquitous and has become one of the leading causes of diarrheal disease; in immunocompromised hosts, the infection can result in a chronic, life-threatening disease. Considering the importance of fruit and vegetable consumption in the daily diet and the need to ensure their safety, the aim of the study was to evaluate the presence of Cryptosporidium sp. in strawberries, lettuce and cilantro marketed in the Metropolitan Area of Costa Rica and to assess the degree of faecal contamination in these foods. For this purpose, 96 samples were analysed using parasitological and molecular methods that included a nested PCR to amplify Cryptosporidium sp. gp60 gene. Moreover, the presence of total and thermotolerant coliforms and Escherichia coli was also determined by culture methods and counts, for further identification using the VITEK system. Direct examination of wet mount and Ziehl-Neelsen stains revealed five Cryptosporidium sp. positive samples by microscopy and 22 positive samples by PCR; the identified species was Cryptosporidium parvum. Cilantro samples presented the highest counts of total, and thermotolerant coliforms and E. coli was identified in14 samples among 82 samples subjected to bacteriological analyses. The detection of C. parvum in raw vegetables and fruits from different provinces in Costa Rica, particularly using molecular techniques, demonstrates the need to strengthen surveillance and control in the production and marketing of these foods, to improve risk assessment and its relevance to public health.

Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome-mitochondrion Ca2+ transfer and signaling in Trypanosoma cruzi.
Calcium ion (Ca2+) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in Trypanosoma cruzi, the etiologic agent of Chagas disease, mediated by the mechano/osmosensitive channel TcPiezo2. Using ultrastructural, biochemical, and live-cell superresolution imaging, we define lysosome-mitochondrion contact sites (LMCs) that enable direct Ca2+ transfer. TcPiezo2 triggers Ca2+ release, which generates perilysosomal nanodomains that drives mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake via the voltage-dependent anion channel and the mitochondrial Ca2+ uniporter complex. Disruption of TcPiezo2-dependent Ca2+ transfer impairs mitochondrial metabolism, perturbs redox homeostasis, induces autophagy, and eventually leads to parasite death. These findings establish LMCs as a signaling platform that directly regulates interorganelle Ca2+ transfer and mitochondrial bioenergetics.

Incidence and Risk Factors for Invasive Mold Infections in Children During First-Line Chemotherapy for Primary Acute Leukemia: A National Retrospective Cohort Study.
BACKGROUND: Invasive mold infections (IMI) are life-threatening complications during treatment for pediatric acute leukemia. Population-based data on IMI incidence, timing, and outcomes during first-line therapy remain limited. We aimed to provide a nationwide epidemiological overview of IMI during first-line treatment of pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and explore potential treatment-related risk factors. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study of all children (<18 years) initiating first-line chemotherapy for AML or ALL in Denmark during 2008-2022. IMIs were classified as proven or probable according to 2020 EORTC/MSGERC criteria by review of microbiology, imaging, pathology, and chart data. Follow-up covered first-line chemotherapy. Competing risk-adjusted cumulative incidence of IMI was estimated, risk factors were evaluated using Cox regression, and survival after IMI was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: Among 621 patients, 43 (6.9%) developed IMI: 14/90 (15.6%) with AML and 29/531 (5.5%) with ALL. In adjusted Cox regression, AML was associated with higher IMI hazard than ALL (HR 5.6, 95% CI 2.6 to 12.1), whereas no other prespecified risk factors were independently associated with IMI. Incidence rates were 38.6 per 100 patient-years in AML and 2.7 in ALL. Nearly half of IMIs occurred beyond 90 days after initiation of first-line chemotherapy. Four patients experienced a second distinct IMI episode; Aspergillus species accounted for 37/47 (79%) episodes and non-Aspergillus molds for 10/47 (21%). IMI-associated death occurred in 10 patients (1.6% of the cohort), yielding a case fatality rate of 23% among IMI cases; IMI was present in 43% of all deaths. CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, IMI occurred more frequently than reported in many previous pediatric studies, particularly in AML. IMIs were observed throughout first-line therapy, despite antifungal prophylaxis, and were associated with substantial mortality, emphasizing the need for sustained clinical vigilance beyond induction.

Atovaquone-proguanil chemoprophylaxis during pregnancy: a case series and a systematic review and meta-analysis.
BACKGROUND: Pregnant women travelling to malaria endemic areas require effective chemoprophylaxis, with limited options including atovaquone-proguanil (AP) for which safety data remain limited. Our objective was to describe the prevalences of pregnancy outcomes and major congenital anomaly (MCA) following AP chemoprophylaxis during pregnancy. METHODS: We combined a case series from the French national Teratology Information Service (CRAT) and a systematic review and meta-analysis (SRMA), including prospective pregnancies exposed to AP for chemoprophylaxis. Outcomes were prevalence of pregnancy outcomes and MCA. The case series included all pregnancies referred to the CRAT with an expected date of delivery between 2009-2025, and known outcome. The SRMA searched Medline, Embase, Cochrane databases and grey literature up to 16/09/2025. Study selection and data extraction were performed using an independent dual review process. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Pooled prevalences were estimated using random-effects models. GRADE was used to assess certainty of evidence. RESULTS: Our case series included 191 AP-exposed pregnancies (133 during first-trimester (T1) and 75 during second/third trimester) resulting in 85.9% livebirths (n=164), 10.0% miscarriages (n=19), 1.0% medical abortions (n=2), 1.0% stillbirth (n=2) and 2.1% elective termination (n=4). The prevalence of MCA among T1-exposed pregnancies with documented MCA status (n=110) was 3.6% (95%CI[1.0;9.0]). The SRMA included four studies, which when combined with our case series (555 AP-exposed pregnancies, 457 during T1) produced a pooled prevalence of livebirths of 80.3% (95%CI[72.3;87.2], I2=67.2%, Phet=0,047), 14.6% miscarriages (95%CI[7.3;23.9], I2=73.2%, Phet=0,024) and 2.7% for MCA (95%CI[1.2;4.8], I2=0.0%, Phet=0,45). Level of evidence was low. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that pregnancy outcomes and MCA following AP chemoprophylaxis exposure are similar to the general population prevalences, with a low level of evidence. These data strengthen the evidence supporting a reassuring safety profile, and AP may represent a reasonable option for pregnant women requiring malaria chemoprophylaxis after risk-benefit assessment.

The Qing Chang Hua Shi Formula combined with allicin alleviates Cryptosporidium parvum infection in immunosuppressed mice and is associated with restoration of NLRP6, IL-18, IFN-γ, and intestinal microbiota.
Cryptosporidium parvum is a highly pathogenic zoonotic parasite with limited therapies. Current study explored the anti-C. parvum effect of Qing Chang Hua Shi Formula (QHF) and allicin in vitro in immunosuppressed mice. In vitro, QHF and allicin inhibited over 90% of C. parvum. In vivo, the 8-day treatment reduced fecal oocyst shedding to 12.88% of the model group. Infection disrupted intestinal homeostasis, reduced tight-junction protein expression, and downregulated NLRP6, while inducing systemic inflammation and elevating IL-18/IFN-γ levels, which were further increased by treatment. Treated mice also showed increased abundance of Archangium and Corallococcus and decreased abundance of Clostridioides and Butyricimonas. Predicted microbial functional pathways revealed enrichment of glycolysis-related genes (L-lactate dehydrogenase [LDH], glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase [GAPDH]) in infected mice, with treatment-associated shifts in amino acid synthesis pathways. Molecular docking suggested potential binding of benzoylpaeoniflorin, baicalin, and wogonoside to C. parvum LDH, ATP/ADP translocase, and gp40/15. Together, these findings indicate that QHF combined with allicin alleviates C. parvum infection in immunosuppressed mice and is associated with restoration of intestinal barrier markers, immune responses, and gut microbiota composition, suggesting a potential therapeutic approach for cryptosporidiosis.IMPORTANCECurrent study demonstrates that Qing Chang Hua Shi Formula (QHF) combined with allicin effectively inhibits Cryptosporidium parvum proliferation and concurrently mitigates intestinal damage and dysbiosis induced by C. parvum infection. QHF treatment was associated with upregulation of NLRP6, improved gut microbiota profiles, and elevated IFN-γ levels. These changes correlated with reduced parasite burden and alleviated intestinal injury, suggesting a potential immunomodulatory role that warrants further mechanistic investigation. Metagenomics disclosed that QHF and allicin were associated with changes in predicted microbial functional pathways, including those involved in glycolysis and amino acid metabolism, and with enrichment of certain bacterial taxa, such as Corallococcus and Archangium. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that benzoylpaeoniflorin and baicalin may bind stably to C. parvum L-lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and ATP/ADP translocase, raising the hypothesis that they could interfere with parasite energy metabolism. However, enzymatic validation is required to confirm this possibility. These findings suggest a potential therapeutic approach for cryptosporidiosis and highlight alterations associated with C. parvum infection.

Perspectives on public health interventions in the management of the COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand.
BACKGROUND: Any government needs to react quickly to a pandemic and make decisions on healthcare interventions locally and internationally with little information regarding the perceptions of people and the reactions they may receive during the implementation of restrictions. METHODS: We report an anonymous online survey in Thailand conducted in May 2020 to assess public perceptions of three interventions in the Thai context: isolation, quarantine and social distancing. A total of 1,020 participants, of whom 52% were women, responded to the survey. RESULTS: Loss of income was the main concern among respondents (>80% for all provinces in Thailand). Traditional media and social media were important channels for communication during the pandemic. A total of 92% of respondents reported that they changed their social behaviour even before the implementation of government policy with 94% reporting they performed social distancing, 97% reported using personal protective equipment such as masks and 95% reported using sanitizer products. CONCLUSIONS: This study showed a high level of compliance from individuals with government enforced or voluntarily controls such as quarantine, isolation and social distancing in Thailand. The findings from this study can be used to inform future government measures to control the pandemic and to shape communication strategies.

"It's Like a Whole Set of Things That We Do": A Qualitative Study of the Roles of Journal Editors-in-Chief.
INTRODUCTION: Journal editors-in-chief (EICs) play a central role in shaping scholarly publishing, yet little is known about how they understand and enact their roles. We explored how medical education journal EICs describe their roles in shaping the publication process. METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study using thematic analysis of interviews with nine medical education journal EICs. The interviews were part of a broader investigation of publication timelines and explored editorial leadership and practices, including experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants' accounts also provided insight into the broader work of leading a journal, which became the focus of the present analysis. RESULTS: Participants described their work not as a set of discrete tasks, but as five interrelated roles: knowledge developer, proactive communicator, steward of time and energy, nurturer, and orchestrator. These roles were enacted simultaneously and often in tension, reflecting the need to balance scholarly rigor, relational commitments, and system constraints. EICs described actively shaping knowledge, orchestrating complex communication networks, safeguarding finite reviewer and editorial resources, supporting authors and editorial teams, and maintaining workflow continuity. Much of this work was characterized as invisible labor occurring behind the scenes and not captured in formal metrics. Participants also highlighted a structural tension between nurturing authors and stewarding limited resources, underscoring the challenges of sustaining both inclusivity and efficiency within a resource-constrained system. DISCUSSION: This study offers a practice-informed framework for understanding EIC work as relational, strategic, and system-oriented. By making visible the often-invisible labor that underpins academic publishing, our findings challenge reductive conceptions of editorial work and highlight the need for training, support, and systemic changes to better align expectations for rigor, inclusivity, and sustainability.

Toxicological Vulnerabilities and Emerging Safety Signals in Modified mRNA Vaccine Technology: A Narrative Review of the COVID-19 Experience.
The rapid deployment in early 2021 of modified mRNA (modRNA) as a vaccine platform for the COVID-19 pandemic sparked a wave of optimism for its potential as a preventive medicine. However, this compacted timeframe may not have fully addressed certain toxicological risks associated with this new technology, which would typically require more extensive preclinical testing. Five years postrollout, an accumulating body of postauthorisation evidence has highlighted safety signals that require closer scrutiny, such as those concerning biodistribution, off-target effects and persistent adverse events. Independent analyses of Phase III trial data and pharmacovigilance reports have raised questions regarding benefit-risk balance and potential long-term biological effects. This narrative review examines the evolution of the toxicological understanding of modified RNA as a vaccine technology from platform design through long-term observational data, identifying areas of uncertainty and vulnerability that may inform future development and regulatory evaluation. The review emphasises that fast-tracked decision-making under exceptional uncertainty requires explicit safeguards to prevent premature certainty and to support learning from emerging evidence over time.

Scoping Review of Lessons Learned During the Pandemic to Improve Intimate Partner Violence Services.
The COVID-19 pandemic restricted access to intimate partner violence (IPV) support systems, increased the risk of IPV, and worsened already complex social and safety issues for survivors. As shelters were forced by public health mandates to adapt the way services were provided, many implemented innovative approaches to delivering care. The purpose of this unregistered review is to describe some of these adaptations and how they can continue to support survivors in a post-pandemic environment. We reviewed 261 identified reports and articles from 2018 to 2022 that were open access or available as full-text sources and included information on the impacts of COVID-19 on IPV and survivors as well as service adaptation. Inclusion criteria also required peer review and that the focus be on the U.S. population, narrowing the scope to 112 final sources. Search terms captured recommendations for different racial and ethnic groups and thematic coding revealed developments in providing services to different communities, within movement and space restrictions, and via telehealth. Researchers overwhelmingly support universal violence screening and education, especially among healthcare providers, and training in trauma-informed care. Many also endorse a community-based approach to violence prevention and service provision that engages multiple sectors and shifts the role of shelters to emergencies only. Lessons learned during the pandemic and new approaches to providing support to survivors of violence, such as telehealth, community collaboration, housing first models, and mobile advocacy, should continue to be studied to show effective avenues for implementation.

Has the COVID-19 pandemic altered social inequalities in child development? A time trend analysis of developmental delays in preschool children by parental education.
BACKGROUND: Child development may have deteriorated during the COVID-19 pandemic, with children from vulnerable backgrounds potentially facing the greatest risks. This study examined time trends in developmental delays among preschool children and whether inequalities in these delays by parental education changed with the onset of the pandemic. METHODS: Analyses used mandatory School Entry Examinations (SEE) in the Aachen region, Germany, covering ten cohorts (2015-2024) and restricted to children identified as being at risk for developmental delays (n = 15,299). The outcome was the number of delayed domains among six assessed. A segmented (interrupted time series) Poisson regression estimated the pre-pandemic trend, the level shift at the break between the 2020 and 2021 cohorts, and the subsequent change in trend, with inequalities by parental education expressed on both the relative and absolute scale. Multiple imputation and inverse probability weighting were applied. RESULTS: Children of less-educated parents showed significantly more delays in every cohort. Delays increased significantly before the pandemic at a comparable rate in all educational groups. Delays rose abruptly in the 2021 cohort in all groups and declined thereafter, remaining elevated. Between the two periods, relative inequality narrowed significantly because delays increased proportionally more among children with moderate and high parental education, whereas absolute inequality was unchanged. CONCLUSION: Children from families with lower educational attainment continued to experience a consistently higher burden of developmental delays. The first cohort assessed after the onset of the pandemic showed an abrupt, population-wide increase, which reduced inequality on a relative scale while leaving the absolute gap between educational groups unchanged. Public health strategies must address both persistent structural disparities and the broad vulnerabilities revealed by global crises.

COVID-19 among people with intellectual disability in comparison to the general population: diagnoses, hospitalizations, deaths, and vaccinations (IDcare).
BACKGROUND: People with intellectual disabilities (ID) were identified as one of the vulnerable groups during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, few studies have investigated a comprehensive set of COVID-19-related outcomes. The aim of this study is therefore to describe COVID-19-related diagnoses, hospitalizations, deaths, and vaccinations among people with ID compared to the general population. METHODS: This register-based cohort study included all people living in Skåne, Sweden, on January 1st, 2014. People with ID and still alive January 1st, 2020, constituted the ID cohort (n = 14 046). Those remaining after excluding people in the same family/household comprised the general population cohort (gPop, n = 1 157 138). Data regarding outcomes were collected from Swedish national and regional registers for 2020 and 2021. RESULTS: People in the ID cohort had higher risk of being diagnosed with COVID-19 but were less likely than those in the gPop cohort to have the diagnosis confirmed by laboratory test. Adults and older people in the ID cohort had higher COVID-19 related healthcare utilization in terms of physical primary care visits in 2020 and hospitalizations in both 2020 and 2021, with some sex and age differences within the ID cohort. Among those with at least one physical primary care contact, adults and older women in the ID cohort had fewer contacts in 2020 compared to their peers in the gPop cohort. Where the number of observations allowed for analyses, people in the ID cohort had higher risk of death from COVID-19 than those in the gPop cohort. CONCLUSIONS: People with ID had similar healthcare utilization as the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic, with the same or higher levels of COVID-related healthcare, and similar vaccination rates. However, people with ID with healthcare contacts had fewer contacts and bed days and higher mortality. Overall, the Swedish COVID-19 strategy regarding vaccination and healthcare prioritization for people with ID seems to have worked as intended.

Non-pharmacological interventions: nomenclature, taxonomy, and working definitions.
Many terms have been used to describe interventions that do not involve the use of pharmacological products in the setting of communicable diseases. Terminology has varied, and terms have included physical, non-pharmaceutical, non-drug, non-pharmacologic, and non-pharmacological interventions, as well as public health measures and public health and social measures. The recent COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the importance of non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs), and the term is now recognized globally. The use of the terms public health measures or public health and social measures has variably been inclusive of the use of vaccines, which would be considered pharmacological products. Given this background and confusion over terminology and descriptions, we have reviewed this topic to provide clarity regarding nomenclature, taxonomy, and definitions, with the aim of ensuring an explicit shared understanding of any interventions that do not involve pharmacological products, given the importance of conducting NPI evaluations for future epidemics and pandemics.

Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19.
Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

Rurality as a Risk Factor for Excess Mortality in Nebraska During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
Introduction/ObjectivesThe COVID-19 pandemic increased mortality across the United States, but its burden was uneven across communities. Rural populations may be vulnerable because of differences in age structure, health care access, preventive behaviors, and vaccination uptake. This study examined the association between rurality and excess mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic in Nebraska.MethodsThis ecological study used Nebraska death certificate data from 2015 through May 2023, COVID-19 laboratory, hospitalization, and vaccination data, and American Community Survey sociodemographic data. Monthly deaths from 2015 through 2019 were used to forecast expected deaths by zip code tabulation area from January 1, 2020, through May 31, 2023, using seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average models. Excess mortality was calculated as observed minus expected deaths. Secondary regression analysis using Poisson regression assessed associations between rurality and excess mortality, with inclusion of demographic, socioeconomic, COVID-19 infection, hospitalization, and vaccination measures as covariates.ResultsNebraska had 63,333 observed deaths and 57,865 expected deaths, corresponding to 5,468 excess deaths. Rurality was the strongest associated factor for excess mortality across pandemic phases, with the strongest association during the pre-vaccine phase. Vaccination was generally associated with reduced excess mortality.ConclusionsRurality was an important risk factor for excess mortality in Nebraska. Findings support targeted rural surveillance, outreach, primary care engagement, and emergency preparedness.

Chinese Patients' Willingness to Use Virtual Visits During and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Repeated Cross-Sectional Study in Zhejiang Province, 2021-2024.
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic has been a critical external driver of telemedicine adoption. As the pandemic entered its later stages, countries worldwide transitioned from stringent containment measures to routine management. This policy shift may in turn have shaped patients' willingness to use (WTU) telemedicine. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to examine the changes in patients' WTU virtual visits during and after the COVID-19 pandemic in China, with particular attention to the policy transition from stringent containment to routine pandemic management, and to identify factors associated with patients' WTU across different survey years. METHODS: Repeated cross-sectional surveys were conducted among 340, 786, 1179, and 1373 hospital outpatients in Zhejiang Province, China, from 2021 to 2024. Using year as a proxy for the evolving COVID-19 containment policy context, this study used binary logistic regression of pooled 2021-2024 repeated cross-sectional data to examine whether survey year was significantly associated with patients' WTU virtual visits. Separate year-specific binary logistic regression was fitted to identify factors associated with patients' WTU in each survey year. RESULTS: The proportion of patients' WTU virtual visits was 70.88% (241/340) in 2021, 71.37% (561/786) in 2022, 62.34% (735/1179) in 2023, and 75.38% (1035/1373) in 2024. In the pooled 2021-2024 repeated cross-sectional analysis, survey year was significantly associated with patients' WTU: compared with 2021, patients' likelihood of being willing to use virtual visits was lower in 2023, but higher in 2024. In the year-specific analyses, educational level and primary source of information were consistently associated with patients' WTU across all 4 years. Visiting hospital tier was additionally associated with WTU in 2022; age and visiting hospital tier were associated with WTU in 2023; and age, monthly income, and self-rated health status were additionally associated with WTU in 2024. Joint Wald tests of year-by-covariate interactions confirmed that the associations of age, visiting hospital tier, monthly income, and self-rated health with WTU varied across survey years. CONCLUSIONS: Patients' WTU remained high across the 2021-2024 transition from stringent COVID-19 containment to routine pandemic management, declining in the first postpandemic wave of 2023 and then rebounding to its highest level in 2024. The correlates of WTU were only partially stable: a college-level education and internet-based information seeking were consistently associated with higher WTU in both the pooled and year-specific analyses, whereas the associations with age, visiting hospital tier, monthly income, and self-rated health varied across survey years and emerged only in specific periods. These findings suggest that virtual visits gained sustained acceptance among patients in economically and digitally developed regions of China, and that telemedicine platform design should accommodate patients with lower educational levels or limited internet skills while outreach extends across a broader range of age groups to support more equitable adoption.

Digital Campaign to Promote COVID-19 Vaccination and Clinical Trial Participation Among Vietnamese Americans: Observational Engagement Study.
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic necessitated innovative approaches to health communication, particularly for non-English-speaking communities. Vietnamese Americans, who report lower rates of English proficiency, faced unique challenges accessing facts and subsequent "infodemic" of rapidly spreading information. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility and engagement patterns of a community-engaged bilingual digital campaign delivered through Google's Display & Video 360 (DV360) platform to Vietnamese Americans in Texas, comparing performance across multiple advertising formats. METHODS: We implemented a 2-phase digital campaign on (DV360): static display advertisements (Phase 1: February 15-March 31, 2022) and audiovisual content (Phase 2: May 26-June 30, 2022). With community-based organizations (CBOs), 6 static displays, 2 videos, and 2 audio advertisements were developed in English and Vietnamese using focus group review and back-translation. Advertisement placements were constrained to a Texas Vietnamese audience segment. Total budget was US $9,472.54. Performance was evaluated using impressions, click-through rate (CTR), cost metrics, cost per click (CPC), cost per thousand impressions (CPM), and cost per view (CPV), with Wilson 95% CI, and two-proportion z-tests for substantive comparisons. RESULTS: The campaign generated 4,974,357 impressions, reaching approximately 1.4 million unique users in Phase 1, and 105,000 in Phase 2. Vietnamese-language display advertisements achieved a higher CTR than English-language advertisements (0.105% vs 0.046%; χ1²=480.6; P<.001; risk ratio 2.29). Mobile placements outperformed desktop within each language (Vietnamese mobile 0.156% vs desktop 0.045%; English mobile 0.064% vs desktop 0.019%). Audio CTR was 1.911% in May but fell to 0.119% in June on small denominators (≈1800 impressions; 5 clicks). Impressions concentrated in expected Texas metropolitan areas (Houston 24.4%, Dallas 19.9%, Austin 7.9%). Phase 2 Google Analytics Behavior Flow showed 55.2% of language-distinguished landings were on Vietnamese pages (χ²1=6.7; P=.01). Cost efficiency was favorable (CPC US $2.35 and CPM US $1.45). CONCLUSIONS: A community-engaged bilingual digital campaign produced measurable in-language engagement among Vietnamese American audiences in Texas. Like other COVID-19 outreach campaigns directed at historically marginalized groups, researchers worked closely with CBOs, paying particular attention to messaging, language translation, and graphic representation in display, audio, and video advertisements to reach the population of interest. What differed from other campaigns was the use of DV360 allowing dissemination across multiple platforms and devices. Results are limited to engagement because direct impact on COVID-19 immunization or participation in clinical trials was not measured. Future directions can explore more clinically significant outcomes, in-language radio advertising, and harnessing AI to develop and monitor public health campaigns.

Exploring Social Media Use and Anxiety Symptoms in Health Care Workers During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Cross-Sectional Secondary Data Analysis.
BACKGROUND: Health care workers (HCWs) experienced significant mental health challenges, particularly anxiety, during the COVID-19 pandemic. Although social media became a primary source of information and connection, it was also a potential source of stress. The influence of social media on HCWs' anxiety is not well understood. OBJECTIVE: This study examined associations between social media use and anxiety symptoms among HCWs during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: We conducted a secondary, cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2021 UC-COVID study (N=427 HCWs). Anxiety symptoms were assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-2 (GAD-2). Social media use across multiple platforms (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, other social media platforms, and other media sources) was evaluated using factor analysis to create a single variable for social media use. Logistic regression models estimated associations between overall social media use and anxiety symptoms, both unadjusted and adjusted for demographic, occupational, and health-related characteristics. RESULTS: Factor analysis supported a single latent factor representing overall social media use, with all platform indicators loading significantly on the factor (P<.001) and with moderate loadings (0.33-0.59). Of 427 HCWs, the mean age was 44.3 (SD 13.5), and the majority identified as female (n=314, 73.5%) and as working in a hospital location (n=136, 43.6%). Facebook was used the most, with 54% (n=230) of participants using the platform at least once per day. A total of 29% reported clinically relevant anxiety symptoms (GAD-2 ≥3). Using the social media variable from the factor analysis, higher social media use was significantly associated with anxiety symptoms (odds ratio [OR] 1.77, CI 1.15-2.73). Older age was significantly associated with reduced anxiety symptoms (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.97, CI 0.95-0.99). HCWs with a history of mental health diagnoses reported higher levels of anxiety symptoms (aOR 2.33, CI 1.35-4.03). Non-Hispanic Asian HCWs reported fewer anxiety symptoms compared to Non-Hispanic White HCWs (aOR 0.39, CI 0.19-0.80). Participants reporting higher income had significantly lower odds of anxiety symptoms than those in the lower-income group (aOR 0.51, CI 0.30-0.87). CONCLUSIONS: Study findings highlight the multifactorial nature of anxiety symptoms in HCWs and the need to consider social media use as an important contributor. Integrating HCWs and multiplatform social media use into a single measure offered an innovative lens on digital behavior and anxiety symptoms. The rapidly evolving digital landscape underscores the need for continued research. Future studies should include emerging social media platforms (ie, TikTok, Reddit, YouTube) as usage patterns shift over time. Longitudinal and mixed methods approaches are necessary to understand patterns and methods of social media use over time. Larger and more diverse HCW samples, stronger mental health measures (eg, GAD-7, depression, and burnout scales), and analyses stratified by clinical role and sociodemographic factors will be essential to guide interventions supporting mental health and well-being.

Decreases in Cancer Mortality During the COVID-19 Pandemic and Mortality Displacement in Aged Societies.
Objectives. To examine whether pandemic-era changes in cancer mortality reflect true improvements or mortality displacement and whether patterns differ by population aging, with updated Global Burden of Disease (GBD) mortality estimates from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation. Methods. We conducted a cross-national ecological analysis using GBD 2023 data from 204 countries and territories. Countries were classified as aged if more than 14% of the population was aged 65 years or older in 2019. The exposure was cumulative COVID-19 age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and the outcome was change in all-cancer ASMR. Results. Among aged societies (n = 55), higher COVID-19 mortality was correlated with larger decreases in cancer mortality (r = -0.45; P = .001). No correlation was observed in non‒aged societies (n = 149; r = 0.08; P = .34), and correlations differed (P < .01). Across all countries and territories, the overall correlation was weak (r = 0.13; P = .06), indicating the inverse correlation was confined to aged populations. Public Health Implications. Decreases in cancer mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic may reflect mortality displacement rather than true improvements, particularly in aging populations. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print October 15, 2026:e1-e4. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308797).

Effectiveness of Diphtheria and Tetanus Toxoids and Acellular Pertussis Vaccine in Children Aged 6 Months-6 Years During a Statewide Pertussis Outbreak - Alaska, May-November 2024.
Widespread use of pertussis vaccines in children has resulted in a >90% reduction in the number of annual pertussis cases in the United States. After a period of low U.S. pertussis incidence during and shortly after the COVID-19 pandemic, incidence increased in 2024. Data on the real-world effectiveness of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids and acellular pertussis vaccine (DTaP) against pertussis during this disease resurgence are limited. In response to documentation of a record high pertussis incidence in Alaska during May-November 2024, DTaP vaccine effectiveness (VE) against pertussis in Alaska children aged 6 months-6 years was evaluated. Adjusted VE was 96.2% among children who had completed the 3-dose primary DTaP series and 85.3% among those who were partially vaccinated. Compared with children who had received ≥3 DTaP doses, the odds of laboratory-confirmed pertussis were approximately 26 times as high in unvaccinated children (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 26.1), and approximately 4 times as high in those who had received 1-2 DTaP doses (adjusted OR = 3.8). These findings reinforce the importance of following pertussis vaccination recommendations to protect for children from the disease and reduce the occurrence of pertussis outbreaks.

Mortality From 1918-1919 Spanish Flu Among the American Expeditionary Forces Analyzed Through People-Powered Research.
INTRODUCTION: The Card Register of Burials of Deceased American Soldiers, 1917-1922 holds the burial cards of American servicemen and women who died at sea or overseas during or after World War I (WWI). We aimed to use this online register to study mortality statistics in the American Expeditionary Forces (AEF) during the 3 waves of Spanish flu in 1918 and 1919. However, the register, which includes 104 file units, lacks database query functionality. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Over 6,000 volunteers attached to the Zooniverse platform for people-powered research submitted 4 million transcription tasks from individual burial cards in the online register. This information was used to create the American WWI Burial Cards Search Tool, which is a free online searchable database that also allows, among others, for study of mortality statistics. RESULTS: The first wave of Spanish flu resulted in a relevant increase in mortality in the AEF. During the second wave, mortality increased significantly, peaking on October 9, 1918, with 474 deaths. Moreover, data show that the weekly mortality rate started to increase already in early August, in contrast to a previous report stating that the second wave of Spanish flu ran its course in the AEF roughly from September 15 onwards. In all, at least 14,494 servicepersons in the AEF died from influenza and/or pneumonia during the deadly second and third waves of Spanish flu. In contrast, mortality from COVID-19 in the U.S. military was low, with 96 deaths as of December 8, 2022. CONCLUSIONS: People-powered research provided a unique possibility to study single-day mortality figures from influenza and/or pneumonia in the AEF during the different waves of Spanish flu. In all, at least 14,494 servicepersons in the AEF died from influenza and/or pneumonia during the second and third waves of Spanish flu, while we show that the weekly mortality rate during the second wave increased already in early August 1918. In contrast, mortality from COVID-19 in the U.S. military was low. Thus, pandemics of respiratory infections have different impacts on mortality in army personnel, depending on specific pathogenic characteristics of the causative agent.

Development and Validation of End-Of-Life Indicators for Dialysis Patients: A National Consensus Study in Taiwan.
BackgroundIdentifying end-of-life (EOL) dialysis patients who may benefit from palliative care remains challenging in Asian healthcare settings where relational autonomy predominates over individual decision-making. We conducted a national consensus study in Taiwan during 2015-2016 to develop validated EOL indicators for dialysis patients, with findings subsequently validated through a decade of clinical experience including the COVID-19 pandemic.MethodsWe conducted a three-phase study: (1) systematic literature review; (2) two-round expert focus groups using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method with 15 multidisciplinary experts; and (3) national survey of nephrologists from 624 dialysis facilities. Nine indicators were evaluated using 9-point Likert scales. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses identified latent constructs.ResultsOf 624 facilities, 337 responded (54.0%), yielding 254 nephrologists with complete responses (22.6% of registered specialists). Two indicators achieved high consensus (≥90%) for both hospice/dying care and advance care planning: prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV) with dialysis in unconscious state, and PMV with multi-organ failure. Factor analysis identified three EOL patient subgroups: ventilator-dependent, critically ill, and functionally dependent, with acceptable CFA model fit (χ2 = 27.6, df = 19, P = 0.091; RMSEA = 0.042; CFI = 0.99). ACP ratings yielded a two-factor structure with adequate fit (χ2 = 35.5, df = 20, P = 0.018; RMSEA = 0.055).ConclusionsDialysis patients with PMV combined with unconsciousness or multi-organ failure represent the highest-consensus EOL indicators in Taiwan. These validated findings offer actionable guidance for hospice and end-of-life care referral within healthcare systems characterized by relational autonomy and collective family-patient-clinician deliberation.

Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) are associated with distinct clinical phenotypes two years after SARS-CoV-2 infection: A data-driven approach.
It is important to determine whether the persistent cognitive and fatigue complaints, as part of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), are associated with underlying patterns and specific symptoms clusters. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate symptom clusters and clinical phenotypes in PASC. We included n = 153 individuals (53 years old, 66% female, 2 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection) categorized into groups with (n = 88) and without (n = 65) PASC, defined by severe fatigue and concentration problems using validated cut-offs. Symptom clusters (i.e., component loadings and component scores) were identified using principal component analyses (PCA, eigenvalue[EV]>1.0), using clinical, somatic, coping and sleep factors, symptom severity, neuropsychological and physical tests (totalling 19 tests and questionnaires). We then used logistic regression techniques on (participant-level) component scores (standardized) to investigate associations with PASC. Finally, K-means clustering methods to identify clinical phenotypes. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, education, nationality and time since infection. PCA identified 5 components, explaining 70% of the variance. We labelled these components as follows: (1) PEM, ME/CFS and sleep symptoms, coping factors (EV = 7.0, 36.9% variance), (2) information-processing speed (EV = 2.5, 13.3%), (3) executive functioning (EV = 1.5, 8.0%, (4) physical performance (EV = 1.2, 6.5%), (5) somatic comorbidities and hospital admission (EV = 1.0, 5.5%). Logistic regression showed that only the first component scores (Odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 97.1 [16.5-570.3], p 0.05), associated with PASC. Cluster analysis revealed two distinct clinical phenotypes among individuals with severe chronic fatigue: one marked by physical impairment and the other by diminished cognitive performance. Consistent with existing literature, we confirmed that PASC is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by extensive, interrelated symptoms. Notably, we identified specific cognitive and physical clinical phenotypes. These findings are important for future targeted diagnosis and treatment.

Sickle cell disease screening: Experiences of parents with positive newborns at Korle Bu TeachingHospital.
OBJECTIVE: To explore parents experiences following receipt of positive newborn screening for sickle cell disease (SCD) test results at a teaching hospital in Ghana. METHODS: Using purposive sampling, data were collected using semi-structured individual guides to interview parents of children attending the Paediatric SCD clinic at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital (KBTH), a major referral health facility in Ghana. Questions were categorized into 3 main areas: parents' reactions to initial positive results, parents' responses to in-clinic counselling, and parents' attitudes towards follow-up clinic care. The Socio-Ecological Model of Health was used to underpin this study. Interviews were conducted face-to-face either in English or a local dialect (Twi), after which they were transcribed verbatim. Data were analyzed using NVivo software and Microsoft Word to identify relevant codes, which were then organized into themes and sub-themes. RESULTS: Twenty-four mothers and one father were interviewed between 2nd November 2021 and 28th January 2022. The ages of their children ranged from 7 months to 3 years 9 months. Seventeen (68%) of the parents were married, 5 (20%) had more than one child enrolled in the clinic, and 10 (40%) reported that they or their partners had SCD. The 7 themes identified were: (i) emotional response after disclosure, (ii) decision to share results, (iii) care and management of newborns at home, (iv) knowledge of genetics of SCD, (v) adherence to routine follow-up, (vi) cost, and (vii) Culture. Positive test results elicited worry, surprise, or shock in the majority, especially those with no previous knowledge of or experience with SCD. Most parents had received counselling and educational information on caring for their positive SCD children at home and the danger signs of SCD. The decision to share test results with others was influenced by fear of stigmatization. While desiring to see their children remain healthy, parents defaulted on clinic visits due to financial difficulties and the COVID-19 pandemic. CONCLUSION: Knowledge of SCD and personal experience influenced parents' reaction to initial positive newborn screening for SCD test results. Culture and Cost were structural barriers to care. There is a need for more education about SCD among the general population and institutions, and there is a need to provide psychological and socioeconomic support for families attending the KBTH clinic.

Barriers to prevention and healthcare-seeking in a fragile humanitarian setting: Evidence from Yemen during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The healthcare system in Yemen is confronted with substantial challenges, especially during pandemics such as COVID-19. In Aden, the COVID-19 pandemic occurred in the context of prolonged conflict, health-system fragility, resource constraints and other ongoing humanitarian challenges.This study aims to explore the barriers community members in Aden face in adopting COVID-19 preventive measures and seeking healthcare during the pandemic, and to identify implications for future outbreak preparedness in fragile humanitarian settings. A qualitative study involving 25 in-depth interviews was conducted with adult community members in Aden. Participants' perceptions of COVID-19 and reported preventive practices were also explored to contextualise the barriers influencing prevention and healthcare-seeking. Interview data were analysed using inductive qualitative content analysis; the Socio-Ecological Model (SEM) was applied as an interpretive framework to contextualise barriers across five interacting levels: intrapersonal/individual, interpersonal, organisational/institutional, community, and public policy/structural. Participants described barriers across five SEM levels: intrapersonal/individual barriers included denial, fear, perceived ineffectiveness of preventive measures and financial constraints; interpersonal barriers included stigma, mockery and social pressure; organisational/institutional barriers included perceived service refusal, concerns about infection prevention and staff preparedness, long waiting times, limited diagnostic testing, increased treatment costs and shortages of medical supplies; community-level barriers included rumours, misinformation and mistrust; and public policy/structural barriers included limited financial support, inadequate implementation of preventive measures, conflict-related constraints and perceived insufficient preparedness. The findings suggest that barriers to prevention and healthcare-seeking were interconnected across the five levels of the socio-ecological context, with individual perceptions and behaviours occurring within interpersonal, organisational, community and wider public policy and structural conditions. Future outbreak preparedness in fragile settings should therefore combine trusted, culturally appropriate risk communication, community engagement, accessible preventive resources, strengthened infection-prevention capacity, diagnostic and referral pathways, and continuity of essential health services.
