Evaluation of pre-Omicron population immunity for SARS-CoV-2 in the Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation (HIVE) cohort.
BACKGROUND: Continued serosurvey for SARS-CoV-2 population immunity is critical for vaccine strain selection and identification of susceptible groups such as young children. We aim to evaluate the use of a high-throughput, low-volume assay to describe strain-specific IgG measurement in a longitudinally followed community based cohort. METHODS: The longitudinal Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation study has observed around 300 households annually for acute respiratory illness. SARS-CoV-2 variant-specific IgG (including original, Delta, Beta, and Omicron variants) concentrations were measured using multiplex electrochemiluminescence (ECL), pseudoviral neutralization (PN), and ACE2 inhibition assays in participants who had serum samples drawn between July 1 and December 31, 2021. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient assessed correlation within and between ECL, ACE2, and PN assays. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated the performance of ECL and ACE2 assays. Generalized additive mixed models estimated population immunity by age against SARS-CoV-2 variants. RESULTS: A total of 156 serum samples from 117 participants were selected for this study. Most (65.8%) were from adults and a majority (77.8%) received vaccination during the analysis period. High correlations were observed within ECL IgG assays (0.95-1.00), within ACE2 inhibition assays (0.70-0.99), and between assay platforms, including ECL versus PN (0.81-0.83) and ACE2 versus PN (0.88-0.95). ROC analysis demonstrated strong discrimination of vaccination status by ECL IgG assays (AUC: 0.84-0.88; sensitivity: 0.88-0.91; specificity: 0.87-0.88). ACE2 inhibition assays showed more variable performance (AUC: 0.53-0.96; sensitivity: 0.17-0.93; specificity: 0.91-1.00), with lower performance observed for some BA.2-related antigens. SARS-CoV-2 IgG concentrations generally increased with age and appeared to plateau in early adulthood, although estimates were imprecise in younger age groups because of small sample sizes. CONCLUSION: We found a high correlation between ECL, ACE2, and PN across variants. Age-specific IgG quantities reflected behavior and infection histories collected by active surveillance.

Measuring destination image dissonance: A compositional data analysis of cross-media representations in Sanya's Tourism.
This study examines Sanya's tourism image disparities across cognitive, spatial, and affective dimensions in Press Generated Content (PGC), Tourist Generated Content (TGC), and Official Generated Content (OGC) (2013-2022), comparing pre-pandemic (2013-2019) and COVID-19 (2020-2022) periods. Results show: cognitive consistency in "tourism/hotels" but TGC focusing on "coastal + food" vs. PGC/OGC emphasizing policy elements; spatial misalignment between policy-driven spaces and tourists' preferred spaces, revealing a systematic dissonance between institutional promotion and on-the-ground practices; affective dominance of "enjoyment/romance" but TGC expressing unmet needs and OGC suppressing negatives. Systematic cognitive divergence exists between official and tourist narratives. The Aitchison distance measuring this divergence jumps from 19.574 in the pre-pandemic phase (2013-2019) to 40.648 during the pandemic-impacted phase (2020-2022), demonstrating that structural gaps between the two narrative systems become more pronounced amid the public health crisis. Targeted strategies are accordingly proposed to narrow such narrative discrepancies.

Global Age-Shift and Growing Inequities in the Idiopathic Epilepsy Burden Among Children and Adolescents (0-19 Years), 1990-2050.
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic epilepsy (IE) remains a leading cause of neurological disability in the pediatric and adolescent population. While global mortality has declined, the evolving structural distribution of the disease burden and the potential impact of external shocks like the COVID-19 pandemic remain poorly quantified. We aimed to assess the global, regional, and national burden of IE among individuals aged 0-19 years from 1990 to 2021 and project trajectories through 2050. METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2021, we analyzed incidence, prevalence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for IE across 204 countries and territories. Temporal trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression to estimate Average Annual Percent Changes (AAPC). We employed bivariate spatial analysis to intersect IE burden with COVID-19 intensity, and quantified health inequalities using the Slope Index of Inequality (SII) and Concentration Index. Future projections were generated via Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort (BAPC) models. RESULTS: In 2021, the global age-standardized prevalence of IE reached 321.41 per 100,000, representing an 8.03% increase since 1990 (AAPC = 0.25%; 95% CI: 0.07%-0.43%). While age-standardized death rates decreased by 21.67% and DALY rates fell by 15.57%, global incidence rose slightly. A shift in the demographic distribution of the disease burden was observed: the primary burden migrated from the <5 age group in 1990 to the 15-19 age group in 2021, likely driven by declining early-childhood mortality. Bivariate spatial analysis identified 29 countries exhibiting geographic overlap between high baseline IE endemicity and intense COVID-19 impact. Inequality indices (SII and Concentration Index) confirmed a progressive consolidation of health loss within low socio-demographic index (SDI) regions. By 2050, despite projected declines in rates, absolute DALY counts are expected to remain high in low-resource settings due to demographic momentum. CONCLUSIONS: The global IE landscape among the 0-19 population has transitioned into a "post-mortality" phase, characterized by improved survival but expanding chronic disability, particularly among late adolescents (15-19 years). The disproportionate burden in low-SDI regions and the systemic vulnerabilities highlighted during the COVID-19 pandemic necessitate a paradigm shift from acute intervention to longitudinal, age-specific care and the urgent closure of the global "treatment gap."

Scaling of SARS-CoV-2 Genomic Divergence with Cumulative COVID-19 Infections.
The rate at which viral lineages accumulate genetic divergence is central to understanding pathogen evolution, yet direct empirical measurements are limited. The COVID-19 pandemic, through the combination of pandemic-scale replication and dense genomic surveillance, offers an opportunity to calibrate this relationship directly. Unlike previous analyses that use time as the independent variable, this study uses cumulative infections, providing an epidemiological clock calibrated in units of replication opportunity that is not confounded by variation in transmission intensity. A total of 1279 SARS-CoV-2 genomes from the Nextstrain open dataset, sampled between February 2020 and February 2023, were paired with contemporaneous estimates of cumulative global infections from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) to model genomic divergence from Wuhan-Hu-1 as a function of cumulative infections. Divergence increased sublinearly across roughly 14 billion infections over three years, with the most diverged circulating genomes accumulating only about 120 substitutions relative to Wuhan-Hu-1. Extrapolating the fitted relationships, generating the roughly 1000 substitutions that separate SARS-CoV-2 from its closest known sarbecovirus relatives would require on the order of 100-300 billion human infection-equivalents. These requirements would increase substantially in wildlife reservoir hosts, where viral replication per infection is orders of magnitude lower. Conservative estimates of the replication opportunity available in Rhinolophus bat populations imply that the common ancestor of SARS-CoV-2 and its nearest sequenced relatives predates modern virological surveillance by roughly a century. More realistic estimates raise this estimate to millennia, suggesting the closest known relatives of SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 cannot have served as their progenitors.

Methadone Treatment Practice in a Changing Landscape: Limited Early Adoption of the Federal Final Rule Among U.S. Opioid Treatment Programs.
BACKGROUND: U.S. COVID-era methadone treatment flexibilities were made permanent through the federal "Final Rule." This study reports opioid treatment program (OTP) early adoption of expanded telehealth services and flexible dosing between the Final Rule's effective and compliance dates (April 2 and October 2, 2024). METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from June 21 to August 14, 2024, among a national convenience sample of 154 OTP administrators. Measures included Final Rule-allowed telehealth services, flexible dosing and clinic dosing requirements. Covariates included rurality, clinic type, state law expanding or limiting methadone access, and whether the clinic was in a county with an opioid overdose death rate exceeding the national median. RESULTS: Forty-four OTP administrators from 21 states completed surveys. Most (90.9%) offered COVID-era telehealth counseling, however expanded telehealth services were limited such as allowing initial health assessments (36.4%), health examinations by telehealth with medication pickup (22.7%), and initial medical examinations via telehealth (15.9%). Clinics required that 52.9% their patients complete daily in-clinic dosing. Multiday "take home" dosing options offered by clinics to over half their patients included 7-days of take-home doses during the first 14 treatment days (18.2% of clinics), 14-days of take-home doses after 15 days of treatment (18.2%), and 28 days of take-home doses after 30 days of treatment (15.9%). CONCLUSIONS: Evidence of early adoption of the 2024 federal Final Rule (42 CFR §8) was not observed among most opioid treatment programs in this sample.

Safety and immunogenicity of a first-generation modified vaccinia virus Ankara-vectored SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate with mRNA-based booster vaccination: A phase 1 trial.
The rapid development of effective COVID-19 vaccines was enabled by the parallel assessment of multiple candidates early in the pandemic, including candidates based on the Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara (MVA) vector platform. This Phase 1 trial (NCT04569383) evaluated the MVA-based vaccine candidate MVA-SARS-2-S, expressing the full-length native SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (Wuhan-HU-1). Between October 2020 and May 2021, 30 healthy, SARS-CoV-2-naive adults received two doses of either 107 or 108 international units (IU) of MVA-SARS-2-S 28 days apart, with 6-month follow-up. A subgroup (n = 12) received two BNT162b2 booster vaccinations. Safety and reactogenicity were primary objectives; secondary and exploratory objectives included S1 seroconversion rates, S-domain-specific antibodies, SARS-CoV-2-neutralizing antibodies, and spike-specific T cell responses. MVA-SARS-2-S demonstrated a good safety profile. No severe or serious adverse events occurred. Immunogenicity was poor: S1-specific seroconversion occurred in 0/15 (107 IU group) and 3/15 (108 IU group) participants. Binding antibodies were predominantly directed against the S2 subunit, with peak median anti-S2 fold changes of 6.0 and 5.2 in the 107 IU and 108 IU groups, respectively. Neutralizing antibodies were detected in one participant (108 IU group); spike-specific T cell responses were observed in 5/15 (107 IU group) and 2/13 (108 IU group) participants. Heterologous BNT162b2 vaccination induced S1 seroconversion and detectable neutralizing antibody and T cell responses in all boosted participants, without safety concerns. In conclusion, while MVA-SARS-2-S was well tolerated and did not adversely affect subsequent BNT162b2 boosting, the vaccine candidate elicited insufficient immunogenicity, underscoring the need for optimized antigen design.

Herpes zoster epidemiology during and after the COVID-19 pandemic: A 5-year retrospective study from primary care in Poland.
BACKGROUND: Herpes zoster (HZ) is caused by reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus and affects 25-30% of individuals, with the highest incidence in adults aged ≥50 years and a lifetime risk exceeding 50% after the age of 85. Its most common complication is postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), i.e., persistent neuropathic pain. Reports of increased HZ incidence during or after SARS-CoV-2 infection suggest potential epidemiological associations requiring further investigation. OBJECTIVES: Our goals were to evaluate the incidence of HZ and its complications during the pandemic and the post-pandemic period in primary care settings in Poland. MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter study in 20 primary care clinics in Poland, covering 43,949-81,091 patients from 2020 to 2024. Incident HZ cases and complications (PHN, herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO), HZ oticus, and disseminated HZ) were identified, and demographic data, including place of residence, were collected. Statistical analyses included χ2 or Fisher's exact tests, Student's t-tests or nonparametric equivalents, odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs), and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis to assess age-related risk of prolonged symptoms. RESULTS: A total of 570 HZ cases were recorded from 2020 to 2024. Incidence ranged from 1.61 to 2.14 per 1,000 persons and increased with age, reaching 6.57 per 1,000 in individuals aged ≥80 years. Patients aged ≥71 years had higher odds of developing PHN (pain persisting for >90 days) than younger patients (OR = 4.47; 95% CI: 2.30-8.67; p < 0.001). Older adults were also more likely to develop HZO (p = 0.001). Rural incidence was significantly lower during the pandemic than in the post-pandemic period (p = 0.005), with no significant differences in urban or semi-urban areas. CONCLUSIONS: The risk of HZ, PHN, and HZO rises with age. During the pandemic (2020-2021), rural incidence was significantly lower than in the post-pandemic period (2022-2024). The study provides updated data on HZ epidemiology in Poland and highlights the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on healthcare access and HZ reporting in rural areas.

Association between COVID-19 vaccination, SARS-CoV-2 infection, and oral lichen planus (OLP) flares: Results from a patient survey.
BACKGROUND: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic immune-mediated mucocutaneous disease. During the COVID-19 pandemic, new cases and flares of OLP were reported after SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination. Immune activation and cytokine release triggered by infection or vaccines are proposed mechanisms, although current evidence is limited. Clarifying this relationship is important for improving patient counseling and management during vaccination efforts. OBJECTIVES: The study aimed to explore the association with an increased occurrence of OLP flares following COVID-19 vaccination or infection. MATERIAL AND METHODS: An 11-question survey was distributed to OLP patients. The questionnaire aimed to inquire about the history of COVID-19 vaccination and infection as it related to subjective flares of OLP (oral redness, ulcerations, pain, or discomfort). Associations with complications were assessed with Fisher's exact or Wilcoxon tests. RESULTS: Seventy-six patients participated in the survey. Twenty percent of study participants reported experiencing a flare after COVID-19 vaccination (n = 13), and 33% after an infection (n = 13). Self-reported OLP flares were significantly associated with whether or not participants also reported vaccine side effects (p = 0.005). Among the 27 participants who reported experiencing systemic post-vaccination side effects (tiredness, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, nausea), 37% (n = 10) also reported an OLP flare compared with 8% (n = 3) of the 38 who did not report systemic side effects from the COVID-19 vaccination. Of the 63 participants who received a 2nd vaccine dose, 21% (n = 13) reported experiencing an OLP flare. Experiencing systemic side effects following the 2nd vaccination was again significantly associated with reporting an OLP flare (p = 0.048). CONCLUSIONS: Overall, OLP flares were not reported at high rates with COVID-19 vaccination or infection. Within these limitations, the findings of the study suggest that participants who experience systemic side effects following a COVID-19 vaccine may be more susceptible to OLP flares. Experiencing an OLP flare following the 1st COVID-19 vaccination was significantly associated with experiencing a flare again after receiving the 2nd vaccination.

Telehealth-related education and training: a systematic review of recent developments since the COVID-19 pandemic.
The pandemic showed the potential of existing telehealth to increase healthcare access but also the need for healthcare workers to be competent and skilled in delivering care through this modality. We undertook a systematic literature review to identify telehealth-related courses developed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and summarised study characteristics, learning objectives, and course content. Articles describing telehealth-related training and education programs implemented between 2020 and 2024 were included. Papers were required to list specific program content or learning objectives for any educational level or type of health professional. Two authors independently extracted data. Quality of articles was assessed against the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines. Quantitative data was summarised and reported using frequencies and percentages, learning objectives were mapped across the six Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) telehealth competency domains, and qualitative categories were thematically synthesised. Of 7547 articles identified, 51 were included. Most courses were implemented in the USA (82%), mostly targeted to undergraduate students (51%), and the number of articles per year increased over time. Most courses were developed by universities (53%), sometimes in collaboration with health services, and content was primarily applicable across multiple specialties. Participants nearly always evaluated the courses (90%). Content included basic knowledge and skills in telehealth, patient safety, and ethics, with learning objectives often on technology and communication. Only four programs included all AAMC telehealth competencies. This review highlights that telehealth education and training has expanded since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, however, current curricula are lacking experiential learning. Courses generally covered telehealth communication competencies in detail, but more content on the ethical and legal requirements, billing, physical examination, patient education, and eligibility for telehealth is required. For efficient resource use, standardised training can be applied across disciplines with addition of site or speciality-specific modules.

Virtual Care Trends in Older Adults with Parkinson's Disease in Urban and Rural Ontario, Canada, During COVID-19.
BACKGROUND: Virtual care services increased during the COVID-19 pandemic, enabling access to physician consultations. Most studies on virtual care in Parkinson's disease (PD) have focused on tertiary centers, limiting generalizability. OBJECTIVE: To describe trends in virtual care use over time in people living with PD in Ontario, Canada, by rural and urban region of residence using health administrative data. METHODS: We conducted a population-based repeated cross-sectional study between March 2020 and August 2023, among community-dwelling people living with PD aged ≥66 years in Ontario, Canada. We used Poisson regression models with generalized estimating equations to estimate rate ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) comparing virtual visit rates in urban versus rural areas across physician specialties (family physicians, neurologists and psychiatrists/geriatricians). RESULTS: Among 24,736 people living with PD in March 2020, 58.6% were male (mean age 77.6 [SD = 7.0] years), and most resided in urban areas (89.9%). Compared to urban residents, rural residents had significantly lower rates of virtual visits to neurologists (adjusted RR = 0.93; 95% CI: 0.90-0.96), family physicians (aRR = 0.73; 95% CI: 0.70-0.77) and geriatricians/psychiatrists (aRR = 0.67; 95% CI: 0.65-0.77). Over 3.5 years, virtual visits declined compared to the first 6 months for neurologists (aRR = 0.23; 95% CI: 0.22-0.25), family physicians (aRR = 0.39; 95% CI: 0.38-0.41) and geriatricians/psychiatrists (aRR = 0.45; 95% CI: 0.40-0.51). CONCLUSION: People living with PD in urban centers accessed virtual care more frequently than those living rurally. Virtual care utilization decreased over time. The sustainability of virtual care and its impact on health equity among people living with PD requires further study.

Establishing influenza epidemic thresholds and intensity levels in Türkiye using the moving epidemic method and assessing concordance with WHO transmission zones: A sentinel surveillance analysis of ten seasons, 2013-2025.
The Moving Epidemic Method (MEM) is the ECDC/WHO-Europe-endorsed approach for establishing influenza epidemic thresholds and intensity levels, yet no positivity-based MEM analysis exists for Türkiye or any country in the WHO Western Asia transmission zone. Weekly influenza positivity rates from FluNet sentinel surveillance were analysed for ten of twelve seasons (2013/2014-2024/2025, excluding two COVID-19 pandemic seasons) using the mem R package with cross-validated optimized slope parameter, and Türkiye's average epidemic curve and thresholds were compared with the Western Asia (excluding Türkiye) and South West Europe zones using Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), root mean square deviation (RMSD) and complementary correlation metrics. The epidemic threshold was 10.59% positivity, with intensity thresholds at 42.56% (medium), 60.92% (high), and 71.38% (very high); cross-validated sensitivity was 0.77, specificity 0.88, and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.65. Türkiye's average curve showed higher concordance with Western Asia (CCC=0.890; RMSD=4.22 percentage points) than South West Europe (CCC=0.672; RMSD=12.48) despite similar Pearson correlations (0.922 vs. 0.939), and the Western Asia epidemic threshold (11.50%) closely matched Türkiye's. These first operational MEM thresholds for Türkiye and the first positivity-based thresholds for the Western Asia zone confirm alignment with the current WHO transmission zone classification and support integration into routine surveillance.

Ethnic inequities in mathematical models for respiratory infectious disease: A systematic review.
COVID-19 was the most recent pandemic to highlight profound ethnic inequities. However, most mathematical epidemiological models do not adequately represent these inequities, limiting the potential for such models to inform equitable public health responses and interventions. This systematic review identifies mathematical models of infectious respiratory disease transmission that report results by ethnic group and surveys the different mathematical modelling approaches used to attempt to capture ethnicity-related outcomes. Only 28 studies met the inclusion criteria, which is rare relative to the volume of infectious disease modelling literature. The most common model frameworks were compartmental models (11 studies), individual-based models (12 studies), and metapopulation models (5 studies). Across these studies, ethnic heterogeneities were represented directly by incorporating some combination of ethnic group population demographics, ethnicity-specific interaction patterns, and ethnicity-specific disease parameters, or indirectly through spatial differences in interaction patterns or disease transmission. Consideration of ethnicity in mathematical models of disease transmission is in its infancy, with only three of the studies published before 2020, but it has the potential to provide improved evidence for public health action that reduces the epidemic burden and inequities across ethnic groups.

Eating Disorders as a Public Health Challenge: A Case Study of Inclusive, Systems-Oriented Treatment in the US Southeast.
Eating disorders in the United States have increased substantially over the past 2 decades, with additional exacerbation during the COVID-19 pandemic. These conditions disproportionately affect adolescents, young adults, and sexual and gender minority (SGM) populations, reflecting the influence of stigma, discrimination, and broader social determinants of health. Given their complexity, high comorbidity, and elevated mortality risk, eating disorders represent a significant public health concern requiring a continuum of care that spans outpatient, partial hospitalization, residential, and inpatient treatment settings. Emerging evidence underscores the importance of trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and affirming approaches in improving engagement and outcomes for SGM individuals, who often encounter barriers to inclusive and competent care. This case study examines NewCircle at Hanover, a recently established eating disorder treatment center in Birmingham, Alabama, that operationalizes an intersectional, SGM-affirming model of care across multiple levels of service. The program integrates evidence-based clinical interventions with intentionally designed organizational structures, physical environments, and expressive therapies to support whole-person recovery. Attention is given to how governance, facility design, and clinical programming intersect to shape treatment engagement, continuity of care, and client experience.

Age-specific COVID-19 case dynamics during school closure periods: Evidence from 12 european countries.
School closures were among the most widely adopted non-pharmaceutical interventions against COVID-19, yet evidence on their association with infection dynamics remains uncertain given their substantial economic and educational costs. This observational study describes age-specific COVID-19 case dynamics during school closure periods across 12 European countries using Generalised Additive Models with zero-crossing derivative analysis and Transfer Entropy. Case dynamics were heterogeneous and non-monotonic across age groups: case counts declined early but rose again within the window among the youngest cohorts (0-4 and 5-9 years). By contrast, the 10-14 group rose steadily with no turning point, and older adolescents and young adults (15-19 and 20-24 years) rose early and then declined. Transfer Entropy analysis, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, revealed asymmetric directional relationship between age cohorts that varied across national contexts. These patterns indicate that case trajectories during closure periods were not uniform across youth age groups, with no age group showing a sustained, uninterrupted decline. Interpreted cautiously, they raise questions about the cost-benefit balance of blanket closure policies when weighed against their documented economic, educational, and distributional costs, and motivate more targeted, age-sensitive quasi-experimental evaluation for future pandemic preparedness.

Impact of Dimethyl Sulfoxide on Early Cardiotoxicity After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
UNLABELLED: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of cryopreserved grafts in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) increased substantially. Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), used as a cryoprotective agent, is well recognized for its infusion-related toxicity; however, its impact on cardiac function remains unclear. METHODS: This prospective study included 96 consecutive patients (median age 46 years) undergoing allogeneic HSCT. Patients were divided according to graft type into cryopreserved (n = 59, 61.5%) and non-cryopreserved (n = 37, 38.5%) groups. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment was performed before and after transplantation. RESULTS: Significant changes were observed in diastolic parameters (E/A, and E/E'), structural parameters (left ventricular mass and left ventricular mass index), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and right ventricular ejection fraction following HSCT. In the cryopreserved group, E/A ratio decreased below the normal range and E/E' ratio increased significantly, whereas no such changes were observed in the non-cryopreserved group. During the 30-day follow-up period, symptomatic cardiovascular toxicity occurred in 5 patients (5.2%), while subclinical cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction was detected in 16 patients (16.7%). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that GLS predicted cardiotoxicity with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88 (95% CI, 0.79-0.98; p < 0.0001). At a cut-off value of - 16.8%, sensitivity was 100% and specificity was 79%. CONCLUSION: Cryopreserved graft administration may be associated with early alterations in left ventricular diastolic function, potentially reflecting DMSO-related cardiotoxicity. GLS appears to be a sensitive marker for the early detection and prediction of cardiotoxicity in patients undergoing allogeneic HSCT.

Dynamic Bronchoscopic Evolution of a Cobblestone-like Appearance in COVID-19-associated Pulmonary Aspergillosis: A Case Report.
Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (CAPA) is associated with high mortality and diagnostic difficulties. We report a fatal case of CAPA with a distinctive cobblestone-like tracheobronchial appearance observed during bronchoscopy. A patient receiving maintenance hemodialysis for chronic kidney disease was admitted with severe COVID-19. Bronchoscopy revealed multiple white tracheobronchial plaques, suggestive of an invasive Aspergillus infection. Despite antifungal therapy, respiratory failure progressed, and repeat bronchoscopy revealed worsening cobblestone-like lesions. The patient died despite receiving intensive treatment. Autopsy confirmed Aspergillus hyphal invasion, corresponding to the bronchoscopic findings, highlighting a rare but diagnostically important airway manifestation of CAPA.

Sputum and oral microbiota profiles are associated with long COVID severity and phenotype post-hospitalisation: a UK multicentre, prospective cohort study.
BACKGROUND: Acute COVID-19 alters the airway microbiota. Whether these changes persist post-COVID-19 and contribute to long COVID is unknown. We aimed to describe the microbiota by long COVID severity and subtype, and identify links with inflammation. METHODS: Adults were prospectively recruited to the longitudinal UK Post-hospitalisation COVID-19 study (PHOSP-COVID). Patients were grouped by previously described "severity clusters" (of ongoing health impairments) and symptom subgroups. Oral and sputum microbiota (at 6 months post-discharge) were characterised through 16S ribosomal RNA gene amplicon sequencing, and microbiota diversity was assessed. Co-occurrence network analysis identified keystone taxa. Associations between keystone taxa and plasma inflammatory proteins were assessed through Spearman's rank correlations. RESULTS: 771 participants had their microbiota assessed. Of participants with oral rinses and "severity cluster" assignment (mean age 57.5 years), 278 out of 722 (38.5%) were women. The "very severe" cluster, in which disease was predominantly pulmonary in nature, was associated with a distinct microbiota profile post-COVID-19. Reduced lung function was associated with a distinct oral microbiota profile. Persistent neurocognitive symptoms were associated with a distinct oral microbiota profile, while gastrointestinal symptoms were associated with a distinct sputum microbiota profile. Microbiota keystone taxa shifted to a higher prevalence of lactic acid bacteria associated with worse health outcomes. Lactic acid bacteria abundance was associated with elevated blood inflammatory proteins. CONCLUSION: Distinct oral and sputum microbiota profiles were associated with pulmonary function and with neurocognitive and gastrointestinal symptoms in long COVID. Shifts in keystone microbiota taxa linked with inflammation, based on worse health outcomes, suggest a potential role change for lactic acid bacteria, which may be associated with the host immune response.

Zika virus serologic responses during pregnancy in a dengue-endemic setting: A prospective cohort study in Thailand.
BACKGROUND: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection during pregnancy has been associated with adverse birth outcomes, including severe neurological abnormalities. Confirmation of infection remains challenging due to the disease's predominantly asymptomatic or mild nature. While real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) is the gold standard, its use in clinical settings and surveillance is limited. Serological point-of-care tests offer alternatives but pose interpretation challenges in Flavivirus-endemic regions. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a prospective cohort of 199 pregnant women attending the antenatal clinic at Rajavithi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand, in 2021-2022 to describe the incidence of ZIKV serologic responses detected by a rapid test and associated pregnancy outcomes. Participants were monitored using the DPP ZCD IgM/IgG (Zika/Chikungunya/Dengue IgM/IgG) System rapid immunochromatography test (Chembio), with RT-qPCR and plaque reduction neutralization testing performed for further assessment. A ZIKV serologic response was defined as a reactive ZIKV immunoglobulin M (IgM) result at enrollment or seroconversion from non-reactive to reactive ZIKV IgM or IgG between study visits. The DPP ZCD rapid test revealed incident ZIKV-reactive serologic responses at 15.4 per 100 person-years, with all affected participants being asymptomatic. All RT-qPCR results were negative, and participants with ZIKV IgG seroconversion had neutralizing antibodies against ZIKV and all 4 Dengue virus (DENV) serotypes. A prior history of DENV infection was associated with increased odds of ZIKV-reactive serologic response (OR 3.53, P value 0.046). CONCLUSION: This prospective study identified serologic responses detected by a ZIKV-reactive rapid test among pregnant women in Thailand. In a highly dengue-immune setting, these responses could reflect true ZIKV exposure, DENV reinfection, flavivirus immune boosting, or serologic cross-reactivity, and therefore cannot be attributed specifically to ZIKV. Rapid serologic testing may support screening and surveillance but cannot establish ZIKV infection or ZIKV-specific exposure without careful interpretation and additional testing.

Entomological investigations into yellow fever outbreak in northern Ghana.
Arboviruses are pathogens of emerging/re-emerging infectious diseases. Half the world's population is at risk. Recent African epidemics confirmed 19,569 cases with 820 deaths. In Ghana, Savannah Region had yellow fever (YF) outbreak in 2021. Reports revealed 35 deaths, 202 suspected cases (case fatality rate (CFR) = 17%), and 70 confirmed cases (CFR = 50%). This paper presents YF outbreak entomological investigations findings. A team with expertise in YF outbreak response were assembled and tasked to assess, contain and/or control the rapid spread of YF. Immature Aedes aegypti were collected in/around houses, and adult sampled using BG-Sentinel traps, oral aspirators and Prokopack. The chikungunya, dengue fever, YF, and Zika viruses screening using real time reverse-transcription PCR (detection limit <10 RNA copies/reaction) followed mosquitoes morphological identification. Breeding containers (12,264) were examined. Larvae (3,885) and pupae (1,186) were obtained from 173 containers (positivity rate = 1.26%). Larvae were identified with short and stout siphons. Pupae had short but distinct serrated spicules on paddle fringe and branched/fanlike (6-7 branches) seta 9-VIII. Out of 1,001 houses surveyed, 130 were positive for larvae/pupae (positivity rate = 12.99%). Receptacles included plastic [46.95% (6,529)], metallic [43.32% (6,024)], clay jar [5.42% (753)], tire [4.06% (565)], and well [0.24% (34)]. WHO larval indices thresholds (BI, CI, HI, and PDI) were used to assess risk. Exactly 1,571 adults were identified [Aedes aegypti aegypti (35), Aedes aegypti formosus (619), and Culex sp. (917)]. Outdoor collection were higher (86.4%) than indoors (13.6%). No arboviruses were detected. Generally, vector indices/densities suggested high-risk arbovirus transmission although vectors were not arbovirus positive. Aedes aegypti formosus was dominant. They are bridge vectors maintaining sylvatic YF cycles and spillover transmission. High risk for YF poses public health threat that calls for Aedes mosquito surveillance systems and vector control strategies. Ae. ae. formosus might be drivers for outbreak and/or YF transmission.

The Storm We Chose: Bundibugyo Virus, Preparedness Injustice, and the Pathogens We Decline to Fight.
The 2026 Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a species for which, unlike Zaire ebolavirus, no licensed vaccine and no approved therapeutic exist. This commentary argues that this absence is not a misfortune of virology but a structurally produced injustice. Bundibugyo virus has been characterised since 2008, has caused lethal outbreaks, and was foreseeably capable of recurrence; more importantly, species-specific and cross-protective countermeasures were scientifically tractable more than a decade before, yet none reached licensure or field readiness. A recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus vaccine expressing the Bundibugyo glycoprotein - built on the same platform as the licensed Zaire vaccine - conferred complete protection in nonhuman primates in 2013; thirteen years later, no clinical-grade material existed when the outbreak began. The gap, we argue, lay not in what science could build but in what the system chose to finish, because preparedness investment concentrated on the species that threatened wealthier and more connected populations. Drawing on the framework of structural injustice and on the authors' prior field experience of concurrent epidemics in the DRC, we distinguish tragic scarcity from produced scarcity, answer the feasibility objection, and argue that closing the gap is an obligation rather than a charity.

Deciphering dengue fever transmission on higher-order networks.
Dengue fever is a viral infection transmitted to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes. Modeling dengue transmission is crucial for control, given its risk to half the world's population. This paper develops a host-to-host transmission model within hypergraphs constructed from simplicial complexes. Necessary conditions for the emergence of Turing instability in dengue dynamical systems naturally coupled on hypergraphs are derived. Furthermore, a multiplex network framework is constructed on hypergraphs by incorporating the influence of information on dengue transmission, and expressions for dengue outbreak thresholds are derived. Theoretical results are verified through numerical simulations. The Turing instability phenomenon in higher-order networks is investigated, while periodic diffusion effects are analyzed. Higher-order networks elevate the thresholds for dengue outbreaks within the multiplex network framework. Finally, to link theory with practice, we employ Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to fit and predict dengue case data. By embedding the transmission model as physical constraints and constructing hypergraphs informed by geographical adjacency and tourism mobility, the PINNs achieves interpretable predictions and accurate parameter estimation. This study offers a feasible framework for understanding and predicting dengue transmission in complex real-world environments.

Adaptation of Bayesian decision analysis for clinical trial design to binary outcomes: illustration for Ebola virus disease treatment.
When designing trials for high-mortality diseases with limited therapies, the conventional 5% type I error rate (α) may be unsuitable. A higher α could benefit seriously ill patients lacking therapeutic alternatives. Bayesian decision analysis (BDA) integrates multiple health consequences into trial design. We extend BDA for trials with binary outcomes to calculate optimal sample sizes (n) and α in an Ebola outbreak context. We consider fixed, two-arm randomized trials with binary outcomes and two types of clinical trial losses: post-trial loss, for not approving an effective treatment or approving an ineffective one; in-trial loss, for not administrating an effective treatment to control-arm patients or for administrating an ineffective treatment to experimental-arm patients. The model incorporates treatment side effects and disease severity into a single loss function, from which BDA-optimal n and α are derived. Using mortality as the outcome, we modeled various epidemic scenarios by varying target population size, mortality rate, and treatment efficacy. In most cases, BDA-optimal α exceeded the conventional one-sided 2.5% and sample sizes are smaller. Simulations comparing BDA-optimized two-arm trials (fixed/sequential) to conventional designs (two-arm/single-arm, fixed/sequential) across outbreak scenarios show comparable statistical power across designs, except when sample size assumptions are incorrect, or when trials started after the outbreak peak; in these situations, BDA-optimized trials show superior powers. This BDA framework provides a promising approach for designing trials with binary outcomes, particularly in high-mortality disease outbreaks, where declining case numbers and uncertain mortality and efficacy data challenge conventional methods.

Clesrovimab in the new era of RSV prevention: one season, one dose, one chance.
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization in infancy worldwide. Historically, prevention relied on monthly palivizumab administration for selected high-risk infants, despite evidence that a substantial proportion of severe RSV disease occurs in previously healthy term infants. The recent introduction of maternal RSV vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies has transformed the prevention landscape. Clesrovimab (MK-1654; Enflonsia) is a long-acting monoclonal antibody designed to provide season-long protection following a single dose. In the pivotal phase 2b/3 CLEVER trial, clesrovimab reduced RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization among infants entering their first RSV season, with a safety profile comparable to placebo. The absolute risk reduction for RSV hospitalization was approximately 1.9 percentage points, corresponding to an estimated number needed to treat of 51 infants over 150 days of follow-up. In this policy-focused clinical perspective informed by a narrative review, we examine the emerging role of clesrovimab within contemporary RSV prevention strategies. We discuss efficacy, safety, implementation challenges, economic considerations, and remaining evidence gaps, including the absence of head-to-head comparisons with nirsevimab, limited post-licensure data, and uncertainties regarding long-term effectiveness and affordability. Future success will depend not only on efficacy but also on equitable access, sustainable implementation, and ongoing surveillance. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The emergence of long-acting monoclonal antibodies has expanded preventive options for infants at risk of RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease during their first RSV season. For clinicians, the key shift is that RSV prevention is increasingly being considered within a broader population-health framework rather than solely as a risk-based intervention for selected high-risk groups. Clesrovimab, alongside nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination, represents one component of an evolving prevention strategy aimed at reducing RSV-associated morbidity and hospitalization during early infancy. From a practical perspective, successful implementation will depend on timely administration, integration into neonatal discharge planning and well-child care pathways, and coordination with maternal immunization programs. As RSV prevention moves into routine clinical practice, equitable access, sustained coverage, affordability, and ongoing post-licensure surveillance will be as important as efficacy demonstrated in clinical trials. Ultimately, the greatest reductions in RSV-related hospitalization are likely to result from effective delivery of preventive strategies to the infants at highest risk during the RSV season. KEY POINTS: RSV continues to impose a substantial burden on infants worldwide despite decades of clinical recognition and supportive care. Most RSV hospitalizations occur in infants without traditional high-risk conditions, highlighting the limitations of selective prophylaxis strategies. Long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal RSV vaccination have transformed prevention from a niche intervention into a population-level public health strategy. Clesrovimab demonstrated significant protection against RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization in healthy infants entering their first RSV season. Future research should focus on comparative effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, long-term safety, implementation in low-resource settings, and optimization of delivery strategies to maximize population impact.

Klebsiella-dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants.
Rotavirus gastroenteritis is the leading cause of infant diarrheal death worldwide. Oral rotavirus vaccine (RVV) prevents illness and death, but efficacy differs between high- and low-income countries and the etiologies are unclear. Here, we describe the relationship between colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, inflammation, and vaccine response across a cohort of infants from Panama, Peru, and the U.S. Vaccine immunogenicity was related to community composition in the first month of life and inverse to increased relative abundance of Klebsiella. Clustering communities into gut types revealed that microbiome configurations with elevated Klebsiella or Escherichia in the first month of life were negatively associated with both seroconversion and rotavirus shedding after vaccination, suggesting potential inhibition of vaccine function or host response. Infants without RVV strain shedding displayed elevated fecal calprotectin in the first month. These results implicate microbiome-augmented infant gut inflammation as a potential impediment to RVV response.

Rapid Differentiation of Vaccine and Wild-Type Measles Virus During an Ongoing Outbreak using a new molecular assay.
BACKGROUND: Differentiating wild and vaccine measles virus (MeV) strains is critical for appropriate healthcare response during outbreak vaccination campaigns. Sequencing, the current standard, is expensive, time-consuming, and limited to specialized laboratories. We developed and implemented a novel differential MeV RT-qPCR assay to address these challenges, which we describe herein. METHODS: We designed a differential two-step assay; the first step, termed MRRV, distinguishes between rubella, wild MeV, and vaccine MeV. The second, termed "MeV differential", differentiates between genotypes A (vaccine), B and D. RESULTS: The assay detects 10-50 copies per reaction and accurately classifies weak clinical samples (Cq > 32), with 100% accuracy, compared with the N gene sequencing gold standard. Evaluated on over 4,000 clinical samples retrospectively and during the 2025-2026MeV outbreak in Israel, the assay revealed that ∼9% of tested originated from vaccine strain. Among tested municipalities, those running active vaccination campaigns had significantly higher vaccine strain detections (>10 cases each) than those with routine vaccination (1-2 cases). Retrospective analysis of samples from 2018-2024 identified a mix of B and D strains. The novel assay successfully identified double infection cases (exposure to a wild strain shortly before or after vaccination). CONCLUSION: The novel assay proved useful both as a diagnostic tool that enables focused, efficient healthcare response, and as an epidemiological tool that provides valuable information in real-time. This assay is faster, cheaper and more amendable for high throughput testing, compared with the gold-standard sequencing classification.

Monoclonal Antibodies for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Infants and Children: An Updated Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Motivated by the emergence of a long-acting monoclonal antibody (clesrovimab), the availability of data from the complete MELODY trial cohort, and results from a large randomized trial (HARMONIE), we updated our prior network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of monoclonal antibodies for preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants. METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials that examined the efficacy and safety of RSV infection prophylaxis with clesrovimab, motavizumab, nirsevimab, palivizumab, and suptavumab versus one another or placebo or no prophylaxis in infants. We performed a frequentist framework random-effects network meta-analysis and used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessments, Developments and Evaluation (GRADE) approach to assess the certainty of evidence. RESULTS: Eighteen trials enrolling 33,283 infants were included. Clesrovimab (odds ratio [OR] 0.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.02-0.37, moderate certainty), motavizumab (OR 0.12; 95% CI 0.07-0.19, moderate certainty), and nirsevimab (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.11-0.34; moderate certainty) were associated with reductions in the rate of severe respiratory syncytial virus infection. Nirsevimab, motavizumab, clesrovimab, and intramuscular palivizumab were associated with reductions in RSV infection, and several agents were also associated with reduced hospitalization. Motavizumab and nirsevimab, and clesrovimab were associated with reductions in broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes. Motavizumab reduced both mechanical ventilation use and intensive care unit admission. No significant differences were found in all-cause mortality and drug-related or serious adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: This updated network meta-analysis confirmed that the effectiveness and safety of clesrovimab were comparable to those of established monoclonal antibodies. Motavizumab, nirsevimab, and clesrovimab showed benefits for broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes.

Measles Vaccine Uptake During the 2025 Texas Measles Outbreak in a San Antonio Military Medical Center.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate changes in measles-containing vaccine (MCV) uptake, inclusive of MMR and MMRV, by age group and over time during the 2025 Texas measles outbreak. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center, observational study comparing January through August 2024 (pre-outbreak) with the same period in 2025 (outbreak) at a military medical center in San Antonio, TX. The study evaluated MCVs administered and recorded in the electronic health record (EHR) to all patients from 0-18 years enrolled during these periods. The primary outcome was the MCV administration rate (doses per 1,000 child-months). Based on this, we estimated incidence rate ratios (IRR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) comparing 2025 vs 2024 overall and by age groups. RESULTS: MCV administration increased from 10.82 per 1,000 child-months in 2024 to 13.22 per 1,000 child-months in 2025, across all age groups (IRR 1.22; 95% CI, 1.11-1.34; p<0.001). This increase was driven by early-dose vaccination in infants aged 6-11 months (IRR 21.09; 95% CI, 9.89-44.98) and children aged 24-47 months (IRR 4.73; 95% CI, 2.84-7.87). MCV administration rates did not clearly differ among children 12-23 months (IRR 1.08; 95% CI, 0.94-1.24), 4-5 years (IRR 1.07; 95% CI, 0.93-1.23), or 6-18 years (IRR 0.54; 95% CI, 0.28-1.06). Peak vaccine uptake occurred early in the outbreak and then declined toward baseline. CONCLUSIONS: At a military medical center in San Antonio, the 2025 Texas measles outbreak was associated with an early transient increase in MCV uptake principally driven by early infant vaccination, and by late summer, the uptake returned toward baseline.

Single Jaundice in Cirrhosis: A Neglected Acute Decompensation of Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure and Mortality.
OBJECTIVES: To compare the risk of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) and short-term outcomes among cirrhotic patients with single jaundice, acute decompensation (AD) (including ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and/or bacterial infection), and non-AD non-jaundice. METHODS: We analyzed cirrhotic inpatients without obstructive jaundice enrolled from two large multicenter prospective cohorts. Patients were divided at admission into classical AD, single jaundice, or non-AD non-jaundice groups. Baseline characteristics, ACLF development, and short-term outcomes were compared between groups. RESULTS: Among 2645 cirrhotic patients, classical AD, single jaundice, and non-AD non-jaundice were observed in 2163 (81.78%), 267 (10.09%), and 215 (8.13%), respectively. The 90-day liver transplant (LT)-free mortality was comparable between single jaundice patients and classical AD patients (15.09% vs. 17.81%, p = 0.266), but significantly higher than non-AD non-jaundice patients (2.45%; p < 0.01). The prevalence of ACLF (16.10% vs. 16.09%, p = 1.000) and pre-ACLF (9.36% vs. 6.43%, p = 0.094) were comparable between the single jaundice and classical AD groups. Intrahepatic precipitants, particularly hepatitis B flare with hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation (odds ratio [OR] 2.69; p = 0.002), spontaneous hepatitis B flare with high HBV-DNA load (OR 23.75; p < 0.001), superimposed hepatitis A/E virus infection on HBV infection (OR 13.40; p < 0.001) and hepatotoxic drug usage (OR 3.64; p < 0.001) were associated with single jaundice. CONCLUSIONS: Cirrhotic inpatients with single jaundice show comparably high short-term mortality and ACLF risk to those with classical AD. Single jaundice shall be considered as an AD event and is predominantly triggered by intrahepatic insults, warranting surveillance equivalent to classical AD and prioritized management of the precipitants.

Rabies and rabies prophylaxis in Egypt: a nationwide cross-sectional study that calls for action.
BACKGROUND: Rabies is a fatal but preventable viral disease that poses a global health threat, especially in developing countries. Despite the high incidence of animal bites reported annually in Egypt, limited data exist regarding the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of the general population toward rabies and rabies prophylaxis. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional study using a structured interview-based survey targeting individuals aged 18 years or older who attended outpatient clinics at nine university hospitals across Egypt. The survey assessed participants' KAP toward rabies and rabies prophylaxis and identified barriers to prophylaxis uptake. RESULTS: Among 1,777 participants who responded to the survey, only 42.8% (n = 760) had good knowledge about rabies and rabies prophylaxis, while the majority, 88.5% (n = 1,572), exhibited a positive attitude toward rabies prophylaxis. Knowledge was higher among those who reported awareness of rabies campaigns in their geographic areas (69.1% vs. 40.5%, p < 0.001) and those who had previously been bitten or attacked by animals (56.1% vs. 41.3%, p < 0.001). Overall, 9.7% (n = 173) of participants reported a history of animal bites or attacks; however, 18.5% (n = 32) of these participants did not receive post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), and 17% (n = 24) did not complete the vaccine schedule. Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake was low, with only 4.3% (n = 23) of high-risk individuals receiving it. Key barriers to rabies prophylaxis included lack of knowledge about the rabies vaccine, reported by 82.4% of participants, lack of knowledge about rabies, reported by 81.7%, and inadequate hospital facilities, reported by 43.1%. CONCLUSIONS: Despite a generally positive attitude toward rabies prophylaxis, knowledge and adherence to prophylactic measures, including pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis, remain relatively inadequate in Egypt. Public health interventions, such as educational campaigns and improved accessibility to vaccination services, are needed to address these gaps and mitigate the public health burden of rabies.

Low-fitness rpoB mutations in rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis: Host immunity, compensatory evolution, and diagnostic challenges.
BACKGROUND: The rpoB S450L mutation is the most prevalent high-fitness rifampicin resistance-conferring mutation in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. However, numerous alternative rpoB mutations associated with varying fitness costs have been reported, particularly in specific clinical settings. This systematic review critically evaluates the relationship between low-fitness rpoB mutations, host immune status, HIV co-infection, compensatory evolution, and diagnostic discordance. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across multiple scientific databases. Studies reporting genetic, phenotypic, structural, or clinical data on rifampicin-resistant M. tuberculosis carrying alternative or borderline rpoB mutations were included. Data were qualitatively synthesized to examine associations among host immune status, bacterial fitness, compensatory evolution, and diagnostic performance. RESULTS: Twenty-one studies met the inclusion criteria. Available clinical evidence indicated a higher prevalence of low-fitness non-S450L rpoB mutations, particularly at codons 430, 435, 441, and 445, among patients with advanced HIV infection. The available evidence suggests that HIV-associated immunosuppression may reduce host-driven purifying selection, facilitating the persistence of low-fitness resistant variants. Genomic and structural studies identified compensatory mutations in rpoA, rpoB, and rpoC that may partially restore bacterial fitness while maintaining rifampicin resistance. Several borderline rpoB mutations also produced discordant results between molecular assays and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing. CONCLUSION: HIV-associated immunosuppression may influence the evolutionary trajectory of rifampicin-resistant M. tuberculosis by facilitating the persistence of low-fitness rpoB mutations. Integrating molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, and host immune profiling may improve the detection and clinical management of rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis, particularly in regions with a high burden of TB-HIV co-infection.

Legionella Detection in Environmental Water Samples Submitted to the Gyeonggi-do Institute of Health and Environment, 2023-2025: Sample-type Differences and the Increasing Contribution of Cooling-tower Water to Positive Samples.
Objectives: Legionella spp. proliferate in artificial water systems, such as cooling towers and water supply and hot water systems of buildings, causing infection through the inhalation of contaminated aerosols. We analyzed the detection characteristics of Legionella spp. within environmental water samples submitted to the Gyeonggi-do Institute of Health and Environment, the Republic of Korea, to determine management priorities. Methods: We analyzed 9,172 Legionella spp. testing records for environmental water samples received from January 2023 through December 2025, summarized by sample type, purpose, submission route, species, and concentration. Chi-square and Cochran-Armitage trend tests were used. Results: Legionella spp. were detected in 570/9,172 samples (6.21%; 95% confidence interval, 5.74-6.73%). Detection differed significantly by sample type (p 10,000 CFU/L. Conclusions: Bathtub and hot water systems require preventive management given their high detection proportions, whereas cooling towers require surveillance priority given their large and increasing contribution to positives. Priorities should combine sample-type detection rates with the size and trend of positive counts. As cooling-tower testing relies largely on voluntary requests, risk-targeted official testing should complement it.

Outcomes of Healthcare-Associated Infections in Respiratory Intensive Care Unit.
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are the major cause of morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, microbiological profile, resistance patterns, risk factors, and outcomes of HAIs in a respiratory ICU (RICU) of a tertiary care hospital in Nepal. METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in RICU. HAIs were diagnosed according to the CDC criteria. Descriptive statistics were reported as mean (SD) and frequencies. Unpaired t-tests, chi-square tests were used for comparisons, and multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the risk factors. RESULTS: Among 121 ICU admissions, 42 patients developed 50 episodes of HAI, yielding a prevalence of 34.7%. Ventilator-associated pneumonia was the most common HAIs. The most frequently isolated organisms were Acinetobacter baumannii in 42.0% and Klebsiella pneumonia in 18.0%. Both were resistance to Ceftriaxone. Resistance to Piperacillin-tazobactam were 85.8% and 77.8% and to carbapenems were 92% and 90% respectively. Tigecycline resistance was seen in 20% of Acinetobacter isolates and none of the Klebsiella isolates. Sensitivity to Polymyxin B was 100%. Mechanical ventilation, urinary catheters and history of prior hospitalization were the strongest predictors of HAI. Patients who developed HAI had a longer ICU stay (9.5 vs. 5.2 days, p=0.001) and higher mortality (28.6% vs. 13.9%, p=0.04). CONCLUSIONS: HAIs, particularly VAP caused by MDR organisms, were common in our ICU and there was a high resistance to beta lactams and carbapenem antibiotics. Low resistance to tigecycline and polymyxin B warrants careful stewardship.

Antimicrobial resistance trends and lineage distribution among invasive pneumococcal disease isolates pre- and post-pneumococcal conjugate vaccine introduction, South Africa.
OBJECTIVES: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) have reduced antimicrobial-resistant invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) globally. We evaluated trends in antimicrobial-resistant IPD and pneumococcal lineages before and after PCV13 introduction in South Africa. METHODS: We analysed national, laboratory-based IPD surveillance reported cases (2005-2020) and compared the incidence of resistant-IPD pre- and post-PCV introduction. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed for six antibiotics, and penicillin-multidrug resistance (penicillin-MDR) was defined as penicillin nonsusceptibility plus resistance to ≥2 additional antibiotic classes. Whole-genome sequencing was used to determine serotypes, sequence types, global pneumococcal sequence clusters (GPSC), and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants. RESULTS: Following PCV introduction, overall IPD and AMR IPD incidence declined substantially. Penicillin-cotrimoxazole nonsusceptible and penicillin-MDR IPD incidence decreased from 5.6 to 0.8 per 100,000 population (percentage decrease -86.5%, confidence intervals [CI] -90.5% to -81.4%) and 5.5 to 0.4 (-93.0%, -95.7% to -89.1%), respectively, in children <5 years, with smaller but significant reductions in the ≥5 years old. Despite these declines, residual PCV13 serotypes, particularly 19A and 19F, continued to contribute notably to penicillin-cotrimoxazole nonsusceptible and penicillin-MDR IPD, respectively, after PCV13 introduction. Non-vaccine serotypes (10A, 15A, 15B/C, 16F, 23B, and 35B) increasingly contributed to resistant IPD in the post-PCV13 era through the expansion of both vaccine-type and non-vaccine-type GPSC lineages. CONCLUSION: PCVs substantially reduced AMR IPD in South Africa, but persistent PCV13 serotypes and expanding resistant non-vaccine-type lineages highlight the potential benefit of higher-valency PCVs, including PCV20.

Cerebrospinal Fluid Cytokine Signatures in Real-Time PCR-Confirmed Acute Bacterial Meningitis: Diagnostic Insights from TNF-α and IL-1β.
BACKGROUND: Acute bacterial meningitis (ABM) is a rapidly progressive central nervous system infection where excessive neuroinflammation contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytokines are key mediators of host immune responses; however, their association with molecular pathogen detection and host inflammatory responses remains incompletely understood OBJECTIVE: To evaluate CSF cytokine responses and their association with molecularly confirmed acute bacterial meningitis METHODS: A total of 246 CSF samples from patients with suspected meningitis, submitted to the department (February 2015 to January 2021) were evaluated. CSF supernatants were used for cytokine quantification, while sediments underwent bacterial culture and Real-time PCR. Cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-12p70, IL-6 and IL-10) were measured using cytometric bead array. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated diagnostic accuracy. RESULTS: Bacterial DNA was detected in 53/246 (21.5%) samples, with Streptococcus pneumoniae being the predominant pathogen, particularly in children under five. Real-time PCR-confirmed cases showed significantly higher CSF TNF-α and IL-1β levels compared with non-confirmed cases (p = 0.013 and p = 0.033), indicating a predominant pro-inflammatory cytokine. Elevated IL-10 levels suggested concurrent anti-inflammatory regulation. ROC analysis demonstrated modest overall discrimination for TNF-α (AUC = 0.657, p = 0.013) and IL-1β (AUC = 0.605, p = 0.162). However, at an optimal threshold of 0.60 pg/ml, TNF-α achieved 100% specificity, establishing high reliability. CONCLUSIONS: Real-time PCR-confirmed acute bacterial meningitis is characterized by a distinct CSF cytokine signature reflecting coordinated pro-inflammatory activation and regulatory immune responses, highlighting CSF TNF-α as a high-specificity adjunctive to molecular assays.

The binding of OTULIN restrains LUBAC activity to prevent TNF-driven immunopathology.
Met1-linked ubiquitin chains (Met1-Ub), synthesized by the linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC) and disassembled by the deubiquitinase OTULIN, regulate inflammatory signaling and cell death. OTULIN activity prevents tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-driven autoinflammatory pathology and embryonic lethality, but the role of the direct OTULIN-LUBAC interaction remains unclear. Here, we show that mice harboring a point mutation in the OTULIN peptide:N-glycanase/UBA- or UBX-containing proteins (PUB)-interacting motif (OTULINY56A), which disrupts LUBAC binding, are viable without spontaneous pathology but are highly sensitive to TNF-induced toxicity and TNF-mediated immunopathology during Listeria monocytogenes infection. Mechanistically, the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction prevents Met1-linked autoubiquitination, thereby limiting LUBAC activity and Met1-Ub conjugation on non-LUBAC substrates. Disrupting the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction increased Met1-Ub accumulation at the TNF receptor signaling complex, which stabilized the signaling complex, increased nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling, and, unlike loss of OTULIN or its activity, protected from TNF-induced apoptosis. Collectively, we identify the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction as a critical brake restricting LUBAC function and Met1-Ub-dependent signaling.

Infectious, Environmental, and Chronic Disease Burden among 1,844 Newly Arrived Humanitarian Migrants in Oklahoma, 2019-2025.
Global displacement has brought increasingly diverse migrant populations into health systems with limited experience managing large-scale humanitarian arrivals, yet contemporary data describing infectious, environmental, and noncommunicable disease burden across heterogeneous newcomer groups remain scarce. A cross-sectional analysis of 1,844 consecutively screened newly arrived individuals who completed the U.S. domestic medical examination at the University of Oklahoma Center for Travel and Immigrant Health between October 2019 and May 2025 was conducted. Screening was performed in accordance with Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Refugee Health Domestic Guidance, with programmatic adaptations. The cohort represented more than 25 countries of origin, with substantial variation across key indicators. Strongyloides stercoralis seropositivity was 14.6% overall, highest among arrivals from Vietnam (27.1%) and Cuba (25.0%). Eosinophilia exhibited low sensitivity (∼12%) for S. stercoralis seropositivity. Elevated blood lead levels (≥3.5 µg/dL) occurred in 19.2% of those tested, concentrated among young Afghan children. Latent tuberculosis infection was identified in 8.9% of patients, with marked country-level gradients. Predeparture antiparasitic therapy coverage was modest (albendazole: 42.2%; ivermectin: 34.2%). Only 6.8% of eligible women had ever undergone cervical cancer screening. Noncommunicable disease burdens varied widely by country of origin. The diverse infectious, environmental, and chronic disease profiles observed across countries of origin highlight the limitations of uniform post-arrival screening. These data support risk-stratified approaches that include targeted infectious disease testing based on country of origin and epidemiological exposures, universal predeparture hepatitis B triple-panel screening, strengthened pediatric lead surveillance, and cancer screening pathways.

Bacteria Pathogen Distribution in Late-Onset Neonatal Sepsis: Trends from a South African Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
Late-onset sepsis (LOS) in neonates is defined as a bloodstream infection occurring after 72 hours of life and is primarily caused by bacterial pathogens, often associated with catheter use and prolonged hospitalization. Despite its clinical and policy relevance, limited data exist on the etiology of neonatal infections in sub-Saharan Africa. This 8-year retrospective study investigated microbial patterns and antibiotic trends of LOS in a South African neonatal unit to inform infection control and antibiotic stewardship strategies. Data from neonates weighing 500 to 2,500 g admitted to the neonatal unit of a public tertiary hospital in Johannesburg (2013-2020) were analyzed for culture-confirmed LOS. Microbial prevalence was stratified by birth weight and year, and temporal shifts were assessed using Joinpoint regression. Among 7,468 neonates, 1,454 LOS episodes occurred (194 per 1,000 live births), with males accounting for 51.1%. Gram-positive bacteria predominated (55.4%), mainly coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS; 37%), followed by Gram-negative bacteria (44.4%), notably extended-spectrum beta lactamase-producing Klebsiella (13.2%) and Acinetobacter baumannii (12.8%). A marked decline in CoNS incidence was observed in 2016 (annual percentage change: -17.6%). Meropenem (35%) and vancomycin (30.5%) were most frequently used, with extreme-low-birth-weight (ELBW) neonates disproportionately affected. Late-onset sepsis remains a persistent challenge, with CoNS as the leading pathogen and increasing multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, particularly in ELBW and very-low-birth-weight infants. The observed decline in CoNS may signal improved infection control, whereas reliance on last-line antibiotics underscores an urgent need for enhanced surveillance, prevention, and antimicrobial stewardship.

Development of a chimeric multi-epitope vaccine targeting surface-exposed proteins of Chlamydia psittaci through immunoinformatics and structural vaccinology.
Chlamydia psittaci is an obligate intracellular zoonotic pathogen that causes psittacosis and severe respiratory illness in humans. Despite its clinical importance, no licensed vaccine is currently available, and antibiotic treatment may not provide long-term protection or prevent recurrent infection. To address this challenge, a computational strategy integrating structural vaccinology and immunoinformatics was used to design a multi-epitope vaccine targeting the major outer membrane porin and the virulence-associated pGP3-D protein of C. psittaci. Cytotoxic T-cell and helper T-cell epitopes were identified and screened to select antigenic candidates. The selected epitopes were joined using linker sequences together with β-defensin-3 and PADRE. The vaccine construct was evaluated using physicochemical analysis, three-dimensional structural modeling, interaction analysis with TLR2, a 500 ns molecular dynamics simulation, MM-GBSA binding free-energy analysis, immune simulation, and in silico cloning. The designed vaccine was predicted to possess favorable antigenicity, a non-allergenic profile, suitable physicochemical properties, and a global population coverage of 92.15%. Computational analyses suggested stable interaction with TLR2 and indicated structural stability of the vaccine-receptor complex during the simulation. Immune simulation predicted increased IgG levels, memory B-cell formation, activation of CD8+ T lymphocytes, and a cytokine profile consistent with Th1-type immune responses. These findings suggest that the proposed construct represents a computationally designed multi-epitope vaccine candidate that requires further evaluation through experimental studies to determine its safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy against C. psittaci.

Clinical features and outcomes of neuroleptospirosis in French Guiana: Insights from a retrospective study (2015-2021).
BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis is a re-emerging public health threat in French Guiana with a broad clinical spectrum. Neurological involvement (neuroleptospirosis) lacks a consensus definition and may be underrecognized. This study aimed to characterize its epidemiology, clinical features, outcomes, and associated factors. METHODS: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted across healthcare facilities in French Guiana from 2015 to 2021. Consecutive hospital-managed patients with laboratory-confirmed or probable leptospirosis were included. Neuroleptospirosis was defined by neurological symptoms combined with objective cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and/or neuro-imaging abnormalities. Patients with and without neurological involvement were compared. RESULTS: Among 146 patients, 18 (12%) met the criteria for neuroleptospirosis, corresponding to a mean annual incidence of 0.88 cases/100,000 inhabitants (95% conference interval [CI], 0.52-1.39). Presentations were meningeal (78% [14/18]), encephalitic (17% [3/18]) or meningoencephalitic (6% [1/18]). Lumbar puncture was performed in 28/146 (19%) patients; pleocytosis was observed in 18/28 (64%). The median CSF leukocyte count was 42 cells/mm3 (interquartile range [IQR], 13-240 cells/mm3), with lymphocytic predominance in 8/13 differential counts (62%). CSF protein was mildly elevated (median, 0.51 g/L; IQR, 0.32-0.88), without hypoglycorrhachia. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed abnormalities in 2/8 patients with neuroleptospirosis: one cerebral infarction and one case of pachymeningitis. Age under 30 years (odds ratio [OR], 5.56; 95% CI, 1.72-18), absence of leukocytosis during hospitalization (OR, 3.29; 95% CI, 1.04-10.39), and absence of thrombocytopenia (OR, 4.46; 95% CI, 1.39-14.32) were associated with neuroleptospirosis. Under our diagnostic criteria, neuroleptospirosis cases were associated with favorable outcomes, with lower odds of sepsis (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.10-0.79), no intensive care unit admissions or deaths. CONCLUSIONS: This study clarifies the clinical spectrum and outcomes of neuroleptospirosis in French Guiana, highlighting the importance of clinical awareness in tropical endemic settings. Prospective studies incorporating systematic CSF analysis and microbiological testing are needed to improve understanding of its pathophysiology and standardize diagnostic pathways.

ZOOJEU: Using Q fever to highlight a participatory science approach for fostering the co-design of management strategies for neglected zoonotic diseases.
BACKGROUND: Decision-making is one of the most difficult aspects of managing neglected zoonotic diseases. Ideally, public health management strategies would account for all stakeholder perspectives. However, in practice, certain stakeholders, notably farmers, are often excluded. ZOOJEU is a participatory science approach designed to tackle this challenge; it uses Q fever in goats in western France as a target system. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ZOOJEU emerged from a transdisciplinary collaboration among researchers in epidemiology, social anthropology, and the public policy sciences. First, we wrote a comic strip based on earlier anthropological research that uncovered the different realities of stakeholders in a region that recently experienced a human Q fever outbreak. Second, a serious game was built to foster mutual understanding among stakeholders and encourage the collaborative co-designing of public health strategies with farmers. Game construction involved compiling lists of tangible and intangible elements that characterise stakeholder experiences of Q fever outbreaks. Then, the game was played by stakeholders at a workshop. RESULTS: The comic strip highlighted issues related to Q fever for the stakeholders. The game was played by 23 stakeholders divided into three sets of players; each set of players included at least one farmer. The players were asked to collectively analyse a situation in which a goat farm is experiencing Q-fever-induced abortions. The players were invited to explain their perspectives and actions using game figures representing elements with which different stakeholders engage with regularly and/or in the context of a zoonosis. The goal was to establish a shared vision of what was happening on the farm. CONCLUSION: The approach appeared to be effective in establishing a common narrative and fostering a more democratic approach to public health while simultaneously accounting for human, animal, environmental, and social health concerns. Its utility as an educational tool should be explored further.

Etiological characteristics and infection-related biomarkers in patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia in the emergency department: A retrospective cohort study.
Severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) remains a leading cause of infectious disease mortality worldwide. Timely identification of causative pathogens and appropriate antimicrobial therapy are critical determinants of patient outcomes. This retrospective cohort study investigated the etiological features of SCAP and their relationship with infection-related biomarkers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), D-dimer (D-D), white blood cell count (WBC), and neutrophil percentage (NEUT), in an emergency department setting. A total of 146 patients with SCAP admitted to Tianjin Medical University General Hospital between March 2018 and March 2019 were included. Pathogen identification was performed through sputum or bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cultures. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.
