Fecal specimens were processed using routine selective culture procedures; isolates were identified with the VITEK 2 Compact system, with VITEK MS confirmation when required, and antimicrobial susceptibility was interpreted according to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) M100, 35th edition. Annual positivity and non-duplicate isolation rates were compared using Pearson χ2 tests. A total of 106 non-duplicate isolates were recovered, including 98 from pediatric inpatients. Annual positivity and non-duplicate isolation rates differed significantly across the 5-year study period (both P < 0.001) and were highest in 2025. Among pediatric cases, children aged 1-3 years accounted for 79.6%, with the 12 to <24-month group accounting for 52.0%. Resistance was high to ampicillin (76.7%), ampicillin/sulbactam (63.3%), trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (46.6%), and ceftriaxone (36.9%). Resistance to ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin was 12.5% and 14.8%, respectively, although intermediate rates were high. Most isolates remained susceptible to piperacillin/tazobactam and carbapenems. These findings show a concentration of laboratory-detected Salmonella among children aged 1-3 years, particularly those aged 12 to <24 months, and substantial resistance to several commonly used agents, supporting continued local surveillance and susceptibility-guided antimicrobial use. IMPORTANCE: Salmonella spp. remain an important bacterial cause of gastrointestinal infection in children, but local data from maternal and child healthcare hospitals are limited. This 5-year retrospective study describes the detection characteristics and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Salmonella spp. isolated from fecal cultures of inpatients in a maternal and child healthcare hospital in Shenzhen, China. The findings show that Salmonella isolates were mainly recovered from young pediatric patients and exhibited high resistance to several commonly used antimicrobial agents, including ampicillin, ampicillin/sulbactam, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and ceftriaxone, while reduced susceptibility to fluoroquinolones was also observed. These results provide institution-specific evidence for empirical treatment decisions, antimicrobial stewardship, and continued surveillance of enteric bacterial pathogens in pediatric and maternal-child healthcare settings.

Regulatory Overview and Considerations for Medical Countermeasures Developed for Radiological/Nuclear Incident Responses.
After the terrorist attacks on September 11 and the anthrax attacks in 2001, the United States Government (USG) implemented several pieces of legislation to enable the federal government to prepare for future threats, including managing and funding product development of medical countermeasures (MCMs). The Project BioShield Act of 20041 and the Pandemic and All Hazards Preparedness Act (PAHPA) of 20062 (with reauthorizations in 20133 and 20194) described and fine-tuned the scope and mission of different agencies in this effort. The Department of Homeland Security is charged with issuing material threat determinations5 from which organizations can model threat scenarios to determine potential health outcomes. The numbers from these models serve as thresholds for planning purposes. Within the radiological and nuclear (Rad/Nuc) space, there are two primary threats that have been identified as threats to national security: nuclear detonation (NucDet) and radiological dispersal devices (RDDs). NucDet is deemed the higher priority threat for planning and MCM development because of its greater potential impact. Health effects associated with nuclear power plant accidents are also considered in planning and preparedness.

A case of concurrent infection with bovine viral diarrhea virus and Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhimurium and its monophasic variant in a beef calf rearing farm.
In July 2022, an outbreak characterized by fever, diarrhea, and mortality occurred among suckling calves at a beef calf-rearing farm in Tottori Prefecture in Japan. A monophasic variant of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (Salmonella 4,[5],12:i:-) was subsequently isolated from a deceased calf. In August 2022, a persistently infected (PI) calf with bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) was identified and subsequently euthanized. Between June and September 2022, the median number of treatments administered per month per calf in the calf-hutch area tended to be higher (P<0.20) and the mortality rate was significantly higher (P<0.05) compared with the same period in 2021. In this outbreak, the PI calf introduced to the farm likely transmitted BVDV to other suckling calves; the resulting immunosuppression may have exacerbated the clinical manifestations of concomitant Salmonella 4,[5],12:i:- infection, leading to substantial production losses on the farm. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a herd-level concurrent infection with BVDV and Salmonella 4,[5],12:i:- in Japan.

Incidence and mortality of invasive fungal infections among patients admitted in intensive care units in India: findings from a multicentric registry-based study (2023-25).
BACKGROUND: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) are challenging to treat in critical care, particularly among patients treated in Intensive care units (ICUs). The existing evidence on IFIs from India remains fragmented. This study characterises IFI incidence, risk factors, resistance pattern, treatment and outcome among patients admitted to ICUs. METHODS: This multicentre observational study leveraged registry data on IFIs among patients admitted to 63 ICUs in eight Advanced Mycology Diagnostic and Research centres in India between January 2023 and November 2025. Patients with proven and probable IFI according to European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer/Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (EORTC/MSGERC) 2020 and the modified Aspergillus intensive care unit (AspICU) 2020 criteria were included. IFI incidence to hospital admission, all-cause in-hospital mortality, pathogen distribution and antifungal susceptibility were recorded. Mortality-associated factors were estimated using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards analysis. FINDINGS: Among 178,417 ICU admissions, 2500 IFI patients were identified with an incidence of 14/1000 admissions (95% CI 13.5-14.6) and all-cause mortality of 53.6% (95% CI 51.7-55.6%). Invasive candidiasis was the most frequently reported (57.1%), followed by invasive aspergillosis (37%), mucormycosis (3.4%), trichosporonosis (1.8%), pneumocystis pneumonia (1.1%), and cryptococcosis (1.2%). Median age of the patients was 45 years (IQR: 26-60), with 61.9% males and 38.1% females. Among candidiasis, Candida tropicalis predominated (35.6%), while Candida auris exhibited high fluconazole resistance (61.7%) and elevated amphotericin B minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) (40.7%). Aspergillus fumigatus (50.8%) and Aspergillus flavus (38.7%) predominated among culture-positive aspergillosis, with generally low MICs. Exploratory multivariable analyses showed that sepsis, chronic liver disease, immunosuppression, corticosteroid exposure, and total parenteral nutrition were associated with higher mortality in invasive candidiasis, whereas mechanical ventilation, corticosteroid exposure, and immunosuppression were associated with higher mortality in invasive aspergillosis. INTERPRETATION: The study findings highlight a high IFI burden and mortality among patients admitted in ICUs of India, with mortality exceeding 50%, underscoring the need for continuous surveillance, rapid diagnostics, infection control and antifungal stewardship. FUNDING: This study was funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Delhi (Grant ID: 157401).

Demographic and epidemiological patterns of reported malaria cases in Aseer Region, Saudi Arabia: An eight-year surveillance analysis.
BACKGROUND: Despite substantial progress toward malaria elimination in Saudi Arabia, imported infections continue to threaten re-establishment of transmission, particularly in southwestern regions. Aseer Region, contains diverse ecological settings that may support malaria vectors. This study examined the demographic and epidemiological characteristics of malaria cases reported in Aseer between 2016 and 2023. METHODS: A retrospective surveillance analysis of malaria surveillance records was conducted using data from the Vector Diseases Control Unit of the Ministry of Health. All laboratory-confirmed malaria cases reported from January 2016 to December 2023 were included. Demographic variables and malaria species were analyzed. Cases were classified as imported, introduced, or local according to World Health Organization definitions. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed using R software, and spatial distribution was mapped using QGIS. RESULTS: A total of 1254 laboratory-confirmed malaria cases were identified during the study period. Annual case numbers declined from 266 in 2016-63 in 2018 before increasing to 343 cases in 2023. Imported infections accounted for 799 cases (63.7%), followed by local (303, 24.2%) and introduced cases (152, 12.1%). Case classification varied significantly by year (χ²=570.54, df=14, p < 0.001). Males represented 84.4% of cases, and the median age was 26 years, with the highest burden among individuals aged 25-34 years (32.9%) and 15-24 years (31.0%). Non-Saudi nationals accounted for 65.1%, with Ethiopian, Sudanese, and Yemeni. Plasmodium falciparum was the predominant species (75.2%), followed by P. vivax (24.3%). In multivariable analysis, nationality and P. vivax infection were independently associated with importation-related malaria, whereas sex was not. CONCLUSION: Malaria in Aseer during 2016-2023 was characterized by fluctuating incidence, increasing predominance of importation-related infections. Multivariable analysis identified non-Saudi nationality and P. vivax infection as factors associated with importation-related malaria. Sustained surveillance, targeted interventions for mobile populations, and continued vector control are essential to prevent re-establishment of indigenous malaria transmission and support national elimination goals.

Disseminated cryptococcosis in systemic lupus erythematosus: Case report.
We report a rare case of disseminated cryptococcosis gattii infection with initial central nervous system manifestations in a 28-year old male under regular treatment for systemic lupus erythematosus since 2020. He presented with headache evolving into hearing loss, hypogeusia, amblyopia and mental confusion. This case highlights the challenge of diagnosing opportunistic fungal infections in patients with chronic immuno-suppression, emphasizing how early targeted management is critical to mitigate severe neurological sequelae and reduce mortality.

A Phase 1/2 Dose-Ranging Safety and Immunogenicity Study of mRNA-Based Candidate Pandemic Influenza Vaccines in Healthy Adults.
BACKGROUND: Influenza A viruses pose a persistent pandemic threat. We report safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity findings for mRNA-1018 pandemic influenza vaccine candidates from a phase 1/2 study in healthy adults. METHODS: In part A, participants were randomized to receive 1 of 4 mRNA-1018 candidates at 1 of 3 dose levels across 2 influenza A groups: (1) H5N8/H5-only or (2) H7N9/H7-only. Part B participants were randomized to receive H5-only-CG. The primary objectives were to evaluate the safety and reactogenicity. The secondary objectives included evaluation of humoral immunogenicity through day 205 by hemagglutination inhibition (HAI), neuraminidase inhibition, and microneutralization assays. RESULTS: Parts A and B comprised 1195 and 304 dosed participants, respectively. Overall, solicited local adverse reactions (ARs) within 7 days of vaccination occurred in 76.8% of participants across vaccine candidates and dose levels, most commonly injection-site pain. Solicited systemic ARs were reported in 62.8% of participants, most frequently fatigue and headache. Postvaccination immune responses, assessed absolutely, by HAI titers and dynamically, by seroconversion rates, tended to increase with vaccine dose. H5-based candidates induced stronger strain-specific HAI. CONCLUSIONS: Vaccine candidates were sufficiently well tolerated and immunogenic. Further development of mRNA pandemic influenza vaccines is warranted.Clinical Trials Registration. NCT05972174.

College mental health and the digital care transition: national trends in distress, help-seeking, and technology-mediated access, 2020-2025.
BACKGROUND: College mental health burden increased during the COVID-19 era while university mental health services rapidly adopted remote and digital modes of care. The population-level co-occurrence of these changes has rarely been described across the pandemic and post-pandemic period. METHODS: We performed a secondary ecological trend analysis of seven publicly available, weighted Healthy Minds Study national reports based on successive independent cross-sectional samples from Winter/Spring 2020 through 2024-2025. The reports contained a nominal 553,785 response records across waves; they were not pooled as a single cohort. Harmonized outcomes included depression, anxiety, suicidal ideation, nonsuicidal self-injury, self-reported academic impairment, treatment use, stigma, resource awareness, and selected digital-care indicators. Changes were summarized descriptively as percentage-point and relative differences; no across-wave significance tests or individual-level associations were estimated. RESULTS: Depression increased from 37% in Winter/Spring 2020 to 44% in 2021-2022 and was 37% in 2024-2025; anxiety increased from 31% to 37% and was 33% in 2024-2025. Self-reported academic impairment of at least 6 days in the prior 4 weeks declined from a Fall 2020 peak of 28% to 16% in 2024-2025. Therapy use increased from 27% to 38%, treatment among students with positive depression/anxiety screens from 51% to 61%, resource awareness from 72% to 83%, and perceived public stigma declined from 51% to 36%. Among therapy users, remote-only care increased from 29% in Fall 2020 to 42% in Winter/Spring 2021, while in-person-only care declined from 35% to 22%; remote-capable care (remote-only plus hybrid) increased from 65% to 77%. In 2024-2025, 7% of the weighted national sample reported a mobile app, online platform, or other digital mental health resource as a provider/resource category. CONCLUSIONS: The observed national estimates show post-peak improvement in several mental health and functional indicators alongside an early-pandemic shift toward remote and hybrid care. Because the analysis used aggregate reports with changing institutional composition, these findings describe population-level trends rather than causal effects or individual recovery.

Calendar month seasonality of HbA1c and its phase relationship with climatological temperature in 633,838 clinical measurements.
OBJECTIVE: HbA1c reflects glucose exposure over the preceding 8-12 weeks. We characterised the lagged seasonal association between monthly climatological temperature normals and HbA1c in a 12-year hospital cohort and examined whether a similar pattern was present in patient-level records. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We analysed 633,838 HbA1c measurements (387,678 patients; 633,737 with complete covariates) from a Chinese tertiary hospital (2014-2025). Cross-correlation was assessed for lags of 0-6 months using monthly HbA1c means and fixed monthly climatological temperature normals. Patient-level distributed-lag regression with cluster-robust standard errors and generalised estimating equations was used as a complementary analysis. RESULTS: HbA1c was inversely correlated with the climatological temperature series most strongly at a 2-month lag (r = -0.297, P < 0.001) rather than concurrently (r = -0.127, P = 0.14). Pooled by calendar month, the lag-2 seasonal association was strong (r = -0.977, R² = 0.955), with a seasonal HbA1c amplitude of 0.235% (2.6 mmol/mol; peak March, trough September), strongest under age 60 and attenuated during COVID-19. Patient-level regression showed a similar lag pattern, with the largest coefficient at lag 2 (β = -0.0088% per °C; 95% CI -0.0093 to -0.0082; P < 0.001), and the individual-level partial R² was 0.15%. CONCLUSIONS: The study identified a reproducible seasonal HbA1c pattern that aligned most strongly with the 2-month-shifted climatological temperature series, with significant correspondence also at 1 and 3 months. Because the exposure was a fixed calendar-month normal, the findings should be interpreted as a lagged seasonal association rather than evidence of a causal temperature effect or a specific 2-month biological delay. The small individual-level partial R² (0.15%) also argues against applying the population amplitude directly to individual treatment decisions. Future research should evaluate whether seasonal contextualisation can optimise laboratory monitoring and re-testing strategies near diagnostic thresholds.

Exploratory analysis of innate immune gene polymorphisms and COVID-19 in-hospital mortality in a large admixed Brazilian cohort.
INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 in-hospital mortality varies substantially among patients, suggesting a role for host genetic factors beyond established clinical risk predictors. METHODS: This case-control study investigated the association of the candidate SNPs rs2241880 (ATG16L1), rs1800450 (MBL2), rs10754558 (NLRP3), and rs12252 (IFITM3), alongside clinical variables, with in-hospital mortality in consecutive hospitalized patients including 505 non-survivors and 535 survivors of acute COVID-19 treated at a public hospital in São Paulo, Brazil, between March and August 2020. Baseline demographic, clinical, and genetic characteristics were compared between groups, and independent predictors of mortality were identified using multivariate logistic regression with Firth's penalized likelihood as the primary model to address quasi-complete separation. RESULTS: Deceased patients were significantly older, more frequently male, and had a higher comorbidity burden. In the Firth penalized model, male sex [exp(β) = 2.30; 95% CI: 1.33-4.02; p = 0.003], immunodeficiency [exp(β) = 5.06; 95% CI: 1.28-24.6; p = 0.019], and mechanical ventilation [exp(β) = 136; p < 0.001] were independent clinical predictors of mortality. Nominally significant exploratory associations were observed for the rs2241880 G/G genotype [ATG16L1; exp(β) = 2.27; 95% CI: 1.09-4.87; p = 0.028] and the rs12252 G/G genotype [IFITM3; exp(β) = 5.83; 95% CI: 1.02-45.7; p = 0.047] with increased mortality risk, and for the rs1800450 T/T genotype [MBL2; exp(β) = 0.03; 95% CI: 0.00-0.94; p = 0.047] with reduced mortality risk; however, none of these associations survived correction for multiple testing. No association was observed for rs10754558 (NLRP3). Variant allele frequencies differed significantly across ethnic groups, particularly for rs12252, whose G allele was more frequent in Black (21.6%) than in White (13.9%) patients (p < 0.001), and a sensitivity analysis adjusting for self-reported ethnicity confirmed the directional consistency of genetic associations with marginally attenuated effect sizes. DISCUSSION: These exploratory findings suggest that innate immune pathways, including autophagy, antiviral restriction, and complement activation, may contribute to COVID-19 mortality risk in the highly admixed Brazilian population and underscore the importance of conducting genetic studies in populations currently underrepresented in global genomic databases. Replication in larger, multi-ancestry cohorts with matched clinical endpoints is warranted to confirm or refute these signals.

[Proximity psychology : clinical presence and perspectives].
Proximity psychology has developed in hospital settings as a continuation of institutional psychiatry, community psychology, and, more recently, emergency psychology implemented during the Covid-19 pandemic. It is characterized by a discreet and regular clinical presence within teams, aimed at supporting subjectivity, creativity, and collective bonds in a context marked by multiple challenges. By fostering spaces for dialogue and symbolization, it enables staff members to preserve their psychological vitality and to act as authors of their own practice. For the institution, it represents both a sustainable investment in occupational health and an ethical form of resistance. The limits of this activity are linked to various institutional challenges.

Enhancing the Activity of Ribokinase from Thermus sp. 2.9 Through Rational Design for the Cascade Synthesis of Modified Nucleotides and Nucleosides.
The pursuit of efficient approaches for the production of promising antiviral and cytostatic pharmaceuticals is a crucial direction in medical biotechnology, especially after the COVID-19 pandemic. Modified nucleosides and nucleotides represent a highly promising class of chemicals for the development of drugs against cancer and viral infections. Being an alternative to traditional chemical synthesis, cascades of nucleic exchange enzymes offer single-step synthesis of such compounds with exceptional stereo- and regioselectivity. Furthermore, employing thermostable enzymes for such cascades offers the advantages of increased substrate solubility, lower solution viscosity, prevention of contamination, and simplified biocatalyst purification via thermal denaturation. The first biocatalyst for two distinct cascade pathways of nucleotide and nucleoside synthesis is ribokinase. In this article, we report improving the activity of ribokinase from Thermus sp. 2.9 (TspRK) for the cascade synthesis of modified nucleosides and nucleotides. We have employed a rational design approach, including Boltz-2 modeling and sequence conservation analysis. We have engineered two mutants, T244I and N272H, achieving a 3-fold increase in ribose phosphorylation rate (kcat). Improving the enzymatic activity of a thermostable ribokinase will serve as the basis for further optimization of cascade synthesis of pharmaceutical modified nucleosides and nucleotides.

Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Prognosis and Emergency Treatment of Patients with Ischemic Stroke in Suzhou, China: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted stroke care globally. This study aimed to assess the impact of COVID-19 on the clinical characteristics, acute treatment, and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in Suzhou, China. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed 506 hospitalized AIS patients from four stroke centers between December 10, 2022, and January 20, 2023. Patients were grouped by COVID- 19 infection status and timing. Clinical data and outcomes were compared with a pre-pandemic cohort from the SUMMITS-II Study. RESULTS: Among included AIS patients, 54.3% were COVID-19-positive. Infected patients had higher baseline NIHSS scores, elevated inflammatory markers, and more in-hospital complications. Intravenous thrombolysis rates increased slightly during the pandemic, despite longer prehospital delays. Emotional disorders were more frequent post-stroke. COVID-19 infection, particularly concurrent with stroke onset, was linked to worse outcomes at 90 days and 1 year. DISCUSSION: The findings suggest that the COVID-19 pandemic significantly influenced the clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke in Suzhou. Patients with AIS with concomitant COVID-19 infection presented with a higher prevalence of vascular risk factors and elevated inflammatory and coagulation markers. Moreover, COVID-19 infection occurring within one week of stroke onset was associated with more severe neurological deficits and poorer short- and long-term prognosis, highlighting the potential role of COVID-19 in worsening stroke outcomes. CONCLUSION: The COVID-19 pandemic adversely affected stroke severity and prognosis. While in-hospital workflows were preserved, delayed presentation and increased systemic burden contributed to unfavorable stroke outcomes. Strengthening stroke care delivery and psychological support during public health crises is essential.

One Space, Many Roles: Flexible Clinical Learning Spaces as an Affordance for Transformative Learning.
Clinical education has always unfolded within particular spaces: the bedside, the outpatient clinic, the simulation lab. Growing student numbers, shorter hospital stays, new educational technologies, and the disruptions of the COVID-19 pandemic have exposed the limits of a single, fixed learning space. This is a perspective paper that synthesizes evidence from clinical education space design, competency-based medical education, workplace learning theory, and health professions technology, rather than reporting findings from primary data collection. This perspective argues that clinical learning spaces should be understood not as static containers but as flexible environments capable of taking on multiple physical, functional, temporal, interactional, and technological forms. Using five metaphors- space as a puzzle, a chameleon, a stage, a network, and a platform- this paper proposes a working framework for medical educators and argues that this variety creates conditions favorable to, though not sufficient alone for, transformative learning, which additionally requires deliberate reflective scaffolding rather than exposure to flexibility by itself. As a conceptual contribution, this framework is intended to inform institutional discussion and guide future empirical evaluation.

SNX17 facilitates entry and infection of Rift Valley fever virus and related bunyaviruses.
Bunyaviruses are a group of multisegmented, negative-sense RNA viruses. Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) is a representative member that can cause sporadic human outbreaks. We previously identified low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1) as a host entry factor for RVFV and several bunyaviruses. This screen also identified additional factors as proviral host proteins, including sorting nexin 17 (SNX17). Here, we describe efforts to characterize SNX17 in bunyaviral infection. Our findings reveal that the removal of SNX17 results in a substantial reduction of RVFV infection in SNX17 knockout (KO) cells. Further analysis revealed that SNX17 removal resulted in a reduction but not complete elimination of LRP1 expression. Importantly, SNX17 interacts with full-length RVFV Gc and, upon infection by RVFV, co-migrates with RVFV to late endosomes. In addition to RVFV, several other bunyaviruses also appear to be dependent on SNX17 for infection, suggesting a potential broader role for SNX17 in bunyaviral entry.

Integrated in vivo and transcriptomic analyses of lethal Oropouche virus infection reveal suppression of pathogenic host responses by antiviral therapy.
Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging arbovirus responsible for large outbreaks of febrile illness in Central and South America, with increasing reports of severe neurological disease and fatal outcomes. Despite its growing public health impact, no approved antiviral therapies or vaccines are currently available. Here, we show that favipiravir, a broad-spectrum nucleoside analogue, robustly suppresses OROV replication and disease in vivo. In a lethal Syrian hamster model, favipiravir treatment provided complete protection against OROV infection, preventing viral dissemination to peripheral organs and the central nervous system, and remained highly effective when administration was initiated after infection. In contrast, insufficient antiviral control resulted in viral neuroinvasion and fatality. To define host responses associated with OROV pathogenesis and their modulation by antiviral therapy, we performed transcriptomic profiling of liver and brain tissues. OROV infection induced interferon-driven inflammatory programs accompanied by marked disruption of metabolic and tissue homeostatic pathways, whereas these transcriptional signatures were largely abrogated by favipiravir treatment. Together, our findings identify favipiravir as a potent antiviral candidate against OROV and provide the first in vivo, tissue-resolved transcriptomic framework of OROV infection, linking effective viral suppression with the prevention of neuroinvasion and pathogenic host responses. These results highlight antiviral intervention as a viable strategy to mitigate OROV-associated disease and mortality.

Vector competence for dengue-2 virus of permethrin resistant/ susceptible Aedes aegypti sub-populations from selected sites in Lamu County, Kenya.
Dengue virus, primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, is endemic in Lamu County. There is currently no definitive treatment for dengue; therefore, vector control remains the most effective method to curb transmission. Prolonged exposure of Ae. aegypti to insecticides may confer resistance. This study aimed to determine the levels of resistance to permethrin, a commonly used insecticide, and to compare the vectorial competence and genetic differences of resistant versus susceptible populations for dengue-2 virus. Ae. aegypti mosquitoes were collected from Lamu (Shela, Hindi, and Mokowe) using traps and assayed for permethrin resistance/ susceptibility. WHO insecticide resistance assays were conducted. The mosquitoes (F2) were exposed to dengue-2 infectious bloodmeals and fully engorged mosquitoes selected, incubated for up to 21 days, and tested for infection and dissemination by plaque assay. Individual legs were dissected from 31 female (F0) mosquitoes for isolation of genomic DNA. Polymerase Chain Reaction was used to amplify the target mitochondrial DNA using HCO2198 and LCO1490 primers. The amplicons were Sanger sequenced to determine genetic diversity. The Shela sub-population displayed susceptibility (>98% mortality), whereas the Hindi and Mokowe sub-populations exhibited resistance, with mortality rates of 47% and 37.6%, respectively. Of the mosquitoes from Hindi (n = 60); Mokowe (n = 90); and Shela (n = 130), n = 14 (23%), n = 24 (27%), and n = 40 (31%) respectively, had midgut infections with dengue-2; while n = 12 (20%), n = 11 (12%), and n = 21 (16%) respectively had disseminated infection. Genetic analysis showed that all the samples were Ae. aegypti formosus sub-species. Haplotype diversity was high at 1.0 while nucleotide diversity was low at 0.01184. These findings suggest Ae. aegypti formosus sub-species is prevalent in Lamu County. The study also demonstrated high infection and dissemination rates among the Ae. aegypti sub- populations.

Impact of initial disease severity and metabolic stress on mortality in patients with suspected external ventricular drain-associated infection.
External ventricular drainage (EVD) remains indispensable for managing intracranial pressure and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) disorders. Despite advances in neurosurgical care and infection prevention, EVD-related infections still contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to identify predictors of mortality and evaluate the clinical relevance of infection-related and metabolic parameters in patients with suspected EVD-associated infection undergoing EVD placement. We retrospectively analyzed all adult patients who underwent EVD insertion and were clinically suspected of having an EVD-associated infection at a tertiary hospital over an 18-month period. Data from electronic medical records included demographics, neurological diagnosis, comorbidities, catheter characteristics, laboratory results, and antimicrobial therapy. EVD-associated infection was defined according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) criteria. Statistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics 26. A total of 102 patients with clinically suspected EVD-associated infection were evaluated. CSF cultures were positive in 33 (32%) cases, most frequently yielding Staphylococcus epidermidis and Acinetobacter baumannii . Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was associated with higher crude mortality rates, likely reflecting greater baseline neurological severity. Initial Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (aOR = 0.85, p = 0.005) was found to be an independent predictor of mortality. Neither sex nor comorbidities predicted death. Hyperglycemia (> 140 mg/dL) and elevated lactate (> 1.2 mmol/L) independently associated with 30-day mortality. Shorter catheterization duration (≤ 5 days) also predicted death, likely reflecting greater neurological compromise. In our selected cohort of patients with clinically suspected EVD-associated infection, CSF culture positivity was not independently associated with mortality, although patients with culture-confirmed infection exhibited higher CSF pleocytosis and Cell Index (CI) values. Among patients with clinically suspected EVD-associated infection, initial neurological severity, together with markers of systemic metabolic stress, were independently associated with 30-day mortality. Hyperglycemia and elevated lactate emerged as key prognostic markers. While elevated CI values may support the diagnosis of culture-confirmed infection, CI did not demonstrate independent prognostic value for mortality. These findings should be interpreted within the context of this selected cohort and should not be generalized to the overall EVD population. Larger prospective studies including a greater number of culture-confirmed infections are needed to confirm these results.

Serological and transcriptomic response of African fruit bats to immune challenge with recombinant vaccines expressing Ebola or Nipah virus antigens.
Bats are hosts to diverse zoonotic viruses which can cause high case fatality rates in humans. Since detecting viruses in bats is difficult, antibodies are often used for surveillance, though their significance remains unclear in the absence of in vivo immunological studies. To address this knowledge gap, we measured antibody production and gene expression in bats following injection with vaccines encoding either a Nipah virus G glycoprotein or an Ebola virus GP glycoprotein. We selected two African bat species with overlapping ranges, Eidolon helvum (confirmed reservoir of henipaviruses) and Epomophorus gambianus (putative reservoir of filoviruses). Using a Luminex-based multiplex microsphere immunoassay and a pseudotype virus neutralization assay, we observed an increase in antibodies against the Nipah glycoprotein in most bats that received the Nipah vaccine. In contrast, we could only detect anti-Ebola glycoprotein antibodies in one bat species, Ep. gambianus, in response to the Ebola vaccine. Transcriptomic analysis in Ei. helvum revealed that genes involved in ISGylation and T-cell differentiation pathways were differentially expressed in response to the Ebola, but not the Nipah, vaccine. These results demonstrate species-specific differences in responses to antigen exposure, offering insights into bat adaptive immune systems and providing calibration for serological data from wild bats.

Agriculture-urban interfaces, social vulnerability and climate change shape West Nile virus risk across the United States.
Climate and land use change are reshaping the dynamics of vector-borne diseases. West Nile virus (WNV), the most widespread zoonotic arbovirus in the United States, illustrates the need to integrate climate, land cover and social vulnerability across heterogeneous landscapes when assessing spatial risk. We present a nationwide, county-level assessment of WNV risk using complementary statistical and mechanistic models to (i) identify socioecological correlates of current WNV incidence and (ii) project vector species-specific, temperature-dependent transmission suitability under mid- and late-century climate change scenarios. We found that land cover gradients, temperature-driven transmission and both occupational and residential exposure are associated with WNV incidence, particularly in mixed urban-agricultural landscapes. Future temperature and land cover projections suggest spatially variable shifts in environmental risk driven by divergent physiological responses among Culex species vectors. Our results highlight temperature and land cover as consistent, mechanistically grounded correlates of WNV risk at the national scale, while underscoring the need for refined, mosquito species-specific analyses at local levels. These insights can inform more targeted surveillance, vector control and climate adaptation strategies. We also identified key knowledge gaps, particularly around host and vector ecology, which must be addressed to improve public health responses in the face of ongoing environmental change.

Budget impact analysis of implementing point-of-care molecular testing for influenza A&B and RSV in Saudi older adult patients across hospital and home-care settings.
INTRODUCTION: The aim of our study is to compare the economic impact of adopting the molecular point-of-care test (mPOCT) for influenza A&B and RSV with current clinical judgment in Saudi Arabia, in both hospital-based and home care older adults. METHODOLOGY: A static Budget Impact Analysis (BIA) was developed in Microsoft Excel to evaluate the clinical and economic consequences of adopting mPOCT for influenza A&B and RSV testing among prevalent older adult patients in Saudi Arabia. The model adopted the perspective of the Saudi healthcare system over a one-season horizon, comparing two diagnostic strategies: current practice based on clinical judgement and a future scenario using mPOCT in both older-adult-friendly hospitals and homecare settings. Parallel decision-tree structures were constructed for influenza and RSV, incorporating test accuracy, diagnostic outcomes, treatment pathways, hospitalization requirements, and mortality. Costs included diagnostics, staff time, outpatient visits, hospital stays, medications, and resources used for complications and inappropriate antibiotic prescribing. Epidemiologic, clinical, and cost inputs were derived from published evidence and supplemented with Saudi-specific data where available. A deterministic sensitivity analysis varied cost parameters ± 20% and clinical parameters across published confidence intervals. RESULTS: Adoption of the mPOCT was associated with substantial cost savings across all modeled (hospital and homecare settings) older adults. For Influenza A&B, total costs decreased from SAR 57,858,038 to SAR 26,933,837 in hospital settings and from SAR 13,254,535 to SAR 7,974,232 in homecare, yielding savings of SAR 30,924,201 and SAR 5,280,303, respectively. For RSV, hospital costs fell from SAR 40,640,192 to SAR 20,706,660, and homecare costs from SAR 9,157,462 to SAR 5,988,728, saving SAR 19,933,531 and SAR 3,168,733, respectively. Overall, mPOCT produced SAR 59,306,768 in combined savings, demonstrating strong economic value for respiratory infection management in Saudi Arabia. CONCLUSION: This BIA demonstrates that implementing the mPOCT platform for influenza A&B and RSV in Saudi Arabia may provide substantial clinical and economic value, particularly for high-risk older adults. By enabling rapid and accurate diagnosis at both hospital and homecare entry points, mPOCT may significantly reduce false negatives, mitigates progression to severe lower respiratory tract infections, and decreases unnecessary antiviral and antibiotic use. These improvements could translate into major reductions in healthcare utilization, including ward and ICU admissions, and may generate considerable cost savings across a single respiratory season.

Clarifying the Evidence Linking Hepatitis A Outbreaks to Imported Strawberries.
The available epidemiologic, microbiological, and traceback evidence does not conclusively establish that the implicated strawberries were contaminated with HAV or that contamination occurred at a farm in Mexico. HAV RNA was not detected in the tested strawberry samples, and the environmental findings did not provide sequence confirmation. Therefore, the country of origin should be distinguished from the actual location of contamination.

Impact of obstructive sleep apnea on outcomes of acute respiratory distress syndrome: propensity matched analysis of a national cohort.
BACKGROUND: The effects of co-existing OSA on the outcomes of ARDS are unclear. OBJECTIVES: This retrospective study aimed to compare the outcomes and resource utilization rates of OSA patients who develop ARDS with a matched control group. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adult patients hospitalized between 2016 and 2019 with a diagnostic code for ARDS were identified within the Nationwide Inpatient Sample. Patients with acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema were excluded. By utilizing propensity score calculations, patients with OSA were individually matched with and compared to patients without OSA. Primary outcomes were mortality, length of stay and total hospitalization charges. RESULTS: 9405 OSA patients were matched with 9206 controls. OSA was independently associated with 34% lower odds of in-hospital mortality (21.1%vs 24.9%; aOR 0.66, 95% CI 0.61-0.72; p < 0.001), shorter length of stay (B - 2.0 days; p < 0.001), and lower total hospitalization charges (B -$74,601; P < 0.001). OSA patients had lower rates of invasive mechanical ventilation (aOR 0.79; p < 0.001) and tracheostomy (aOR 0.66; p < 0.001) but higher noninvasive ventilation use (aOR 1.40; p < 0.001). In a subgroup analysis of OSA patients, NIV was associated with fewer tracheostomies (aOR 0.61; p < 0.001) and lower charges (B -$26,625; p < 0.001) but was not associated with mortality or length of stay. CONCLUSIONS: In this nationally representative cohort, preexisting OSA was paradoxically associated with lower mortality, shorter hospitalization, and reduced resource utilization in ARDS. These findings suggest possible protective mechanisms warranting further prospective investigation.

Paediatric mpox during Sierra Leone's 2024 to 2025 clade IIb outbreak: A national surveillance and outbreak-investigation study of 415 children.
BACKGROUND: Evidence on paediatric mpox during contemporary African clade IIb outbreaks remains limited. We described paediatric cases in Sierra Leone's 2024-2025 clade IIb G.1 outbreak by person, time, and place and examined clinical care, outcomes, vaccination records, and documented exposures. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study using the national District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) mpox database, supplemented by patient charts and outbreak-investigation forms. Among 5,466 cases with recorded age, 415 (7.6%) were children younger than 15 years; 188 (45.3%) were aged 0-4 years, 121 (29.2%) were aged 5-9 years, and 106 (25.5%) were aged 10-14 years. Of 415 paediatric cases, 411 (99.0%) were laboratory-confirmed. Outcome was recorded for 261 children (62.9%); three died (1.1%, exact 95% CI 0.2 to 3.3). Care location was recorded for 285 children; 216 (75.8%) received hospital care for isolation, clinical management, or both. Three sporadic paediatric cases of mpox-like illness were reported from 2017 through 2024; notifications then rose rapidly from April 2025 and peaked in May. Western Area Urban accounted for 195/413 cases with known district (47.2%); crude notified paediatric rates were highest in Western Area Urban, Koinadugu, and Falaba. Household or caregiving contact was the most common documented exposure among 246 classifiable investigation forms (141, 57.3%). Mpox vaccination status was recorded for 27/54 cases aged 12-14 years; six were vaccinated. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Children were not spared during Sierra Leone's clade IIb outbreak. Response plans should include children in case finding, contact follow-up, clinical care, and vaccination assessment. DHIS2 should capture epidemiological links, clinical outcomes, vaccine eligibility and status, and potential exposure settings through standardised fields.

Infection of macrophages by mpox virus activates inflammasome and cell death, informing multitarget therapeutic strategies.
Severe mpox virus (MPXV) infection causes immunopathological manifestations in patients. Here, we provide clinical evidence of MPXV-induced inflammation in a large patient cohort and demonstrate direct macrophage infection in skin tissues from an autopsied mpox patient. In human macrophages, MPXV efficiently enters, replicates, and produces infectious particles. Infection activates both AIM2 and NLRP3 inflammasomes, triggering inflammatory responses and three forms of programmed cell death: pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis. Inflammasome inhibition reduces MPXV-induced inflammation and cell death without affecting viral replication. Screening clinically used anti-inflammatory drugs identified flufenamic acid, which suppresses MPXV-induced inflammation and cell death and, unexpectedly, also inhibits viral infection. Combined treatment with flufenamic acid and the antiviral brincidofovir further enhances suppression of viral infection, inflammatory response, and cell death, while largely preventing MPXV-induced transcriptomic reprogramming in macrophages. These effects were consistent across clade IIb, Ia, and Ib strains associated with the 2022-2023 global and recent African outbreaks. Together, our findings provide insight into MPXV immunopathology and support multitarget therapeutic strategies for severe mpox.

Comparing the Efficacy of Negative-Pressure Ventilation to Noninvasive, Positive-Pressure Ventilation in Children With Acute Respiratory Failure.
BACKGROUND: Negative-pressure ventilation (NPV) avoids a positive-pressure facial interface, but contemporary multi-center pediatric data comparing NPV with noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation (NIV) are limited. We describe modern NPV epidemiology and compare outcomes with NIV in children younger than 3 years with acute respiratory failure. METHODS: We conducted a multi-center retrospective cohort study using the Virtual Pediatric Systems (VPS) database. Children younger than 3 years who received NPV or NIV during a pediatric ICU (PICU) admission for acute or acute-on-chronic respiratory failure were included; outpatient use of either modality was excluded. Subjects were categorized according to initial respiratory support modality. The primary outcome was endotracheal intubation after initiation of noninvasive respiratory support. The primary analysis used multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression with center included as a random intercept. Propensity-score matching using Pediatric Risk of Mortality III score, age, sex, weight, diagnostic variables, and center was performed as a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Crude intubation rates were higher in the NPV group than in the NIV group (27.3% vs 10.4%, P < .001). After adjustment for measured subject-level factors and center-level clustering, ventilation modality was not independently associated with intubation (NIV vs NPV adjusted OR 0.675, 95% CI 0.393-1.158, P = .154). In the propensity-score-matched cohort, intubation remained numerically higher in the NPV group but was not statistically significant (NPV vs NIV OR 1.64, 95% CI 0.92-2.93, P = .12). CONCLUSIONS: In this multi-center retrospective cohort, NPV was used in a small minority of children younger than 3 years with acute respiratory failure. After adjustment for measured confounders and center-level clustering, ventilation modality was not independently associated with intubation. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal patient selection and the role of NPV in pediatric acute respiratory failure.

Impact of Cardiometabolic Risk Factor Burden and Therapeutic Control on the Prognosis of Alcohol-Related Hepatitis: A Biopsy-Proven Cohort Study With External Multicentre Validation.
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRF) have traditionally been overlooked in alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) and their prognostic impact in alcohol-related hepatitis (AH) remains poorly defined. We evaluated the influence of CMRF burden and therapeutic control on complications and mortality in AH. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 100 patients with biopsy-proven AH. CMRF (obesity, hypertension, diabetes, hyper-triglyceridaemia, low HDL cholesterol) and therapeutic control prior to admission were assessed. A cardiometabolic burden (CMB) score (0-10), incorporating CMRF number and control, was constructed. External validity was tested in an independent multicentre cohort of 332 patients with clinically diagnosed AH. RESULTS: In the primary cohort, patients with CMRF had higher 1-year mortality than those without (48% vs. 25%, p = 0.030) and more frequent in-hospital complications. Clustered CMRF (≥ 3) independently predicted 1-year mortality after adjustment for MELD, age and sex (HR = 4.1, 95% CI: 1.66-10, p = 0.002). Increasing CMB scores (≥ 5) similarly associated with higher mortality (HR = 4.4, 95% CI: 1.76-11, p = 0.002). These findings were reproduced in the external cohort, where ≥ 3 CMRF predicted 1-year mortality (HR = 3.0, 95% CI: 1.97-4.7, p < 0.001). Furthermore, ≥ 3 CMRF independently predicted 1-year mortality beyond MELD and Lille response in treated patients (HR = 2.6, 95% CI: 1.46-4.5, p = 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Clustered (≥ 3) and poorly controlled CMRF significantly impair survival and increase complication rates in AH. These findings, confirmed in an independent multicentre cohort, support integrating systematic cardiometabolic evaluation into routine clinical ALD management.

Vaccinations in pregnancy: An update for a changing time.
Maternal immunization is one of the most effective public health interventions to reduce infectious morbidity and mortality in pregnant women, fetuses, and newborns. Despite robust evidence supporting vaccine safety and effectiveness in pregnancy, global uptake has declined following the COVID-19 pandemic, contributing to resurgent outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases. While national immunization schedules vary, there is broad international consensus recommending influenza and tetanus-diphtheria-acellular pertussis (Tdap) vaccination during pregnancy, with increasing adoption of maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization. This review provides an updated, globally relevant summary of recommended vaccines before, during, and after pregnancy, highlights vaccines under development, and discusses implementation challenges. Strengthening maternal immunization requires coordinated action across governments, healthcare systems, industry, and media to improve access, trust, and equity in vaccine delivery.

From eradicating wild poliovirus to eradicating vaccine-derived polioviruses: why oral polio vaccine use must now be ended.
Wild poliovirus (WPV)2 was eradicated globally in 1999, and WPV3 was eradicated in 2012. Since 2016, endemic transmission of WPV1 has remained restricted to Afghanistan and Pakistan. Circulating vaccine-derived polioviruses (cVDPVs) have become the leading cause of poliovirus transmission and paralytic disease globally. As cVDPVs originate from oral poliovirus vaccine (OPV) strains, the polio endgame must address both cVDPV outbreaks and the mechanism that generates them. We propose defining cVDPV eradication as sustained zero disease, zero transmission, and zero emergence of new cVDPV lineages. Continued OPV use exposes children, predominantly in low- and middle-income countries, to avoidable risks of vaccine-associated paralysis and cVDPV outbreaks. Accelerated transition to inactivated poliovirus vaccine-only schedules and cessation of OPV use are essential for a sustainable and equitable polio endgame.

Structural insights into the binding potential of natural therapeutic leads as antiviral agents against human Metapneumovirus nucleoprotein.
Human metapneumovirus (hMPV), a member of the family Pneumoviridae and the genus Metapneumovirus, is a prevalent cause of respiratory tract infections, leading to severe complications and even death. As of now, there are no approved specific antiviral drugs or vaccines for hMPV, underscoring the need for potential therapeutic candidates. Hence, the present study employed a structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) of prepared ligands from CMNPD and SPECS databases against the hMPV nucleoprotein. Multi-level precision screening identified CMNPD3066, CMNPD12667, CMNPD25748, SPECS-AE-765, and SPECS-AP-123 as the top computationally prioritized compounds. These compounds demonstrated favourable predicted interactions with the docking scores ranging from -9.8 to -7.5 kcal/mol, and post-docking MMGBSA binding free energies ranging from -74.02 to -54.81 kcal/mol. Further, ADME/T evaluation predicted that these candidates were not involved in the violation of Lipinski's rule of five (Ro5) and all demonstrated favourable pharmacokinetic profiles. Subsequent 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations (MDS) and essential dynamics (ED) analyses, including principal component analysis (PCA) and free energy landscape (FEL) mapping, revealed the conformational stability of the nucleoprotein-ligand complexes throughout the simulation period. Collectively, the study concludes that the identified hit molecules are promising binding candidates for therapeutic development against hMPV and warrant further experimental and clinical validation.

Association between air sampling for viral respiratory pathogens and acute respiratory tract infection cases in the emergency department.
The emergency department (ED) is a common site for respiratory viral surveillance, but air sampling has not been thoroughly explored in this setting. In this study, we observed a significant association between COVID-19, influenza A, and RSV detection via air sampling in an ED waiting room and clinical viral testing.

Biologic and small-molecule therapies for inflammatory bowel disease: mechanisms, comparative evidence and the emerging pipeline.
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is a chronic immune-mediated disorder of rising global prevalence, with newly industrialised nations now entering the phase of most rapid growth. Its therapeutic landscape has transformed since 2020. Three selective interleukin (IL)-23p19 antagonists have been approved for both UC and CD; two sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators and a second-generation Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor have entered routine practice; subcutaneous formulations have altered delivery; and the first formal head-to-head trials, together with placebo-controlled trials incorporating an active reference arm, have begun to replace indirect comparison with direct evidence. In parallel, the ORAL Surveillance trial prompted a class-wide boxed warning that recalibrated, but did not eliminate, the role of JAK inhibitors. Three further strategies have generated late-phase data: anti-TL1A antibodies, which target a pathway not previously addressed pharmacologically in IBD; the miR-124 enhancer obefazimod; and the oral IL-23 receptor antagonist peptide icotrokinra. Several of these results are available only from conference presentations or company announcements and await peer review. Despite this expansion, induction remission rates remain clustered between roughly 15% and 50%, and endoscopic remission rates lower still. This review synthesises the mechanistic basis, pivotal evidence, comparative effectiveness, safety and regulatory status of approved and investigational therapies for IBD, and how treat-to-target principles, early advanced therapy and emerging biomarkers are reshaping positioning. It also covers two areas comparable reviews omit: acute severe ulcerative colitis, where advanced therapy is least well evidenced, and positioning in newly industrialised nations, where tuberculosis and hepatitis B endemicity and reimbursement, not efficacy alone, often determine the choice of mechanism.

Fluoroquinolone resistance-associated determinants in ciprofloxacin-susceptible Shigella isolates from Senegal.
INTRODUCTION: Fluoroquinolones remain important therapeutic options for shigellosis, but the accumulation of chromosomal and plasmid-mediated resistance determinants threatens their continued effectiveness. Genomic data on fluoroquinolone resistance-associated determinants in Shigella from West Africa remain limited. Here, we investigated the epidemiological, phenotypic, and genomic characteristics of clinical Shigella isolates recovered through Senegal's national sentinel surveillance system between 2020 and 2021, with particular emphasis on fluoroquinolone resistance-associated genomic determinants. METHODS: Stool specimens collected from patients with acute diarrhea were cultured for Shigella, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing. Genomes were analyzed for antimicrobial resistance determinants, quinolone resistance-determining region (QRDR) mutations, plasmid replicons, virulence-associated genes, sequence types, and core-genome phylogenetic relationships. RESULTS: Among 900 diarrheal stool specimens, 22 Shigella isolates were recovered, including 12 S. flexneri, 7 S. sonnei, and 3 S. boydii. All isolates were phenotypically susceptible to ciprofloxacin, whereas qnrS1 was detected in 9/22 isolates (40.9%) and the QRDR substitution gyrA S83L in 4/22 (18.2%). These determinants occurred in non-overlapping isolates, and no gyrA S83V or parC QRDR mutation was detected. IncFII replicons were identified in all isolates, while additional replicons showed heterogeneous distributions across species and sequence types. The fluoroquinolone resistance-associated determinants were distributed across distinct genetic backgrounds rather than being restricted to a single lineage. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that phenotypic susceptibility to ciprofloxacin may coexist with fluoroquinolone resistance-associated genomic determinants in clinical Shigella isolates. Integrating WGS with routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing may strengthen surveillance of emerging fluoroquinolone resistance in Shigella in Senegal and West Africa.

Recurrent gene conversions and subcluster-specific variants are associated with Mycobacterium tuberculosis adaptation to intensive host pressure: a comparative genomic study.
BACKGROUND: Long-read sequencing has revealed complex variations, such as gene conversions in immunologically critical PE/PPE gene families, yet their role in Mycobacterium tuberculosis host adaptation remains unclear. METHODS: We performed a comparative genomic analysis across a gradient of host-imposed selective pressure: chronic within-host infection, latent household transmission, and a 21-year clonal outbreak in Bern, Switzerland. RESULTS: We observed a constrained accumulation of mutational events across distinct epidemiological settings, with rates ranging from 0.36 to 0.81 events per genome per year. Under minimal host-imposed selection, the pathogen accumulated only small-scale variants (i.e., SNPs and indels). During the outbreak, however, the genetic diversity landscape shifted toward larger-scale variants, including recurrent gene conversions and structural variations. Notably, an early PPE19-to-PPE18 conversion emerged in the ancestral strain and was maintained across the entire lineage. In contrast, 86% of variants were transient singletons, with only a small proportion persisting under selection. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest a framework in which M. tuberculosis maintains genomic stability through purifying selection, while retaining the capacity to generate adaptive diversity through large-scale genetic rearrangements in immunologically relevant genomic features under intensified host pressure.

One Health genomic surveillance of Klebsiella pneumoniae in Belgium demonstrates large genomic diversity, presence of ESBLs and carbapenemases and circulation of clones across sectors.
Klebsiella pneumoniae is an important reservoir and disseminator of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes. Multidrug-resistant lineages, particularly extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing and carbapenem-resistant strains, represent an important public health threat. This study characterized antimicrobial resistance and genomic diversity of K. pneumoniae across One Health compartments in Belgium and investigated genomic relatedness within and across sectors. Between 2019 and 2022, 888 presumptive K. pneumoniae isolates were collected from diseased animals (n = 311), wastewater (n = 299), the food chain (n = 178), and human clinical samples (n = 100). Following selection based on isolation source and AMR characteristics, 286 WGS-confirmed K. pneumoniae isolates were characterized for AMR and virulence determinants, plasmid replicons, population structure, and phylogenomic relatedness. Phenotypic and genotypic resistance showed high concordance for third-generation cephalosporins (93.4%) and carbapenems (89.2%). Carbapenemase genes encoding KPC, NDM, OXA-48-like, and VIM enzymes were detected in 67 isolates from humans (n = 56) and wastewater (n = 11), but not in food-chain or diseased-animal isolates. Population structure was highly diverse, with ST307, ST15, ST147, and ST11 representing the most frequently detected high-risk lineages. Thirteen novel STs were identified in 18 K. pneumoniae isolates. Seventeen genomic clusters were identified, including 13 within-sector and four cross-sector clusters. Notably, an ST147 cluster comprising two poultry-meat isolates and a human clinical isolate showed no SNP differences, indicating very close genomic relatedness across sectors. Overall, our findings demonstrate a genetically diverse K. pneumoniae population alongside the circulation of clinically relevant high-risk lineages across One Health compartments and support integrated genomic surveillance to better understand their dissemination.

Case Report and literature review: complications of the association between rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary tuberculosis is one of the major public health issues globally. According to the World Health Organization, it is among the top 10 causes of death caused by a single pathogen. In Romania, its reported incidence rate in 2024 was approximately 60 per 100,000 people, making it the country with the highest incidence in Europe. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by the destruction of the small joints along with symmetrical distribution and multiorgan involvement. Pulmonary manifestations are more common in males with positive serology and can involve the lungs, airways, or pleura. Short-term corticotherapy may be initiated in patients with severe symptoms, and biological therapy (anti-TNF alpha drugs) may be used in those with inefficiency of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, with an increased risk for disseminated forms of tuberculosis in those with latent infection. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present the case of a 38-year-old male patient with a 5-year history of seropositive RA who was treated with methotrexate and methylprednisolone, without any prior investigations for latent tuberculosis infection or any chest radiography performed, and was admitted with severe respiratory failure. The results of thoracic computed tomography showed bilateral pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum, with pulmonary lesions suggestive of a diagnosis of tuberculosis, which was confirmed by bacteriological testing of samples. CONCLUSION: The coexistence of two severe diseases-one requiring immunosuppressive treatment and the other one favored by immunosuppression-in a country with a high prevalence of tuberculosis infection and in the absence of latent tuberculosis infection screening or periodic pulmonological assessment can lead to severe, life-threatening complications that require complex, multidisciplinary, long-term, and expensive management.

Burden and factors associated with depressive symptoms among adults receiving tuberculosis treatment in South India: A cross-sectional study.
PURPOSE: Depression is a common but under-recognized comorbidity among persons with tuberculosis (PwTB), adversely affecting treatment adherence, clinical outcomes, and quality of life. This study estimated the prevalence and factors associated with moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms among adults receiving anti-tuberculosis treatment in Bengaluru, India. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study between May 2023 and October 2024 among adult PwTB attending tuberculosis units under urban Bengaluru. Participants who had completed the intensive phase of treatment were enrolled using a multistage sampling strategy. Data were collected through structured interviews and review of treatment records. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms was defined as PHQ-9 ≥ 10. Logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors was used to identify associations. RESULTS: Among 200 participants (median age:34 years; 53.5% female), the overall prevalence of moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms was 56.5% (95% CI:50.2-63.1). Moderate depressive symptoms were most common (30.5%), followed by moderately severe (17.5%) and severe depressive symptoms (8.5%). Females had higher prevalence across all severity categories. In adjusted analysis, female gender (aOR 3.2; 95%CI:1.8-12.3), belonging to upper-lower to lower socioeconomic class (aOR 2.5; 95%CI:1.9-6.7), and perceived partial financial dependence (aOR 1.8; 95%CI:1.4-8.1) were associated with moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms. None of the participants had receipt of Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana benefits recorded in the Ni-kshay portal at the time of interview. CONCLUSION: More than half of PwTB had moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms. Exploratory adjusted analysis suggested associations with gender and socioeconomic vulnerabilities that require confirmation in larger studies. Integrating routine mental health screening, strengthening counselling services, and ensuring social protection support within TB care programs are urgently needed to improve outcomes and advance person-centred TB care.

Delayed introduction, transmission variation and susceptible dynamics explain spatial asynchrony during Republic of Korea's large pertussis outbreak.
Infectious disease outbreaks typically exhibit a large-scale spatial synchrony, reflecting coupling through shared environmental forcing and human mobility. Exceptions to this theoretical expectation have been reported, but the conditions under which synchrony breaks down remain poorly understood. Republic of Korea's 2024-2025 pertussis outbreak provides a striking example, during which epidemic trajectories diverged substantially throughout the country: notably, the decline in spatial synchrony with distance was more pronounced than that reported in many previous outbreaks. Integrating high-resolution surveillance data from 252 municipalities and a Bayesian transmission model, we show that heterogeneity in introduction timing and differences in local transmission levels, which may reflect differences in either contact patterns or susceptibility, can drive such fine-scale asynchrony even when all locations share identical seasonal forcing for transmission rates. In particular, regional variation in baseline transmission levels can drive differential levels of susceptible depletion, thus shaping the potential for multiple epidemic waves. This analysis offers a unique perspective on spatio-temporal epidemic dynamics that depart from classical epidemic theory.

New Delhi Metallo-β-Lactamase Plasmidomes of Intensive Care Unit Clinical and Environmental Enterobacterales Isolates.
BACKGROUND: There are limited data on the molecular epidemiology of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM)-producing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) in Latin America, despite the high burden of NDM-CRE in the region. This study characterized bla NDM-harboring plasmids from CRE from patients and the environment of an Argentine hospital. METHOD: We performed whole-genome sequencing of 40 environmental isolates (Klebsiella complex, n = 11; Enterobacter cloacae, complex n = 16; Citrobacter freundii, n = 10; Serratia marcescens, n = 3) and 4 clinical isolates (Klebsiella pneumoniae, n = 4) recovered from the environment and rectal surveillance samples of patients in the same intensive care units (ICUs) at a tertiary care center in Argentina, July 2023-February 2024, respectively. Representative genomic groups underwent Oxford Nanopore sequencing and hybrid genome assembly for complete plasmid characterization. Resolved bla NDM-harboring plasmids were compared across species and publicly available reference sequences to characterize plasmid relatedness and dissemination patterns. RESULTS: Ten representative genomic groups were identified across species, including 7 defined sequence types and 3 assigned in this study. bla NDM-1 and bla NDM-5 were present in 72.5% (29/40) and 27.5% (11/40) of environmental isolates, respectively (all 4 clinical isolates were bla NDM-5). Hybrid assembly of the representative genomic groups revealed bla NDM-1 was located on highly conserved plasmids belonging to the IncC incompatibility group across multiple CRE species. bla NDM-5 was restricted to Klebsiella spp. and was associated with structurally diverse plasmids including IncF- and IncHI1B/IncFIB-type backbones in both environmental and patient isolates. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the ICU environment as a reservoir for bla NDM plasmids.

Carbapenem-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria: Mechanisms, Pathogen-Specific Strategies.
Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (CRGNB)-including carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA), and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB)-pose a critical threat to public health due to their high associated morbidity and mortality. Key resistance mechanisms involve carbapenemase production, porin mutations, efflux pump overexpression, penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) alterations, and biofilm formation, with prevalence varying geographically and by species. Effective management requires identifying the infection site, assessing disease severity, and determining the pathogen and its resistance profile to guide antimicrobial selection. Recommended agents include ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, imipenem-relebactam, aztreonam-avibactam, ceftolozane-tazobactam, sulbactam-durlobactam, colistin, and tigecycline. For CRE, treatment depends on the carbapenemase type: KPC-producing strains are managed with novel β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations (ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, meropenem-vaborbactam); MBL-producing strains with ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam or aztreonam-avibactam; and OXA-48-type-producing strains with ceftazidime-avibactam alone. For CRPA, ceftolozane-tazobactam is the primary option, while CRAB is treated with sulbactam-durlobactam-based combination therapy. However, disparities in treatment access persist; while these novel agents are recommended, alternative salvage strategies are often required in resource-limited settings. This review details the epidemiology of CRGNB, outlines pathogen-specific resistance mechanisms and corresponding therapies, highlights knowledge gaps, and suggests future directions to inform prevention and treatment efforts.

Serotype and Commodity Contributions to Quinolone Resistance Trends Among FSIS NARMS Salmonella Isolates, 2013-2023.
Food-animal surveillance can identify antimicrobial-resistance patterns that may affect foodborne disease risk, but pooled summaries can obscure commodity and serotype drivers. This study analyzed public FSIS NARMS cecal and HACCP/slaughter-source Salmonella records accessed through FDA NARMS Now to examine quinolone-resistance trends by calendar period, commodity, and serotype. Records were filtered to Salmonella isolates with reported growth collected from 2013 to 2023. Calendar periods were defined descriptively as 2013-2016, 2017-2022, and 2023 to bracket major U.S. antimicrobial-stewardship milestones, including completion of GFI #213 implementation in 2017 and implementation of GFI #263 in 2023; these periods were treated as temporal landmarks rather than causal policy exposures. Outcomes were ciprofloxacin non-susceptibility, ciprofloxacin resistance only, and nalidixic acid resistance. Analyses included commodity-stratified percentages with Wilson 95% confidence intervals, serotype contribution summaries, and binomial models with standard errors clustered by year. The dataset included 42,232 Salmonella isolates; 41,608 were tested for ciprofloxacin and 41,606 for nalidixic acid. Overall, ciprofloxacin non-susceptibility increased from 1.96% in 2013-2016 to 17.84% in 2017-2022 and 25.71% in 2023. Nalidixic acid resistance increased from 1.36% to 17.02% and 24.01%, respectively. These increases were concentrated in chickens, where ciprofloxacin non-susceptibility rose from 1.7% to 28.7% and 42.4%. Salmonella Infantis accounted for 75.0% of all ciprofloxacin non-susceptible isolates, and Infantis plus Enteritidis accounted for 85.6%. After excluding both serotypes, adjusted period odds ratios were substantially attenuated. Findings indicate that quinolone-resistance trends in FSIS NARMS food-animal Salmonella data were strongly shaped by chicken-associated serotype composition, supporting serotype-aware surveillance.

Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study of the Prevalence and MIC-Based Antimicrobial Resistance of Salmonella spp. in Poultry in Morocco.
Salmonella spp. are major foodborne pathogens transmitted through contaminated poultry products. The emergence of antibiotic-resistant strains complicates treatment and increases the risk of multidrug-resistant (MDR). In Morocco, data on antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles in poultry-associated Salmonella remain limited. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and AMR patterns of Salmonella spp. isolated from poultry samples collected in Morocco in 2023. A total of 1339 poultry samples (ceca, turkey, and chicken meat) were collected using a representative stratified sampling approach from slaughterhouses, farms, and retail markets across the 10 regional directorates of Morocco. The isolation of Salmonella spp. was performed according to ISO 6579-1:2017, and identification was confirmed via matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry. Antimicrobial susceptibility to 15 antibiotics was evaluated using Sensititre EUVSEC3 plates. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were interpreted according to epidemiological cutoff values established by the European Committee on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing. MDR was defined as resistance to at least one antimicrobial agent in three or more antibiotic classes. Salmonella spp. were detected in 155 out of the 1339 samples, with an overall prevalence of 11.6% and regional variation. The category-specific prevalence was 13.8% (48/348) for chicken meat, 12.3% (45/367) for turkey meat, and 10.0% (62/624) for cecal samples. Resistance to nalidixic acid (94.2%), ciprofloxacin (92.3%), tetracycline (63.9%), ampicillin (36.8%), trimethoprim (27.7%), chloramphenicol (16.1%), gentamicin (10.3%), cefotaxime (4.5%), amikacin (3.9%), and ceftazidime (0.6%) was detected, whereas resistance to meropenem was not detected. Overall, 69.7% of the isolates were classified as multidrug-resistant and were mainly resistant to quinolones, tetracyclines, and beta-lactams. These findings highlight the need for strengthened antimicrobial stewardship, improved surveillance, and stricter regulation of antibiotic use in poultry production to reduce public health risks.

Carcass Hygiene Outcomes Associated with Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) Implementation and Stage-Specific Verification in Pig Abattoirs in Taiwan, 2018-2025.
In late 2020, Taiwan launched an official Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) certification program for abattoirs. This study evaluated microbiological outcomes associated with program implementation using nationwide Salmonella surveillance data from pig abattoirs in Taiwan (2018-2025) together with stage-specific verification in the 12 abattoirs that had been certified under the program after an official on-site audit. Verification sampling covered three points on the slaughter line: before antimicrobial washing (Pre-CCP), after antimicrobial washing (CCP1, decontamination), and after chilling (CCP2). Among the 12 certified abattoirs, the Salmonella-positive rate was 6.7% during the prepolicy baseline period (2018-2020) and 2.9% during the implementation period (2021-2025), corresponding to a pooled relative risk of 0.43 (95% CI: 0.23-0.84; P = 0.0107). During the implementation period, the Salmonella-positive rate was significantly lower in the certified cohort than in non-HACCP abattoirs (P < 0.0001). Stage-specific verification showed lower contamination at later processing stages: the pooled Salmonella-positive rate was 8.5% at Pre-CCP, 3.5% at CCP1, and 0.1% at CCP2. Median aerobic plate counts (APCs) were 4.00 log10 (CFU/cm2 + 1) at Pre-CCP, 3.03 at CCP1, and 1.77 at CCP2, an overall difference of 2.23 log10 units between Pre-CCP and CCP2, and median generic Escherichia coli (E. coli) counts were 0.59, 0.03, and 0.00, respectively. These findings indicate that official HACCP implementation was associated with improved carcass hygiene in the certified cohort and support the use of quantitative microbiological data for routine CCP verification under commercial slaughter conditions.

Rethinking tuberculosis and human immunodeficiency virus as a syndemic: Implications for global prevention and care.
Tuberculosis remains the leading infectious cause of death among people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). An estimated 10.7 million people developed tuberculosis worldwide in 2024, including 619,000 people living with HIV, while tuberculosis caused an estimated 150,000 deaths among people living with HIV. The two epidemics are better understood as a syndemic than as a co-infection because they concentrate in the same populations, interact biologically, and share adverse social conditions. Evidence indicates that integrating tuberculosis and HIV services shortens the time to antiretroviral therapy initiation but has not demonstrated a mortality benefit in meta-analysis or a cluster-randomized trial. Service integration improves coordination within healthcare, but does not address many of the conditions driving the burden outside the clinic. Evidence from India illustrates this gap. In a cluster-randomized trial, household food rations reduced tuberculosis incidence among contacts by about 40%, and the World Health Organization now recommends nutritional support for contacts in food-insecure settings. Prevention therefore needs clinical measures alongside action on undernutrition, housing, income, and access to care.

Tick-borne diseases in French Guiana: A comprehensive review pinpointing differences from mainland France.
French Guiana (FG), an Amazonian French territory, represents a unique ecological and epidemiological setting for tick-borne diseases (TBDs). In contrast to mainland France, where TBDs are well-documented, data from FG remain scarce.
