We carried out a systematic review using the PRISMA criteria for our search of the PubMed, ScienceDirect, and SciELO data bases. We identified 68 articles, of which 43 met our inclusion criteria. Data from FG were compared with those originating from mainland France. Albeit highly prevalent in Europe, and notwithstanding detection of a distinct Borrelia species in bird-associated ticks, there have been no confirmed autochthonous cases of Lyme disease in French Guiana. Conversely, Q fever occurs more frequently in this overseas territory than in mainland France, even though its causative agent, Coxiella burnetii, has been detected only one time in a local tick. While Rickettsia spp. are widely present in tick populations, no human rickettsiosis has been reported. As for Anaplasma and Ehrlichia spp., they have been identified in wildlife, domestic animals, and ticks, but with only one documented human case of chronic anaplasmosis, which was caused by a novel species, Candidatus Anaplasma sparouinense. Other pathogens, including Babesia, Bartonella, and filarial nematodes, have been detected in animals or ticks, but without evidence of human infection. Of note, emerging conditions have been described, one example being alpha-gal syndrome, an allergy triggered by tick bites to mammalian meat. To summarize, available data remain limited, and in all likelihood, the burden of TBDs in FG is underestimated. Integrated research combining human, animal and environmental surveillance is needed to more precisely characterize epidemiology, assess risks, and facilitate preventive strategies.

Hospital-based prevalence of culture-confirmed melioidosis among high-risk patients in India, 2023-25: a multicentre prospective study.
BACKGROUND: Melioidosis is not a nationally notifiable disease in India, and the absence of systematic surveillance has contributed to substantial under-recognition and fragmented epidemiological data. We aimed to determine the hospital-based prevalence of culture-confirmed melioidosis among hospitalised adults at high risk of melioidosis in India. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, multicentre, hospital-based prevalence study between Jan 1, 2023, and Dec 31, 2025, across 15 tertiary care centres in India. Adults (aged ≥18 years) hospitalised with predefined community-acquired infectious syndromes and diabetes or chronic kidney disease were enrolled. Melioidosis was defined by culture confirmation. The primary outcome was hospital-based prevalence. Prespecified secondary analyses assessed geographical, syndrome-specific, and seasonal variation; factors associated with melioidosis; and clinical characteristics and in-hospital outcomes. FINDINGS: Among 2953 patients, 262 (8·9% [95% CI 7·9-10·0]) had culture-confirmed melioidosis, with marked geographical heterogeneity. Prevalence was highest in Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka, and among patients presenting with extrapulmonary abscesses and bone and joint infections. Cases clustered during the monsoon months. Factors independently associated with melioidosis included monsoon admission (adjusted odds ratio 1·40 [95% CI 1·08-1·83]), male sex (2·33 [1·64-3·32]), outdoor high-risk occupation (1·94 [1·47-2·56]), and groundwater as the primary drinking-water source (3·25 [2·48-4·26]). Bacteraemia occurred in 152 (58%) of 262 patients with melioidosis, and 50 (19%) died in hospital. INTERPRETATION: Melioidosis is a frequent and severe infection among high-risk hospitalised adults in India, with substantial geographical variation and strong environmental and seasonal associations. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing and heightened clinical awareness among high-risk patients. FUNDING: Indian Council of Medical Research.

Population-specific transcriptomic shifts underlie secondary metabolic diversification in Aspergillus flavus Link and the domestication of Aspergillus oryzae (Ahlb.).
The genomic signatures of microbial domestication remain poorly understood within the context of natural population variation. Here, we demonstrate that Aspergillus oryzae, the filamentous fungus used in soy sauce and sake production, shares more recent ancestry with a predominantly northern, largely non-aflatoxigenic population of Aspergillus flavus (population C). A. oryzae isolates also overlap with the recently described, clinically enriched A. flavus population D, suggesting multiple domestication events. All isolates tested retained pathogenicity in a zebrafish infection model. At the transcriptomic level, populations are significantly differentiated and respond differently to spore density, suggesting population-specific adaptations to ecological conditions. Although most transcriptomic variation was consistent with phylogenetic relationships, several co-expression modules exhibited significantly greater divergence than expected from phylogeny alone, suggesting that phenotypic diversification may sometimes occur through the reorganization of transcriptomic architectures. A. oryzae also displayed elevated expression of a carbohydrate-metabolism module; however, this pattern was consistent with phylogenetic differentiation, suggesting that enhanced carbohydrate metabolism may have begun evolving prior to domestication or may be most apparent under fermentation-relevant conditions. Population-specific variation is also evident among secondary metabolite (SM) gene clusters. While A. oryzae shows markedly reduced expression of aflatoxin biosynthesis genes, this trend does not extend across the entire secondary metabolome. Using machine-learning-based gene regulatory network inference, we identified population-specific transcriptomic differences linked to distinct transcription factors, with evidence for both cis- and trans-acting regulatory divergence, but no changes in global regulators such as laeA. Together, these findings provide new insights into the domestication of A. oryzae, its global significance, and the microevolution of fungal secondary metabolic pathways.

Pooled prevalence and associated study-level factors of Echinococcus metacestode infection in ruminants in China: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Ruminant echinococcosis represents an important livestock-associated component of Echinococcus transmission in China, but national evidence on host-specific prevalence and associated study-level factors remains fragmented. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the pooled prevalence of Echinococcus metacestode infection in Chinese small ruminants and bovines and identified significant associated study-level factors. Six databases were searched from inception to April 10, 2026, following PRISMA guidelines. Cross-sectional studies reporting both examined and positive animals were included, and pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects models, subgroup analyses, and meta-regression. A total of 279 studies were included. The pooled prevalence was 24.46% (95% CI: 21.21-27.47) in small ruminants and 21.00% (95% CI: 17.47-24.77) in bovines. In both host groups, significantly higher prevalence was associated with E. granulosus infection, high-altitude areas, particularly > 4000 m, lower-temperature regions, and farm-derived samples. Significant temporal declines were also observed in both small ruminants and bovines, especially after 2012. In small ruminants, additional significant factors included older age, especially animals > 6 years, northwestern China. In bovines, host species was the main host-specific significant factor, with yaks showing the highest prevalence and dairy cattle the lowest. Although not statistically significant, sheep showed a higher prevalence than goats, and higher numerical estimates were also observed in grazing animals, autumn samples, and areas with annual rainfall < 400 mm. These findings support targeted surveillance of high-burden host groups and ecological settings and highlight the need for integrated ruminant echinococcosis control under a One Health framework.

Evaluation of a recombinant matrix antigen 1-based indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for serodiagnosis of Toxoplasma gondii infection in goats.
Toxoplasma gondii is an important zoonotic parasite affecting humans and livestock, and reliable serological tools are needed for disease surveillance in small ruminants. This study developed and evaluated a recombinant T. gondii matrix antigen 1 (TgMAG1) based indirect ELISA (iELISA) for detecting anti T. gondii antibodies in goat sera from northeastern Thailand. A truncated TgMAG1 fragment (amino acids 31-93) was selected to minimize cross-reactivity with Neospora caninum, expressed in Escherichia coli, and confirmed by SDS-PAGE, western blotting, and mass spectrometry. Overall, 213 goat sera were tested using latex agglutination test (LAT), indirect fluorescent antibody test (IFAT), and the TgMAG1-based iELISA. Seroprevalence was 34.7% by LAT and 38.5% by IFAT. Using LAT as the comparator, the iELISA showed 90.5% relative sensitivity (rSe; 95% CI: 81.7-95.3%), 85.6% relative specificity (rSp; 95% CI: 78.8-90.5%), and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.91 (Cohen's kappa [κ] = 0.73); using IFAT, rSe was 92.7% (95% CI: 84.9-96.6%), rSp was 66.4% (95% CI: 58.0-73.9%), and the AUC was 0.85 (κ = 0.54). These findings suggest the TgMAG1-based iELISA offers high rSe for detecting T. gondii exposure in goats, though further validation with broader serum panels is warranted to confirm its rSp.

Giardia duodenalis in domestic cats from the US and Canada: Prevalence and zoonotic potential.
Giardia duodenalis is a flagellated commensal protozoan that can infect both humans and animals. Infection can result in clinical signs such as diarrhea or, more often, the infection can be subclinical. Within the G. duodenalis species, there are several major genetic assemblages, A - H. Certain assemblages are species specific (C and D in dogs, F in cats) while assemblages A and B can infect humans as well as other mammals. This retrospective study used data collected from a commercial reference laboratory (Antech Diagnostics, Mars Petcare Science & Diagnostics). Real-time PCR data using fecal qPCR panel (KeyScreen™ GI Parasite PCR) for Giardia duodenalis and potential zoonotic assemblages A/B in 157,616 domestic cat stool samples from North America collected between March 8, 2022, to August 31, 2023, was used. Variables including age, sex, altered status, season, and geographic region were assessed to identify associations with cats that were detected for G. duodenalis and potential zoonotic assemblages A/B. The overall prevalence of G. duodenalis was 6.3% (9,962/157,616) and of those detected, 18.5% (1,840/9,962) were assemblages A/B. Cats that were G. duodenalis detected were more likely to be male, intact, less than one-year old, and in the Midwest. In general, lowest detection occurred during the summer months. Zoonotic potential detection was highest in cats aged less than one-year (19.7%; 1,011/5,137). These data highlight the importance of routine fecal screening in domestic cats to detect parasites, particularly those, like Giardia, of One Health concern, and provides prevalence, and risk factor information that aids clinical veterinary decision-making.

Characteristics and associated risk factors of opportunistic infection in children with systemic lupus erythematosus in under-resourced areas.
ObjectiveInfection is a major factor in morbidity and mortality among pediatric systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients, particularly opportunistic infections (OI), which can result in severe clinical outcomes. There is a scarcity of data regarding OI in children with SLE in resource-limited areas. This study aimed to determine the incidence of OI in childhood SLE, describe their characteristics, and identify associated risk factors.MethodsThis study is a retrospective and prospective study from January 2009 to November 2025 at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital, Thailand. Data on demographics, clinical features, laboratory parameters, types of OI, and outcomes were analyzed. Conditional logistic regression analysis was used to identify risk factors for OI in pediatric SLE.ResultsAmong 177 children with SLE, 38 patients developed OI. Person-year incidence of OI was 3.4 per 100 person-year (95% CI: 2.3-4.9). The most common OIs were Candida spp. (27.0%), Aspergillus spp. (13.5%), and Cytomegalovirus (CMV) (13.5%) with respiratory and mucocutaneous sites being the most frequently affected. Pulse intravenous methylprednisolone (IVMP) use during the past 3 months and high disease activity, defined as SLEDAI-2K score ≥ 11, were associated with an increased risk of OI in the multivariate model (adjusted OR, aOR 16.12; 95% CI 3.42-75.85 and aOR 3.46; 95% CI 1.44-8.31, respectively). Other variables, including cumulative prednisolone dose, cumulative cyclophosphamide exposure, complement 3 (C3) and C4 level, absolute lymphocyte count, and serum albumin, were not significantly associated with OI development after adjustment for potential confounders.ConclusionFungal and CMV infections were common OI in pediatric SLE. This finding underscores the importance of clinical vigilance regarding OI and the implementation of preventive strategies in SLE patients with the recent pulse IVMP exposure or high disease activity.

Accurate starting points for one-shot G0W0 and Bethe-Salpeter equation calculations via effective tuning of range-separated hybrid functionals.
The accuracy of one-shot G0W0 and Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) calculations depends strongly on the underlying starting-point eigensystem, which is commonly obtained from a mean-field density-functional approximation. Range-separated hybrid (RSH) functionals provide a particularly effective starting point; however, conventional optimally tuned RSH procedures often require costly, system-specific, multi-step optimizations of the range-separation parameter ω. In this work, we show that a recently proposed effective tuning protocol [Singh et al., J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 16(32), 8198-8208 (2025)] for RSH functionals can serve as an efficient alternative for determining ω used in G0W0 and BSE calculations. This simplified tuning scheme yields range-separation parameters that are effectively equivalent to those obtained from more elaborate tuning strategies, while avoiding their substantial computational overhead. The resulting tuned RSH eigensystems provide reliable starting points for many-body perturbation theory. In particular, one-shot G0W0 calculations based on effectively tuned RSH orbitals reproduce reference ionization potentials with high accuracy, while subsequent BSE calculations yield quantitatively reliable neutral excitation energies, optical absorption spectra, and excitonic properties for a diverse set of molecular systems and clusters. These results demonstrate that effective RSH tuning offers a practical and broadly applicable route to accurate quasiparticle and excited-state calculations, combining the accuracy of optimally tuned starting points with the low computational cost required for routine applications of G0W0 and BSE.

Spatiotemporal feature-based investigation of major depressive disorder and emotion recognition using functional near infrared spectroscopy.
Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) remains one of the most prevalent psychiatric conditions worldwide, with a marked increase in incidence and severity following the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite its rising burden, clinical diagnosis continues to rely on subjective assessments, lacking objective and reproducible neurobiological markers. Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) has emerged as a promising non-invasive imaging technique capable of capturing the spatiotemporal dynamics of cerebral hemodynamics, particularly within the prefrontal cortex-a key region involved in emotional regulation and cognitive control. In this study, we propose a spatiotemporal feature-based framework for MDD classification and emotion-related brain state recognition. Thirty MDD patients and thirty demographically matched healthy controls underwent fNIRS recording while exposed to emotional auditory stimuli. By analyzing group-level differences in oxyhemoglobin concentrations and β_values derived from a general linear model (GLM), we identified significant prefrontal abnormalities in the MDD group, particularly under negative emotional conditions. These alterations were most prominent in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), a region consistently implicated in emotion dysregulation. The classification model, based on fNIRS-derived activation features, achieved 90% accuracy for MDD detection and 85% for emotion recognition. These results demonstrate that integrating spatial and temporal features improves sensitivity to depression-related cortical dysfunction, offering a potential objective biomarker for diagnosis and novel insight into emotion-specific neurocircuitry in MDD. This work supports the clinical feasibility of fNIRS-based biomarkers and advances understanding of affective brain processing in depression.

Nosocomial Respiratory Syncytial Virus in the Post-Pandemic Era: Evolving Epidemiology and Integrated Prevention Strategies.
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Pandemic non-pharmaceutical interventions virtually eliminated respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) circulation in 2020-2021, and their relaxation was followed by unprecedented off-season resurgences. This narrative review, informed by a structured literature search, synthesizes current evidence on healthcare-associated RSV (HA-RSV), including transmission dynamics, vulnerable inpatient populations, and integrated prevention strategies, in the post-pandemic era. METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC (January 2000-October 2025) using two complementary strategies, supplemented by WHO and CDC guidance. Primary hospital-based studies reporting laboratory-confirmed HA-RSV cases formed the core evidence set; surveillance reports, systematic reviews, and guidance were used as labeled contextual evidence and synthesized narratively. RESULTS: Twenty-nine primary studies from neonatal, pediatric, adult, geriatric, and immunocompromised settings provided direct evidence on HA-RSV, which accounted for 3-15% of RSV hospitalizations depending on setting and case definition and was associated with prolonged stay, escalation of respiratory support, higher costs, and, in children, higher mortality than community-onset infection. Universal masking and pre-admission screening were followed by reductions in HA-RSV in most before-after studies. Post-pandemic surveillance shows earlier, less predictable RSV activity and periods of concurrent circulation with influenza and SARS-CoV-2. RSV spreads mainly through short-range respiratory particles and contaminated hands and surfaces; asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic healthcare workers are one potential source of introduction. CONCLUSIONS: Prevention of HA-RSV rests on hand hygiene, transmission-based precautions, environmental disinfection, rapid molecular diagnostics, and supportive healthcare-worker and visitor policies, escalated according to local surveillance rather than the calendar. Immunoprophylaxis and vaccination reduce severe RSV disease in eligible groups, but direct evidence that they prevent healthcare-associated transmission is lacking.

Prescribing Appropriateness and Clinical Outcomes in Hospitalized Adults with COVID-19 in Jazan, Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Background: The COVID-19 pandemic required repeated revision of national treatment protocols; evaluating prescribing against the guidance then in force is central to stewardship. Objective: To characterize clinical outcomes of adults hospitalized with COVID-19 in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, and to assess prescribing appropriateness using the Medication Appropriateness Index (MAI) benchmarked against contemporaneous Ministry of Health (MOH) guidance. Methods: Single-center retrospective cohort study of all adults (aged 18 years or over) admitted with COVID-19 between 1 March 2020 and 28 February 2021. Two trained clinical pharmacists independently applied the MAI to 1018 prescriptions. All associations were examined in univariable, unadjusted analyses. Results: Hypertension (44.1%), diabetes (38.7%), end-stage renal disease (13.7%), and cardiac disease (12.4%) were prevalent. In-hospital mortality was 26.8% (121/451 patients with a determinate outcome). Diabetes (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.32-3.08), hypertension (OR 1.92, 95% CI 1.26-2.93), and cardiac disease (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.15-3.64) were each associated with higher unadjusted odds of death; patients who died were on average 15.8 years older (p < 0.0001). Overall, 936 of 1018 prescriptions (91.9%) were appropriate; rates ranged from 99.4% (311/313) for enoxaparin to 42.9% (6/14) for hydroxychloroquine, the latter based on a small number of prescriptions. Inappropriate prescriptions were flagged mainly in the duration (82.9%) and indication (70.7%) domains, and receipt of at least one inappropriate prescription was not associated with mortality (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.31-1.12; p = 0.10). Conclusions: Anticoagulants and corticosteroids were largely prescribed in line with contemporaneous MOH guidance; several repurposed agents were not. These findings support an MAI-based audit against the guideline version in force as a tool for quality control.

Rotavirus epidemiology, genotypes, and changes during the COVID-19 pandemic in an unvaccinated population, Denmark 2014-2024.
OBJECTIVES: Rotavirus is a major cause of gastroenteritis in children worldwide. Denmark has no routine rotavirus vaccination programme. We aimed to describe national trends in rotavirus epidemiology and genotype distribution from 2014 to 2024, including changes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: Data on all diagnostic rotavirus analyses performed in Denmark between 2014 and 2024 were obtained from the Danish Microbiology Database. A subset of rotavirus-positive samples was submitted to the national reference laboratory for genotyping and linked with epidemiological data. RESULTS: A total of 18,246 rotavirus episodes were identified, and 1800 samples were selected for genotyping. The number of episodes declined during the COVID-19 restrictions in 2020-2021, followed by a substantial increase in 2022. The median age of infected patients increased from 20 to 27 months before the pandemic to 32 months in 2022. Test positivity returned to pre-pandemic levels in 2023-2024, whereas incidence remained elevated. Genotype distribution shifted over time, with G1P[8] dominating in 2014-2015, G3P[8] in 2016-2017 and 2022-2024, and G9P[8] in 2019-2021. Reinfections were uncommon. CONCLUSIONS: Rotavirus epidemiology in Denmark changed substantially during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, with changes in disease incidence, age distribution, and circulating genotypes. Continued surveillance remains important to monitor epidemiological trends.

Yellow Fever Reemergence in Tolima, Colombia 2024-2025: An Eco-epidemiological Study.
BACKGROUND: Yellow fever virus is transmitted by mosquitoes among humans and non-human primates (NHPs) in South America. The 2024-2025 yellow fever (YF) outbreak was notable for its spread into new areas, including the department of Tolima in Colombia's Andean region. We investigated the eco-epidemiology of human and NHP YF cases to understand the patterns and factors associated with the Tolima outbreak. METHOD: We collected spatiotemporal, sociodemographic, and mortality data on human YF cases in Tolima, as well as the locations of deceased NHPs with YF. We then conducted exploratory, descriptive, and spatial statistical analyses to identify risk factors and hotspots for YF. We then used inferential spatiotemporal modeling to compare ecological and sociodemographic factors. RESULTS: From September 2024 to October 2025, 116 human and 53 non-human primate YF cases were detected in Tolima. Among the human cases, 77% were male (89/116), and the median age was 47 (interquartile range 34-63). Of these cases, 45 (39%) died, and older age was associated with increased odds of death (adjusted odds ratio, 1.43 per 10 years; 95% confidence interval, 1.18-1.78). There was significant clustering among human and NHP cases. Higher rainfall and poverty/deprivation were associated with increased YF incidence at the neighborhood level, and rainfall during the outbreak was above average due to La Niña. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate significant mortality from YF, which reemerged in Tolima after nearly a century. Rural populations with greater ecological risk and poverty/deprivation could benefit from targeted vaccination strategies for YF.

Early-warning surveillance of West Nile and Usutu viruses in wetland and larval habitat waters and in mosquito excreta using digital PCR.
West Nile virus (WNV) and Usutu virus (USUV) are mainly avian mosquito-borne pathogens, increasingly cause human and equine disease in temperate regions. Mostly asymptomatic, current surveillance in France is reactive, based on clinical and veterinary reports, delaying signals for vector control and preventative interventions. We implemented in Southern France, in 2024 and 2025, a proactive surveillance methodology combining molecular xenomonitoring of mosquito excreta and environmental water detection of viral RNA in wetlands and mosquito larval habitat, through a multiplex reverse transcription digital PCR workflow. The analytics process was characterised through the limits of blank, detection, and quantification. Low-level positives were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. WNV and USUV RNA repeated detections revealed previously unrecognized, cryptic circulations up to 19 weeks before the first WNV human cases and equine alert. Environmental surveillance represents a paradigm shift for early detection of emerging Culex-borne arboviruses and a key enabler of proactive and effective One Health responses.

Endogenous anti-Ebola virus GP1,2 antibodies interfere with detection of secreted glycoprotein in the blood of EVD patients.
Ebola disease (EBOD) is a highly infectious disease with severe hemorrhagic symptoms. It is caused by orthoebolaviruses, which include the Ebola virus (Orthoebolavirus zairense) (EBOV) causing Ebola virus disease (EVD), the most lethal EBOD to humans. Through co-transcriptional polymerase stuttering and subsequent proteolytic processing, its GP gene produces multiple protein products, including secreted glycoprotein (sGP) and structural membrane-associated trimeric GP1,2. Although sGP is known to circulate in the blood, its physiological significance in disease pathology remains speculative. We quantified sGP using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in 36 acute human EVD cases from the 10th and 11th EVD outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) using single-time-point biobanked samples. We detected and quantified sGP in four patients with strong GP gene transcription (GP Ct 25), regardless of their anti-EBOV GP1,2 IgG results. While two patients, MAM179 and MAM271, had notably strong GP transcription (Ct < 25), their high amounts of endogenous anti-EBOV GP1,2 IgG might have interfered with detection by the assay detection antibody, a human anti-EBOV GP1,2/sGP IgG. Furthermore, the addition of sera containing anti-EBOV GP1,2 IgG reduced the binding between sGP and anti-EBOV GP1,2/sGP used as detection antibodies. This suggested that the level of sGP in circulation is strongly linked to the intensity of GP transcription. Additionally, circulating sGP in this context would form complexes with anti-GP1,2 antibodies, hence hindering additional antibody binding for detection.IMPORTANCEInsight into the mechanism of immune function by the Ebola virus secreted glycoprotein (sGP) in humans is essential for better understanding viral pathogenesis, immune protection, and immune evasion strategies. Research utilizing samples from patients who are infected with or have survived infection with the Ebola virus offers an unparalleled opportunity to determine the immunological significance of sGP. This research evaluates, in acutely infected patients from Ebola virus disease outbreaks, the role of EBOV sGP in modulating antibody responses directed against viral entry glycoprotein. By elucidating how sGP influences antibody-mediated immunity, the study advances our understanding of a conserved immune-evasion mechanism shared across all orthoebolaviruses. These investigations are valuable resources for designing more efficacious vaccines, therapies, and biomarkers for monitoring Ebola virus diseases.

A comparative analysis of rapid diagnostic tests and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays for dengue diagnosis: a retrospective study in a tertiary care hospital in India.
UNLABELLED: Dengue fever remains a major public health concern in India, where rapid and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective patient care and outbreak control. While enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) serves as the diagnostic standard, NS1 antigen-based rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) offer faster and more accessible alternatives, particularly in resource-limited settings. This retrospective study analyzed 3,488 patient samples tested using both NS1Ag-RDT and NS1Ag-ELISA between January 2023 and December 2024. Using ELISA as the reference standard, the diagnostic accuracy of NS1Ag-based RDT was determined. 1,036 cases were ELISA-positive and 2,452 cases were ELISA-negative; the RDT identified 988 true positives, 2,274 true negatives, 178 false positives, and 48 false negatives. The NS1Ag-RDT demonstrated a sensitivity of 95.36% and specificity of 92.74%, indicating strong agreement with NS1Ag-ELISA. These findings support the utility of NS1Ag-based RDTs as reliable tools for early dengue diagnosis, while highlighting the need for multicentric studies incorporating RT-PCR to further validate diagnostic performance across diverse settings. IMPORTANCE: Dengue virus infection continues to represent a public health burden in endemic regions, where timely and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective patient management and outbreak control. In this context, NS1 antigen-based diagnostic assays play an essential role in routine clinical practice, particularly in resource-limited settings due to limited access to molecular diagnostics. This study provides robust, real-world evidence on the diagnostic performance of NS1 antigen-based rapid diagnostic tests through a large retrospective analysis of 3,488 patient samples collected over a 2-year period at a tertiary care center in India. The findings demonstrate high sensitivity and specificity of NS1Ag-RDTs when compared with NS1Ag-based enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and further highlight seasonal variations in diagnostic accuracy, offering clinically relevant insights that can inform diagnostic strategies during peak transmission periods. This work strengthens the evidence base supporting NS1-based diagnostics in dengue-endemic settings and contributes data of significant relevance to virology-focused research and public health practice.

National prioritisation of zoonotic diseases in Rwanda: a One Health modified Delphi consensus study.
INTRODUCTION: The Quadripartite One Health Joint Plan of Action and the WHO's Pandemic Agreement emphasise operationalising the One Health (OH) approach to strengthen global preparedness, prevention and response to emerging health threats. In line with these global commitments, Rwanda has developed a national One Health Strategic Plan to enhance multisectoral collaboration across the human, animal and environmental health sectors. However, effective implementation requires substantial investment in integrated surveillance, preparedness and response systems, highlighting the need for an evidence-based prioritisation framework to guide resource mobilisation and strategic allocation. This exercise aimed to prioritise zoonotic diseases of public health importance in Rwanda using criteria including disease burden, outbreak potential, morbidity and mortality, socioeconomic impact, availability of diagnostic tools, transboundary risk and the effectiveness of prevention and control measures. METHODS: A modified Delphi approach was employed, consisting of (1) a planning phase to develop prioritisation criteria and survey instruments, (2) two rounds of expert surveys and (3) a consensus-building workshop using Mentimeter for anonymous voting. All the activities were conducted in Kigali, Rwanda. 25 experts representing the Ministries of Health, Agriculture and Environment; national regulatory agencies; the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board; Rwanda Wildlife Conservation, Gorilla Doctors; the University of Rwanda; the University of Global Health Equity and development partners including Igisekuruza Tree (iGiTREE), Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) and United States Agency for International Development (USAID) participated. Additional technical support was provided by the Pan-African One Health Institute. RESULTS: Rabies, zoonotic tuberculosis and toxoplasmosis emerged as the highest-priority zoonotic diseases within their respective categories. Participants identified limited transdisciplinary training opportunities, inadequate sustainable financing mechanisms and insufficient data integration across sectors as key barriers to effective OH implementation. CONCLUSION: Strengthening integrated surveillance systems, improving multisectoral data sharing and investing in a competent OH workforce are critical for enhancing preparedness against priority zoonoses. Furthermore, regular prioritisation exercises will ensure that disease rankings remain current and responsive to evolving risks.

Assessment of the Public's Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Rabies in the Republic of Guinea.
Rabies remains a major public health problem in resource-limited countries, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. The objective of this study was to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of the population regarding rabies in the Republic of Guinea. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 2733 participants in five regions (Boké, Kindia, Labé, Siguiri, and N'Zérékoré). Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered via KoboCollect and then analyzed using DATAtab and R software. Descriptive analyses, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify associated factors. In total, 66% of respondents had heard of rabies, but significant gaps were observed regarding modes of transmission and prevention measures. Dog bites were identified as the primary mode of transmission by 37.87% of participants. Canine vaccination was recognized as a preventive measure by 45.01% of respondents. Attitudes were predominantly poor (88.84% scored below the predefined 70% acceptability threshold, i.e., "low/unfavorable attitude," versus 10.79% moderate and 0.37% good), and 73.80% of participants exhibited inappropriate practices (versus 8.05% average and 18.15% good). Overall, 53.1% of respondents had a low level of knowledge, 29.3% an average level, and 17.6% a good level. A statistically significant association was observed between knowledge level and postexposure practices (p < 0.001). In a first multivariable logistic regression model (dependent variable: acceptable attitude, yes/no), educational level, age, and occupation were significantly associated with attitudes. In a second, separate multivariable model (dependent variable: dog bite, yes/no), none of the variables examined were significantly associated with dog bites, except age ≥ 50 years (adjusted OR = 1.98; 95% CI: 1.20-3.25; p = 0.006). These results highlight significant gaps in knowledge and practices related to rabies in Guinea. Strengthening targeted awareness campaigns, improving access to postexposure prophylaxis, and promoting canine vaccination are essential to reducing the burden of rabies. Because this study did not include animal, environmental, or surveillance data, an integrated "One Health" approach is recommended here as a forward-looking direction for future multisectoral intervention, rather than a conclusion directly supported by the present findings.

One-Year Clinical Course of Patients With Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Admitted to a Home Palliative Care Program: An Extension Study.
INTRODUCTION/AIMS: Longer term data on ALS patients receiving home palliative care are scarce. We extended follow-up of a 6-month cohort to 12 months to characterize the trajectory of function, symptoms, vital support (noninvasive ventilation [NIV], gastrostomy, and/or tracheostomy), and advance care planning (ACP). METHODS: In this prospective, single-center study, 34 consecutive ALS patients in a home palliative care program (SAMOT, Palermo) were assessed at baseline, 2, 4, 6, and 12 months, using Karnofsky, ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R), Edinburgh Cognitive and Behavioural ALS Screen (ECAS), Edmonton Symptom Assessment Scale (ESAS), dysphagia, vital support, and advanced care planning (ACP). RESULTS: Ten patients (29.4%) died over 12 months (70% at home); 26 completed the 12-month assessment. Karnofsky (34.4-27.7) and ALSFRS-R (27.1-21.7) declined significantly throughout (both p < 0.0005). Total ESAS rose from 15.7 to 23.7 (p < 0.0005); anxiety increased significantly between T4 and T12. NIV use rose from 20.6% to 50.0% (p = 0.014), while tracheostomy remained stable. Documented end-of-life decisions rose to 70.4% at 6 months but plateaued (69.2% at 12 months); no living wills were completed. Cognitive impairment on ECAS was present in about half of patients, unchanged over time. No patient was referred to or admitted to hospice. DISCUSSION: Extending follow-up beyond 6 months shows continuous functional decline and rising symptom burden, and highlights late-onset anxiety and early-plateauing ACP. Despite progressive needs, this home palliative care model appeared to support most patients at home until death over 1 year, within this single-center, non-comparative cohort.

Impact and cost-effectiveness of national implementation of rotavirus vaccination in Vietnam: A modeling study.
BACKGROUND: In Vietnam, rotavirus remains a leading cause of severe acute gastroenteritis resulting in hospitalization. Although rotavirus vaccines are available in the private sector-primarily accessible to urban children-the Expanded Programme on Immunization has only piloted the vaccine in select provinces. This study assessed the impact and cost-effectiveness of national rotavirus vaccination in Vietnam to inform policy decision on nationwide implementation. METHODS: We used a transparent static cohort model with a granular weekly age structure (< 5 years) to project rotavirus gastroenteritis (RVGE) cases, visits, hospitalizations, and deaths in children under five years, comparing no vaccination to nationwide vaccination with the domestic ROTAVIN vaccine over 10 years starting in 2026. Model inputs drew from global, regional, and local data including pre-vaccine incidence in Vietnam, local vaccine effectiveness and waning data, and treatment costs (governmental and societal perspectives) sourced from a local cost of illness study and hospital records (converted to 2025 USD). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses addressed parameter uncertainty. RESULTS: Over ten years, ROTAVIN vaccination was projected to reduce RVGE health burden by 42%, averting 97,776 (95% uncertainty interval 72,722-342,311) hospital admissions and 433 (330-1300) deaths. The program would cost US$39.5 million ($30.7-$117.7 million) for ten birth cohorts (2026-2036). From the governmental perspective, at least 62% of vaccination costs would be offset by healthcare savings. The cost per DALY averted was estimated at $982 (governmental perspective), while the program was cost-saving from the societal perspective in the base case. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness, with a 99% probability of cost-effectiveness from the governmental perspective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of 0.5 times Vietnam's GDP per capita (and 100% from the societal perspective). CONCLUSIONS: Nationwide ROTAVIN vaccination could avert a substantial health and economic burden in Vietnam and would be highly cost-effective given recently published thresholds.

Optimal Corticosteroid Use in Patients With Severe Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
BACKGROUND: The Lille score is an established tool to guide corticosteroid (CS) response and treatment in severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH), MELD score >20. However, its use in clinical trials has remained inconsistent. We performed this meta-analysis to compare mortality and infection rates between studies using Lille-guided versus those using CS not guided by the Lille score. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (2007-2025) evaluating treatment arms using CS in severe AH. Pooled mortality and infection rates at 28, 90, and 180 days were calculated for Lille-guided and non-Lille-guided arms. RESULTS: Fourteen corticosteroid-treated arms from 13 trials (N=1,294) were included, of which four studies (n=437) used CS guided by the Lille score. Mortality was lower in Lille-guided arms compared with non-Lille-guided arms at 28 days: [8 (2-14) vs 21 (13-29)] %, P=0.01, and at 90 days [15 (10-20) vs 40 (25-56)] %, P<0.001, but similar at 180 days [35 (16-54) vs 48 (34-62)] %, P=0.27. Infection rates at corresponding time points were 14 (11-17), 26 (14-38), and 32 (19-44), without differences between Lille- and non-Lille-guided CS arms. Substantial heterogeneity existed across studies, mainly due to differences in the publication year of the 28-day mortality outcome. CONCLUSION: Lille-guided CS use is associated with lower mortality across follow-up periods without a significant difference in infection rates. These findings support the use of the Lille score to guide CS therapy in patients with severe AH.

Targeting the Cav1.2-KCa1.1 axis prevents rabies virus internalization and protects against lethal infection.
Rabies is an almost always fatal disease caused by rabies virus (RABV). Once RABV enters the central nervous system, the mortality rate is almost 100%. Therefore, preventing RABV from entering the nervous system is crucial for the development of anti-RABV therapeutics. Here, we found that the L-type calcium channel Cav1.2 pore-forming subunit (Cav1.2) and potassium calcium-activated channel subfamily M alpha 1 (KCa1.1) are involved in the internalization of RABV using an siRNA approach. RABV glycoprotein interacts with Cav1.2, a process that is required for the subsequent activation of the channel. The activated Cav1.2 then interacts with and activates KCa1.1 to regulate the endocytosis of RABV by promoting the F-actin polymerization. Importantly, diltiazem, a blocker of Cav1.2 and an FDA-approved drug, has been shown to substantially reduce mortality in mice infected with RABV. Approximately 70% of mice survived following treatment with diltiazem at 50 mg/kg, whereas the 25 mg/kg dose resulted in 26% survival. Our findings suggest that Cav1.2 is a promising target for the development of antiviral drugs against rabies and enhances our comprehension of the RABV entry mechanism.

Clinical Burden of Disease and Demographics in Older Adults Hospitalized with RSV Infection in England: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes significant disease in older and comorbid adults. Current UK vaccination recommendations restrict eligibility to adults ≥ 75 years, 65-74 years with chronic respiratory disease or immunosuppression, and those in care homes, but evidence on clinical burden in adults < 75 years with comorbidities is limited. This study assessed patient characteristics, healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), and mortality in adults hospitalized with RSV in England. METHODS: Population-based retrospective cohort study using linked Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and Hospital Episode Statistics. Adults ≥ 60 years hospitalized with RSV between October 2014 and March 2019 were included. We defined RSV episodes as 90 days post-diagnosis. We defined cases using diagnosis codes for confirmed RSV (RSV-specific) or acute lower respiratory tract infection with exclusion of other causative pathogens (RSV-possible). All-cause HCRU (hospitalizations, critical care admissions, outpatient attendance, primary care consultations, and prescriptions) and case fatality rates were assessed. Results were stratified by age (60-74 and ≥ 75 years), case definitions (RSV-specific, RSV-possible), and comorbidity profiles (chronic respiratory disease, immunocompromised, cardiovascular disease). RESULTS: A total of 97,712 hospitalized episodes in those aged ≥ 60 years were included in the analysis, of which 785 (0.8%) were RSV-specific cases (n = 338 aged 60-74 years, n = 447 aged ≥ 75 years). In RSV-specific cases, median (IQR) cumulative length of stay (LoS) for those ≥ 75 years was 10.00 (6.00-22.00) days, which was equivalent to or lower than each comorbidity subgroup in those aged 60-74 years, with the longest LoS in those immunocompromised (11.50 [7.00-26.00] days). Critical care admissions were more often observed across comorbidity stratifications (13.85-22.34%) compared to those ≥ 75 years (5.03%). All-cause and RSV-related case fatality rates for RSV-specific cases were highest among those ≥ 75 years (all-cause: 19.3%; RSV-related: 10.3%). CONCLUSIONS: HCRU within RSV episodes in those aged 60-74 years across comorbidity profiles was equal to or greater than that in those aged ≥ 75 years. These findings highlight the need to prioritize consideration of comorbidity groups that could benefit from RSV vaccination.

Antimicrobial resistance profiling of Streptococcus suis isolated from neurological cases in Chilean pigs.
Streptococcus suis is an important swine pathogen and an emerging zoonotic bacterium, with multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains representing an increasing concern for both animal and public health. This report describes the pathological findings and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of MDR S. suis isolates recovered from the central nervous system of two pigs from a commercial swine farm in south-central Chile. Brain and spinal cord samples were examined by histopathology and microbiological culture, followed by bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using an antibiogram and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) analysis. Histopathological examination revealed non-suppurative inflammatory lesions characterized by mononuclear perivascular cuffing, consistent with meningoencephalomyelitis and myelitis. S. suis was isolated from the brain and/or spinal cord of both pigs. MIC testing demonstrated resistance to spectinomycin, ampicillin/amoxicillin, ceftiofur, penicillin, florfenicol, enrofloxacin, clindamycin, tilmicosin, tulathromycin, tylosin tartrate, tiamulin, sulfadimethoxine, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, oxytetracycline, and chlortetracycline, indicating an MDR phenotype. Both isolates remained susceptible to gentamicin, while variable susceptibility was observed for danofloxacin, neomycin, tulathromycin, tiamulin, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first report of MDR S. suis associated with neurological disease in pigs from Chile. These findings provide additional information on the antimicrobial susceptibility of S. suis in Chile and support the need for broader antimicrobial resistance surveillance under a One Health framework, as well as the prudent use of antimicrobials in swine production.

Persistence and epidemiological relevance of Salmonella enterica Newport in public-access waters from a central California coastal agricultural region.
Salmonella enterica Newport is one of the most common serotypes linked to fresh produce-associated salmonellosis outbreaks in the United States. In this study, we examined the genetic diversity and epidemiological relevance of 20 Newport strains recovered from Salinas Valley watersheds between 2012 and 2016. Multilocus Sequence Typing (MLST) identified two sequence types (STs), with ST118 representing 70% of isolates and ST45 comprising the remainder. Core-genome MLST (cgMLST) resolved 12 cgSTs, with cgST132506 being the most common. Phenotypic analyses revealed lineage-specific traits, including enhanced biofilm formation and reduced river-water survival in cgST132506 strains. Additionally, ST45 strains adhered significantly better to cantaloupe rind but produced less biofilm on glass surfaces compared with ST118 strains. Epidemiological relevance was assessed by examining matched strains in identified Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) clusters using the Pathogen Detection pipeline. Two strains were classified as persistent (>500 matches), six as intermediate (50-500), and twelve as transient (<50). Persistent and intermediate strains, considered strains of concern (SOCs), were genomically related to known outbreak strains and widely detected across the United States, including those linked to the 2012 cantaloupe-associated outbreak and the 2017 watermelon-associated outbreak. Although no significant difference in attachment to cantaloupe rind was observed between SOCs and transient strains, SOCs displayed greater river-water survival, while transient strains produced significantly more biofilm. Diverse Newport strains were isolated from the two watersheds examined, and multiple SOCs were recovered from three locations, highlighting the need for targeted investigations into contamination sources in these areas.

[Whole-genome sequencing-based molecular characterization of Salmonella associated with foodborne disease outbreaks in Wuxi City from 2014 to 2024].
This study analyzed the molecular characteristics of Salmonella isolates associated with foodborne outbreaks in Wuxi City using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). Epidemiological data from 16 outbreaks (2014-2024) and 68 Salmonella isolates were collected. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and WGS were performed. ResFinder, PlasmidFinder, and PointFinder were used to annotate resistance genes, plasmids, and mutations. A core-genome SNP phylogenetic tree was constructed. Among the 68 Salmonella isolates, ST11 Salmonella Enteritidis was the predominant clone. The overall antimicrobial resistance rate was 95.59%, with a multidrug resistance (MDR) rate of 55.88%. High resistance rates were observed for nalidixic acid (75.00%), streptomycin (69.12%), and ampicillin (57.35%). Compared with the non-S. Enteritidis isolates, S. Enteritidis exhibited significantly higher MDR rates and resistance rates to penicillins, β-lactam inhibitor combinations, and quinolones (all P<0.05). A total of 24 antimicrobial resistance genes were identified, with aac(6')-Iaa and blaTEM-1B being the most prevalent, and a high concordance was observed between genotypic and phenotypic resistance. IncF and IncX were the predominant plasmid replicon types. Phylogenetic analysis showed that isolates clustered primarily according to serotype and sequence type (ST). Isolates from the same outbreak were highly homologous, with pairwise SNP differences ranging from 0 to 7, whereas isolates from one outbreak exhibited substantial genetic divergence (342 SNPs). In conclusion, Salmonella outbreaks in Wuxi from 2014 to 2024 are predominantly caused by ST11 S. Enteritidis, which exhibits a high level of resistance to commonly used antimicrobial agents. Whole-genome sequencing could effectively distinguish co-isolates with low genetic relatedness, providing high-resolution evidence for outbreak source tracing and epidemiological investigations.

Seropositivity and Antigen-Specific Seroreactivity to Leptospira spp. In Equids from Three Regions of Veracruz, Mexico.
Information on Leptospira spp. exposure in Mexican equids remains limited. This cross-sectional study evaluated seropositivity and antigen-specific seroreactivity in 313 apparently healthy equids enrolled by convenience sampling in Los Tuxtlas (n = 119), Sotavento (n = 108), and Capital (n = 86), Veracruz, Mexico, from 2 October 2023 to 6 March 2024. Sera were examined by the microscopic agglutination test (MAT) against 13 antigens; titers ≥ 1:100 defined seropositivity. Overall seropositivity was 57.5% (180/313; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 52.0-62.9), with regional proportions of 49.6%, 65.7%, and 58.1%, respectively (unadjusted p = 0.048). Modified Poisson models with robust variance were fitted separately for region with species and region with sex. For Sotavento versus Los Tuxtlas, the adjusted prevalence ratio was 1.33 after adjustment for species (95% CI: 1.06-1.67) and 1.33 after adjustment for sex (95% CI: 1.06-1.66). Antigen-specific seroreactivity was most frequent for Australis (63/313; 20.1%), Bratislava (62/313; 19.8%), and Pyrogenes (57/313; 18.2%); these are overlapping antigen responses, not mutually exclusive serogroup estimates. Environmental and management exposures were not measured at the animal level. The findings support surveillance at the animal-human-environment interface but do not demonstrate active shedding or zoonotic transmission.

Genomic evidence of clonal and IncX3 plasmid-mediated dissemination of blaNDM-7 in the Klebsiella pneumoniae complex.
BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), particularly those carrying New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM) variants, pose a major global health threat. Among these, NDM-7 has attracted increasing attention due to its enhanced carbapenemase activity and clinical relevance. This study investigated the prevalence, genomic characteristics and dissemination of blaNDM-7-positive Klebsiella pneumoniae complex isolates from clinical and environmental sources in Yangzhou, China. METHODS: A total of 401 clinical isolates, 282 hospital surface swabs and 366 wastewater samples collected between 2018 and 2024 were screened for blaNDM. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing were performed to characterize resistance profiles, genomic features and phylogenetic relationships. Conjugation and serial-passage assays were used to assess plasmid transferability and stability, respectively. RESULTS: Seven blaNDM-7-positive isolates were identified, including one clinical isolate, one hospital environmental isolate and five wastewater isolates. All exhibited multidrug resistance. The blaNDM-7 gene was located on highly conserved ∼46 kb IncX3 plasmids that exhibited high conjugation frequencies (10-5-10-4) and stability (96.0%-98.7% mean retention after approximately 600 generations). Phylogenetic analysis revealed close genomic relatedness among the six ST196 K. quasipneumoniae isolates recovered from different sources, with only 0-7 core-genome SNP differences. All six isolates were recovered within approximately 6 months, consistent with recent common ancestry and possible clonal dissemination across settings. CONCLUSIONS: The close genomic relatedness of ST196 isolates from different sources supports possible clonal dissemination, while the high conservation, transferability and stability of IncX3 plasmids highlight their important role in the dissemination of blaNDM-7. These findings underscore the importance of continued genomic surveillance of blaNDM-7 and its associated mobile genetic elements across clinical and environmental settings.

Biliary Microbiology and Antimicrobial Treatment Modification in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Cholecystostomy for Acute Cholecystitis: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
OBJECTIVE: To describe bile culture yield, organism distribution and antimicrobial treatment modification in patients undergoing percutaneous cholecystostomy (PC) for acute cholecystitis who were unsuitable for early cholecystectomy. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 84 consecutive patients who underwent PC between December 2021 and December 2025. Index bile cultures were classified as positive, no growth, or not obtained. We analysed organisms, polymicrobial growth, empirical antimicrobial therapy, treatment modification and clinical outcomes by culture status and disease severity. RESULTS: Bile was cultured in 71 patients (84.5%), and 33 cultures were positive (46.5% of sampled patients; 39.3% of the cohort). Seven positive cultures (21.2%) were polymicrobial. The leading isolates were Escherichia coli (n=13), Enterococcus faecium (n=9) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (n=8). Ceftriaxone plus metronidazole was the most common empirical regimen (52/84, 61.9%). Treatment was modified in 20 patients (23.8%); half of the modified regimens contained a carbapenem. Modification was more frequent among patients requiring intensive care (46.2% versus 13.8%; crude odds ratio [OR] 5.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.83-15.67) and those with Tokyo grade III disease (41.9% versus 13.2%; crude OR 4.75, 95% CI 1.63-13.81). No statistically significant difference was detected between the positive-culture and no-growth groups in treatment modification (24.2% versus 23.7%), in-hospital adverse events (24.2% versus 31.6%), 30-day mortality (12.1% versus 13.2%) or 90-day mortality among evaluable patients (6/32 [18.8%] versus 10/37 [27.0%]). CONCLUSION: Bile obtained during PC had a substantial microbiological yield and grew predominantly enteric organisms. Treatment modification was more frequent in clinically severe disease, but no statistically significant difference was detected between positive-culture and no-growth groups. Bile culture should inform a structured reassessment of antimicrobials after source control, rather than automatic treatment escalation.

Epidemiology, clinical, phenotypic and genotypic characteristics of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii from Qatar.
BACKGROUND: In healthcare, multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii is associated with significant morbidity, mortality and limited treatment options. This study evaluates the epidemiology, clinical, phenotypic, and genotypic characteristics of MDR Acinetobacter baumannii from Qatar. METHODS: We conducted a prospective study from 2017 to 2020 of all clinical Acinetobacter baumannii isolates subjected to phenotypic testing. We performed identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using MALDI-TOF MS (Billerica, MA, USA) and BD PhoenixTM (BD Diagnostics, Durham, NC, USA), as well as the E test (Liofilchem®, Roseto degli Abruzzi, Italy). We performed whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analyses on bacterial isolates. RESULTS: Out of 536 Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, 62 (11.6%) were MDR, with a decreasing trend. Isolation sites were urinary (42%), respiratory (29%), bloodstream (16%), and skin and soft tissues (13%). Hospital acquisition was recorded in 97% of cases, isolated from older patients with multiple comorbidities and prior antimicrobial exposure, leading to a 30-day mortality of 16%. Phenotypic evaluation revealed extensive antimicrobial resistance to meropenem, ampicillin-sulbactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, ceftolozane-tazobactam, meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem- relebactam, while the most active agents were tigecycline and cefiderocol. Genomic analysis of 39 isolates revealed predominance of sequence type 2 (n = 27). All resistant Acinetobacter isolates carried AmpC beta-lactamases and the blaOXAAb, (blaOXA-51-like family) family of carbapenem resistance genes. The predominant carbapenemases were blaOXA-23, while 7 isolates carried blaNDM-1. CONCLUSION: Multidrug-resistant A. baumannii was infrequently isolated, predominantly ST2, mainly from elderly patients with multiple risk factors. Extensive resistance profiles limit treatment options, with promising in vitro results for tigecycline and cefiderocol.

Ambient temperature variability and newly diagnosed tuberculosis: Evidence from a time-stratified case-crossover study.
BACKGROUND: Environmental factors, particularly temperature-related exposures, are increasingly recognized as important determinants of tuberculosis (TB) disease progression and symptom manifestation. However, the evidence regarding the associations of heat exposure, cold exposure, and diurnal temperature range (DTR) with newly diagnosed TB remains limited and inconsistent. METHODS: Data from Anhui Province between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2024 were analyzed using a two-stage analytical framework based on a time-stratified case-crossover study design. City-specific associations between temperature and TB were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis. Effect estimates were presented as relative risks (RRs) with corresponding confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: A total of 243,577 newly diagnosed TB cases were reported during the study period. Compared with the median daily mean temperature, extreme heat exposure (95th percentile of daily mean temperature) was positively associated with newly diagnosed TB (RR = 1.218, 95% CI = 1.171, 1.267). In contrast, extreme cold exposure (fifth percentile of daily mean temperature) was negatively associated with newly diagnosed TB (RR = 0.837, 95% CI = 0.784, 0.893). Additionally, a greater DTR (95th percentile) was positively associated with newly diagnosed TB compared with the median DTR (RR = 1.320, 95% CI = 1.153, 1.512). These associations remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSION: Environmental temperature conditions are significantly associated with TB diagnosis. These findings suggest that temperature variability may influence the timing of TB diagnosis and highlight the importance of incorporating meteorological information into climate-sensitive TB surveillance and public health preparedness.

From test result to surveillance record: A narrative review of malaria RDT data quality in African health information systems.
PURPOSE: Malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) generate information used for clinical care and routine surveillance. However, surveillance reliability depends not only on whether a test correctly identifies infection but also on whether the observed result is recorded, aggregated, transmitted, and interpreted accurately. This review aimed to examine weaknesses in the pathway from malaria RDT results to routine surveillance data and identify practical approaches to improving data quality. METHODS: A structured narrative search of PubMed, Google Scholar, and World Health Organization resources was conducted for English-language publications issued from January 2010 to 10 September 2026. Search terms combined "malaria," "rapid diagnostic test," "routine health information system," "health management information system," "HMIS," "DHIS2," "data quality," "recording," "reporting," "completeness," "concordance," and "timeliness." Empirical studies from African settings were prioritized. Non-African evidence was included only when it offered potentially transferable implementation lessons. Findings were synthesized according to the stages of the data pathway and the dimensions of data quality examined. RESULTS: Evidence from Kenya, Senegal, Uganda, and a multicountry African evaluation identified incomplete reporting, discordance between source registers and DHIS2, aggregation errors, ambiguous zero and missing values, inconsistent indicator definitions, and limited feedback to healthcare facilities. Missing counts of people tested remove the denominator needed to interpret test positivity and can make changes in testing practices appear to be changes in malaria transmission. Standardized indicators, routine source verification, supportive supervision, and interoperable offline-capable digital tools may improve data quality, although their effects vary by setting. Automated RDT readers are promising but require further evaluation of feasibility, equity, governance, and sustainability. CONCLUSION: Malaria surveillance depends on both the validity of the original diagnostic result and the integrity of the subsequent information pathway. Data-quality interventions should be selected according to the point of failure, supported by local evidence, and evaluated before large-scale implementation.

Postoperative Candida auris Bloodstream Infection Following Cardiac Surgery: Diagnostic Delay and Serial Changes in Azole MIC Values: A Case Report.
BACKGROUND: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen associated with healthcare-associated outbreaks and invasive infections, particularly in critically ill patients. Early recognition remains challenging due to nonspecific clinical presentations and overlap with bacterial infections. Postoperative bloodstream infection due to C. auris, especially following cardiac surgery, is still relatively uncommon and may be underrecognized in clinical practice. CASE PRESENTATION: A 69-year-old man developed persistent fever, dyspnea, and bilateral postoperative pulmonary infiltrates after modified Morrow surgery and bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement. The pulmonary findings were clinically diagnosed as severe pneumonia, although imaging was nonspecific and also raised the possibility of pulmonary edema or heart failure. Despite broad-spectrum anti-infective therapy, his condition did not improve. Three separate catheter-drawn blood cultures collected on 21, 24, and 28 July 2025 subsequently yielded Candida auris, confirming candidemia. No respiratory specimen yielded C. auris; therefore, the pulmonary abnormalities were considered concurrent with, rather than microbiologically attributable to, the bloodstream infection. Antifungal susceptibility testing showed persistently high fluconazole MICs, while itraconazole and voriconazole MICs increased in the third isolate. Because validated C. auris-specific clinical breakpoints were unavailable for these agents, the MIC findings were interpreted descriptively. Following adjustment of antifungal therapy and continued supportive care, the patient became afebrile, achieved clinical stabilization, and had a negative follow-up blood culture before discharge. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of Candida auris bloodstream infection in postoperative patients, where clinical features may mimic bacterial pneumonia. Persistent fever unresponsive to empirical antimicrobial therapy should prompt early consideration of invasive fungal infection. Timely microbiological diagnosis and appropriate antifungal treatment are essential for improving outcomes. Increased awareness of C. auris infection in surgical and hospitalized patients is critical for early recognition and effective management.

Prevalence and Type Distribution of Malaria Among Children in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
BACKGROUND: Malaria remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children in sub-Saharan Africa. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the prevalence and type distribution of malaria among children in Ethiopia and species-specific patterns. METHODS: All appropriate databases and gray literature were searched to find relevant articles. Studies reporting the prevalence of malaria among children were included. The quality of each study was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment Scale (NOS). Data were extracted using Microsoft Excel 2016, and analysis was done using STATA 16.0 statistical software. The pooled prevalence and its associated factors of malaria were determined using a random effect model. Heterogeneity between studies was assessed using the Cochrane Q-test statistics and I 2 test. Furthermore, publication bias was checked by the visual inspection of the funnel plot and using Egger's and Begg's statistical tests. Subgroup analyses were conducted by region and parasite species. RESULTS: The pooled prevalence of malaria among children in Ethiopia was 17.96% (95% CI: 11.92-24.01). Subgroup analysis showed significant regional variation (p < 0.001), with the highest prevalence in Afar (41.90%) and the lowest in Benishangul-Gumuz (3.90%). Plasmodium falciparum was the dominant species (59%), followed by Plasmodium vivax (35%) and mixed infections (6%). Evidence of publication bias and small-study effects was observed; however, sensitivity analysis indicated that the overall estimate was robust. Species-wise, pooled proportions were P. falciparum (0.59; 95% CI: 0.59-0.60), P. vivax (0.35; 95% CI: 0.34-0.35), and mixed infections (0.06; 95% CI: 0.04-0.08). CONCLUSION: Malaria remains a major public health challenge among Ethiopian children, with significant regional and species variation. Strengthened, region-specific malaria control strategies are essential to reduce transmission and improve child health outcomes.

Longitudinal dynamics of angiopoietin-1, angiopoietin-2 and soluble thrombomodulin during recovery from paediatric cerebral malaria in Ghana.
Cerebral malaria (CM) remains a leading contributor to paediatric mortality and long-term neurocognitive sequelae in sub-Saharan Africa, driven by a complex interplay between Plasmodium falciparum sequestration and host endothelial dysfunction. Clinical recovery is typically defined by parasite clearance and neurological improvement; however, the temporal relationship between vascular restoration and symptomatic resolution remains inadequately characterized. This study aimed to delineate the recovery kinetics of angiopoietin imbalance and soluble thrombomodulin (sTM) in CM and determine whether these pathways resolve in a coordinated or sequential manner. In this prospective longitudinal cohort study, we assessed 30 Ghanaian children with CM, 30 with uncomplicated malaria (UM) and 34 age-matched healthy controls. Serial measurements of angiopoietin-1 (ANG1), angiopoietin-2 (ANG2) and sTM were performed with CM at admission, coma recovery, and on days 7 and 14 thereafter, and UM at presentation and on days 7 and 14. Among CM cases, abnormal ANG2:ANG1 ratios increased from 10% at admission to 53% at coma recovery, then declined to ≤12% by day 14 thereafter. Abnormal sTM levels decreased more gradually, from 71 to 15% over the same period, suggesting a temporal dissociation between functional endothelial stabilization and structural endothelial repair. UM displayed milder, transient sTM elevations, which resolved more rapidly. These findings reveal a lag between clinical stabilization and biomarker normalization, suggesting a post-treatment window of microvascular vulnerability. Concurrent monitoring of ANG and sTM may provide complementary mechanistic insights into malaria pathophysiology and inform risk stratification, longitudinal monitoring, and the development of endothelial-targeted adjunctive therapies for paediatric malaria.

rLci5 and rKDDR: Recombinant antigens with high diagnostic potential for human visceral leishmaniasis.
Human visceral leishmaniasis (HVL) is a major public health threat given its broad geographic distribution and potentially fatal course, underscoring the need for early and accurate diagnosis. This study evaluated the performance of the recombinant proteins rLci5 and rKDDR-plus (a kinesin-derived degenerate repeat recombinant protein) for the serological diagnosis of HVL. Indirect ELISAs using rLci5 and rKDDR-plus were standardized with different antigen concentrations, primary and secondary antibody dilutions, and peroxidase-conjugated Protein. The standardized indirect ELISAs were evaluated alongside the LSH Ab ECO Teste, a commercial rK39-based rapid immunochromatographic test, using a panel of human serum samples with confirmed HVL-positive (n = 59) and HVL-negative (n = 81) status, as well as sera from individuals with other infections (n = 85). The reference standard for positivity in HVL diagnosis of serum panel was a positive parasitological examination of bone marrow aspirate, either alone or in combination with a positive rK39 rapid test; HVL-negative status was defined by negative results using the same criteria. Results were normalized using the reactivity index (RI). Diagnostic performance was assessed by sensitivity, specificity, ROC curves analysis, McNemar's test, and Cohen's Kappa index. ELISA-rLci5 showed 91.5% sensitivity, 97.5% specificity, whereas ELISA-rLci5 using Protein A showed 89.9% sensitivity, and 95.0% specificity. ELISA-rKDDR-plus presented 98.3% sensitivity, 98.8% specificity; ELISA-rKDDR-plus using the Protein A showed 98.3% sensitivity, and 98.8% specificity. Although protein A increased mean optical density values, it did not translate into improved diagnostic accuracy. The LSH Ab ECO Teste showed 91.5% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Both recombinant antigens showed similar diagnostic performance of the LSH Ab ECO Teste, a rK39-based rapid test used in Brazil. Protein A proved to be a viable alternative to conventional secondary antibodies, increasing signal intensity, but not influencing the diagnostic performance. These findings support rLci5 and rKDDR-plus as promising candidates for improved HVL serodiagnosis.

Geographical Variation in Antimalarial Drug Resistance Marker Prevalence across the Southern African Elimination Eight Region.
Global efforts to control and eliminate malaria are threatened by antimalarial drug resistance. The WHO recommends molecular surveillance of resistance markers as a complementary approach to therapeutic efficacy studies. Here, the first regional analysis of antimalarial resistance markers across six southern African countries spanning diverse transmission intensities and geographies is reported. Dried blood spots, collected from rapid diagnostic test-positive individuals in Angola, Eswatini, Namibia, and Zambia in 2023, Mozambique in 2022, and South Africa between 2022 and 2024 using a standardized collection method, were analyzed using a Plasmodium falciparum-targeted amplicon sequencing protocol. The distribution of resistance markers was spatially heterogeneous. Validated markers of artemisinin partial resistance (ART-R) were rare. However, more than 30% of samples from eastern Namibia and Zambia's Western and Central Provinces carried the candidate kelch13 P441L ART-R marker. Other ART-R markers (kelch13 R515K, P553L, P574L, A675V) were detected at a prevalence rate 99%) across all countries, whereas the chloroquine resistance marker K76T, in the chloroquine resistance transporter (crt) was nearly absent in most districts. The sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance dihydropteroate synthase (dhps)-dihydrofolate reductase quintuple mutation was approaching fixation (>95%) in 35% of districts. Northern Angola was a clear outlier, with a lower dhps K540E prevalence (≤20%) but a higher crt K76T prevalence (48% to 56%). This pronounced spatial heterogeneity underscores the need for timely high-resolution local resistance data generation and sharing to safeguard antimalarial drug efficacy and guide malaria control and elimination strategies across the region.

Mobility hinders malaria elimination goals in the Brazilian Amazon.
INTRODUCTION: Human mobility across the Brazilian Amazon-shaped by frontier development, land-use change, mining activity, and climatic shocks-remains a major barrier to malaria elimination. Brazil aims to eliminate Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) by 2030 and Plasmodium vivax (Pv) by 2035, yet malaria incidence has plateaued since 2020. We quantify parasite-specific mobility and assess how importations drive malaria reintroduction and reestablishment in areas approaching elimination. METHODS: We analyzed 5,521,411 de-identified malaria cases from Sivep-Malaria (2003-2023) across 808 municipalities in the nine-state Brazilian Amazon. We (i) used multivariable monthly sequence analysis to classify "Municipal Malaria Importation Trajectories" (MMITs) using local/imported composition, incidence per 1,000, and source/sink network typologies; (ii) characterized mobility networks by parasite species and locality type (rural, urban, settlement, indigenous, mining); and (iii) developed a parasite-specific rule-based classification procedure to identify reintroduction, and defined reestablishment as sustained local transmission. RESULTS: Sequence analysis produced five MMIT clusters, spanning municipalities nearing elimination to areas with sustained high local transmission and distinct profiles of declining transmission with intense vs. moderate importation. Overall, 959,281 cases (17.38%) were imported. Cases were predominantly Pv (81.68%), with Pf comprising 17.15%; Pf was more common among imported than locally acquired infections. Mobility patterns shifted after mid-2020: by 2023, > 50% of exported cases originated in mining localities despite ~0.2% land coverage, with Pf importation increasingly concentrated in municipalities overlapping the Yanomami Indigenous Land. From 2006-2023, we identified 63 Pf and 221 Pv reintroduced locally acquired cases following ≥3 years of zero local transmission, leading to reestablishment in 6 and 23 municipalities, respectively, and generating 864 subsequent Pf and 6,524 subsequent Pv cases. Post-reintroduction transmission persisted for long periods (mean 762 days for Pf; 815 days for Pv). CONCLUSION: Malaria elimination in Brazil is increasingly hindered by parasite-specific mobility, especially linked to mining-indigenous confluences, and by repeated reintroduction in receptive municipalities nearing elimination (notably along the arc of deforestation). Mobility-informed surveillance and targeted reactive strategies are essential to achieve and sustain Brazil's malaria elimination goals.

Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid Cellularity Reflects Peripheral Cytopenias and Fungal Burden but Not Short-Term Outcomes in Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis.
We characterized leukocyte profiles in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) of 63 patients with hematologic malignancy and culture-documented invasive pulmonary aspergillosis and evaluated associations with peripheral blood leukocyte counts, Aspergillus burden, respiratory coinfections, and clinical outcomes. BALF cellularity mirrored peripheral cytopenias yet increased with higher Aspergillus burden and respiratory coinfections, consistent with both systemic immune availability and local inflammatory stimuli. However, BALF cellularity was not independently associated with 42-day mortality, which was driven by persistent neutropenia and critical illness. These findings suggest BALF cellularity may not be an independent determinant of short-term outcomes but rather reflects underlying host and disease context.

Candidozyma auris in the United States: insights from the National Association of Long-Term Hospitals Network.
OBJECTIVE: Understand current prevention practices used for Candidozyma auris and identify target areas for improvement. DESIGN: Electronic survey. SETTING: Long-term acute care hospitals (LTACHs). PARTICIPANTS: National Association of Long-Term Hospitals (NALTH) network facilities located in the United States. METHODS: REDCap survey distributed by email to 56 facilities in the NALTH network exploring knowledge and perceptions related to C. auris screening methods, prevention practices, barriers to prevention, and tools needed to improve containment. RESULTS: Among 33 responses from 56 LTACHs, 23 (70%) had ever identified at least one case of C. auris infection or colonization. Eighteen (54%) reported identifying cases of C. auris within the past three months and nine (27%) had experienced suspected within-facility transmission. All facilities employed multimodal approaches for C. auris infection prevention.
