The current study examines the associations among different dimensions of past large-scale crisis-related stress (i.e., relationships and academic life, social isolation, and fear of contagion during the COVID-19 pandemic), perceived family support, and current individual deviant behaviors among youths, while also investigating indirect associations through deviant peer association. METHOD: a community sample of 606 adolescents and emerging adults (Mage = 18.52 ± 2.89; %F = 48.8%) completed an online survey. Path analysis was employed to examine the relationships among the variables of interest. RESULTS: the assessed model showed adequate fit to the data, accounting for 59.9% of variance in individual deviant behaviors. Stress due to social isolation was positively associated with individual deviant behaviors both directly and indirectly through deviant peer association, whereas stress due to fear of contagion and perceived support from family were negatively associated with individual deviant behaviors both directly and indirectly through deviant peer association. CONCLUSIONS: the current findings highlight the need to investigate the interplay of specific stress experiences, family dynamics, peer influences, and individuals' endorsement of deviance following a large-scale crisis. Results provide insights for future research and preventive efforts targeting contemporary youth deviance.

Experiences and Expressions of Stress Among US Food Industry Workers During the 2020 Covid-19 Pandemic.
INTRODUCTION: The Coronavirus pandemic (Covid-19) exposed legacies of deep inequality, including who could afford protection from exposure. As part of the essential workforce, food industry workers continued fully in-person work throughout the pandemic and associated shutdowns. OBJECTIVE: To qualitatively examine US food worker experiences and stressors during the 2020 Covid-19 pandemic. METHODS: Thirty-four open-ended phone interviews were conducted from May through September 2020 with people who grew (n = 2), processed (n = 5), cooked (n = 9), sold (n = 17), and/or delivered (n = 5) food in the United States. Audio recordings were transcribed and coded for themes of stress, health, and workplace environment. RESULTS: Interviewees reported widespread disruption across US food system workplaces (e.g., reduced staffing, role changes, and increased workloads). Expressions of stress clustered into 4 themes: financial strain, concern about getting/transmitting Covid-19, sustained uncertainty, and overburdening. Workers' experiences revealed a need for self-reliance while their work and life environments were repeatedly overhauled. CONCLUSION: Results align with similar investigations into food workers' stress and limited protections before, during, and after the pandemic. The study contributes evidence for stronger worker support systems and positions food workers' lived experiences as vital to research and policy.

Resurgence of Sexually Transmitted Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Men Who Have Sex With Men Living With HIV.
In 2023-2025, HCV transmission in men who have sex with men (MSM) living with HIV in Hong Kong resurged. This study aims to assess the epidemiologic patterns between 2011 and 2025. Among 288 MSM with sexually acquired HCV infection, 73% were diagnosed at least 12 months after HIV diagnosis, and 98% had ever achieved HIV viral load suppression. Comparing with Period 1 (2015-2022) featuring a large HCV genotype 3a cluster (89 diagnoses) and a few smaller HCV genotype 1a clusters (size of 2 to 13), Period 2 (2023-2025) was dominated by two HCV genotype 1a clusters (7 and 16 new diagnoses). Transmission of genotype 3a viruses subsided in Period 2, with only 3 new diagnoses. Comparing with Period 1, a higher proportion of MSM with HCV diagnoses in Period 2 self-reported sexualised injecting drug use (OR = 3.82, 95% CI 1.59-9.20) and HCV direct-acting antivirals therapy (no treatment as reference group, OR = 3.72, 95%CI 1.82-7.60). The epidemic rebound by a different HCV genotype was likely contributed by increased engagement in chemsex and post-COVID-19 population mobility.

Respiratory Viral Infections in Febrile Children With Lymphoreticular Malignancies: A Single-Centre Descriptive Study.
Children with lymphoreticular malignancies are highly vulnerable to respiratory viral infections (RVIs) because of disease- and chemotherapy-related immunosuppression, yet data on their epidemiology, clinical spectrum, and outcomes from resource-limited settings remain scarce. This study aimed to characterize the seasonal distribution, clinical presentation, and outcomes of RVIs other than SARS-CoV-2 in febrile children with lymphoreticular malignancies at a tertiary care centre in India. In this prospective, descriptive, cross-sectional study (May 2023-November 2024), 33 children under 12 years of age with lymphoreticular malignancies were enrolled at a tertiary care centre in Delhi, India, contributing 70 febrile episodes with respiratory symptoms. All episodes were screened for SARS-CoV-2 by rapid antigen test at admission, independent of the viral PCR panel, and none tested positive. Nasopharyngeal swabs were analyzed by multiplex real-time PCR (TRUPCR® Respiratory Viral Pathogen Panel Kit, 3B BlackBio, Bhopal, India; CFX96™, Bio-Rad, Hercules, CA, USA) targeting 18 other respiratory viral pathogens. Respiratory viruses were detected in 34% of episodes (24/70). The most prevalent viruses identified were human coronavirus (HCoV α/β, 21%), human rhinovirus (HRV, 17%), human parainfluenza virus type 3 (HPIV-3, 13%), influenza A (IAV,13%), and human adenovirus (HAdV, 13%). Co-infections occurred in 13% of virus-positive episodes, with HAdV being the predominant co-pathogen. Upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) predominated (87%). Among virus-positive episodes, breathlessness (p = 0.005), URTI/LRTI classification (p < 0.001), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR; p < 0.001), and abnormal chest radiography (p < 0.001) were significantly associated with viral status. Two patients (6%) died, both attributed to lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) caused by human parainfluenza virus type 4 (HPIV-4). The remaining 66% of episodes were PCR-negative. No SARS-CoV-2 was detected in this cohort at any point during the study period. In approximately one-third of febrile episodes of children with hematologic malignancies, a viral pathogen could be detected. Both fatalities in this cohort were associated with HPIV-4-related LRTI; although the numbers are small, this finding warrants clinical attention and continued epidemiological surveillance in this population. Multiplex PCR supports targeted management; prospective, multicentre stewardship studies are needed.

The association between green space, socioeconomic deprivation, and COVID-19 infection: a population-based cross-sectional study.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the association between green space, socioeconomic deprivation, and infection with COVID-19 in Northern Ireland (NI). METHODS: This cross-sectional study included all NI individuals who were tested for COVID-19 in 2020 and 2021 (N = 519,005). Analyses were conducted using multilevel logistic regression models. The proportion of green space was measured within neighborhoods in 2020 and expressed as quintiles. RESULTS: Of the participants, 318,198 (61.31%) had records of testing positive for COVID-19. The results indicated that individuals living in areas with higher woodland cover had lower odds of reporting a positive COVID-19 test result (e.g., fifth quintile: OR = 0.939; 95% CI = 0.894, 0.987). However, individuals living in areas with higher grassland cover had higher odds of reporting a positive COVID-19 test result (e.g., fifth quintile: OR = 1.062; 95% CI = 1.018, 1.108). These associations were stronger in deprived neighborhoods. CONCLUSION: Woodland may provide opportunities for safer social contact while attempting to balance the risk of viral transmission and the potential for positive health behaviors, particularly in more socioeconomically deprived areas. The government should work with urban planners and improve the availability of green spaces as part of future pandemic preparedness strategies.

Distribution, carbapenem resistance and DTR dynamics of ESKAPEEc pathogens from pediatric bloodstream infections in Sichuan Province, 2017-2025: epidemiological characteristics under COVID-19 pandemic and emerging linezolid MIC creep.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the distribution and antimicrobial resistance evolution of ESKAPEEc pathogens causing pediatric bloodstream infections in Sichuan Province across the COVID-19 era, and to systematically evaluate the epidemiology of carbapenem resistance (CR), difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR), and MIC drift in vancomycin and linezolid, thereby addressing a long-standing gap in longitudinal pediatric multidrug-resistant surveillance in Southwest China. METHODS: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted using pediatric blood culture data from 134 healthcare institutions in Sichuan Province between 2017 and 2025. A total of 20,018 isolates were included and stratified into pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and DTR classification were interpreted according to CLSI M100 (35th edition) criteria. Statistical analyses were performed using WHONET 5.6 and SPSS 26.0. RESULTS: A total of 5,236 ESKAPEEc isolates were identified, accounting for 26.2% of all bloodstream isolates. Detection rates increased during the pandemic period and declined thereafter. Carbapenem resistance rates in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae were significantly higher in the post-pandemic period compared with the pre-pandemic baseline. The overall DTR prevalence was 8.6%, with Acinetobacter baumannii exhibiting the highest DTR burden (87.3%) despite a declining temporal trend, whereas DTR in K. pneumoniae increased progressively over time. Reliance on CR criteria alone failed to identify a substantial proportion of DTR-positive E. coli isolates. All Staphylococcus aureus isolates remained susceptible to vancomycin and linezolid in vitro, with stable vancomycin MIC distributions; however, a high-MIC subpopulation among linezolid-treated MRSA isolates increased significantly over time (r=0.767, P = 0.016). Distinct age-stratified differences were observed in both pathogen distribution and resistance profiles. CONCLUSIONS: The COVID-19 pandemic exerted a bidirectional and sustained impact on the pediatric ESKAPEEc landscape and resistance ecology in Sichuan Province. Post-pandemic escalation of carbapenem resistance persists. The persistently high DTR burden in A. baumannii and early MIC drift toward linezolid in MRSA represent two critical regional threats in pediatric infectious disease management. Regional surveillance systems should incorporate DTR metrics alongside CR monitoring and implement age-stratified, precision-based antimicrobial stewardship strategies.

Parkinson's disease mortality in the United States, 1999-2025: a national multiple-cause-of-death analysis with projections to 2030.
BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder in the United States and a growing driver of late-life disability and death. We characterized U.S. PD-related mortality from 1999 to 2025 and projected it to 2030. METHODS: In this serial cross-sectional analysis of CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data, PD-related deaths in adults aged ≥45 years were identified using ICD-10 code G20 recorded anywhere on the death certificate. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 were decomposed by joinpoint regression and projected to 2030 using a log-scale ensemble weighted by rolling-origin back-test error, stratified by sex, age, race and ethnicity, census region, and degree of urbanization. RESULTS: Among 1,149,731 PD-related deaths (59.8% men), the overall AAMR was 32.74 in 1999 and 41.03 (95% CI 40.70-41.35) in 2025, but the full-window trend was not significant (average annual percent change 0.56%; -0.10 to 1.22; p = 0.099). A steep 2014-2021 rise (annual percent change 4.70%; p < 0.001) was followed by a non-significant decline, negative in 13 of the 14 strata observed through 2025. COVID-19 was co-listed on 10.15% of PD-mentioned deaths in 2020 and 0.79% in 2025, accounting for 58% of the 2019-2020 rise and 55% of the 2021-2024 decline; excluding these deaths the series was close to flat (39.88 in 2020; 40.71 in 2025). The projected 2030 AAMR was 41.73 (95% prediction interval 33.97-51.27), essentially unchanged from 2025; however, deaths are projected to rise from 62,162 to 70,825, with approximately 87% of the increase attributable to population aging. Restricting to PD as the underlying cause gave a steeper increase (+86.2% versus +25.3%), arguing against ascertainment drift. Between 1999-2007 and 2017-2025, nursing home deaths fell from 49.24 to 35.48%, while home deaths rose from 19.37 to 34.93% and hospice deaths from 0.88 to 8.25%. CONCLUSION: Age-adjusted PD-related mortality did not change significantly between 1999 and 2025. Most of the post-2021 decline reflects the unwinding of COVID-19 co-listing rather than an improvement in underlying mortality, a mechanism that is now nearly exhausted. Projections indicate a plateau in the standardized rate, while absolute deaths rise with population aging, and end-of-life care has shifted from institutions to homes.

Procedural safeguards in remote criminal hearings.
INTRODUCTION: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, criminal courts across the United States have started to conduct more remote proceedings using video teleconferencing technology. Although remote criminal hearings are often more cost-efficient and accessible than traditional in-person hearings, they introduce a set of new challenges to upholding defendants' rights, such as the right to effective attorney representation and due process. The new hearing format also creates operational difficulties, such as technology malfunctions and the management of documents and exhibits. METHODS: This study examines the procedural safeguards established in current state and federal laws and regulations for remote criminal proceedings. RESULT: A review of legal codes shows that, in most states, the statutory procedural safeguards are either inadequate or too superficial to address the challenges introduced by remote criminal proceedings. DISCUSSION: The limitations identified in this study raise concerns about whether remote proceedings can fulfill equivalent standards as in-person proceedings. This study calls for legislators and court administrators to implement stronger procedural safeguards when authorizing remote criminal hearings.

Homicide Mortality Among Female Adolescents and Women Aged 15 to 44 Years and US State Abortion Policies.
IMPORTANCE: Homicide is a leading cause of death among female adolescents and women aged 15 to 44 years (hereinafter, women of reproductive age) in the US. Whether homicide trajectories differed across state abortion policy environments after the COVID-19 surge and the Dobbs v Jackson Women's Health Organization (hereinafter, Dobbs) decision is unclear. OBJECTIVES: To characterize national homicide trends among women of reproductive age and assess whether post-2022 trajectories in homicide mortality among women of reproductive age diverged between states with and without sustained abortion bans. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This quasi-experimental study used national interrupted time series and comparative interrupted time series analyses of homicide mortality from January 1, 2016, through December 31, 2024, among women of reproductive age. EXPOSURE: The COVID-19 pandemic and sustained state abortion bans after Dobbs. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcome was monthly homicide deaths. The population-offset Poisson model estimated differential post-Dobbs changes in homicide rates. Absolute rate differences, excess deaths, and years of life lost were estimated from fitted and counterfactual Poisson models. States with sustained total or near-total abortion bans after Dobbs were compared with states without such bans; states with partial or legally fluid restrictions were excluded. A triple-difference analysis comparing those aged 15 to 29 years with those aged 45 to 59 years served as a negative-control analysis. RESULTS: The analysis included 19 118 homicide deaths among women of reproductive age. Nationally, homicide increased sharply during the COVID-19 surge and subsequently decreased, with no clear national level or slope change beginning in July 2022. In policy-stratified analyses, however, homicide trajectories diverged. After July 2022, the exposed states (those with total or near-total abortion bans) vs unexposed states homicide monthly rate ratio (RR) was 1.006 (95% CI, 1.000-1.011; P = .03). Across calendar years 2023 and 2024, the fitted homicide rate in exposed states was higher than the modeled counterfactual (2023: RR, 1.07; 95% bootstrap interval, 1.01-1.13; and 2024: RR, 1.15; 95% bootstrap interval, 1.03-1.29). This corresponded to an estimated 48 excess deaths (95% bootstrap interval, 11-81) in 2023 and 87 excess deaths (95% bootstrap interval, 20-149) in 2024. A triple-difference model indicated greater post-Dobbs divergence among those aged 15 to 29 years than those aged 45 to 59 years (monthly ratio of RRs, 1.017; 95% CI, 1.000-1.034; P = .046); placebo Dobbs dates yielded nonsignificant results. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, national homicide mortality rates among women of reproductive age returned toward prepandemic levels after COVID-19, but post-2022 trajectories diverged across state abortion policy environments. The findings suggest that national improvements in homicide mortality rates among women of reproductive age may mask less-favorable homicide trends among women of reproductive age in states with sustained abortion bans.

Qualitative Exploration of Need for Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health Care and Service Pathways Readiness During Pandemic in Nepal.
BACKGROUND: COVID-19 pandemic disrupted adolescents' access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services for adolescents in Nepal. This study explored adolescents' and health care provider's perspectives on how the COVID-19 pandemic affected adolescents' SRH information and services, SRH-related behaviours, and factors that strengthen care and service pathways during the pandemic in Nepal. METHODS: This study used qualitative methods and adapted the social cognitive theory as an analytical framework to explore individual, social and environmental influences on adolescents' sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information and services pathways during the COVID-19 pandemic. A total of 86 participants were included in the study, including 64 adolescents (15-19 years) and 22 service providers. For this, total of six focus group discussions, 12 in-depth interviews and 22 key informant interviews were conducted. Thematic analysis was conducted to identify, analyse and interpret the data. RESULT: The study findings showed that COVID-19 disrupted adolescents' SRH information and services pathways through interconnected environmental, social and individual factors. School closures reduced access to school-based SRH information and opportunities to interact with teachers and peers, while interruptions in service delivery compromised adolescent's pathways to SRH information and services. Adolescents reported changes in sexual behaviours and mental health effects during pandemic. Strengthening adolescents' pathways to SRH information and service during crises requires provider's capacity strengthening, conducting virtual child club programmes for self-help and social interaction, digital information and psychosocial services, and prioritising coordinated interventions among stakeholders. CONCLUSION: Maintaining adolescent SRH care during public health emergencies requires an ecosystem approach addressing individual, social and environmental factors together. Adolescents' SRH needs during public health emergencies extend beyond the availability of clinical services and include opportunities for emotional, social and trusted support. Strengthening adolescents' self-efficacy, conducive social environments, and community-based actors such as Female Community Health Volunteers (FCHVs) along with accessible, confidential and adolescent-responsive services, helps maintain continuity of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) information and care during emergencies. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This manuscript is developed from the study done under the larger project that was designed to address sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) of adolescents and women in the Sindhupalchowk district. The study adopted a participatory approach through active engagement with adolescents, community actors, health service providers, and local stakeholders throughout the research process. Different consultation meetings were held with these stakeholders to identify research priorities, refining research questions and development of study tools to ensure contextual relevance and responsiveness to community SRHR needs. The findings further emphasise the importance of community-based SRHR approaches, strengthening local actors and volunteers and fostering adolescent self-efficacy in supporting adolescent responsive services during public health emergencies.

Unpacking the Impact and Experience of Working With Lived Experience Partners in Mental Health Research-Exploring Research Team and Public Partner Perspectives.
INTRODUCTION: Patient and Public Involvement (PPI) in mental health research is encouraged by funders in the United Kingdom, supported by guidance and best practice standards. This includes a commitment to learning and understanding impact. This paper explores the experiences of individuals who worked together for 7 years within an intervention study to understand differing perspectives and conceptualisations of how PPI shaped the research study. METHODS: Using an instrumental case study design, qualitative data were collected in three workshops: university-based study team (n = 4), Lived Experience Advisory Panel (LEAP) (n = 5), and mixed composition (n = 8). Two workshops explored study set up and intervention development, the other explored a qualitative process evaluation study within the randomised controlled trial. RESULTS: We recognised impact as tangible and practical, both facilitated and hindered through relational connections which contribute to ways of working that frame research. Data evidenced that both LEAP and study team members experienced a journey of learning and development in doing PPI that included friction and 'choppy waters'. The study team valued lived experience partners and the knowledge and expertise they brought from the outset. However, issues such as low confidence in doing PPI among study team, changes in PPI team structure, COVID-19 pandemic moving work online and challenging some LEAP members over the relevance of their own lived experiences to the study, meant the journey was at times difficult. DISCUSSION: Impact is about much more than quantifiable economic value. It is nuanced and benefits from multi-perspective explorations that move beyond surface-level practical observations to achieve deeper understanding of how lived experience expertise shapes complex research processes, across extended time periods, including the role of team dynamics. CONCLUSION: PPI in research requires flexibility and open-mindedness to create a positive inclusive team culture and benefits from regular reflective learning with open feedback, so that timely tangible changes can be agreed. PUBLIC CONTRIBUTIONS: This study was designed by LEAP members and the PPI study coordinator employed at a mental health charity. Workshops were co-facilitated by two people working from a lived experience perspective who are lead authors on this paper. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN93895792.

The α2-Subunit Preferring GABA Positive Allosteric Modulator, N-Desmethyl-Clobazam in Peripheral Neuropathic Pain Patients: Results of a Phase IIa Randomised Placebo-Controlled Ascending Dose Study.
BACKGROUND: N-desmethyl clobazam (NDMC), an α2-preferring-α1-sparing-GABAA modulator, was promising in preclinical models and Phase I studies, demonstrating antihyperalgesic properties without associated sedation. This Phase IIa trial aimed at exploring the effect of NDMC in peripheral neuropathic pain (NP) patients. METHOD: Randomised, ascending doses, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, evaluating 40, 60, 120 mg of NDMC. Primary outcome was the change in weekly average daily pain (WADP) on a Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) from baseline (V1) to the end of the study (V7). Secondary outcomes included sedation (subjective NRS), quality of life (SF36), global and patient impression of change (CGI, PCGI). PK and safety data were collected. The study was prematurely terminated due to recruitment challenges related to the COVID-19 pandemic. RESULTS: Thirty-three out of the planned 76 patients were enrolled. The mean reduction in WADP from V1 to V7 was -1.53 points for placebo and -1.99 across all NDMC doses (delta = 0.46, p = 0.47). When analysed according to NDMC plasma concentrations, the mean WADP reduction was 1.53 (SD 1.58) for placebo 1.78 (SD 1.79) for NDMC < 1000 ng/mL, and 2.40 (SD 1.46) for NDMC ≥ 1000 ng/mL. The prevalence of 30% pain reduction was 38.5% (placebo) and 83.3% (NDMC ≥ 1000 ng/mL). Logistic regression analysis indicated that NDMC ≥ 1000 ng/nL was predictive of a 30% pain reduction (odds ratio = 12.5, p = 0.04). NDMC was well tolerated. CONCLUSION: Despite being underpowered, this study revealed a consistent exposure-response relationship along with a favourable safety profile for NDMC in patients with NP. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrial.gov (NCT03375034); kofam.ch (SNCTP000003517). SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This work presenting the Phase II data of the new antihyperalgesic compound, N-Desmethyl-Clobazam (NDMC) in peripheral neuropathic pain patients support further investigation into the role in modulating GABAergic pathways as a potential therapeutic target for neuropathic pain. This objective is particularly relevant given the limited efficacy of standard pharmacological treatments for neuropathic pain, which often requires a multimodal approach targeting the multiple pathways involved in pain pathophysiology.

High levels of domestic transmission and drug resistance -analysis of national surveillance data for shigellosis, the Netherlands, 2018 to 2024.
BACKGROUNDAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) among Shigella species is increasing, which is concerning. Strengthening surveillance is key to obtaining accurate, timely and actionable data on shigellosis.AIMWe aimed to describe Dutch national shigellosis surveillance data from 2018 to 2024, spanning the implementation of national genomic surveillance in 2022.METHODSWe described notified shigellosis cases and used logistic regression models to analyse associations between shigellosis and age, sex, year of infection, province, MSM (men who have sex with men) association, travel status, severity of disease and Shigella species.RESULTSIn 2018-2024, 3,020 shigellosis cases were notified. Incidence of shigellosis decreased during the COVID-19 pandemic years 2020-2021 but returned to pre-pandemic incidence in 2023 and 2024. Most cases were males (n = 1,887; 62.5%). Of the 1,731 cases with available data, 732 (42.3%) reported recent contact with MSM, representing 24.2% of all shigellosis cases. The proportion of extensive drug resistant (XDR) isolates increased from 2018 (1/58) to 2023 (24/109; 22.0%) (p < 0.001). Cases were more likely to be part of a cluster if they reported a recent MSM contact (p < 0.001) or harboured an XDR isolate (p < 0.001). Cases with recent MSM contact were more likely to harbour an XDR strain (p < 0.001).CONCLUSIONImplementation of genomic surveillance facilitated detection of clusters, provided more timely data on AMR and allowed for more detailed analyses of risk factors for Shigella transmission. Continued intervention efforts promoting hygiene and raising awareness on shigellosis and AMR are important to curb the increase of XDR shigellosis.

Genome-Wide Association Studies of Hospitalized Influenza Identify Four Risk Loci and Reveal Shared and Unique Genetic Factors Compared With COVID-19.
BACKGROUND: Influenza remains a significant global health burden, potentially leading to hospitalization and mortality. Although previous studies have explored genetic susceptibility to influenza infection, the genetic basis of influenza hospitalization and its relationship with respiratory diseases like COVID-19 remain poorly understood. METHODS: We performed a binary GWAS of hospitalized influenza using UK Biobank data (UKBB; 1037 cases/404,108 controls) and then meta-analyzed results with the FinnGen GWAS, yielding 11,171 cases and 782,400 controls. A time-to-event GWAS in UKBB was also performed to identify genetic factors underlying the timing (age) of first influenza hospitalization. p-values from both analyses were integrated by the harmonic mean p-value (HMP) method to enhance association detection. Further differentiation and colocalization analyses with COVID-19 investigated their distinct and shared genetic features. An integrative framework combining functional annotations, multi-omics analyses, and phenome-wide scans prioritized key risk and differential genes. RESULTS: The binary GWAS meta-analysis identified three loci (ST6GAL1, AASDHPPT, SPATS2L) associated with hospitalization risk. The time-to-event GWAS recognized UGT2B4 as linked to hospitalization timing. HMP analysis, which combines evidence across the binary and time-to-event analyses, identified ST6GAL1 (p = 3 × 10-9) and UGT2B4 (p = 3.63 × 10-8) as genome-wide significant; however, each signal was driven predominantly by one component test, ST6GAL1 by the binary meta-analysis (meta p = 1.5 × 10-9), and UGT2B4 by the time-to-event analysis (SPACox p = 1.82 × 10-8), rather than showing independent support from both analyses. Differentiation analysis identified 29 loci and two tissues distinguishing influenza from COVID-19, whereas analysis of shared association signals (cofdr) highlighted candidate shared genetic factors, including ST6GAL1 and ICAM5 (gene-level PPA ≥ 0.9). CONCLUSIONS: This study uncovers the genetic architectures of hospitalized influenza. It also highlights genetic differences and similarities with COVID-19, providing hypothesis-generating insights that may inform future functional and therapeutic research.

Telemedicine and the Attractiveness of a Family Medicine Career Among Hungarian Medical Students: Implications for the Digital Health Primary Care Workforce.
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Telemedicine expanded rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic and is now embedded in primary care, a field facing an acute workforce crisis. Whether it could make a general practitioner (GP) career more attractive to future physicians has largely been unexplored. We assessed fifth-year medical students' perceptions of telemedicine and factors associated with viewing it as increasing the attractiveness of GP work. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 140 of 154 fifth-year students at the University of Debrecen, Hungary (response rate 91%), completed a self-developed, paper-based questionnaire in early 2026. Ordinal data were analysed with non-parametric tests, a composite perceived usefulness score, and binary logistic regression, with Holm-Bonferroni correction for pre-specified comparisons. RESULTS: Awareness was near-universal (98.6%), but self-perceived knowledge was modest and showed no association with usefulness ratings (rho = 0.024, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.19). Synchronous and clinical data modalities were rated more useful than informal text channels, and 82.9% preferred hybrid working. Only 32.1% thought telemedicine would make GP work more attractive; this perception was independently associated with GP career interest (adjusted OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.47-4.57) but not with sex, age, or knowledge. CONCLUSIONS: Telemedicine is viewed as useful but appears to reinforce existing career interest rather than independently attract students to general practice.

Viral Respiratory Infections: COVID-19.
On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic. By late 2024, COVID-19 had become endemic, with regional surges caused by new variants and declining population immunity. Case fatality rates have decreased because of vaccination and the emergence of less virulent variants, but long COVID persists as a public health concern. Because of structural issues, including those related to employment, housing, health care access, and mistrust, minority and low-income individuals are at higher risk for COVID-19 infection and mortality. Preventive strategies include shared decision-making about vaccination for individuals 6 months and older, two vaccine doses for adults 65 and older, and vaccination for pregnant and breastfeeding individuals. COVID-19 can be distinguished from influenza and respiratory syncytial virus infection through testing. Rapid antigen tests are faster but less sensitive than polymerase chain reaction tests. Outpatient care of COVID-19 focuses on symptomatic relief and early antiviral use when indicated. Inpatient treatment involves remdesivir, corticosteroids, interleuken-6 inhibitors, anticoagulation, and respiratory support. Long-term complications of COVID-19 include cardiovascular, pulmonary, neurologic, mental health, and renal conditions. Thrombotic risk peaks during acute infection and remains elevated for up to 1 year. An effective community response to COVID-19 requires equitable vaccine access, integrated care, and rebuilding of patient trust to counter misinformation.

Viral Respiratory Infections: Upper and Lower Respiratory Tract Infections.
Respiratory infections are a major health concern and are divided into upper and lower respiratory tract infections. Upper respiratory tract infections are mostly viral and self-limiting; billions of cases occur globally each year. Lower respiratory tract infections such as pneumonia and bronchitis can cause significant illness, especially in children, older adults, and individuals with comorbidities or immunocompromise. In 2021, lower respiratory tract infections caused more than 2 million deaths globally, mainly in low- and middle-income countries. Preventive measures include hand hygiene, masks, ventilation, vaccination, and pharmacologic prophylaxis. Vaccines for influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus infection are available in the United States. Vaccines for human metapneumovirus, parainfluenza viruses, and human rhinovirus are in development. Differentiating viral from bacterial infections is challenging. Biomarkers such as procalcitonin and C-reactive protein can guide antibiotic use. Treatment of viral respiratory infections is mainly supportive, with use of intranasal decongestants and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Early use of zinc and vitamin C may shorten symptom duration; evidence for vitamin D, probiotics, and echinacea varies. Judicious antibiotic use prevents antimicrobial resistance, and treatment with no or delayed antibiotics is often sufficient. Most viral respiratory infections resolve in 1 to 2 weeks, although coughing may persist longer. Patient education about self-care, prevention, and antibiotic use is key to better outcomes and reduced health care burden.

Global physical activity resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic: an observational study of 5.17 million exercise app users across 65 countries.
INTRODUCTION: Physical activity (PA) is a critical health behaviour often disrupted by public health crises. Prior research has primarily relied on self-reported surveys, limiting timely and scalable insights. This study examines how large-scale digital exercise data can enhance real-time PA prediction and support interventions to strengthen PA resilience during global public health crises. METHODS: We analysed PA data from 5.17 million individuals across 65 countries, collected via a smartphone PA tracking app between January 2019 and June 2021. The dataset includes longitudinal exercise histories, sociodemographic characteristics, geographic locations and social network connections. We developed statistical and machine learning models-including linear regressions, neural networks (NNs) and graph neural networks (GNNs)-to predict weekly PA adherence (defined as at least 150 min of exercise per week in line with WHO recommendations) before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Models predicted each week's adherence using the individual's exercise history from the preceding 1-3 weeks, together with sociodemographic, weather and pandemic-related variables. We also applied surrogate models and econometric analyses to assess the associations of individual and urban-level attributes with PA resilience globally. RESULTS: In a US county subsample where all model classes could be compared (Middlesex County, MA), the GNN achieved the highest predictive performance for weekly PA adherence, with 89.9% accuracy pre-pandemic and 82.1% during the pandemic. At the global level, the NN model demonstrated similar predictive performance (accuracy 87.6% and 82.8%). Personal exercise history was the strongest predictor, improving model accuracy by 20 percentage points, while increased model complexity or the addition of social network features yielded modest gains. Marked global disparities were observed: cities in lower- and upper-middle-income countries experienced greater reductions in PA during the pandemic compared with cities in high-income countries. Females, socially connected individuals and residents in cities with better access to outdoor sports infrastructure were more likely to maintain regular PA during the pandemic. CONCLUSION: Digital PA data can enable accurate, real-time prediction of PA adherence and inform individual and environmental factors influencing global PA resilience during crises. This approach holds promise for informing targeted interventions and urban policy strategies to enhance health resilience and reduce global health disparities.

What is in the Dust? Species-Level Profiling Reveals Pathogenic and Protective Potential of Microbial Communities in Daycare and Home Environments.
Indoor environments are rich in microbial diversity, which is influenced by multiple factors, including human activities, occupancy levels and the presence of pets. Environment-associated taxa were found to be prevalent in daycare and human-associated taxa in home environments during the COVID-19 pandemic, a period marked by profoundly altered social mixing and hygiene practices. In this study, we investigated the structure of microbial communities and their ecological profiles in daycare and home dust in the post-COVID-19 era. Microbial communities in household dust remain more heterogeneous, with a higher prevalence of human-associated species, than daycare samples. Full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing enabled species-level taxonomic resolution, yet approximately 40% of amplicon sequence variants remained unclassified, underscoring the vast, novel microbial diversity within our indoor environments encountered in everyday life. AI-assisted ecological profiling revealed a higher burden of pathogens and opportunistic pathogens in home environments than in daycares. Interestingly, the presence of pets had limited influence on microbial diversity in household dust. Finally, several species with known probiotic properties and immunostimulatory potential were present in both environments, reinforcing the notion that microbial exposure during the critical window of early childhood may confer protection against various non-communicable diseases including asthma, childhood leukaemia and other cancers.

Lactation supports implemented within the Canada Prenatal Nutrition Program: findings from a national survey.
INTRODUCTION: Supporting breastfeeding is integral to the Canada Prenatal Nutrition Program (CPNP), although details on lactation support implementation are limited. This research aimed to assess lactation support delivery by CPNP sites across Canada, excluding Quebec, and how the COVID-19 pandemic affected services. METHODS: From May to July 2023, we conducted a cross-sectional survey; 207 sites were invited to participate. We investigated the types of lactation supports delivered; how and by whom; and the role of site characteristics (locality, Community Action Program for Children funding, breastfeeding clinic on-site, primary healthcare facility on-site) and funding sources (CPNP only, CPNP and other funds, other funds only) on lactation support provision. RESULTS: All respondents (n = 91 sites) reported providing at least one lactation support: 95% offered educational materials, 89% community referrals, 77% personalized support from a community-based provider, 69% live education sessions, 68% breast pumps, 51% peer support programming, 34% personalized support from a board-certified lactation professional, and 34% lactation-related supplies. Most sites continued to offer lactation supports during the COVID-19 pandemic but faced multiple service provision challenges. Availability of lactation supports that required additional resources beyond CPNP core funds varied by site characteristics. To provide lactation supports, particularly personalized support, most sites reported relying heavily on non-CPNP funds (e.g. donations, private funding). CONCLUSION: Lactation support delivery varied widely across CPNP sites, with access differing by site characteristics and external resource availability. Increased programmatic guidance and support of core lactation resources holds potential to ensure consistent lactation support availability and reduce disparities in perinatal health and nutrition.

Direct Certification With Medicaid and School Lunch Participation Among Maryland Public Schools.
IMPORTANCE: States may join the US Department of Agriculture Direct Certification with Medicaid (DCM) program, allowing schools to use Medicaid participation to automatically qualify students for free and reduced-price school meals (F/RP). DCM also informs the Identified Student Percentage (ISP), which determines eligibility for the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP). Pre-COVID-19 evaluations found mixed associations between DCM and school meal participation. Pandemic-era policies included free meals for all students, which has ended in most states. Therefore, a postpandemic evaluation of DCM is warranted. OBJECTIVE: To examine the association of Maryland's DCM implementation in the 2022-2023 school year (SY22-23) with ISP, CEP eligibility and enrollment, and school lunch participation. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this cohort study, publicly available school-level data were used to examine annual ISP, CEP participation, and school lunch participation among public schools in Maryland. A school-level fixed effects model evaluated changes in school lunch participation before (SY18-19 and SY19-20) and after (SY22-23 and SY23-24) DCM implementation among non-CEP schools. A 2-way fixed effects model tested the association between CEP enrollment and school lunch participation among schools newly eligible for CEP due to DCM. Data analyses were conducted from July to December 2025. EXPOSURE: DCM implementation. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: ISP, CEP eligibility and enrollment, and school lunch participation. RESULTS: Among 1252 schools, 856 (68.4%) were elementary, 221 (17.7%) were middle, and 175 (14.0%) were high schools; 734 (58.6%) were suburban, 258 (20.6%) were located in rural or small towns, and 260 (20.8%) were urban. Mean (SD) ISP increased from 25.9% (17.5%) in SY21-22 to 37.3% (19.6%) in SY22-23 after DCM implementation. In SY23-24, CEP eligibility and enrollment increased by 26.7 and 22.2 percentage points, respectively. School lunch participation increased by 1.9 (95% CI, 1.1-2.8) percentage points (P < .001) among non-CEP schools post-DCM (SY22-23 and SY23-24). Among schools newly participating in CEP, school lunch participation increased by 6.5 (95% CI, 4.6-8.3) percentage points (P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of Maryland public schools, DCM implementation was associated with increases in direct certification for F/RP meals, CEP participation, and lunch participation. DCM implementation may support school meal participation in the post-COVID-19 pandemic context. Programs such as CEP and Medicaid may warrant policy attention to support school meal access and its benefits for student health and academic outcomes.

Bidirectional Synergistic Interaction Between Influenza Virus and SARS-CoV-2 in the Postpandemic Era: A Modeling Study.
INTRODUCTION: Influenza and COVID-19 are major respiratory diseases whose co-circulation dynamics are not fully understood. Surveillance data from the postpandemic period, free from the confounding effects of nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPIs), provide a unique opportunity to study their interactions. This study aimed to (1) estimate the direction and strength of the epidemiological interactions between influenza virus and SARS-CoV-2 and (2) quantify the impact of these interactions on the cumulative disease burden. METHODS: We developed a deterministic influenza virus × SARS-CoV-2 12-compartmental model SIR × SEIR using weekly laboratory surveillance data from Hong Kong between 2023 and 2025. Interaction parameters were introduced across multiple pathways to quantify the effect of one virus on the transmission of the other. Model parameters were estimated via maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), with uncertainty assessed using bootstrap resampling. Counterfactual simulations were conducted to evaluate the impact of interactions on cumulative infection incidence. Sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate the robustness of our findings. RESULTS: The model identified a significant bidirectional synergistic interaction. Specifically, prior exposure to SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a relative risk of influenza virus infection that was 1.24 (95% CI: 1.13, 1.35) times higher compared to the scenario without interaction, while SARS-CoV-2 infection and recovery from it were associated with relative risks of influenza virus infection that were 2.43 (2.20, 2.66) and 12.04 (10.93, 13.17) times higher, respectively. Additionally, influenza virus infection was associated with a relative risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection that was 2.39 (2.17, 2.62) times higher, and recovery from influenza was associated with a relative risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection that was 9.92 (9.00, 10.84) times higher. Counterfactual analysis demonstrated that this interaction substantially amplified epidemic sizes. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides strong epidemiological evidence that influenza virus and SARS-CoV-2 exhibit a bidirectional synergistic interaction at the population level, which significantly elevates the total disease burden. These findings underscore the urgent need for multifaceted public health preparedness, including enhanced clinical management and multiplex testing, optimized vaccination strategies, and integrated multipathogen surveillance to mitigate the amplified burden from influenza virus-SARS-CoV-2 synergy.

Plerixafor and G-CSF Versus Placebo and G-CSF in Moderately Mobilizing Patients With Multiple Myeloma to Optimize Hematopoietic Stem Cell Collection Results (OPTIMIZE).
Efficient collection of hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) is essential for autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) in multiple myeloma (MM). Although plerixafor is routinely used in poor mobilizers, its role in patients with intermediate mobilization capacity remains unclear. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase IV trial, MM patients with peripheral blood (PB) CD34+ counts of 15-40 cells/μL after steady-state G-CSF mobilization were randomized to receive plerixafor or placebo. The primary endpoint was successful collection of ≥ 6.0 × 106 CD34+ cells/kg, sufficient for two ASCTs, during a single apheresis session. Secondary endpoints included CD34+ kinetics, graft composition, colony-forming capacity, engraftment, immune reconstitution, and safety. Twenty-one patients were enrolled before premature study termination due to changes in first-line MM therapy and the COVID-19 pandemic. Plerixafor significantly increased PB CD34+ cell counts compared with placebo (p < 0.001). All patients receiving plerixafor achieved the primary endpoint, whereas none in the placebo group achieved it (p < 0.001). Mean CD34+ yield was significantly higher with plerixafor (10.4 ± 1.9 × 106/kg vs. 2.9 ± 1.3 × 106/kg; p < 0.001). Plerixafor-mobilized grafts contained significantly higher numbers of primitive hematopoietic progenitor subsets and demonstrated increased CFU-GM formation, indicating enhanced clonogenic potential. Despite marked differences in graft quantity and quality, engraftment kinetics, graft sustainability, and immune reconstitution were comparable between groups. In MM patients with intermediate mobilization capacity, the addition of plerixafor markedly improved stem cell mobilization efficiency and enriched grafts with functionally robust progenitor cells. These findings suggest that selected patients beyond conventional poor mobilizers may benefit from plerixafor-assisted mobilization. Trial Registration: EudraCT nr.: 2016-004122-41.

Alcohol Use Trajectories Across Disasters: Associations With Depression and Illness Anxiety.
BACKGROUND: Alcohol use often fluctuates following disasters, but individual trajectories and their links to mental health remain poorly understood. This study examined long-term patterns of alcohol use among disaster-exposed adults and their associations with depression and illness anxiety (a preoccupation with having or acquiring a serious illness). METHODS: Data (N = 941) came from five waves (2016-2024) of the Survey of Trauma, Resilience, and Opportunity among Neighborhoods in the Gulf (STRONG), a longitudinal cohort of adults in the U.S. Gulf Coast region. Growth mixture modeling identified latent trajectories of alcohol use across nine years encompassing multiple disasters (Deepwater Horizon oil spill, hurricanes, COVID-19 pandemic). Multinomial regression examined demographic and disaster exposure correlates of trajectory membership. Linear mixed-effects models assessed associations between drinking trajectories and longitudinal changes in depression and illness anxiety. RESULTS: A four-class model best fit the data: Low Stable (36%), Elevated Stable (47%), Decreasing (11%), and Increasing (7%) drinking trajectories. Elevated Stable drinkers were younger, more educated, and less likely to be female or Black. Disaster exposure differed modestly by class, with only oil spill exposure and COVID-19 disruptions associated with drinking patterns. Over time, depression increased among Elevated Stable and Increasing drinkers, while illness anxiety rose among Elevated Stable and Decreasing drinkers. CONCLUSIONS: Alcohol use and mental health trajectories following disasters are heterogeneous and interrelated. Persistent or increasing drinking was linked to worsening depression, while illness anxiety followed distinct patterns. Tailored prevention and intervention strategies should consider individual drinking trajectories and disaster context.

Temporal Trends of Serum Epstein-Barr Virus DNA Positivity Among Clinically Tested Pediatric Patients in Hangzhou, China, 2016-2025: A 10-Year Retrospective Study.
This study aimed To describe the 10-year temporal trends of serum Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA positivity among pediatric patients tested at Hangzhou Children's Hospital, and to explore demographic and seasonal variations across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. A total of 11,689 serum samples from children aged 0-15 years who underwent EBV nucleic acid testing at Hangzhou Children's Hospital from January 2016 to December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed, including 2,160 positive results. Demographic characteristics (sex, age), visit type (outpatient/inpatient), and temporal distributions (year, month) were examined. Monthly detection rates were calculated using monthly testing denominators. Group comparisons were performed using chi-square tests; the linear-by-linear association Chi-square test was applied to annual rates. Multivariable negative-binomial regression with offset for monthly test volumes and interrupted time-series analysis (ITSA) were used to evaluate independent associations with secular trend, seasonality, and pandemic phase. The overall EBV-DNA detection rate was 18.48% (2,160/11,689) among tested samples. A deduplication sensitivity analysis yielded a corrected patient-level rate of 18.26%, confirming robustness. Females (20.04%) had a higher rate than males (17.26%, χ2 = 14.66, p 0.05). In this hospital-based tested population, serum EBV-DNA positivity showed a significant upward secular trend over 2016-2025. The post-pandemic increase was primarily driven by a pre-existing secular trend rather than a discrete "rebound" attributable to immunity debt. Due to selection bias from non-standardized testing indications, these findings should not be generalized to the general pediatric community. Future studies with population-based sampling and serological differentiation of primary infection versus reactivation are needed.

Barriers to Voice Behavior in Online and Hybrid Multidisciplinary Team Meetings: A Qualitative Study.
RATIONALE: Guidelines for the treatment of a variety of diseases and medical conditions increasingly call for decision-making by a multidisciplinary team, which typically takes place during multidisciplinary team meetings (MDTMs). However, studies examining in-person MDTMs show that the decision-making processes during such meetings often fall short of optimal performance due to participants refraining from exercising voice behavior-denoting the communicative act of sharing one's perspectives, suggestions, and concerns related to the patient's diagnosis and treatment options with fellow participants. The expanding digitalization and the COVID-19 pandemic have led to an increase in online and hybrid meetings, potentially introducing new obstacles to participants' voice behavior. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: The present paper aims to explore the challenges encountered by participants of online and hybrid MDTMs in exercising their voice behavior. METHODS: Observations of neuro-oncology MDTMs in two Dutch hospitals and interviews with chairpersons and participants of the observed MDTMs. RESULTS: Respondents encountered difficulties in expressing their perspectives, ideas, and concerns during online and hybrid meetings, which could be attributed to (1) the absence of non-verbal cues, (2) technological deficiencies, (3) a personal lack of focus, (4) suboptimal layout of the meeting room, and (5) challenges in building relationships with other attendees. CONCLUSIONS: Obstacles to voice behavior in MDTMs are multifaceted, with specific barriers inherent to online and hybrid meetings that are not present in in-person meetings.

Reallocating Surgical Activity to Expand Critical Care Capacity During the SARS-CoV-2 Pandemic: A Descriptive and Analytical Study in a French University Hospital Network.
RATIONALE: The ability to anticipate ICU beds mobilizable through elective surgical postponements during health system shocks remains poorly quantified. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: Using real-world COVID-19 deprogramming data, we combined a classification of acceptable surgical deferral times with predictive models of expected surgical activity to estimate ICU capacity that can be generated in crisis scenarios. METHOD: We conducted a retrospective time-series analysis of all surgical procedures performed from 2017 to 2021 in three AP-HP university hospitals. Procedures were classified as non-deferrable (red), deferrable 1 month (green). Expected weekly surgical volumes for 2020-2021 without pandemic disruption were predicted using models trained on 2017-2018 and validated on 2019 (XGBoost, Holt-Winters). Multivariable linear regression quantified the association between postponed procedures and ICU beds opened, enabling projection of capacity gains under different postponement scenarios. RESULTS: Among 196,469 procedures, 59% were red, 20% orange, and 21% green. Surgical activity declined by 13% in 2020% and 8% in 2021, while ICU capacity increased by up to 85 and 46 beds, respectively. Reductions were mainly driven by postponement of green procedures (IRR 0.78 [0.75-0.80]). Only postponed green procedures were significantly associated with ICU bed expansion (β = 0.75, 95% CI 0.53-0.97; p < 0.001), accounting for 34.6% of ICU bed demand. CONCLUSION: Clinically acceptable postponement of low-priority elective surgery contributes substantially to ICU surge capacity. Integrating prioritization and predictive modeling into preparedness strategies may support balanced, data-driven responses to future healthcare system shocks.

Danger, Duty, Resilience: A Phenomenological Study of Nurse Anesthetists' Lived Experiences During the Rwanda Marburg Outbreak.
Marburg virus disease, a hemorrhagic fever without approved vaccine or cure, emerged in Rwanda in late 2024. During the outbreak, nurse anesthetists provided critical care to severely ill patients, including infected colleagues. Healthcare workers comprised most confirmed cases, with anesthetists and nurses among the earliest fatalities. The voices of nurse anesthetists reveal the essence of the phenomenon. This study used the methods of inductive phenomonology to discover the essential meaning of the lived experiences of nurse anesthetists working in Kigali referral hospitals during the outbreak. Semistructured interviews conducted in English and Kinyarwanda were theme analyzed using qualitative software and secondary content analysis. All participants were experienced, practicing nurse anesthetists, of whom three tested positive for the virus after caring for Marburg patients. Five major themes emerged to encompass the essence of the phenomenon: endured trauma, duty amid danger, chaos to coordination, stigma and isolation, and transformation through crisis. Participants endured the profound trauma of panic, danger, grief, despair, and social rejection alongside professional commitment, resilience, and a renewed vision for their role in health crises.

Combined Effects of Biomarkers in NLRP3 Inflammasome Axis and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Multivessels Disease.
BACKGROUND: Inflammation plays a crucial role in adverse outcomes of coronary artery disease. NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activates 2 classical pathways: interleukin-1β (IL-1β)/IL-6/high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and IL-18/IL-6/hsCRP. However, the predictive value of pathway-related biomarkers, particularly their combinations, remains to be systematically evaluated. OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to explore the predictive value of individual and combined biomarkers from 2 pathways for long-term cardiovascular risk in patients with multivessel disease (MVD). METHODS: From a prospective, multicenter cohort, 1,058 consecutive patients with MVD were enrolled. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular event (MACCE-4P), a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, revascularization, and stroke. RESULTS: During a median 2-year follow-up (IQR: 2.0-2.1 years), 130/1,058 (12.3%) MACCE-4P occurred. After multivariable adjustment, higher levels of IL-1β (HR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.15-2.32), IL-6 (1.72, 1.20-2.46), and hsCRP (1.59, 1.09-2.30) were associated with increased MACCE-4P risk, whereas IL-18 was not. For combined analysis, any 2-biomarker combination from either the IL-1β/IL-6/hsCRP or IL-18/IL-6/hsCRP pathway significantly predicted higher MACCE-4P risk (HR range: 1.84-2.19), with further risk elevation observed for the 3-biomarker combinations (HR: 3.09; 95% CI: 1.80-5.31 for IL-1β pathway; HR: 2.26; 95% CI: 1.24-4.14 for IL-18 pathway). The 4-biomarker combination (IL-1β+IL-6+IL-18+hsCRP) also predicted significantly higher MACCE-4P risk (HR: 2.64; 95% CI: 1.36-5.14). Notably, 3-/4-combined biomarkers demonstrated significant incremental predictive value over single biomarkers. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with MVD, combined assessment of NLRP3-associated inflammatory biomarkers offers significant incremental predictive value beyond individual biomarkers. These findings highlight the importance of integrating multiple inflammatory biomarkers to better identify patients with residual inflammatory risk.

Spatiotemporal disease suitability prediction for Oropouche virus and the role of vectors across the Americas.
Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging arbovirus with increasing outbreaks in South America, yet its environmental drivers and potential range remain poorly understood. Using ecological niche modeling (ENM) with random forests, we assessed the environmental suitability of OROV and its primary vector, Culicoides paraensis, across Brazil and the Americas. We evaluated five pseudo-absence sampling techniques, considering pseudo-absence ratios, buffer radii, and density smoothing factors to determine the most effective modeling approach. Key environmental predictors included humidity, agricultural land-use, and forest cover, while temperature had minimal influence for both the virus and the vector. The resulting suitability model identifies high transmission risk areas in Central and South America, and reveals that environmental suitability patterns align with seasonal fluctuations in case numbers, with peaks in Amazonian states at the beginning of the year and an expansion into non-Amazonian regions later in the year. A bivariate suitability map highlighted strong spatial overlap between OROV and Culicoides paraensis, with potential co-suitability areas with Culex quinquefasciatus mosquito, a suspected secondary vector. These findings enhance understanding of OROV transmission dynamics, supporting risk assessment, surveillance, and vector control strategies.

Temporal and Spatial Distribution of Dengue Case Fatality Rates in Bangladesh: A Retrospective Investigation.
Dengue remains a significant public health challenge in Bangladesh, with considerable variation in disease burden and mortality. This study aimed to assess how dengue case fatality rates (CFRs) had varied across months, seasons, and geographic regions of Bangladesh. A retrospective observational study was conducted from January 2021 to December 2025 using surveillance data obtained from the Directorate General of Health Services, Bangladesh (DGHS). Descriptive statistical analyses were performed to estimate dengue CFR. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the association between the studied variables and dengue CFR. Seasonal and trend components of the data were examined through LOESS-based decomposition to understand underlying time-series patterns. Over the past 5 years, a total of 6,15,991 dengue cases and 3,079 deaths, with an overall CFR of 0.49%, were recorded. The year-wise highest CFR was recorded in 2024 (0.56%; 95% CI: 0.52-0.62). The month-wise and season-wise mean CFRs were recorded highest in February (1.21%) and winter (0.74%), respectively, while the division-wise highest mean CFR was recorded in Dhaka (0.60%). In addition, the month of February (AOR = 3.09; 95% CI 1.59-5.38; p < 0.001) and the winter season (OR = 1.61; 95% CI 1.41-1.82; p < 0.001) had significantly higher odds for dengue CFR. Compared to Dhaka, most of the other divisions had significantly (p < 0.001) lower odds for dengue CFR. The year 2024 had significantly (p < 0.001) higher odds for dengue CFR compared to most other years under study. This present study identified the critical time and high-risk areas in Bangladesh, underscoring the need for public health interventions and enhanced surveillance systems.

Multi-omics integration reveals tissue-specific biosynthesis of sesquiterpenoids in the medicinal plant Eupatorium lindleyanum.
BACKGROUND: Eupatorium lindleyanum is a medicinal plant rich in bioactive sesquiterpenoids, yet the genetic and regulatory basis underlying their biosynthesis remains completely unexplored. In particular, the marked tissue-specific accumulation of these compounds-abundant in aerial organs but scarce in roots-lacks a molecular explanation. RESULTS: Here, we integrated UPLC-MS/MS-based metabolomics with RNA-Seq transcriptomics to comprehensively profile sesquiterpenoid metabolites and their associated gene expression signatures across root, stem, leaf, and flower tissues of Eupatorium lindleyanum. A total of 321 sesquiterpenoids were identified, exhibiting distinct tissue-specific accumulation patterns with highest abundance in flower, followed by leaf. Comparative analysis revealed 299 differentially accumulated sesquiterpenoid metabolites (DSMs), which were clustered into three major groups with preferential accumulation in leaf (Cluster 1), flower (Cluster 2), and root (Cluster 3). Transcriptome sequencing generated 99.43 Gb of clean data, yielding 147743 unigenes. Integration of metabolomic and transcriptomic datasets screened 20 structural genes (88 unigenes) involved in sesquiterpenoid biosynthesis, including MVA pathway genes (ACAT, HMGCS, HMGCR, MVK, PMK, MVD), MEP pathway genes (dxs, dxr, ispD, ispE, ispF, ispG, ispH), and downstream modification genes (FDPS, IDI, GAS, GDS, NES1, GAO, FLDH). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) further prioritized hub genes within modules significantly correlated with key sesquiterpenoids. Additionally, five transcription factor families (AP2/ERF, NAC, WRKY, MYB, and bHLH) were identified as potential regulators based on strong correlations with DSMs accumulation. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first comprehensive view of tissue-specific sesquiterpenoid biosynthesis in Eupatorium lindleyanum, establishing a prioritized set of candidate genes and regulators for functional validation. Our findings offer a foundational resource for metabolic engineering and molecular breeding aimed at enhancing the production of pharmacologically active sesquiterpenoids in this medicinal species.

Accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure to forecast chikungunya outbreaks in Reunion Island and Paraguay: a mathematical modelling study.
BACKGROUND: Heterogeneity in mosquito exposure at a fine spatial scale is well documented but often neglected in mathematical models of arbovirus transmission, particularly for real-time forecasting. We aimed to assess whether accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure improves the ability of transmission models to reproduce past chikungunya outbreaks and to forecast an ongoing outbreak in real time. METHODS: We extended an existing transmission model, originally developed to forecast dengue outbreaks in Reunion Island and incorporating seasonality, to include heterogeneity in mosquito exposure. We compared this model to versions assuming homogeneous exposure, evaluating their ability to reproduce the 2005-06 Reunion Island outbreak and the 2023 Paraguay Metropolitana subregion outbreak. We then used the heterogeneity model to forecast the 2025 Reunion Island outbreak in real time. FINDINGS: Accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure at a fine spatial scale was crucial to accurately reproduce Reunion Island's 2005-06 outbreak. Homogeneity models either overestimated final seroprevalence (80% vs 38% observed) or required a reduction of approximately 50% in the basic reproduction number following interventions, which is implausible. The heterogeneity level estimated from this outbreak transferred successfully to the Metropolitana outbreak, accurately forecasting epidemic trajectory and final seroprevalence (∼40% vs ∼75% for the homogeneity model). Under the same assumption, the heterogeneity model successfully forecasted the peak of the 2025 Reunion Island outbreak (∼400 emergency room visits per week) and timing (April), nearly two months ahead. A post-outbreak serosurvey indicated that the heterogeneity model underestimated final seroprevalence (46·1% vs 61·6% observed), whereas the homogeneity model overestimated final seroprevalence (78·5%), suggesting that heterogeneity in 2025 might have been lower than that in 2005-06. INTERPRETATION: These results highlight how incorporating heterogeneity in mosquito exposure can improve chikungunya outbreaks forecasting. Our approach showed strong predictive performance in settings with climatic seasonality and holds promise for forecasting future chikungunya and other arbovirus outbreaks. FUNDING: EU; Laboratoire d'Excellence Integrative Biology of Emerging Infectious Diseases programme; Agence Nationale de Recherches Sur le Sida, les Hépatites Virales et les Maladies Infectieuses Émergentes; Agence Nationale de la Recherche.

Multi-Country Human-to-Human Andes Virus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship: A Disaster Report on Prehospital, Health Care Facility, and Public Health System Challenges - Essential Knowledge for Frontline Clinicians.
The Andes Virus (ANDV) outbreak reported on May 2, 2026, aboard a luxury vessel departing from Ushuaia, Patagonia, Argentina, was caused by an Orthohantavirus unique in its person-to-person transmissibility in contrast to zoonotic transmission characteristic of better-known hantaviruses. Containment required coordinated international management because passengers and crew embarked and disembarked at several international ports-of-call prior to outbreak recognition, resulting in cross-border transmission potential. Among those who disembarked, several traveled on flights to various destinations. Cases subsequently manifested in multiple countries, including Tristan da Cunha, Spain, France, Switzerland, South Africa, Canada, and The Netherlands. Upon notification, international health authorities implemented containment measures, such as contact tracing, quarantine, and isolation. Uniquely, ANDV poses distinctive risks due to its immediately prodromal presymptomatic transmission potential, initial non-specific flu-like symptoms, prolonged incubation period, conceivable long-term neurologic and endocrinologic sequalae, high case fatality rates (CFRs), and possibility of international dissemination. This report describes the successful management of a multi-national outbreak associated with cruise-ship travel, a setting with unique challenges. It also examines implications and challenges for prehospital, health care facility, and public health systems for future ANDV outbreaks. The event was characterized by delayed recognition, international spread, and complex coordination across multiple jurisdictions and sectors, including medical and public health authorities, policy- and decision-makers, crisis and emergency risk-communication experts, media, logistics, transportation, and security. Rapid implementation of public health measures coupled with clinician implementation of the Identify-Isolate-Inform (3I) model, a clinical framework to detect and prevent the spread of infectious disease, at the prehospital and health care facility levels are critical actions that can contain future ANDV outbreaks.

Congenital Arboviruses: A Review.
Congenital arboviruses represent a significant public health concern because of their ability to cross the placental barrier and adversely affect fetal development. In this review, we delineate the epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, and diagnostic challenges associated with key congenital arboviral infections, including Zika, dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, Oropouche, and West Nile virus. While vertical transmission mechanisms vary among arboviruses, inflammation, placental disruption, and viral replication within fetal tissues are common pathological features. Early diagnosis is complicated by overlapping clinical symptoms, limited laboratory capacity in endemic areas, and cross-reactivity in serological tests for flaviviruses. In this review, we highlight the need for improved surveillance, targeted diagnostics, and preventive strategies, including vector control and maternal vaccination, to reduce the burden of congenital arboviral diseases. Understanding the maternal-fetal dynamics of arboviral infections is essential for developing effective public health interventions and mitigating long-term outcomes in affected populations.

Integrated Experimental, Chemometric, and In Silico Analyses of Larvicidal Supercritical Extracts From Myrtaceae Species Against Aedes aegypti.
Supercritical extracts from five Myrtaceae species were evaluated for larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti (A. aegypti) and investigated through chemical profiling, concentration-response modeling, chemometric analysis, and molecular modeling. Leaf extracts of Corymbia citriodora, Eugenia uniflora (E. uniflora), Plinia cauliflora (P. cauliflora), Psidium cattleianum (P. cattleianum), and Psidium guajava were characterized by GC-MS and tested at 60-300 µg mL- 1 for 72 h. We also performed molecular docking analyses of the identified compounds against two A. aegypti targets, AeSCP-2 (PDB: 1PZ4) and AeHKT (PDB: 6MFB), and Drosophila melanogaster acetylcholinesterase (DmAChE; PDB: 6XYU), a homologous model of insect AChE. All extracts caused mortality, although responses differed among species. P. cattleianum and E. uniflora were highly active across the tested range, whereas P. cauliflora showed weaker, heterogeneous, and non-monotonic responses. PCA revealed marked compositional differences among species but no significant mortality gradient along the first two components. A grouped cross-validated regression tree showed modest predictive performance, indicating associations between covarying chemical profiles and mortality rather than independent compound effects. Docking against AeSCP-2, AeHKT, and DmAChE, followed by molecular dynamics of the AeSCP-2-β-sitosterol complex, identified structurally plausible ligand-target associations. Overall, the study demonstrates species-dependent larvicidal activity and provides experimentally testable hypotheses for prioritizing extracts, compounds, and molecular targets in future investigations.

Detection of Anaplasma capra in Patients with Suspected Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever, Turkey, 2022.
Anaplasma capra is a recently discovered bacterial tickborne pathogen that was first identified in goats in 2012 and later in humans in China in 2015. We detected and genetically characterized A. capra in adult patients with suspected Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF) in Turkey during the 2022 outbreak. We screened all patients for A. capra by using nested PCR targeting the gltA and groEL genes. We confirmed CCHF by molecular and serological tests. Of 263 patients, 6 (2.28%) were positive for A. capra. Sequence analysis revealed 84.16%-100% gltA gene similarity and 90.24%-100% groEL gene similarity with GenBank entries. Phylogenetic analysis confirmed all A. capra gene sequences belonged to genotype 1. Our results demonstrate clinical evidence of genotype 1 A. capra infection in humans. Our findings highlight the need for clinicians to consider A. capra in the differential diagnosis of CCHF-like symptoms, especially in endemic areas.

Meta-analysis of Maternal and Fetal Outcomes of Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever during Pregnancy.
Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF) during pregnancy is associated with severe maternal and fetal complications, but evidence remains limited to heterogeneous case reports. We synthesized patient-level data from published and unpublished cases identified through systematic database searches and direct collaboration with centers in CCHF-endemic areas. We harmonized patient-level clinical, laboratory, obstetric, treatment, and outcome data for 55 pregnancies. The maternal mortality rate was 28.8% (15/52), and fetal loss occurred in 57.4% (31/54) of cases. Maternal mortality rates increased with advancing gestation, reaching 31.3% in the third trimester, but fetal loss was highest (85.7%) in the first trimester. Ribavirin treatment during the third trimester was associated with lower observed maternal mortality rates (odds ratio 0.33, 95% CI 0.13-0.84; p = 0.031). Our findings highlight gestational age-specific risks of CCHF and support the need for standardized management protocols and strengthened CCHF surveillance during pregnancy in endemic regions.

Early Action Review of Detection, Notification, and Response Timeliness during Cross-Border Bundibugyo Virus Disease Outbreak, Uganda, 2026.
Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), an Ebola virus species with no licensed vaccine or therapeutic, reemerged in May 2026 as a cross-border outbreak in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. During a 2-day workshop, July 8-9, 2026, we conducted an early action review of the outbreak response using the 7-1-7 framework (7 days to detect, 1 day to notify, 7 days to complete early response actions) to assess timeliness and identify bottlenecks and enablers across 9 response pillars. Uganda declared its outbreak on May 15, 2026; by July 8, the country had recorded 20 confirmed cases (15 imported, 5 locally transmitted) and a case-fatality rate of 15%. Uganda met all 3 targets: detection in 6 days, notification in <1 day, and response completion in 2 days. Low clinical suspicion, cross-border data-sharing gaps, fragmented digital systems, and delayed community engagement were common bottlenecks; strong leadership and coordination structures were most cited enablers.

Plasma Exchange for Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome: A Mechanistic Case for an Untested Intervention.
Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) carries a case fatality rate of 35%-40% and has no approved pharmacologic treatment. Its pathophysiology is rooted in the plasma compartment: cytokines, viral antigens, immune complexes, and platelet-binding glycoproteins circulate as drivers of immunopathologic endothelial injury, noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, and cardiogenic depression. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) achieves bulk clearance of plasma-borne mediators and is established by the American Society for Apheresis (ASFA) for numerous indications that share an analogous mechanistic rationale. This commentary argues that the immunopathology of HPS maps onto the therapeutic targets of TPE, that any intervention would need to be timed to the early cardiopulmonary phase, and that the coagulopathic dimension of the disease provides a mechanistic argument for incorporating plasma into the replacement strategy. We deliberately situate this rationale against the uneven record of TPE in diseases of comparable pathophysiology, in which the intervention has been effective in some settings and without demonstrable benefit in others. The recent Andes virus outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, which produced a multinational cluster of severe cardiopulmonary cases, prompted us, as transfusion medicine and apheresis physicians, to articulate this hypothesis.
